Soft-float chosen over fixed-point for v0: the only float work is per-frame normalization over small vectors (~hundreds of values), microseconds even soft-float on the ARM926 — re-validating a fixed-point reimplementation isn't worth it until profiling says so. A generated header (not hand-ported constants) keeps the firmware data in lockstep with the proven prototype and re-emittable when the corpus/params change; plain PODs + flat arrays avoid coupling to firmware struct layout. `game_task` is pure compute on the existing video frame queue + `FretboardLink_Send`, so no new peripheral / no re-apply-patch churn. |
```text
133	| 2026-06-15 | **Navigator is observation-driven: each loop iteration runs whichever plan step's `expected_from` matches the currently observed screen (not a fixed program counter).** Verbs: `practice_run` + generic `goto`. Selections strum the signed delta from the observed cursor; FULL SONG/FULL SPEED strum up until the selection stops moving. | One rule gives the three behaviours the nav doc needs: normal progress (next screen matches the next step), the `part_select` skip (an absent part means the observed `difficulty_select` matches a later step and the part step is simply never run), and recovery (an off-plan screen matches no step → press RED to back up until a known screen reappears, then resume). Delta-from-observed-selection is sticky-default-safe; saturate-until-stable avoids a blind strum count (and is the agreed `section_select` mechanism). Closed-loop verification is implicit: a mis-fire just means the next observation matches no expected step → recover. |
134	| 2026-06-15 | **Offline navigator is proven against a simulated GH3 menu (`simgame`) behind an `Observer`/`Actuator` seam; the real observer is exercised via a `CorpusObserver`.** | No console/actuator offline, so the sim is the test oracle (with configurable part-absent / sticky / misfire to actually exercise the control logic). The seam is the firmware boundary — swap in the CV observer + fretboard link to port. The `CorpusObserver` runs the whole practice run on real corpus frames through the phase-1–3 vision stack (0 fallbacks in the default config), proving the observer's outputs are exactly what the controller consumes. |
135	| 2026-06-15 | **Setlist (main/bonus) is read from the page background colour — warmth = R−B over a large background ROI (median, robust to overlaid text) — not from the setlist tabs.** | 100% clean and 100% under slop. The "setlist"/"bonus" tabs are only on screen when the first song is selected — they scroll off for song 2+ (Greg), so a tab ROI is empty for 63/64 frames (that earlier approach was ~75%). The page itself is always visible and differs by setlist: main = yellow parchment, bonus = whiter. R−B is offset-invariant and gain-preserving, so it survives the analog slop. (Song ID already yields the setlist via match-all; this is an independent, now-reliable confirmation.) |
136	| 2026-06-15 | **song_select reader = low-res grayscale grid over the highlight-slot ROI, matched against all 64 per-song templates with a small read-time offset search; setlist derived from the winning song, not the tab.** Grid 32×6, offsets dx∈{-6,-3,0,3,6}/dy∈{-3,0,3}. | 64/64 clean, ~99.1% slop. Matching all 64 (vs filtering by a setlist read first) means main/bonus separation is automatic and removes any dependence on reading the setlist first. The slot grid must be fine to separate ~40 short titles by ink pattern, but a fine grid over a tight ROI is shift-sensitive (translate robustness ~70%); a small offset search re-aligns per frame and recovers it to ~100% (overall slop 90.5%→99.1%) at modest cost (the ROI is small). Per-frame luma normalization handles gain/offset. The per-setlist first song (Slow Ride/Avalancha) sits one row lower (list can't scroll up past it), so its template is built from a second, lower ROI; both ROIs are fingerprinted at read time and each template scores against the one it came from. |
137	| 2026-06-15 | **"Reading" menu items / song titles = closed-set bitmap matching, NOT char-level OCR; char/digit OCR is reserved for open-ended values (scores).** | We have a reference snapshot per menu item and per song, so the selected item/song is recognized by matching its fixed region against the known templates (the same fingerprint idea as the screen classifier). Per-character decoding is only needed where there's no template — i.e. scores/multipliers/note counts — which is a later, separate phase. Keeps phase 2 free of OCR. |
138	| 2026-06-15 | **Static-list highlight reader = per-screen menu geometry (band + ordered items + axis) + per-cell "deviation from unselected baseline" with per-frame colour normalization; argmax over cells.** Scope = the 8 fixed-count static lists; `section_select` (variable list) and `song_select` (fixed-slot) deferred. | GH3 marks selection by *changing* a row (colour shift / highlight bar), not always by making it brightest — a luma/white argmax collided on most screens (flat scores). Comparing each cell to its own learned unselected appearance ("what changed") handles every highlight style and baselines out background art (main_menu / practice_end sit over collage). Baseline uses only *unselected* exemplars per cell so it's non-degenerate at K=2 (a median-over-all collapses to the midpoint and can't separate two items — that bug showed as exactly 1/2 on the three two-item screens). Per-frame normalization (subtract mean cell colour, scale by spread) cancels the analog gain/offset slop, lifting slop robustness ~90%→~99%. Result: 100% clean / 99.4% slop on 33 labelled frames. Baselines are learned from the corpus (a `SelectionCalibration`, parallel to the classifier's centroids); the firmware port bakes them. Band geometry was placed by auto-locating each selection's highlight from the labelled frames, not by eyeballing. |
139	| 2026-06-15 | **`items` are stored in on-screen order (top→bottom / left→right). Confirmed by visual inspection + the validated reader that all three 2-item screens match the `gh3_navigation.md` index order: `quit_confirm` = cancel(top)/quit(bottom), `part_select` = lead(top)/rhythm(bottom), `training_menu` = tutorials(left)/practice(right).** | An earlier crude white-min-channel *residual* diagnostic (used only to locate rows) was fooled by the light highlight bar and reported inverted rows for the 2-item screens, which raised a false flag. The actual reader (per-cell deviation from unselected baseline) reads each frame's true selection (2/2 per screen) — and since the highlighted cell is the one that deviates, a correct read proves `items` order = physical order. Full-res frames confirm cancel/lead/tutorials are the top/left items, matching the nav-doc indices. No discrepancy; nothing for M10 to reconcile here. |
140	| 2026-06-15 | **Prototype lives in its own `tools/gameplay/` subproject (own uv env + this journal); phase 1 is host-only (no firmware export yet).** | The observer+navigator are a distinct workstream that will grow (highlight reader, navigator, firmware module), so a dedicated subproject with its own journal (CLAUDE.md rule 4) is cleaner than folding into `marvin-perf` (a perf-log decoder). Host-only keeps the first phase focused on proving the algorithm; the firmware-consumable template export is deferred to the actual M9 port. |
141	| 2026-06-15 | **Screen classifier = coarse fixed-region mean-BGR fingerprint + nearest-centroid (per-class) + two-gate UNKNOWN reject (`d_best ≤ t_abs` AND `margin ≥ t_margin`).** Default config 12×8 grid, 5×5 samples/region, per-frame normalization on. | Matches Q10 (fixed-region/colour, not general CV) and the static nature of GH3 screens. Coarse region averaging buys positional-slop tolerance; the design is integer-L1 over uint8 vectors so the firmware port is mechanical. Default chosen empirically from the eval sweep — see normalization decision. |
142	| 2026-06-15 | **Per-frame normalization is on by default; it is required for value-slop robustness.** | The Wii feed is analog component → HDMI, so it carries gain/offset value slop. With raw means, brightening a frame moves its fingerprint far from its centroid in absolute L1 → false UNKNOWN; robustness to gain/offset was 65/202 and 22/202. Standardizing each frame's fingerprint to a fixed mean/std cancels affine gain/offset and lifted slop-robustness to ~99.8% (offset 155→202/202) at negligible cost (normalization is over the ~288-element vector, microseconds). |
143	| 2026-06-15 | **Threshold recommendation accepts every legitimate in-class match (`t_abs = 1.2 × worst in-class LOO distance`), with a soft margin gate (`0.5 × smallest in-class margin`); unseen-screen rejection is a *reported* secondary metric, not something we trade real-screen accuracy for.** | First-pass logic tuned `t_abs`/`t_margin` to separate held-out impostors, which over-rejected real screens (every LOO "failure" was a false UNKNOWN, not a misclassification). The observer's primary job is correctly identifying the 13 known screens; some genuinely-novel screen leaking through is acceptable and handled by the navigator's closed-loop + RED-recovery. Impostor leak is logged (9/101 at the default config) for honesty. |
144	| 2026-06-15 | **Sample density is a first-class fingerprint knob (dense vs N×N lattice per region); default subsampled (5×5).** | The on-device cost is dominated by reading the frame out of the uncached `.region_nocache` framebuffer (marvin journal 2026-05-20), so it's memory-bound. Dense = full-frame touch ≈ 7–20 ms; a sparse lattice mirrors cv_marvin_v1's existing 5×5 patch sampling and is sub-millisecond. The coarse average absorbs the extra sampling noise — eval shows subsampled matches dense on accuracy/robustness — so the cheap path is the default. |

148	## Hardware cost note (SAM9X75 port target)
149	
150	ARM926EJ-S, ARMv5TE, single core, up to 800 MHz, no SIMD. The classifier is **memory-bound,
151	not compute-bound** — the dominant cost is reading frame pixels from the uncached DDR
152	framebuffer (~50–150 MB/s sequential; ~50–150 ns per strided single access). Compute
153	(per-region integer sums + an L1 distance over 13 templates ≈ a couple thousand byte ops) is
154	microseconds.
155	
156	- Dense (every pixel, 720×480×3 ≈ 1.04 MB): **~7–20 ms**.
157	- Subsampled lattice (default 12×8 × 5×5 = 2400 reads): **~0.1–0.4 ms**.
158	
159	Either is far from "seconds"; the observer needs only a few Hz for menu navigation, so the
160	subsampled path costs <1% CPU at 5–10 Hz.

196	## Session log
197	
198	### 2026-07-07 — prototype: title **length + prefix** song reader (`songselect_prefix.py`) — negative result
199	
200	Greg flagged the `song_select` reader mis-reading certain songs on real hardware and asked
201	whether a minimal-OCR "length + prefix" approach could do better. **CSV analysis** of the
202	64-song catalog (`data/games/gh3-wii/songs.csv`): the full title charset is 54 glyphs, but the
203	identifying signal is up front — **`(title length, first 2 case-insensitive chars)` uniquely
204	separates all 64 songs** (7-char case-insensitive prefix alone also does; first-2 alone leaves
205	15 collision groups, e.g. "The…" ×5, so length is the tie-breaker).
206	
207	Built a **parallel** reader (`gameplay/songselect_prefix.py`, original `songselect.py`
208	untouched): reads only the **title sub-band** (top ~30% of the slot ROI; artist/year is below),
209	and matches on two features — normalized **ink extent (length)** + a low-res normalized luma
210	grid over the **leading window** of the title — with the same read-time offset search. Distance
211	= `prefix_L1 + length_weight·|Δlength|`.
212	
213	**Result — it does not beat the whole-slot match; it's a useful negative:**
214	- Clean corpus **64/64** (ties baseline). But **worst inter-song margin collapses** (~0.04–0.79
215	  vs baseline **5.63**), and analog-slop robustness is **~88% at best vs baseline 99.1%**.
216	- Category breakdown pinpoints why: gain/offset/noise **100%**, but **scale ~58–60%**,
217	  **translate ~85%**. Rendered title lengths are packed **~1 px apart** (min gap 0 px on a
218	  330 px ROI), so the length feature that must break the many shared-prefix ties has **no margin
219	  against overscan/underscan (±3% ≈ ±10 px)** — exactly the analog slop we can't avoid.
220	- **Root cause / takeaway:** the information-theoretic sufficiency of (length, first-2-chars)
221	  does **not** survive as *analog bitmap* features. Many titles share leading glyphs (matches
222	  the CSV collision groups), so the prefix grid barely separates them, and the length tie-breaker
223	  is the single most scale-fragile feature. The whole-slot match wins because it uses the entire
224	  title's ink as independent evidence.
225	- **The real "minimal OCR" path is discrete, not bitmap:** classify the first ~2–3 glyphs to
226	  actual character *labels* + read an integer length → exact-key lookup, immune to
227	  analog-distance collapse. That needs a glyph classifier (segmentation + per-glyph templates;
228	  ~26 glyph classes cover all first-3 prefixes) — a bigger lift with a one-frame-per-song data
229	  constraint, deferred pending Greg's call. **Caveat:** the corpus is clean digital captures
230	  (baseline already 100%/99.1% here), so it does not reproduce the on-hardware mis-reads Greg
231	  sees — the synthetic slop envelope is only a proxy. Files: `gameplay/songselect_prefix.py` (new).
232	
233	**Follow-up (same day) — the port is faithful; the misreads are an integration gap (active-area
234	offset not applied by the CV readers).** Greg gave four real on-hardware misreads
235	(paint_it_black→cult_of_personality, same_old_song_and_dance→my_name_is_jonas,
236	cult_of_personality→kool_thing, raining_blood→before_i_forget) and noted the corpus is exported
```

```text
1	"""song_select reader: which song is in the highlight slot, and which setlist.
2	
3	`song_select` is fixed-slot — the selected song sits in a fixed highlight slot
4	while the list scrolls under it. We identify the song by **matching the selected
5	title line's low-resolution bitmap against the known per-song templates**
6	(closed-set nearest-match, the same idea as the screen classifier; deliberately
7	*not* char-level OCR — we have a reference image of every song). The ROI is
8	registered on the highlighted title glyphs (right of the album-art thumbnail);
9	see `metadata.SONG_SLOT_ROI`.
10	
11	Two wrinkles, both from the corpus:
12	- Each setlist's first song (Slow Ride on main, Avalancha on bonus) sits one row
13	  lower (the list can't scroll up past it), so its template comes from
14	  `SONG_FIRST_ROI`; every other song uses `SONG_SLOT_ROI`. At read time we
15	  fingerprint both ROIs and compare each template against the ROI it was built
16	  from.
17	- main vs bonus setlists overlap by position, so we first read which setlist tab
18	  is lit and match only within that catalog.
19	
20	The slot fingerprint is a low-res grayscale grid over the ROI (fine enough to
21	separate ~40 short titles by their ink pattern), normalized per frame to cancel
22	the analog gain/offset slop. Integer-friendly for the firmware port.
23	"""
24	
25	from __future__ import annotations
26	
27	from collections import defaultdict
28	from dataclasses import dataclass
29	
30	import numpy as np
31	
32	from .corpus import Sample
33	from .fingerprint import _to_canonical
34	from .metadata import (
35	    SETLIST_BG_ROI,
36	    SONG_FIRST_ROI,
37	    SONG_SLOT_ROI,
38	    song_from_filename,
39	)
40	
41	# Luma weights (B, G, R) /256.
42	_LUMA_W = np.array([29, 150, 77], dtype=np.float64)
43	
44	FIRST = "first"
45	SLOT = "slot"
46	
47	
48	@dataclass(frozen=True)
49	class SongConfig:
50	    cols: int = 32  # horizontal cells across the title (captures the ink pattern)
51	    rows: int = 6   # vertical cells down the title line
52	    # Small read-time offset search (px) that re-aligns the slot before matching —
53	    # this is what makes the fine grid tolerant of the analog path's positional
54	    # slop (without it, a few-px shift drops translate robustness to ~70%).
55	    dx_search: tuple[int, ...] = (-6, -3, 0, 3, 6)
56	    dy_search: tuple[int, ...] = (-6, -3, 0, 3, 6)
57	
58	
59	DEFAULT_SONG_CONFIG = SongConfig()
60	
61	
62	@dataclass(frozen=True)
63	class SongTemplate:
64	    setlist: str
65	    index: int
66	    song_id: str
67	    roi_kind: str  # SLOT or FIRST
68	    vec: np.ndarray
69	
70	
71	@dataclass(frozen=True)
72	class SongCatalog:
73	    templates: list[SongTemplate]
74	    config: SongConfig
75	    setlist_warmth_threshold: float  # bg (R-B) above this => main (yellow), else bonus
76	
77	
78	@dataclass(frozen=True)
79	class SongResult:
80	    setlist: str
81	    index: int
82	    song_id: str
83	    dist: float
84	    margin: float  # 2nd-best dist - best dist (higher = more confident)
85	
86	
87	def _luma_grid(image: np.ndarray, roi: tuple[int, int, int, int], cfg: SongConfig) -> np.ndarray:
88	    """Per-frame-normalized low-res luma grid over an ROI -> length cols*rows."""
89	    img = _to_canonical(image)
90	    x0, y0, x1, y1 = roi
91	    patch = img[y0:y1, x0:x1].astype(np.float64)
92	    luma = patch @ _LUMA_W / 256.0  # (h, w)
93	    ys = np.linspace(0, luma.shape[0], cfg.rows + 1).round().astype(int)
94	    xs = np.linspace(0, luma.shape[1], cfg.cols + 1).round().astype(int)
95	    cells = np.empty((cfg.rows, cfg.cols), dtype=np.float64)
96	    for r in range(cfg.rows):
97	        for c in range(cfg.cols):
98	            cells[r, c] = luma[ys[r]:ys[r + 1], xs[c]:xs[c + 1]].mean()
99	    v = cells.reshape(-1)
100	    v -= v.mean()
101	    s = v.std()
102	    return v / s if s > 1e-6 else v
103	
104	
105	def _bg_warmth(image: np.ndarray) -> float:
106	    """Warmth (R - B) of the page background — median over the BG ROI is robust to
107	    the song text painted over it. High = yellow (main), low = white (bonus)."""
108	    img = _to_canonical(image)
109	    x0, y0, x1, y1 = SETLIST_BG_ROI
110	    patch = img[y0:y1, x0:x1].reshape(-1, 3).astype(np.float64)
111	    med = np.median(patch, axis=0)  # (B, G, R)
112	    return float(med[2] - med[0])
113	
114	
115	def build_song_catalog(samples: list[Sample], config: SongConfig = DEFAULT_SONG_CONFIG) -> SongCatalog:
116	    templates: list[SongTemplate] = []
117	    warmth: dict[str, list[float]] = defaultdict(list)
118	    for s in samples:
119	        if s.screen_id != "song_select":
120	            continue
121	        parsed = song_from_filename(s.path.name)
122	        if parsed is None:
123	            continue
124	        setlist, index, song_id = parsed
125	        roi_kind = FIRST if index == 0 else SLOT
126	        roi = SONG_FIRST_ROI if roi_kind == FIRST else SONG_SLOT_ROI
127	        templates.append(
128	            SongTemplate(setlist, index, song_id, roi_kind, _luma_grid(s.image, roi, config))
129	        )
130	        warmth[setlist].append(_bg_warmth(s.image))
131	    # Threshold midway between the two setlists' mean background warmth.
132	    main_w = np.mean(warmth["main"]) if warmth["main"] else 0.0
133	    bonus_w = np.mean(warmth["bonus"]) if warmth["bonus"] else 0.0
134	    threshold = float((main_w + bonus_w) / 2.0)
135	    return SongCatalog(templates=templates, config=config, setlist_warmth_threshold=threshold)
136	
137	
138	def read_setlist(image: np.ndarray, catalog: SongCatalog) -> str:
139	    """Which setlist is active ("main"/"bonus"), from the page background colour."""
140	    return "main" if _bg_warmth(image) >= catalog.setlist_warmth_threshold else "bonus"
141	
142	
143	def _shift(roi: tuple[int, int, int, int], dx: int, dy: int) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
144	    x0, y0, x1, y1 = roi
145	    return (x0 + dx, y0 + dy, x1 + dx, y1 + dy)
146	
147	
148	def read_song(image: np.ndarray, catalog: SongCatalog, setlist: str | None = None) -> SongResult:
149	    """Identify the selected song by nearest-template match.
150	
151	    Matches across the whole catalog (both setlists) by default — main/bonus
152	    bitmaps are distinct, so the setlist falls out of the winning song and we
153	    don't depend on the (less reliable) tab read. Pass `setlist` to restrict.
154	
155	    A small offset search per candidate ROI re-aligns the slot before scoring, so
156	    the fine grid tolerates the analog path's positional slop.
157	    """
158	    cfg = catalog.config
159	    cand = [t for t in catalog.templates if setlist is None or t.setlist == setlist]
160	
161	    # One fingerprint per (roi_kind, offset), reused across all templates.
162	    fps: dict[tuple[str, int, int], np.ndarray] = {}
163	    for dx in cfg.dx_search:
164	        for dy in cfg.dy_search:
165	            fps[(SLOT, dx, dy)] = _luma_grid(image, _shift(SONG_SLOT_ROI, dx, dy), cfg)
166	            fps[(FIRST, dx, dy)] = _luma_grid(image, _shift(SONG_FIRST_ROI, dx, dy), cfg)
167	
168	    def best_dist(t: SongTemplate) -> float:
169	        return min(
170	            float(np.abs(fps[(t.roi_kind, dx, dy)] - t.vec).sum())
171	            for dx in cfg.dx_search
172	            for dy in cfg.dy_search
173	        )
174	
175	    scored = sorted(((best_dist(t), t) for t in cand), key=lambda kv: kv[0])
176	    best_d, best = scored[0]
177	    second_d = scored[1][0] if len(scored) > 1 else best_d
178	    return SongResult(
179	        setlist=best.setlist, index=best.index, song_id=best.song_id,
180	        dist=best_d, margin=second_d - best_d,
181	    )
182
```

```text
1	"""Static-list highlight reader: which menu row is selected.
2	
3	Given an already-classified static-list screen and its `MenuLayout`, divide the
4	menu band into `count` equal cells along the layout axis and decide which cell is
5	selected. GH3 marks the selected item by *changing* it (a highlight bar, or
6	brighter/colour-shifted text) — not always by making it the brightest — so the
7	robust signal is **per-cell deviation from that cell's unselected appearance**:
8	the selected cell is the one that has changed most from how it looks when not
9	selected.
10	
11	That unselected appearance is learned per screen from the corpus (a
12	`SelectionCalibration`, analogous to the classifier's centroids; the firmware
13	port would bake these). Two details make it work:
14	
15	- Baseline per cell uses only the samples where that cell is *unselected*, so it
16	  is non-degenerate even for two-item screens (where a median-over-all collapses
17	  to the midpoint and can't tell the cells apart).
18	- Cell colours are normalized per frame (subtract the mean cell colour, scale by
19	  the spread) before comparing, which cancels the global gain/offset value-slop of
20	  the analog-component -> HDMI path. This takes slop robustness from ~90% to ~99%.
21	"""
22	
23	from __future__ import annotations
24	
25	from dataclasses import dataclass
26	
27	import numpy as np
28	
29	from .corpus import Sample
30	from .fingerprint import CANONICAL_H, CANONICAL_W, _to_canonical
31	from .metadata import HORIZONTAL, MENU_LAYOUTS, MenuLayout, selected_item_from_filename
32	
33	
34	@dataclass(frozen=True)
35	class SelectionResult:
36	    index: int  # selected cell index (= item index, items are in screen order)
37	    item: str
38	    scores: tuple[float, ...]  # per-cell deviation from unselected baseline
39	    margin: float  # best - second-best (confidence; higher = less ambiguous)
40	
41	
42	@dataclass(frozen=True)
43	class SelectionCalibration:
44	    """Per-screen, per-cell unselected baseline colours (normalized space)."""
45	
46	    baselines: dict[str, np.ndarray]  # screen_id -> (count, 3) float
47	
48	
49	def _cell_bounds(layout: MenuLayout) -> list[tuple[int, int, int, int]]:
50	    x0, y0, x1, y1 = layout.band
51	    n = layout.count
52	    if layout.axis == HORIZONTAL:
53	        edges = np.linspace(x0, x1, n + 1).round().astype(int)
54	        return [(int(edges[i]), y0, int(edges[i + 1]), y1) for i in range(n)]
55	    edges = np.linspace(y0, y1, n + 1).round().astype(int)
56	    return [(x0, int(edges[i]), x1, int(edges[i + 1])) for i in range(n)]
57	
58	
59	def cell_colors(image: np.ndarray, layout: MenuLayout) -> np.ndarray:
60	    """Per-frame-normalized mean BGR of each menu cell — shape (count, 3).
61	
62	    Normalization (subtract the mean cell colour, divide by the spread) makes the
63	    reader invariant to global gain/offset.
64	    """
65	    img = _to_canonical(image)
66	    rows = []
67	    for (x0, y0, x1, y1) in _cell_bounds(layout):
68	        x0c, x1c = max(0, x0), min(CANONICAL_W, x1)
69	        y0c, y1c = max(0, y0), min(CANONICAL_H, y1)
70	        rows.append(img[y0c:y1c, x0c:x1c].reshape(-1, 3).mean(axis=0))
71	    c = np.asarray(rows, dtype=np.float64)
72	    c -= c.mean(axis=0)
73	    std = c.std()
74	    return c / std if std > 1e-6 else c
75	
76	
77	def build_selection_calibration(samples: list[Sample]) -> SelectionCalibration:
78	    """Learn each modelled screen's per-cell unselected baseline from the corpus.
79	
80	    For each cell, average its (normalized) colour over the samples in which that
81	    cell is *not* the selected one.
82	    """
83	    baselines: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
84	    for sid, layout in MENU_LAYOUTS.items():
85	        acc: list[list[np.ndarray]] = [[] for _ in range(layout.count)]
86	        for s in samples:
87	            if s.screen_id != sid:
88	                continue
89	            item = selected_item_from_filename(s.path.name)
90	            if item is None or item not in layout.items:
91	                continue
92	            sel = layout.index_of(item)
93	            cc = cell_colors(s.image, layout)
94	            for c in range(layout.count):
95	                if c != sel:
96	                    acc[c].append(cc[c])
97	        if all(acc):  # every cell has at least one unselected exemplar
98	            baselines[sid] = np.stack([np.mean(a, axis=0) for a in acc])
99	    return SelectionCalibration(baselines=baselines)
100	
101	
102	def read_selection(
103	    image: np.ndarray, layout: MenuLayout, calibration: SelectionCalibration
104	) -> SelectionResult:
105	    baseline = calibration.baselines[layout.screen_id]
106	    cc = cell_colors(image, layout)
107	    dev = np.linalg.norm(cc - baseline, axis=1)
108	    order = np.argsort(dev)[::-1]
109	    best = int(order[0])
110	    margin = float(dev[best] - (dev[int(order[1])] if len(order) > 1 else 0.0))
111	    return SelectionResult(
112	        index=best, item=layout.items[best], scores=tuple(float(d) for d in dev), margin=margin
113	    )
114
```

```text
1	"""Fixed-region colour fingerprint (the Q10 recognizer primitive).
2	
3	A frame is partitioned into a coarse `cols x rows` grid of fixed rectangles; each
4	region collapses to its mean (B,G,R). The fingerprint is the concatenated uint8
5	vector, length `3 * cols * rows`. Coarse averaging is what makes this tolerant of
6	the positional slop introduced by the Wii's analog-component -> HDMI path: a
7	sub-cell shift just moves a few pixels between neighbours and washes out.
8	
9	Two knobs matter for the firmware port (memory-bound on uncached DDR reads — see
10	the plan's hardware-cost section):
11	
12	- `samples_per_region`: None computes a dense mean (touches every pixel ~= a
13	  full-frame scan, ~7-20 ms on the SAM9X75). An integer N samples an N x N lattice
14	  per region instead (~cols*rows*N*N reads total, sub-millisecond), trading a little
15	  estimate noise for speed. The coarse average absorbs that noise.
16	- `normalize`: when True, the vector is standardized to a fixed mean/std per frame,
17	  which cancels the global gain/offset value-slop of the analog path. Raw vs
18	  normalized is chosen empirically in `evaluate.py`.
19	
20	Everything is shaped to port 1:1 to integer C: accumulate pixel sums over fixed
21	rectangles (or fixed sample coords), divide, then an L1 compare downstream.
22	"""
23	
24	from __future__ import annotations
25	
26	from dataclasses import dataclass
27	
28	import numpy as np
29	from PIL import Image
30	
31	CANONICAL_W = 720
32	CANONICAL_H = 480
33	BPP = 3  # BGR
34	
35	# Standardization targets for the normalized variant (uint8 midpoint-ish).
36	_NORM_MEAN = 128.0
37	_NORM_STD = 48.0
38	
39	
40	# Defaults chosen empirically in evaluate.py against the corpus: 12x8 normalized
41	# subsampled gives 96% LOO (= 100% of multi-sample classes) and ~99.8% slop
42	# robustness at ~0.1-0.4 ms on the SAM9X75. Normalization is what buys value-slop
43	# (gain/offset) robustness from the analog-component path.
44	@dataclass(frozen=True)
45	class FingerprintConfig:
46	    cols: int = 12
47	    rows: int = 8
48	    samples_per_region: int | None = 5  # None = dense; N = N x N lattice
49	    normalize: bool = True
50	
51	    @property
52	    def length(self) -> int:
53	        return self.cols * self.rows * BPP
54	
55	    @property
56	    def pixel_reads(self) -> int:
57	        """Pixels touched per classification — the on-device cost driver."""
58	        if self.samples_per_region is None:
59	            return CANONICAL_W * CANONICAL_H
60	        return self.cols * self.rows * self.samples_per_region**2
61	
62	
63	DEFAULT_CONFIG = FingerprintConfig()
64	
65	
66	def _to_canonical(image: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
67	    """Ensure a uint8 HxWx3 array at the canonical 720x480 (resize if needed)."""
68	    if image.dtype != np.uint8:
69	        image = image.astype(np.uint8)
70	    if image.shape[:2] == (CANONICAL_H, CANONICAL_W):
71	        return image
72	    # Defensive only — real captures are already native 720x480. Resize via PIL
73	    # (BGR in, BGR out; channel order is irrelevant to a resize).
74	    im = Image.fromarray(image, mode="RGB")
75	    im = im.resize((CANONICAL_W, CANONICAL_H), Image.BILINEAR)
76	    return np.asarray(im, dtype=np.uint8)
77	
78	
79	def _region_bounds(n: int, extent: int) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
80	    """Split [0, extent) into n contiguous integer spans."""
81	    edges = np.linspace(0, extent, n + 1).round().astype(int)
82	    return [(int(edges[i]), int(edges[i + 1])) for i in range(n)]
83	
84	
85	def _lattice(lo: int, hi: int, n: int) -> np.ndarray:
86	    """n sample coordinates inside [lo, hi), centred in their sub-cells."""
87	    fracs = (np.arange(n) + 0.5) / n
88	    return (lo + fracs * (hi - lo)).astype(int).clip(lo, hi - 1)
89	
90	
91	def fingerprint(image: np.ndarray, config: FingerprintConfig = DEFAULT_CONFIG) -> np.ndarray:
92	    """Compute the fixed-region fingerprint of a BGR frame.
93	
94	    Returns a uint8 vector of length `config.length`, region-major (row 0 first),
95	    each region contributing [B, G, R].
96	    """
97	    img = _to_canonical(image)
98	    ys = _region_bounds(config.rows, CANONICAL_H)
99	    xs = _region_bounds(config.cols, CANONICAL_W)
100	
101	    means = np.empty((config.rows, config.cols, BPP), dtype=np.float64)
102	    for r, (y0, y1) in enumerate(ys):
103	        for c, (x0, x1) in enumerate(xs):
104	            if config.samples_per_region is None:
105	                patch = img[y0:y1, x0:x1, :]
106	            else:
107	                yy = _lattice(y0, y1, config.samples_per_region)
108	                xx = _lattice(x0, x1, config.samples_per_region)
109	                patch = img[np.ix_(yy, xx)]
110	            means[r, c] = patch.reshape(-1, BPP).mean(axis=0)
111	
112	    vec = means.reshape(-1)
113	    if config.normalize:
114	        std = vec.std()
115	        if std > 1e-6:
116	            vec = (vec - vec.mean()) / std * _NORM_STD + _NORM_MEAN
117	        else:
118	            vec = np.full_like(vec, _NORM_MEAN)
119	    return vec.round().clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
120
```

```text
6	**BGR** order, matching marvin's native framebuffer layout (capture is BGR888
7	packed; see marvin journal 2026-05-02).

26	def corpus_dir() -> Path:

36	    image: np.ndarray  # uint8, HxWx3, BGR
37

39	def load_bgr(path: str | Path) -> np.ndarray:
40	    """Load an image file as a uint8 HxWx3 BGR array."""
41	    with Image.open(path) as im:

43	    return rgb[:, :, ::-1].copy()  # RGB -> BGR

46	def load_corpus(directory: str | Path | None = None) -> list[Sample]:
47	    """Load every `*.png` in the corpus directory as labelled `Sample`s.
48

50	    directory is empty or missing.

53	    files = sorted(d.glob("*.png"))
54	    if not files:
```

```text
3	Single source of truth aligning the prototype's screen ids with the screen names
4	in `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md`. The classifier emits one of these ids
5	(or the sentinel UNKNOWN); the firmware `gameplay_engine` port will reuse the same
6	names.
7	
8	Corpus files are named `<prefix>__<selection>.png` (or just `<prefix>.png` for
9	single-shot screens). The screen *class* is the prefix; the selection suffix is
10	the highlighted item, which a later slice (the highlight reader) handles. Two
11	prefixes are renamed here to match the nav-doc node names.

15

19	# Canonical screen ids, matching the gh3_navigation.md catalog. Order is the
20	# nominal practice-run flow, then the overlays/dialogs.
21	SCREEN_IDS: tuple[str, ...] = (
22	    "main_menu",
23	    "training_menu",
24	    "tutorials_menu",
25	    "song_select",
26	    "part_select",
27	    "difficulty_select",
28	    "section_select",
29	    "speed_select",
30	    "loading",
31	    "in_song",
32	    "pause_menu",
33	    "quit_confirm",
34	    "practice_end_menu",
35	)
36	
37	# Corpus filename prefixes whose canonical id differs from the prefix itself.
38	# Everything else maps by identity.
39	_PREFIX_RENAMES: dict[str, str] = {
40	    "difficulty": "difficulty_select",
41	    "speed": "speed_select",
42	}
43	
44	
45	def screen_id_for_filename(filename: str) -> str:
46	    """Map a corpus PNG filename to its canonical screen id.
47	
48	    `main_menu__training.png` -> `main_menu`; `difficulty__hard.png` ->
49	    `difficulty_select`; `loading.png` -> `loading`. Raises ValueError if the
50	    resulting id isn't a known screen.
51	    """
52	    stem = filename.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
53	    if stem.endswith(".png"):
54	        stem = stem[: -len(".png")]
55	    prefix = stem.split("__", 1)[0]
56	    screen_id = _PREFIX_RENAMES.get(prefix, prefix)
57	    if screen_id not in SCREEN_IDS:
```

```text
24	def _config_from_args(args: argparse.Namespace) -> FingerprintConfig:
25	    spr = None if getattr(args, "dense", False) else args.samples
26	    return FingerprintConfig(
27	        cols=args.cols,
28	        rows=args.rows,
29	        samples_per_region=spr,
30	        normalize=args.normalize,
31	    )
32	
33	
34	def cmd_classify(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
35	    config = _config_from_args(args)
36	    samples = load_corpus()
37	    templates = build_templates(evaluate.labelled_fps(samples, config), config)
38	    rec = evaluate.recommend_thresholds(samples, config)
39	    t_abs, t_margin = rec.rec_t_abs, rec.rec_t_margin
40	
41	    image = load_bgr(args.image)
42	    result = classify_image(image, templates, t_abs=t_abs, t_margin=t_margin)
43	    print(
44	        f"{result.screen_id}\t(best={result.best_id} dist={result.best_dist} "
45	        f"margin={result.margin}; thresholds t_abs={t_abs} t_margin={t_margin})"
46	    )
47	    layout = MENU_LAYOUTS.get(result.screen_id)
48	    if layout is not None:
49	        calibration = build_selection_calibration(samples)
50	        sel = read_selection(image, layout, calibration)
51	        print(f"  selection: [{sel.index}] {sel.item}\t(margin={sel.margin:.2f})")
52	    elif result.screen_id == "song_select":
53	        catalog = build_song_catalog(samples)
54	        song = read_song(image, catalog)
55	        print(
56	            f"  song: [{song.setlist} #{song.index}] {song.song_id}\t"
57	            f"(dist={song.dist:.0f} margin={song.margin:.1f})"
58	        )
59	    return 0
60	
61	
62	def cmd_rows(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
63	    """Debug the static-list reader: per-cell scores for one screen image."""
64	    image = load_bgr(args.image)
65	    screen_id = args.screen or screen_id_for_filename(args.image)
66	    layout = MENU_LAYOUTS.get(screen_id)
67	    if layout is None:
68	        print(f"rows: {screen_id!r} is not a modelled static-list screen", file=sys.stderr)
69	        return 2
70	    sel = read_selection(image, layout, build_selection_calibration(load_corpus()))
71	    truth = selected_item_from_filename(args.image)
72	    print(f"{screen_id}  axis={layout.axis} band={layout.band}")
73	    for i, (item, (x0, y0, x1, y1)) in enumerate(zip(layout.items, _cell_bounds(layout))):
74	        mark = " <== selected" if i == sel.index else ""
75	        star = " (TRUE)" if truth == item else ""
76	        print(f"  [{i}] {item:<16} dev={sel.scores[i]:>5.2f}  cell=({x0},{y0},{x1},{y1}){mark}{star}")
77	    if truth is not None:
78	        print(f"predicted={sel.item}  true={truth}  {'OK' if sel.item == truth else 'WRONG'}")
79	    return 0
80	
81	
82	def cmd_eval(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
83	    config = _config_from_args(args)
84	    print(evaluate.run_report(config=config, sweep=not args.no_sweep))
85	    return 0
86	
87	
88	def cmd_export_c(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
89	    """Write the recognizer metadata as a C header for the firmware port."""
90	    from .export_c import build_metadata_header
91	
92	    header = build_metadata_header()
93	    if args.out:
94	        from pathlib import Path
95	
96	        Path(args.out).write_text(header)
97	        print(f"wrote {args.out} ({len(header)} bytes)", file=sys.stderr)
98	    else:
99	        sys.stdout.write(header)
100	    return 0
101	
102	
103	def cmd_navigate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
104	    """Plan a practice run and execute it closed-loop against the simulated menu."""
105	    plan = plan_practice_run(args.song, args.difficulty, part=args.part)
106	    print(f"plan: practice-run song #{args.song}, {args.difficulty}, {args.part}")
107	    for i, step in enumerate(plan.steps):
108	        print(f"  {i}. [{step.expected_from}] {step.desc} -> {step.expected_to}")
109	
110	    cfg = SimConfig(part_present=not args.skip_part, sticky=({"difficulty_select": 2} if args.sticky else {}))
111	    game = SimGame("main_menu", cfg)
112	    controller = NavController(SimObserver(game), SimActuator(game))
113	    end = controller.run(plan)
114	    print("\nsim trace:")
115	    for line in controller.trace:
116	        print(f"  {line}")
117	    print(f"\nend: {end.screen}  chosen={game.state.chosen}")
118	    return 0 if end.screen == plan.goal else 1
119	
120	
121	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
122	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
123	        prog="gameplay",
124	        description="GH3 game-state engine prototype: screen classifier.",
125	    )
126	    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="command")
127	
128	    def add_fp_args(sp: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
129	        d = FingerprintConfig()  # chosen defaults
130	        sp.add_argument("--cols", type=int, default=d.cols, help=f"grid columns (default {d.cols})")
131	        sp.add_argument("--rows", type=int, default=d.rows, help=f"grid rows (default {d.rows})")
132	        sp.add_argument(
133	            "--samples", type=int, default=d.samples_per_region,
134	            help=f"N x N samples per region (default {d.samples_per_region}); ignored with --dense",
135	        )
136	        sp.add_argument("--dense", action="store_true", help="dense per-region mean (every pixel)")
137	        sp.add_argument(
138	            "--normalize", action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction, default=d.normalize,
139	            help="per-frame value normalization (on by default; --no-normalize to disable)",
140	        )
141	
142	    p_classify = sub.add_parser("classify", help="Classify one image against the corpus templates.")
143	    p_classify.add_argument("image", help="path to a PNG/BGR frame")
144	    add_fp_args(p_classify)
145	    p_classify.set_defaults(func=cmd_classify)
146	
147	    p_eval = sub.add_parser("eval", help="Evaluate the classifier against the corpus.")
148	    add_fp_args(p_eval)
149	    p_eval.add_argument("--no-sweep", action="store_true", help="skip the parameter sweep")
150	    p_eval.set_defaults(func=cmd_eval)
151	
152	    p_rows = sub.add_parser("rows", help="Debug the static-list selection reader on one image.")
153	    p_rows.add_argument("image", help="path to a PNG/BGR frame")
154	    p_rows.add_argument("--screen", help="screen id (default: inferred from filename)")
155	    p_rows.set_defaults(func=cmd_rows)
156	
157	    p_export = sub.add_parser("export-c", help="Emit recognizer metadata as a C header for the firmware.")
158	    p_export.add_argument("--out", help="output .h path (default: stdout)")
159	    p_export.set_defaults(func=cmd_export_c)
160	
161	    p_nav = sub.add_parser("navigate", help="Plan + run a practice run against the simulated menu.")
162	    p_nav.add_argument("--song", type=int, default=0, help="song index (default 0)")
163	    p_nav.add_argument("--difficulty", default="hard", help="easy|medium|hard|expert (default hard)")
164	    p_nav.add_argument("--part", default="lead", help="lead|rhythm (default lead)")
165	    p_nav.add_argument("--skip-part", action="store_true", help="simulate a song with no part_select")
166	    p_nav.add_argument("--sticky", action="store_true", help="simulate a sticky (non-zero) difficulty default")
167	    p_nav.set_defaults(func=cmd_navigate)
168	
169	    return p
170	
171	
172	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
173	    parser = build_parser()
174	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
175	    if args.command is None:
176	        args = parser.parse_args(["eval"])
177	    return args.func(args)
178	
179	
180	if __name__ == "__main__":
181	    sys.exit(main())
182
```

```text
1	"""Nearest-centroid screen classifier with an UNKNOWN reject rule.
2	
3	Each screen class is represented by one centroid fingerprint (the mean over its
4	corpus samples) — a small fixed-size template, which is the per-state metadata the
5	firmware `gameplay_engine` will eventually carry. Classification is L1 distance to
6	every centroid, argmin, then a two-part accept test:
7	
8	    accept best iff  d_best <= t_abs  AND  (d_second - d_best) >= t_margin
9	
10	Otherwise the result is UNKNOWN. The navigator's recovery path depends on a
11	trustworthy UNKNOWN, so the margin gate (am I *clearly* closer to one class than the
12	next?) matters as much as the absolute gate. All math is integer L1 over uint8
13	vectors, matching the firmware target.
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	from dataclasses import dataclass
19	
20	import numpy as np
21	
22	from .fingerprint import FingerprintConfig, fingerprint
23	from .screens import UNKNOWN
24	
25	# Coarse fallback thresholds for the default normalized 12x8 config; callers
26	# should prefer values recommended by `evaluate.recommend_thresholds` for the
27	# actual config in use (distance scale depends on grid size + normalization).
28	DEFAULT_T_ABS = 7000
29	DEFAULT_T_MARGIN = 600
30	
31	
32	@dataclass(frozen=True)
33	class Templates:
34	    ids: tuple[str, ...]
35	    centroids: np.ndarray  # (K, L) uint8
36	    config: FingerprintConfig
37	
38	
39	@dataclass(frozen=True)
40	class Classification:
41	    screen_id: str  # a canonical id, or UNKNOWN
42	    best_id: str  # nearest centroid regardless of reject (for diagnostics)
43	    best_dist: int
44	    second_dist: int
45	
46	    @property
47	    def margin(self) -> int:
48	        return self.second_dist - self.best_dist
49	
50	    @property
51	    def accepted(self) -> bool:
52	        return self.screen_id != UNKNOWN
53	
54	
55	def build_templates(
56	    labelled_fps: dict[str, list[np.ndarray]], config: FingerprintConfig
57	) -> Templates:
58	    """Build per-class centroids from labelled fingerprints (id -> [fp, ...])."""
59	    ids = tuple(sorted(labelled_fps))
60	    centroids = np.empty((len(ids), config.length), dtype=np.uint8)
61	    for i, sid in enumerate(ids):
62	        stack = np.stack(labelled_fps[sid]).astype(np.float64)
63	        centroids[i] = stack.mean(axis=0).round().clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
64	    return Templates(ids=ids, centroids=centroids, config=config)
65	
66	
67	def _l1_to_centroids(fp: np.ndarray, centroids: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
68	    diff = centroids.astype(np.int32) - fp.astype(np.int32)
69	    return np.abs(diff).sum(axis=1)
70	
71	
72	def classify_fp(
73	    fp: np.ndarray,
74	    templates: Templates,
75	    t_abs: int = DEFAULT_T_ABS,
76	    t_margin: int = DEFAULT_T_MARGIN,
77	) -> Classification:
78	    """Classify a precomputed fingerprint against templates."""
79	    dists = _l1_to_centroids(fp, templates.centroids)
80	    order = np.argsort(dists, kind="stable")
81	    best_i = int(order[0])
82	    best_d = int(dists[best_i])
83	    second_d = int(dists[order[1]]) if len(order) > 1 else (best_d + t_margin)
84	    best_id = templates.ids[best_i]
85	
86	    accept = best_d <= t_abs and (second_d - best_d) >= t_margin
87	    return Classification(
88	        screen_id=best_id if accept else UNKNOWN,
89	        best_id=best_id,
90	        best_dist=best_d,
91	        second_dist=second_d,
92	    )
93	
94	
95	def classify_image(
96	    image: np.ndarray,
97	    templates: Templates,
98	    t_abs: int = DEFAULT_T_ABS,
99	    t_margin: int = DEFAULT_T_MARGIN,
100	) -> Classification:
101	    """Classify a raw BGR frame (fingerprints it with the templates' config)."""
102	    fp = fingerprint(image, templates.config)
103	    return classify_fp(fp, templates, t_abs=t_abs, t_margin=t_margin)
104
```

```text
1	"""Evaluation harness for the screen classifier.
2	
3	Proves the fingerprint+nearest-centroid design against the corpus and reports
4	everything needed to pick parameters and thresholds before any firmware port:
5	
6	1. Leave-one-out cross-validation -> per-class accuracy + confusion matrix.
7	2. Whole-class hold-out -> impostor distances, validating the UNKNOWN reject.
8	3. Threshold recommendation from the in-class vs impostor distance separation.
9	4. Robustness pass over the analog-slop envelope (`perturb.envelope`).
10	5. SAM9X75 time-per-classification estimate at the configured sample density.
11	
12	All distances are integer L1 over uint8 fingerprints.
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	from collections import defaultdict
18	from dataclasses import dataclass
19	
20	import numpy as np
21	
22	from . import perturb
23	from .classifier import (
24	    DEFAULT_T_ABS,
25	    DEFAULT_T_MARGIN,
26	    Templates,
27	    _l1_to_centroids,
28	    build_templates,
29	    classify_fp,
30	)
31	from .corpus import Sample, load_corpus
32	from .fingerprint import CANONICAL_H, CANONICAL_W, BPP, FingerprintConfig, fingerprint
33	from .highlight import build_selection_calibration, read_selection
34	from .metadata import MENU_LAYOUTS, selected_item_from_filename, song_from_filename
35	from .screens import UNKNOWN
36	from .songselect import build_song_catalog, read_setlist, read_song
37	
38	# Uncached-DDR read model for the SAM9X75 port (see plan's hardware-cost section).
39	_DDR_BW_MB_S = (50.0, 150.0)  # dense sequential, single-beat, no cache-line burst
40	_UNCACHED_LAT_NS = (50.0, 150.0)  # per strided single-pixel access (subsampled)
41	
42	
43	def labelled_fps(samples: list[Sample], config: FingerprintConfig) -> dict[str, list[np.ndarray]]:
44	    out: dict[str, list[np.ndarray]] = defaultdict(list)
45	    for s in samples:
46	        out[s.screen_id].append(fingerprint(s.image, config))
47	    return dict(out)
48	
49	
50	# ─── 1. Leave-one-out CV ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
51	
52	
53	@dataclass
54	class LooResult:
55	    config: FingerprintConfig
56	    t_abs: int
57	    t_margin: int
58	    n_total: int
59	    n_correct: int
60	    n_unknown: int
61	    per_class_acc: dict[str, tuple[int, int]]  # id -> (correct, total)
62	    confusion: dict[tuple[str, str], int]  # (true, pred) -> count
63	    single_sample_classes: tuple[str, ...]
64	
65	    @property
66	    def accuracy(self) -> float:
67	        return self.n_correct / self.n_total if self.n_total else 0.0
68	
69	
70	def loo_eval(
71	    samples: list[Sample],
72	    config: FingerprintConfig,
73	    t_abs: int = DEFAULT_T_ABS,
74	    t_margin: int = DEFAULT_T_MARGIN,
75	) -> LooResult:
76	    fps = [fingerprint(s.image, config) for s in samples]
77	    ids = [s.screen_id for s in samples]
78	    counts = defaultdict(int)
79	    for sid in ids:
80	        counts[sid] += 1
81	    single = tuple(sorted(c for c, n in counts.items() if n == 1))
82	
83	    per_class: dict[str, list[int]] = {sid: [0, 0] for sid in counts}
84	    confusion: dict[tuple[str, str], int] = defaultdict(int)
85	    n_correct = n_unknown = 0
86	
87	    for i, (fp_i, true_id) in enumerate(zip(fps, ids)):
88	        held: dict[str, list[np.ndarray]] = defaultdict(list)
89	        for j, (fp_j, id_j) in enumerate(zip(fps, ids)):
90	            if j != i:
91	                held[id_j].append(fp_j)
92	        templates = build_templates(dict(held), config)
93	        pred = classify_fp(fp_i, templates, t_abs=t_abs, t_margin=t_margin).screen_id
94	
95	        per_class[true_id][1] += 1
96	        confusion[(true_id, pred)] += 1
97	        if pred == true_id:
98	            per_class[true_id][0] += 1
99	            n_correct += 1
100	        elif pred == UNKNOWN:
101	            n_unknown += 1
102	
103	    return LooResult(
104	        config=config,
105	        t_abs=t_abs,
106	        t_margin=t_margin,
107	        n_total=len(samples),
108	        n_correct=n_correct,
109	        n_unknown=n_unknown,
110	        per_class_acc={k: (v[0], v[1]) for k, v in per_class.items()},
111	        confusion=dict(confusion),
112	        single_sample_classes=single,
113	    )
114	
115	
116	# ─── 2. Whole-class hold-out (UNKNOWN reject) + 3. threshold recommendation ────
117	
118	
119	# Accept legitimate in-class matches with this much headroom above the worst one,
120	# so normal frame-to-frame and analog-slop variation doesn't get falsely rejected.
121	_ABS_HEADROOM = 0.20
122	
123	# The margin gate only exists to reject near-ties; keep it well below the smallest
124	# legitimate in-class margin so it never rejects a real screen.
125	_MARGIN_FRACTION = 0.5
126	
127	
128	@dataclass
129	class ThresholdRecommendation:
130	    in_class_dist_max: int  # worst correct-match distance (LOO)
131	    in_class_margin_min: int  # worst correct-match margin (LOO)
132	    impostor_dist_min: int  # nearest a held-out class got to a wrong centroid
133	    impostor_margin_max: int
134	    rec_t_abs: int
135	    rec_t_margin: int
136	    impostor_leak: int  # held-out impostors that t_abs would accept (false positives)
137	    n_impostors: int
138	
139	
140	def _loo_in_class_stats(samples, config) -> tuple[list[int], list[int]]:
141	    """LOO best-distance and margin for samples whose nearest class is correct."""
142	    fps = [fingerprint(s.image, config) for s in samples]
143	    ids = [s.screen_id for s in samples]
144	    dists: list[int] = []
145	    margins: list[int] = []
146	    for i, (fp_i, true_id) in enumerate(zip(fps, ids)):
147	        held: dict[str, list[np.ndarray]] = defaultdict(list)
148	        for j, (fp_j, id_j) in enumerate(zip(fps, ids)):
149	            if j != i:
150	                held[id_j].append(fp_j)
151	        if true_id not in held:  # single-sample class: no own centroid under LOO
152	            continue
153	        templates = build_templates(dict(held), config)
154	        d = _l1_to_centroids(fp_i, templates.centroids)
155	        order = np.argsort(d, kind="stable")
156	        if templates.ids[int(order[0])] != true_id:
157	            continue  # misclassified — not an in-class exemplar
158	        dists.append(int(d[order[0]]))
159	        margins.append(int(d[order[1]] - d[order[0]]) if len(order) > 1 else 1 << 30)
160	    return dists, margins
161	
162	
163	def _holdout_impostor_stats(samples, config) -> tuple[list[int], list[int]]:
164	    """For each class, remove it entirely and record how close its samples land to
165	    the *nearest surviving* class (distance + margin) — these must be rejected."""
166	    by_class: dict[str, list[np.ndarray]] = defaultdict(list)
167	    for s in samples:
168	        by_class[s.screen_id].append(fingerprint(s.image, config))
169	    dists: list[int] = []
170	    margins: list[int] = []
171	    classes = sorted(by_class)
172	    for held_out in classes:
173	        kept = {c: v for c, v in by_class.items() if c != held_out}
174	        if not kept:
175	            continue
176	        templates = build_templates(kept, config)
177	        for fp in by_class[held_out]:
178	            d = _l1_to_centroids(fp, templates.centroids)
179	            order = np.argsort(d, kind="stable")
180	            dists.append(int(d[order[0]]))
181	            margins.append(int(d[order[1]] - d[order[0]]) if len(order) > 1 else 0)
182	    return dists, margins
183	
184	
185	def recommend_thresholds(samples, config) -> ThresholdRecommendation:
186	    in_d, in_m = _loo_in_class_stats(samples, config)
187	    imp_d, imp_m = _holdout_impostor_stats(samples, config)
188	
189	    in_d_max = max(in_d) if in_d else 0
190	    in_m_min = min(in_m) if in_m else 0
191	    imp_d_min = min(imp_d) if imp_d else (1 << 30)
192	    imp_m_max = max(imp_m) if imp_m else 0
193	
194	    # Primary gate: accept every legitimate in-class match plus headroom. Never
195	    # tune t_abs down to chase impostor rejection — that just rejects real screens.
196	    rec_t_abs = round(in_d_max * (1.0 + _ABS_HEADROOM)) if in_d_max else (1 << 30)
197	    # Secondary gate: soft margin, strictly below the smallest legit in-class margin.
198	    rec_t_margin = max(0, int(in_m_min * _MARGIN_FRACTION))
199	
200	    # Honest secondary metric: how many whole-class-holdout impostors slip past
201	    # t_abs (genuinely-unseen screens that resemble a known one). Not a false
202	    # rejection of real screens — reported, not minimized at their expense.
203	    leak = sum(1 for d in imp_d if d <= rec_t_abs)
204	
205	    return ThresholdRecommendation(
206	        in_class_dist_max=in_d_max,
207	        in_class_margin_min=in_m_min,
208	        impostor_dist_min=imp_d_min,
209	        impostor_margin_max=imp_m_max,
210	        rec_t_abs=rec_t_abs,
211	        rec_t_margin=rec_t_margin,
212	        impostor_leak=leak,
213	        n_impostors=len(imp_d),
214	    )
215	
216	
217	# ─── 4. Robustness pass ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
218	
219	
220	@dataclass
221	class RobustnessResult:
222	    per_category: dict[str, tuple[int, int]]  # category -> (stable, total)
223	    n_total: int
224	    n_stable: int
225	
226	    @property
227	    def stability(self) -> float:
228	        return self.n_stable / self.n_total if self.n_total else 0.0
229	
230	
231	def robustness_eval(
232	    samples: list[Sample],
233	    config: FingerprintConfig,
234	    t_abs: int,
235	    t_margin: int,
236	    seed: int = 1234,
237	) -> RobustnessResult:
238	    """Train on the full clean corpus, then classify perturbed copies of each
239	    sample. Stable = perturbed prediction still equals the true class."""
240	    templates = build_templates(labelled_fps(samples, config), config)
241	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
242	    per_cat: dict[str, list[int]] = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])
243	    n_total = n_stable = 0
244	    for s in samples:
245	        for category, _name, pimg in perturb.envelope(s.image, rng):
246	            pred = classify_fp(
247	                fingerprint(pimg, config), templates, t_abs=t_abs, t_margin=t_margin
248	            ).screen_id
249	            ok = pred == s.screen_id
250	            per_cat[category][0] += int(ok)
251	            per_cat[category][1] += 1
252	            n_total += 1
253	            n_stable += int(ok)
254	    return RobustnessResult(
255	        per_category={k: (v[0], v[1]) for k, v in per_cat.items()},
256	        n_total=n_total,
257	        n_stable=n_stable,
258	    )
259	
260	
261	# ─── 5. Hardware time estimate ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
262	
263	
264	def hw_time_estimate_ms(config: FingerprintConfig) -> tuple[float, float]:
265	    """Estimate SAM9X75 ms/classification for `config`'s sample density.
266	
267	    Dense touches every pixel (bandwidth-bound); subsampled is strided single
268	    accesses (latency-bound). Returns (fast_est, slow_est) ms.
269	    """
270	    if config.samples_per_region is None:
271	        nbytes = CANONICAL_W * CANONICAL_H * BPP
272	        fast = nbytes / (_DDR_BW_MB_S[1] * 1e6) * 1e3
273	        slow = nbytes / (_DDR_BW_MB_S[0] * 1e6) * 1e3
274	        return (fast, slow)
275	    reads = config.pixel_reads
276	    fast = reads * _UNCACHED_LAT_NS[0] / 1e6
277	    slow = reads * _UNCACHED_LAT_NS[1] / 1e6
278	    return (fast, slow)
279	
280	
281	# ─── Static-list highlight (selection) reader ──────────────────────────────────
282	
283	
284	@dataclass
285	class SelectionEvalResult:
286	    per_screen: dict[str, tuple[int, int]]  # screen_id -> (correct, total)
287	    failures: list[tuple[str, str, str]]  # (filename, true_item, pred_item)
288	    n_total: int
289	    n_correct: int
290	
291	    @property
292	    def accuracy(self) -> float:
293	        return self.n_correct / self.n_total if self.n_total else 0.0
294	
295	
296	def _labelled_selection_samples(samples: list[Sample]):
297	    """Yield (sample, layout, true_item) for samples whose filename encodes a
298	    selection on a modelled static-list screen."""
299	    for s in samples:
300	        layout = MENU_LAYOUTS.get(s.screen_id)
301	        if layout is None:
302	            continue
303	        true_item = selected_item_from_filename(s.path.name)
304	        if true_item is None or true_item not in layout.items:
305	            continue
306	        yield s, layout, true_item
307	
308	
309	def selection_eval(
310	    samples: list[Sample], perturb_envelope: bool = False, seed: int = 1234
311	) -> SelectionEvalResult:
312	    calibration = build_selection_calibration(samples)
313	    per: dict[str, list[int]] = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])
314	    failures: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
315	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
316	    for s, layout, true_item in _labelled_selection_samples(samples):
317	        variants = [(s.path.name, s.image)]
318	        if perturb_envelope:
319	            variants = [
320	                (f"{s.path.name}[{name}]", pimg)
321	                for _cat, name, pimg in perturb.envelope(s.image, rng)
322	            ]
323	        for fname, img in variants:
324	            pred = read_selection(img, layout, calibration).item
325	            per[s.screen_id][1] += 1
326	            if pred == true_item:
327	                per[s.screen_id][0] += 1
328	            else:
329	                failures.append((fname, true_item, pred))
330	    n_total = sum(t for _c, t in per.values())
331	    n_correct = sum(c for c, _t in per.values())
332	    return SelectionEvalResult(
333	        per_screen={k: (v[0], v[1]) for k, v in per.items()},
334	        failures=failures,
335	        n_total=n_total,
336	        n_correct=n_correct,
337	    )
338	
339	
340	# ─── song_select reader (fixed-slot bitmap match) ──────────────────────────────
341	
342	
343	@dataclass
344	class SongEvalResult:
345	    n_total: int
346	    n_song_ok: int  # song + setlist correct via match-all (the primary path)
347	    n_setlist_ok: int  # independent setlist read from page bg colour
348	    n_setlist_slop_ok: int  # ...under the analog-slop envelope
349	    margin_min: float  # worst nearest-wrong-song margin (clean)
350	    slop_ok: int
351	    slop_total: int
352	    failures: list[tuple[str, str, str]]  # (filename, true song_id, pred setlist:song_id)
353	
354	    @property
355	    def song_acc(self) -> float:
356	        return self.n_song_ok / self.n_total if self.n_total else 0.0
357	
358	    @property
359	    def setlist_acc(self) -> float:
360	        return self.n_setlist_ok / self.n_total if self.n_total else 0.0
361	
362	    @property
363	    def setlist_slop_acc(self) -> float:
364	        return self.n_setlist_slop_ok / self.slop_total if self.slop_total else 0.0
365	
366	    @property
367	    def slop_acc(self) -> float:
368	        return self.slop_ok / self.slop_total if self.slop_total else 0.0
369	
370	
371	def song_eval(samples: list[Sample], seed: int = 1234) -> SongEvalResult:
372	    catalog = build_song_catalog(samples)
373	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
374	    n = song_ok = setlist_ok = setlist_slop_ok = 0
375	    slop_ok = slop_total = 0
376	    margins: list[float] = []
377	    failures: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
378	    for s in samples:
379	        parsed = song_from_filename(s.path.name)
380	        if parsed is None:
381	            continue
382	        setlist, _index, song_id = parsed
383	        n += 1
384	        setlist_ok += read_setlist(s.image, catalog) == setlist
385	        r = read_song(s.image, catalog)  # match-all: yields song + setlist
386	        margins.append(r.margin)
387	        if r.song_id == song_id and r.setlist == setlist:
388	            song_ok += 1
389	        else:
390	            failures.append((s.path.name, song_id, f"{r.setlist}:{r.song_id}"))
391	        for _cat, _name, pimg in perturb.envelope(s.image, rng):
392	            slop_total += 1
393	            rp = read_song(pimg, catalog)
394	            slop_ok += rp.song_id == song_id and rp.setlist == setlist
395	            setlist_slop_ok += read_setlist(pimg, catalog) == setlist
396	    return SongEvalResult(
397	        n_total=n, n_song_ok=song_ok, n_setlist_ok=setlist_ok,
398	        n_setlist_slop_ok=setlist_slop_ok,
399	        margin_min=min(margins) if margins else 0.0,
400	        slop_ok=slop_ok, slop_total=slop_total, failures=failures,
401	    )

404	# ─── Orchestration / reporting ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

406	
407	def run_report(

432	    )

434	    lines.append(f"  est. SAM9X75 time/classification: {fast:.2f}-{slow:.2f} ms")
435	    dfast, dslow = hw_time_estimate_ms(FingerprintConfig(samples_per_region=None))
436	    lines.append(f"  (dense full-frame for reference: {dfast:.1f}-{dslow:.1f} ms)")
437	    lines.append("")
438	
439	    lines.append("threshold recommendation:")

441	        f"  in-class:  dist_max={rec.in_class_dist_max}  margin_min={rec.in_class_margin_min}"
442	    )

445	    )

447	    lines.append(

449	    )
450	    lines.append("")

452	    lines.append(
453	        f"leave-one-out: {loo.n_correct}/{loo.n_total} correct "

455	    )

470	    for cat in sorted(rob.per_category):

473	    lines.append("")

506	    if sweep:

508	        configs = [
```

```text
1	"""Synthetic analog-slop perturbations for robustness testing.
2	
3	The corpus snapshots are clean digital captures over the perf-log path, so they
4	lack the distortions the real Wii feed has: it is analog component video converted
5	to HDMI before capture. To test whether the classifier survives that, we inject
6	the two slop families it introduces:
7	
8	- **value slop** — gain (brightness scaling), offset, sensor/analog noise;
9	- **positional slop** — sub-cell translation, slight scale (overscan in/out).
10	
11	Transforms operate on uint8 HxWx3 BGR arrays and are deterministic given an rng.
12	`envelope()` yields a fixed, named battery used by `evaluate.py`.
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	from collections.abc import Iterator
18	
19	import numpy as np
20	from PIL import Image
21	
22	
23	def adjust_gain(img: np.ndarray, gain: float) -> np.ndarray:
24	    return np.clip(img.astype(np.float32) * gain, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
25	
26	
27	def adjust_offset(img: np.ndarray, offset: float) -> np.ndarray:
28	    return np.clip(img.astype(np.float32) + offset, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
29	
30	
31	def add_noise(img: np.ndarray, sigma: float, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
32	    noise = rng.normal(0.0, sigma, size=img.shape)
33	    return np.clip(img.astype(np.float32) + noise, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
34	
35	
36	def translate(img: np.ndarray, dx: int, dy: int) -> np.ndarray:
37	    """Shift by (dx, dy) px, filling exposed edges by replication."""
38	    h, w = img.shape[:2]
39	    padded = np.pad(img, ((abs(dy), abs(dy)), (abs(dx), abs(dx)), (0, 0)), mode="edge")
40	    y0, x0 = abs(dy) - dy, abs(dx) - dx
41	    return padded[y0 : y0 + h, x0 : x0 + w]
42	
43	
44	def rescale(img: np.ndarray, factor: float) -> np.ndarray:
45	    """Zoom about the centre by `factor`, then centre-crop/pad back to the
46	    original size (factor>1 = overscan crop, factor<1 = borders appear)."""
47	    h, w = img.shape[:2]
48	    nw, nh = max(1, round(w * factor)), max(1, round(h * factor))
49	    im = Image.fromarray(img, mode="RGB").resize((nw, nh), Image.BILINEAR)
50	    scaled = np.asarray(im, dtype=np.uint8)
51	
52	    out = np.empty_like(img)
53	    # x axis
54	    if nw >= w:
55	        sx = (nw - w) // 2
56	        xs_src, xs_dst, cw = sx, 0, w
57	    else:
58	        dx = (w - nw) // 2
59	        xs_src, xs_dst, cw = 0, dx, nw
60	    if nh >= h:
61	        sy = (nh - h) // 2
62	        ys_src, ys_dst, ch = sy, 0, h
63	    else:
64	        dy = (h - nh) // 2
65	        ys_src, ys_dst, ch = 0, dy, nh
66	
67	    if nw < w or nh < h:  # borders exposed — fill by edge replication
68	        edge = np.pad(scaled, ((0, 0), (0, 0), (0, 0)), mode="edge")
69	        out[:] = np.pad(
70	            edge,
71	            ((ys_dst, h - ys_dst - ch), (xs_dst, w - xs_dst - cw), (0, 0)),
72	            mode="edge",
73	        )
74	    else:
75	        out[ys_dst : ys_dst + ch, xs_dst : xs_dst + cw] = scaled[
76	            ys_src : ys_src + ch, xs_src : xs_src + cw
77	        ]
78	    return out
79	
80	
81	def envelope(img: np.ndarray, rng: np.random.Generator) -> Iterator[tuple[str, str, np.ndarray]]:
82	    """Yield (category, name, perturbed_image) over a fixed slop battery."""
83	    yield "gain", "gain-0.85", adjust_gain(img, 0.85)
84	    yield "gain", "gain-1.15", adjust_gain(img, 1.15)
85	    yield "offset", "offset-neg20", adjust_offset(img, -20)
86	    yield "offset", "offset-pos20", adjust_offset(img, 20)
87	    yield "noise", "noise-sigma6", add_noise(img, 6.0, rng)
88	    yield "noise", "noise-sigma12", add_noise(img, 12.0, rng)
89	    yield "translate", "shift-x4", translate(img, 4, 0)
90	    yield "translate", "shift-y4", translate(img, 0, 4)
91	    yield "translate", "shift-xy6", translate(img, -6, 6)
92	    yield "scale", "overscan-1.03", rescale(img, 1.03)
93	    yield "scale", "underscan-0.97", rescale(img, 0.97)
94
```

```text
8	
9	Layout is plain PODs + flat arrays so the firmware can consume it directly:
10	- screen classifier: `gp_fp_config`, `gp_screen_ids[]`, `gp_centroids[][]`, thresholds.
11	- static-list reader: `gp_menus[]` (geometry) + per-menu item-id and baseline arrays.
12	- song reader: `gp_song_*` config/ROIs + `gp_song_templates[]` + per-song vec arrays.
13	
14	Floats are the per-frame-normalized baselines/song vectors (soft-float on the
15	ARM926, over small vectors — see the journal's port decision). `uint8` centroids
16	and integer thresholds/ROIs are exact.
17	"""
```

```text
94	def selected_item_from_filename(filename: str) -> str | None:

113	# the top. So 38/39 main + 24/25 bonus use SONG_SLOT_ROI; each setlist's song 0
114	# uses SONG_FIRST_ROI. Both ROIs cover the highlighted *title* line only (the
115	# selected title glyphs, right of the album-art thumbnail), which we match

128	# setlist's parchment is yellow, the bonus page is whiter. A large background ROI
129	# (median is robust to the song text over it); warmth = R - B separates them
130	# (offset-invariant, gain-preserving, so it survives the analog slop).
131	SETLIST_BG_ROI = (60, 60, 330, 300)

134	def song_from_filename(filename: str) -> tuple[str, int, str] | None:
135	    """Parse a song_select corpus filename into (setlist, index, song_id).
136	
137	    `song_select__04_rock_and_roll_all_nite.png` -> ("main", 4, "rock_and_roll_all_nite")
138	    `song_select__bonus_07_generation_rock.png`  -> ("bonus", 7, "generation_rock")
139	    Returns None for non-song_select filenames.
140	    """
141	    sel = selected_item_from_filename(filename)
142	    if sel is None:
143	        return None
144	    setlist = "main"
145	    if sel.startswith("bonus_"):
146	        setlist = "bonus"
147	        sel = sel[len("bonus_") :]
148	    head, _, song_id = sel.partition("_")
149	    if not head.isdigit() or not song_id:
150	        return None
151	    return setlist, int(head), song_id
```

```text
1	"""Load the labelled GH3 screen corpus.
2	
3	The corpus is the renamed snapshot set at `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/`
4	(720x480 PNGs). Each image's screen-class label comes from its filename via
5	`screens.screen_id_for_filename`. Images are returned as uint8 HxWx3 arrays in
6	**BGR** order, matching marvin's native framebuffer layout (capture is BGR888
7	packed; see marvin journal 2026-05-02).
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import os
13	from dataclasses import dataclass
14	from pathlib import Path
15	
16	import numpy as np
17	from PIL import Image
18	
19	from .screens import screen_id_for_filename
20	
21	# tools/gameplay/gameplay/corpus.py -> repo root is parents[3].
22	_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
23	_DEFAULT_CORPUS_DIR = _REPO_ROOT / "firmware" / "marvin" / "docs" / "gh3_screens"
24	
25	
26	def corpus_dir() -> Path:
27	    """Resolve the corpus directory (overridable via $GAMEPLAY_CORPUS_DIR)."""
28	    env = os.environ.get("GAMEPLAY_CORPUS_DIR")
29	    return Path(env) if env else _DEFAULT_CORPUS_DIR
30	
31	
32	@dataclass(frozen=True)
33	class Sample:
34	    screen_id: str
35	    path: Path
36	    image: np.ndarray  # uint8, HxWx3, BGR
37	
38	
39	def load_bgr(path: str | Path) -> np.ndarray:
40	    """Load an image file as a uint8 HxWx3 BGR array."""
41	    with Image.open(path) as im:
42	        rgb = np.asarray(im.convert("RGB"), dtype=np.uint8)
43	    return rgb[:, :, ::-1].copy()  # RGB -> BGR
44	
45	
46	def load_corpus(directory: str | Path | None = None) -> list[Sample]:
47	    """Load every `*.png` in the corpus directory as labelled `Sample`s.
48	
49	    Sorted by filename for determinism. Raises FileNotFoundError if the
50	    directory is empty or missing.
51	    """
52	    d = Path(directory) if directory is not None else corpus_dir()
53	    files = sorted(d.glob("*.png"))
54	    if not files:
55	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no PNGs found in corpus dir {d}")
56	    return [
57	        Sample(screen_id=screen_id_for_filename(f.name), path=f, image=load_bgr(f))
58	        for f in files
59	    ]
60
```

```text
11	/* Split [0, extent) into `n` spans; edge(i) = round(i*extent/n). */
12	static int gp_edge(int i, int extent, int n)
13	{
14	    return (int)lround((double)i * (double)extent / (double)n);
15	}
16	
17	const gp_menu_layout_t *gp_menu_for_screen(uint8_t screen)
18	{
19	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_N_MENUS; i++)

26	/* Mean BGR over [x0,x1)×[y0,y1), clamped to the frame. */
27	static void gp_rect_mean_bgr(const uint8_t *frame, int w, int h,
28	                             int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1, float out[3])
29	{
30	    if (x0 < 0) { x0 = 0; }  if (x1 > w) { x1 = w; }
31	    if (y0 < 0) { y0 = 0; }  if (y1 > h) { y1 = h; }
32	    uint32_t sb = 0u, sg = 0u, sr = 0u, n = 0u;
33	    for (int y = y0; y < y1; y++)
34	    {
35	        const uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)w + (uint32_t)x0) * GP_BPP;
36	        for (int x = x0; x < x1; x++)
37	        {
38	            sb += p[0]; sg += p[1]; sr += p[2];
39	            p += GP_BPP;
40	            n++;
41	        }
42	    }
43	    if (n == 0u) { out[0] = out[1] = out[2] = 0.0f; return; }
44	    out[0] = (float)sb / (float)n;
45	    out[1] = (float)sg / (float)n;
46	    out[2] = (float)sr / (float)n;
47	}

49	int gp_read_selection(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height,
50	                      const gp_menu_layout_t *menu)
51	{
52	    if (width != GP_CANON_W || height != GP_CANON_H) { return -1; }
53	    int count = menu->count;
54	    if (count > GP_SEL_MAX_CELLS) { count = GP_SEL_MAX_CELLS; }
55	
56	    float col[GP_SEL_MAX_CELLS][3];
57	    int bx0 = menu->band[0], by0 = menu->band[1], bx1 = menu->band[2], by1 = menu->band[3];
58	    for (int c = 0; c < count; c++)
59	    {
60	        int x0, y0, x1, y1;
61	        if (menu->axis == GP_AXIS_H)
62	        {
63	            y0 = by0; y1 = by1;
64	            x0 = bx0 + gp_edge(c, bx1 - bx0, count);
65	            x1 = bx0 + gp_edge(c + 1, bx1 - bx0, count);
66	        }
67	        else
68	        {
69	            x0 = bx0; x1 = bx1;
70	            y0 = by0 + gp_edge(c, by1 - by0, count);
71	            y1 = by0 + gp_edge(c + 1, by1 - by0, count);
72	        }
73	        gp_rect_mean_bgr(frame, width, height, x0, y0, x1, y1, col[c]);
74	    }
75	
76	    /* Normalize per frame: subtract per-channel mean across cells, divide by the

78	    float mean[3] = {0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f};
79	    for (int c = 0; c < count; c++)

81	    for (int ch = 0; ch < 3; ch++) { mean[ch] /= (float)count; }

88	            var += d * d;
89	        }

91	    if (std < 1e-6f) { std = 1.0f; }

93	    int best = 0;
94	    float best_dev = -1.0f;

101	            float v = (col[c][ch] - mean[ch]) / std;
102	            float d = v - base[ch];
103	            dev += d * d;
104	        }
105	        if (dev > best_dev) { best_dev = dev; best = c; }
106	    }

118	    for (int r = 0; r < GP_SONG_ROWS; r++)

121	        int cy1 = y0 + gp_edge(r + 1, ph, GP_SONG_ROWS);

126	            int cx1 = x0 + gp_edge(c + 1, pw, GP_SONG_COLS);
127	            if (cx0 < 0) { cx0 = 0; }  if (cx1 > w) { cx1 = w; }

170	    int noff = 0;
171	    for (int ix = 0; ix < GP_SONG_NDX; ix++)
172	        for (int iy = 0; iy < GP_SONG_NDY; iy++)
173	        {
174	            gp_song_grid(frame, width, height, slot_roi,  gp_song_dx[ix], gp_song_dy[iy], s_slot_grids[noff]);
175	            gp_song_grid(frame, width, height, first_roi, gp_song_dx[ix], gp_song_dy[iy], s_first_grids[noff]);
176	            noff++;
177	        }
178	
179	    float best_d = 1e30f;
180	    int best_t = -1;
181	    for (int t = 0; t < GP_N_SONGS; t++)
182	    {
183	        const float *vec = gp_song_templates[t].vec;
184	        const float (*grids)[GP_SONG_LEN] =
185	            (gp_song_templates[t].roi_kind == GP_SONG_ROI_FIRST) ? s_first_grids : s_slot_grids;
186	        float tbest = 1e30f;
187	        for (int o = 0; o < noff; o++)
188	        {
189	            float d = 0.0f;
190	            for (int i = 0; i < GP_SONG_LEN; i++) { d += fabsf(grids[o][i] - vec[i]); }
191	            if (d < tbest) { tbest = d; }
192	        }
193	        if (tbest < best_d) { best_d = tbest; best_t = t; }
194	    }
195	
196	    out->tmpl = (int16_t)best_t;
197	    out->setlist = (best_t >= 0) ? gp_song_templates[best_t].setlist : 0;
198	    out->index = (best_t >= 0) ? gp_song_templates[best_t].index : 0;
199	    return 0;
200	}
201
```
</details></tool-use>

 `./tools/marvin-perf/README.md`

```text
1	# marvin-perf
2	
3	Host-side decoder and analyzer for the marvin firmware **perf-log** wire format.
4	
5	The firmware emits framed binary records (schema version 5) over its USB-device
6	CDC ACM port. This tool consumes that stream live, records it to disk, and
7	replays captures offline. Summary analyses (latency attribution, drop
8	accounting, stack high-water trends) are produced by the `serve` viewer, not a
9	standalone CLI verb.
10	
11	Wire format source-of-truth lives in the firmware tree at
12	[`firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h`](../../firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h).
13	The Python schema mirror in [`marvin_perf/records.py`](marvin_perf/records.py)
14	must match it byte-for-byte; bump `EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` (Python side) and
15	`PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` (firmware side) together.
16	
17	## Setup
18	
19	All Python work runs through [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). First-time
20	bootstrap:
21	
22	    cd tools/marvin-perf
23	    uv sync --group viewer   # include viewer deps for the serve command
24	
25	`uv sync` creates `.venv/` and writes `uv.lock`. Subsequent invocations use the
26	existing venv automatically. Omit `--group viewer` if you only need the headless
27	CLI helpers (record, set-mask, set-overlay, snapshot, export-ml).
28	
29	## Usage
30	
31	    # Launch the visual review server (default when no subcommand is given)
32	    uv run marvin-perf
33	    uv run marvin-perf serve
34	    uv run marvin-perf serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765
35	    uv run marvin-perf serve --capture session.bin   # pre-load a capture on startup
36	
37	    # Capture raw bytes from the marvin USB-device CDC port
38	    uv run marvin-perf record --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --out session.bin
39	    uv run marvin-perf record --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --out-dir session/   # perf.bin + manifest.json
40	
41	    # Push a type-mask to a running device without attaching for capture
42	    uv run marvin-perf set-mask --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --types ALL
43	
44	    # Toggle the per-fret target rings on the SENSING strip
45	    uv run marvin-perf set-overlay --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --on
46	
47	    # Capture one full video frame from a running device and save it
48	    uv run marvin-perf snapshot --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --out snapshots/
49	
50	    # Export a capture as a SensiML-format CSV for MPLAB ML training
51	    uv run marvin-perf export-ml session/ --out session.csv --labels actuator-fb
52	
53	## Tests
54	
55	    uv run pytest
56	
57	Fixtures under [`tests/fixtures/`](tests/fixtures/) are hand-built byte streams
58	covering one frame per record type plus framing edge cases (FCS mismatch,
59	truncated payload, mid-stream join needing SOF resync).
60
```
</details></tool-use>
