```text
44:- **Phase 2 — selection + song readers — done (firmware code-complete, builds in MPLAB per
50:  extended to both readers (match the prototype on real frames). Song match densely re-reads its
74:**Phase 3 — song_select reader (done, host-only).** Identify the selected song by matching
75:the highlight-slot bitmap against the 64 per-song templates (closed-set, not OCR).
84:**Phase 2 — static-list highlight reader (done, host-only).** Within an already-classified
86:items + menu-band geometry) + a per-cell "deviation from unselected baseline" reader.
112:2. ✅ **Static-list highlight reader** — read which menu row is selected on the 8
114:   reader, `section_select` variable list.)
115:3. ✅ **`song_select` reader** — fixed-slot bitmap match of the highlight slot against the 64
121:5. ⬜ **Number/score region readers** — score, multiplier, etc. This is where char/digit
122:   glyph recognition (open-ended values, no template) actually belongs.
124:   ✅; Phases 1–3 (observer / readers / controller) ⬜. See Current focus for the phase plan.
132:| 2026-06-15 | **Port to marvin firmware is phased (Phase 0 exporter → 1 observer → 2 readers → 3 controller); numerics stay soft-float for v0; metadata ships as a generated C header (`gameplay export-c`).** No MCC regen needed. | The firmware is built/flashed by Greg in MPLAB (I write + syntax-review C), so phases land "code-complete, pending build"; M9 (observer) and M10 (controller) are already separate milestones, so the phase split mirrors them. Soft-float chosen over fixed-point for v0: the only float work is per-frame normalization over small vectors (~hundreds of values), microseconds even soft-float on the ARM926 — re-validating a fixed-point reimplementation isn't worth it until profiling says so. A generated header (not hand-ported constants) keeps the firmware data in lockstep with the proven prototype and re-emittable when the corpus/params change; plain PODs + flat arrays avoid coupling to firmware struct layout. `game_task` is pure compute on the existing video frame queue + `FretboardLink_Send`, so no new peripheral / no re-apply-patch churn. |
136:| 2026-06-15 | **song_select reader = low-res grayscale grid over the highlight-slot ROI, matched against all 64 per-song templates with a small read-time offset search; setlist derived from the winning song, not the tab.** Grid 32×6, offsets dx∈{-6,-3,0,3,6}/dy∈{-3,0,3}. | 64/64 clean, ~99.1% slop. Matching all 64 (vs filtering by a setlist read first) means main/bonus separation is automatic and removes any dependence on reading the setlist first. The slot grid must be fine to separate ~40 short titles by ink pattern, but a fine grid over a tight ROI is shift-sensitive (translate robustness ~70%); a small offset search re-aligns per frame and recovers it to ~100% (overall slop 90.5%→99.1%) at modest cost (the ROI is small). Per-frame luma normalization handles gain/offset. The per-setlist first song (Slow Ride/Avalancha) sits one row lower (list can't scroll up past it), so its template is built from a second, lower ROI; both ROIs are fingerprinted at read time and each template scores against the one it came from. |
137:| 2026-06-15 | **"Reading" menu items / song titles = closed-set bitmap matching, NOT char-level OCR; char/digit OCR is reserved for open-ended values (scores).** | We have a reference snapshot per menu item and per song, so the selected item/song is recognized by matching its fixed region against the known templates (the same fingerprint idea as the screen classifier). Per-character decoding is only needed where there's no template — i.e. scores/multipliers/note counts — which is a later, separate phase. Keeps phase 2 free of OCR. |
138:| 2026-06-15 | **Static-list highlight reader = per-screen menu geometry (band + ordered items + axis) + per-cell "deviation from unselected baseline" with per-frame colour normalization; argmax over cells.** Scope = the 8 fixed-count static lists; `section_select` (variable list) and `song_select` (fixed-slot) deferred. | GH3 marks selection by *changing* a row (colour shift / highlight bar), not always by making it brightest — a luma/white argmax collided on most screens (flat scores). Comparing each cell to its own learned unselected appearance ("what changed") handles every highlight style and baselines out background art (main_menu / practice_end sit over collage). Baseline uses only *unselected* exemplars per cell so it's non-degenerate at K=2 (a median-over-all collapses to the midpoint and can't separate two items — that bug showed as exactly 1/2 on the three two-item screens). Per-frame normalization (subtract mean cell colour, scale by spread) cancels the analog gain/offset slop, lifting slop robustness ~90%→~99%. Result: 100% clean / 99.4% slop on 33 labelled frames. Baselines are learned from the corpus (a `SelectionCalibration`, parallel to the classifier's centroids); the firmware port bakes them. ## Overview
```
The prototype uses a consistent "reader" idiom: a frozen-dataclass **Config** (grid dims + offset-search), a frozen **Template** (label + `vec`), a frozen **Catalog/Calibration** (list of templates + config + thresholds, built from the corpus), and a frozen **Result** (label + `dist`/`margin`). ROIs are `(x0, y0, x1, y1)` tuples in canonical **720x480** space. All matching is L1 distance over per-frame-normalized vectors, argmin, with a `margin` = second-best − best. This ports 1:1 to integer C.

---

## 1. `gameplay/songselect.py` — the closest analog to a digit reader
Path: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/gameplay/gameplay/songselect.py`

End-to-end structure (frame + config → ROI sample → low-res grid → template match with offset search):

- **Config** (grid + read-time offset search):
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SongConfig:
    cols: int = 32
    rows: int = 6
    dx_search: tuple[int, ...] = (-6, -3, 0, 3, 6)
    dy_search: tuple[int, ...] = (-6, -3, 0, 3, 6)
DEFAULT_SONG_CONFIG = SongConfig()
```

- **The ROI→fingerprint sampler** — this is the exact routine a digit-cell fingerprint should mirror (canonicalize, slice ROI, luma-project via BGR weights, resample into a `rows×cols` grid of cell means, then zero-mean/unit-std normalize per frame):
```python
_LUMA_W = np.array([29, 150, 77], dtype=np.float64)  # (B,G,R)/256

def _luma_grid(image, roi: tuple[int,int,int,int], cfg: SongConfig) -> np.ndarray:
    img = _to_canonical(image)
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = roi
    patch = img[y0:y1, x0:x1].astype(np.float64)
    luma = patch @ _LUMA_W / 256.0
    ys = np.linspace(0, luma.shape[0], cfg.rows + 1).round().astype(int)
    xs = np.linspace(0, luma.shape[1], cfg.cols + 1).round().astype(int)
    cells = np.empty((cfg.rows, cfg.cols), dtype=np.float64)
    for r in range(cfg.rows):
        for c in range(cfg.cols):
            cells[r, c] = luma[ys[r]:ys[r+1], xs[c]:xs[c+1]].mean()
    v = cells.reshape(-1)
    v -= v.mean(); s = v.std()
    return v / s if s > 1e-6 else v
```

- **Template / Catalog / Result dataclasses:**
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SongTemplate: setlist:str; index:int; song_id:str; roi_kind:str; vec:np.ndarray

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SongCatalog: templates:list[SongTemplate]; config:SongConfig; setlist_warmth_threshold:float

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SongResult: setlist:str; index:int; song_id:str; dist:float; margin:float
```

- **Build from corpus** — `build_song_catalog(samples, config=DEFAULT_SONG_CONFIG)` filters `s.screen_id == "song_select"`, parses the label via `song_from_filename`, picks the ROI variant, and stores `_luma_grid(...)` as the template `vec`.

- **The offset search** (`read_song`) — precomputes one fingerprint per `(roi_kind, dx, dy)` (reused across all templates), then scores each template as the **min** over the offset grid; this is exactly the pattern to replicate per digit position:
```python
def _shift(roi, dx, dy):
    x0,y0,x1,y1 = roi; return (x0+dx, y0+dy, x1+dx, y1+dy)

def read_song(image, catalog, setlist=None) -> SongResult:
    cfg = catalog.config
    cand = [t for t in catalog.templates if setlist is None or t.setlist == setlist]
    fps = {}
    for dx in cfg.dx_search:
        for dy in cfg.dy_search:
            fps[(SLOT, dx, dy)]  = _luma_grid(image, _shift(SONG_SLOT_ROI, dx, dy), cfg)
            fps[(FIRST, dx, dy)] = _luma_grid(image, _shift(SONG_FIRST_ROI, dx, dy), cfg)
    def best_dist(t):
        return min(float(np.abs(fps[(t.roi_kind, dx, dy)] - t.vec).sum())
                   for dx in cfg.dx_search for dy in cfg.dy_search)
    scored = sorted(((best_dist(t), t) for t in cand), key=lambda kv: kv[0])
    best_d, best = scored[0]
    second_d = scored[1][0] if len(scored) > 1 else best_d
    return SongResult(best.setlist, best.index, best.song_id, best_d, second_d - best_d)
```
Distance metric: `np.abs(fp - vec).sum()` (L1). Confidence: `margin = second_best − best`.

Note: there is also `songselect_prefix.py` (8.7 KB, not requested) in the same dir if you want an alternate matching variant.

## 2. `gameplay/metadata.py` — config/ROI data structures
Path: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/gameplay/gameplay/metadata.py`

- **Coordinate convention is confirmed `(x0, y0, x1, y1)`** in canonical 720x480 space. Two styles coexist:
  - Menu bands live in a `dict[str, MenuLayout]` (`MENU_LAYOUTS`), keyed by `screen_id`, each with `band: tuple[int,int,int,int]`, an `items` tuple, and an `axis` (`VERTICAL="v"`/`HORIZONTAL="h"`). Has `.count` and `.index_of(item_id)`.
  - The song reader uses **module-level ROI constants**, not a dict:
```python
SONG_SLOT_ROI  = (183, 233, 385, 266)   # (x0,y0,x1,y1)
SONG_FIRST_ROI = (183, 282, 385, 315)
SETLIST_BG_ROI = (60, 60, 330, 300)
```
- Filename parsing helpers live here too: `selected_item_from_filename(filename) -> str|None` (splits on `__`, strips `.png`) and `song_from_filename(filename) -> tuple[str,int,str]|None` returning `(setlist, index, song_id)`.
- The module docstring already anticipates your work: *"char-level OCR, which is only needed later for open-ended values like scores."*

**To add a score block in the same idiom**, mirror the song_select section: add module-level ROI constants keyed by gameplay mode (e.g. a `SCORE_ROI: dict[str, tuple[int,int,int,int]]` mapping mode→ROI, or per-mode constants), plus a `score_from_filename(...)` parser if you label frames with their numeric value. Digit glyph templates (0–9) are better built at catalog-build time in `score.py` (as `_luma_grid` vectors) rather than stored as literals here — metadata should hold only the geometry (per-mode score ROI, digit count/pitch), consistent with how `songselect.py` keeps `vec`s in the catalog and only ROIs in metadata.

## 3. `gameplay/highlight.py` + `gameplay/fingerprint.py` — normalization + grid helpers
Paths: `.../gameplay/highlight.py`, `.../gameplay/fingerprint.py`

Reusable helpers (import these directly — `songselect.py` imports `_to_canonical` from `fingerprint`):

## Overview
The prototype uses a consistent "reader" idiom: a frozen-dataclass **Config** (grid dims + offset-search), a frozen **Template** (label + `vec`), a frozen **Catalog/Calibration** (list of templates + config + thresholds, built from the corpus), and a frozen **Result** (label + `dist`/`margin`). ROIs are `(x0, y0, x1, y1)` tuples in canonical **720x480** space. All matching is L1 distance over per-frame-normalized vectors, argmin, with a `margin` = second-best − best. This ports 1:1 to integer C.

## 1. `gameplay/songselect.py` — the closest analog to a digit reader
Path: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/gameplay/gameplay/songselect.py`

End-to-end structure (frame + config → ROI sample → low-res grid → template match with offset search):

- **Config** (grid + read-time offset search):
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SongConfig:
    cols: int = 32
    rows: int = 6
    dx_search: tuple[int, ...] = (-6, -3, 0, 3, 6)
    dy_search: tuple[int, ...] = (-6, -3, 0, 3, 6)
DEFAULT_SONG_CONFIG = SongConfig()
```

- **The ROI→fingerprint sampler** — this is the exact routine a digit-cell fingerprint should mirror (canonicalize, slice ROI, luma-project via BGR weights, resample into a `rows×cols` grid of cell means, then zero-mean/unit-std normalize per frame):
```python
_LUMA_W = np.array([29, 150, 77], dtype=np.float64)  # (B,G,R)/256

def _luma_grid(image, roi: tuple[int,int,int,int], cfg: SongConfig) -&gt; np.ndarray:
    img = _to_canonical(image)
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = roi
    patch = img[y0:y1, x0:x1].astype(np.float64)
    luma = patch @ _LUMA_W / 256.0
    ys = np.linspace(0, luma.shape[0], cfg.rows + 1).round().astype(int)
    xs = np.linspace(0, luma.shape[1], cfg.cols + 1).round().astype(int)
    cells = np.empty((cfg.rows, cfg.cols), dtype=np.float64)
    for r in range(cfg.rows):
        for c in range(cfg.cols):
            cells[r, c] = luma[ys[r]:ys[r+1], xs[c]:xs[c+1]].mean()
    v = cells.reshape(-1)
    v -= v.mean(); s = v.std()
    return v / s if s &gt; 1e-6 else v
```

- **Template / Catalog / Result dataclasses:**
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SongTemplate: setlist:str; index:int; song_id:str; roi_kind:str; vec:np.ndarray

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SongCatalog: templates:list[SongTemplate]; config:SongConfig; setlist_warmth_threshold:float

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SongResult: setlist:str; index:int; song_id:str; dist:float; margin:float
```

- **Build from corpus** — `build_song_catalog(samples, config=DEFAULT_SONG_CONFIG)` filters `s.screen_id == "song_select"`, parses the label via `song_from_filename`, picks the ROI variant, and stores `_luma_grid(...)` as the template `vec`.

- **The offset search** (`read_song`) — precomputes one fingerprint per `(roi_kind, dx, dy)` (reused across all templates), then scores each template as the **min** over the offset grid; this is exactly the pattern to replicate per digit position:
```python
def _shift(roi, dx, dy):
    x0,y0,x1,y1 = roi; return (x0+dx, y0+dy, x1+dx, y1+dy)

def read_song(image, catalog, setlist=None) -&gt; SongResult:
    cfg = catalog.config
    cand = [t for t in catalog.templates if setlist is None or t.setlist == setlist]
    fps = {}
    for dx in cfg.dx_search:
        for dy in cfg.dy_search:
            fps[(SLOT, dx, dy)]  = _luma_grid(image, _shift(SONG_SLOT_ROI, dx, dy), cfg)
            fps[(FIRST, dx, dy)] = _luma_grid(image, _shift(SONG_FIRST_ROI, dx, dy), cfg)
    def best_dist(t):
        return min(float(np.abs(fps[(t.roi_kind, dx, dy)] - t.vec).sum())
                   for dx in cfg.dx_search for dy in cfg.dy_search)
    scored = sorted(((best_dist(t), t) for t in cand), key=lambda kv: kv[0])
    best_d, best = scored[0]
    second_d = scored[1][0] if len(scored) &gt; 1 else best_d
    return SongResult(best.setlist, best.index, best.song_id, best_d, second_d - best_d)
```
Distance metric: `np.abs(fp - vec).sum()` (L1). Confidence: `margin = second_best − best`.

Note: there is also `songselect_prefix.py` (8.7 KB, not requested) in the same dir if you want an alternate matching variant.

# Score-reader (Phase 5) recon — gameplay tools + marvin firmware

Note on naming: the `tools/gameplay/docs/journal.md` slice list calls this **item 5** ("Number/score region readers"), while `firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md` and `SPEC.md` call the same work **M9 Phase 3** ("number/score readers"). Same feature, two numbering schemes. It is confirmed **not started** in either tree.

## 1. Eval harness — `tools/gameplay/gameplay/evaluate.py`

Structure (module docstring lists the five proven-before-port checks):

- **Leave-one-out CV** — `loo_eval(samples, config, t_abs, t_margin) -> LooResult` (lines 70-113). For each sample, rebuilds centroids from all *other* samples, classifies the held-out one; accumulates `per_class_acc: dict[str,(correct,total)]` and `confusion: dict[(true,pred),int]`. `LooResult.accuracy` property.
- **Threshold recommendation** — `recommend_thresholds(samples, config) -> ThresholdRecommendation` (185-214), driven by two helpers: `_loo_in_class_stats` (worst legit in-class distance/margin) and `_holdout_impostor_stats` (whole-class hold-out → how close an unseen class lands to a surviving centroid). `rec_t_abs = round(in_d_max*1.20)` (`_ABS_HEADROOM=0.20`), `rec_t_margin = in_m_min*0.5` (`_MARGIN_FRACTION`). Reports `impostor_leak` — honest false-accept count, *reported not minimized*.
- **Robustness (clean vs slop)** — `robustness_eval(samples, config, t_abs, t_margin, seed=1234) -> RobustnessResult` (231-258). Trains on the full clean corpus, then classifies `perturb.envelope(s.image, rng)` copies; `per_category: dict[str,(stable,total)]`, `stability` property.
- **HW-time estimate** — `hw_time_estimate_ms(config) -> (fast, slow)` (264-278). Dense = bandwidth-bound over `_DDR_BW_MB_S=(50,150)`; subsampled = latency-bound `reads * _UNCACHED_LAT_NS(50,150)/1e6`.
- **Per-config sweep** — inside `run_report(...)` (506-525): iterates `(cols,rows) × spr × normalize`, printing `LOO / robust / ms` per config.

**Existing reader-eval precedents you should mirror** (these are the real template for a `score_eval`, not the classifier eval):
- `selection_eval(samples, perturb_envelope=False, seed) -> SelectionEvalResult` (309-337): `per_screen`, `failures: list[(filename,true,pred)]`, `accuracy`. Ground truth pulled from filename via `selected_item_from_filename`. Runs once clean and once with `perturb.envelope` (see `run_report` 476-489).
- `song_eval(samples, seed) -> SongEvalResult` (371-401): richest example — carries `n_song_ok`, `margin_min`, and separate `slop_ok/slop_total` counters, iterating `perturb.envelope` per sample. Ground truth from `song_from_filename`.

**What a `score_eval` should look like, following this pattern:** a dataclass `ScoreEvalResult` with `n_total`, `n_exact_ok` (full-number exact match), `n_digit_ok/n_digit_total` (per-digit accuracy), `slop_exact_ok/slop_digit_ok` over `perturb.envelope`, and `failures: list[(filename, true_str, pred_str)]`. Exact-match property `= n_exact_ok/n_total`; per-digit `= n_digit_ok/n_digit_total`. It needs a per-frame ground-truth score (see §4 — this is the gating problem) analogous to `song_from_filename`. It would be added to `run_report` as a new block and given a CLI verb in `cli.py` (currently `classify`/`eval`/`rows`/`export-c`/`navigate`; there is no dedicated `score` verb yet).

## 2. Perturbation battery — `tools/gameplay/gameplay/perturb.py`

Operates on uint8 HxWx3 **BGR** arrays; deterministic given an rng. Two families (value slop, positional slop). Reusable signatures:

- `adjust_gain(img, gain: float)` — `clip(img*gain, 0, 255)`
- `adjust_offset(img, offset: float)` — `clip(img+offset,...)`
- `add_noise(img, sigma: float, rng)` — additive gaussian
- `translate(img, dx: int, dy: int)` — edge-replicated pixel shift
- `rescale(img, factor: float)` — zoom about centre, centre-crop/pad (overscan/underscan)

`envelope(img, rng) -> Iterator[(category, name, image)]` yields the fixed battery — exact parameter envelope:

| category | variants |
|---|---|
| `gain` | 0.85, 1.15 |
| `offset` | -20, +20 |
| `noise` | sigma 6.0, sigma 12.0 |
| `translate` | (4,0), (0,4), (-6,6) |
| `scale` | rescale 1.03 (overscan), 0.97 (underscan) |

For score robustness, reuse `envelope` unchanged (same analog-slop model). Note the `translate` ±4–6 px envelope is the relevant stressor for per-digit ROI registration — the song reader (journal 2026-06-15) found tight ROIs are shift-sensitive and needed a read-time offset search to recover, which is directly applicable to digit-cell alignment.

## 3. C-export style — `export_c.py` → `gameplay_metadata.h`, and the firmware reader port

**Codegen helpers** in `export_c.py`:
- `_c_ident(name)` — `-`→`_`
- `_u8_rows(arr, indent)` — renders a 2-D uint8 array as brace-wrapped C rows (used for `gp_centroids[N][LEN]`)
- `_floats(vec)` — comma-joined `%.6gf` literals
- `build_metadata_header(samples=None) -> str` — builds everything with `w = L.append`; guarded by `#ifndef GAMEPLAY_METADATA_H`, `#include <stdint.h>`.

**How per-class `uint8` templates + ROIs are emitted today** (the pattern to copy for digits):
- Screen classifier: `#define GP_FP_*`, `gp_screen_ids[]`, `static const uint8_t gp_centroids[GP_N_SCREENS][GP_FP_LEN]` via `_u8_rows(templates.centroids)`, integer thresholds `GP_CLS_T_ABS/GP_CLS_T_MARGIN`.
- Selection reader: per-menu `gp_menu_<id>_items[]` + `gp_menu_<id>_baseline[]` (float), then a `gp_menu_layout_t` struct `{screen, axis, count, uint16_t band[4], items*, baseline*}` and `gp_menus[]` table.
- Song reader (closest analog to a score-ROI reader): `#define GP_SONG_COLS/ROWS/LEN`, ROIs emitted as brace macros `#define GP_SONG_SLOT_ROI {x0,y0,x1,y1}` (see lines 146-147), offset-search arrays `gp_song_dx[]/gp_song_dy[]`, per-template `gp_song_vec_<i>[LEN]` float arrays, and a `gp_song_template_t {setlist,index,roi_kind,song_id,vec*}` table.

**To emit digit templates + score ROIs in the same style:** add a block that writes `#define GP_DIGIT_COLS/ROWS/LEN`, a score-region ROI macro `#define GP_SCORE_ROI {..}` (and per-font ROIs since training vs career score boxes differ in position/font), per-digit-glyph templates via `_u8_rows(...)` (a `gp_digit_templates[10][LEN]` for each font — mirrors `gp_centroids`), and any integer per-digit match thresholds. Two fonts → two template banks (e.g. `GP_FONT_TRAIN` white-proportional, `GP_FONT_CAREER` green-segmented), selectable like `roi_kind`/`setlist` are today. Keep templates `uint8` + integer thresholds (exact) per the header's stated convention; the journal's port decision only allows floats for per-frame-normalized vectors.

**Firmware port style** — `firmware/marvin/default/src/game/gameplay_select.{h,c}`:
- Header declares pure, non-reentrant readers driven by `gameplay_metadata.h`: `gp_menu_for_screen`, `int gp_read_selection(frame,w,h,menu)`, `int gp_read_song(frame,w,h,gp_song_t*)` with an output struct.
- `.c` shows the integer-math idioms to reuse: `gp_edge(i,extent,n)` (splits a band into n spans by `round(i*extent/n)`), `gp_rect_mean_bgr(...)` (uint32 accumulators over a clamped rect), per-frame normalization (subtract mean, divide by spread), argmin/argmax over templates with `fabsf` L1, and an offset search (`gp_song_dx/dy`) with static scratch buffers. Uses soft-float only for the small normalized vectors; distances/indexing are integer. A `gp_read_score(frame,w,h,gp_score_t*)` would segment the score ROI into digit cells with `gp_edge`, fingerprint each cell, and nearest-template match against the emitted per-font digit banks — same shape as `gp_read_song`.

Current `gameplay_metadata.h`: 13 screens (`in_song` is index 1), 8 menus, song tables. **No digit/score/glyph tables exist yet** (grep clean).

## 4. DATA AVAILABILITY — the gating problem

### `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/` (the labelled corpus, 101 PNGs, 720×480)
Filename encodes the label (`screen__selection.png`), loaded by `corpus.py` / `screens.py`. **Exactly one gameplay frame:** `in_song__training.png`. It is **training mode** and shows a score of **1138** in the white proportional font (with a "2" multiplier). There is **no career-mode in-song frame** in this labelled set, and **no score label is encoded** anywhere — the corpus filename scheme only carries a screen id / menu selection, never a numeric value. So the proven-corpus path gives you a single white-font example and zero green-font examples, with no machine-readable score ground truth.

### `tools/marvin-perf/snapshots/` (186 PNGs, 720×480 RGB)
These are **raw device video-frame captures** (produced by `marvin-perf snapshot`, README line 48) — unlabelled, named only `snapshot-NNNN.png`. **The only non-PNG in the directory is `.DS_Store`. No manifest, JSON, CSV, or sidecar labels of any kind.** Sampling confirms they are a mixed session spanning menus and gameplay:
- `0001` main_menu; `0050` song_select (bonus list); `0075` song_select (bonus list); `0180` "You Rock!" end screen.
- **Career/quickplay in-song frames with legible scores:** `0100` = "3938", `0125` = "11437", `0150` = "19979" (green segmented digits + a "3" multiplier). These show both venues/backgrounds and both font renderings.

So the scores **are visually present and legible** in a good number of these frames, but **the ground truth is not recorded anywhere** — you would have to hand-label (read the digits off each frame) to build a corpus. There is also no index of which snapshot is which screen/mode.

### `tools/marvin-perf/captures/` (5 songs: hitme, rockroll, slowride, story, talkdirty)
Each dir has `manifest.json` + `perf.bin` (perf-log binary, schema v4/5); sibling `*-hard.csv` files. These are **fretboard sensor time series** — columns `timestamp,fb_seq,ph_green..ph_orange,fret_green..fret_orange,strum`. **No score column, no video, not GH3 screen data.** Not usable as score ground truth.

### Repo-wide search for score ground truth / digit labels
- The `score` grep hits in firmware (`results/`, `dashboard_feed`, `perf_log_records.h`, `console.c`) are the **marvin device's own trainer scoring**, unrelated to GH3 on-screen OCR.
- `firmware/marvin/data/games/gh3-wii/songs.csv` is the **song catalog** (metadata/BPM), not per-play scores.
- `spec.md` line 509 documents a proposed reference-data CSV schema `player,game,setlist,index,song,difficulty,part,score,accuracy_pct,notes_hit,notes_total,timestamp` — but **no file matching that schema exists** (grep for `accuracy_pct`/`notes_hit` in `*.csv` returns nothing). It is an aspirational schema only.

### Bottom line on data
- **Labelled score data: none exists.** Zero frames anywhere carry a machine-readable ground-truth score.
- **Unlabelled raw material: plentiful and legible.** ~186 raw gameplay/menu snapshots (a meaningful fraction are in-song with readable scores) plus one labelled training-mode in-song frame.
- **Font coverage from existing images:** career/green-segmented digits appear in multiple snapshots; the white/proportional training font appears in `in_song__training.png` (score 1138) and at least one snapshot (`0125`, "11437"). Both fonts are observable, but you must **hand-label** every frame's score/digits before any `score_eval` (exact-match + per-digit) can run — this is the primary prerequisite that gates the plan. A natural approach mirroring the existing corpus convention would be to curate score-bearing snapshots into a directory with the score encoded in the filename (e.g. `score__career__019979.png`) and add a `score_from_filename` parser paralleling `song_from_filename`.

**Key files:** `tools/gameplay/gameplay/{evaluate,perturb,export_c,metadata,corpus,cli}.py`; `firmware/marvin/default/src/game/{gameplay_metadata.h,gameplay_select.h,gameplay_select.c}`; corpus at `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/in_song__training.png`; raw frames at `tools/marvin-perf/snapshots/snapshot-*.png`.

**What a `score_eval` should look like, following this pattern:** a dataclass `ScoreEvalResult` with `n_total`, `n_exact_ok` (full-number exact match), `n_digit_ok/n_digit_total` (per-digit accuracy), `slop_exact_ok/slop_digit_ok` over `perturb.envelope`, and `failures: list[(filename, true_str, pred_str)]`. Exact-match property `= n_exact_ok/n_total`; per-digit `= n_digit_ok/n_digit_total`. It needs a per-frame ground-truth score (see §4 — this is the gating problem) analogous to `song_from_filename`. It would be added to `run_report` as a new block and given a CLI verb in `cli.py` (currently `classify`/`eval`/`rows`/`export-c`/`navigate`; there is no dedicated `score` verb yet).

## 2. Perturbation battery — `tools/gameplay/gameplay/perturb.py`

Operates on uint8 HxWx3 **BGR** arrays; deterministic given an rng. Two families (value slop, positional slop). Reusable signatures:

- `adjust_gain(img, gain: float)` — `clip(img*gain, 0, 255)`
- `adjust_offset(img, offset: float)` — `clip(img+offset,...)`
- `add_noise(img, sigma: float, rng)` — additive gaussian
- `translate(img, dx: int, dy: int)` — edge-replicated pixel shift
- `rescale(img, factor: float)` — zoom about centre, centre-crop/pad (overscan/underscan)

`envelope(img, rng) -&gt; Iterator[(category, name, image)]` yields the fixed battery — exact parameter envelope:

| category | variants |
|---|---|
| `gain` | 0.85, 1.15 |
| `offset` | -20, +20 |
| `noise` | sigma 6.0, sigma 12.0 |
| `translate` | (4,0), (0,4), (-6,6) |
| `scale` | rescale 1.03 (overscan), 0.97 (underscan) |

For score robustness, reuse `envelope` unchanged (same analog-slop model). Note the `translate` ±4–6 px envelope is the relevant stressor for per-digit ROI registration — the song reader (journal 2026-06-15) found tight ROIs are shift-sensitive and needed a read-time offset search to recover, which is directly applicable to digit-cell alignment.

## 3. C-export style — `export_c.py` → `gameplay_metadata.h`, and the firmware reader port

**Codegen helpers** in `export_c.py`:
- `_c_ident(name)` — `-`→`_`
- `_u8_rows(arr, indent)` — renders a 2-D uint8 array as brace-wrapped C rows (used for `gp_centroids[N][LEN]`)
- `_floats(vec)` — comma-joined `%.6gf` literals
- `build_metadata_header(samples=None) -&gt; str` — builds everything with `w = L.append`; guarded by `#ifndef GAMEPLAY_METADATA_H`, `#include &lt;stdint.h&gt;`.

**How per-class `uint8` templates + ROIs are emitted today** (the pattern to copy for digits):
- Screen classifier: `#define GP_FP_*`, `gp_screen_ids[]`, `static const uint8_t gp_centroids[GP_N_SCREENS][GP_FP_LEN]` via `_u8_rows(templates.centroids)`, integer thresholds `GP_CLS_T_ABS/GP_CLS_T_MARGIN`.
- Selection reader: per-menu `gp_menu_&lt;id&gt;_items[]` + `gp_menu_&lt;id&gt;_baseline[]` (float), then a `gp_menu_layout_t` struct `{screen, axis, count, uint16_t band[4], items*, baseline*}` and `gp_menus[]` table.
- Song reader (closest analog to a score-ROI reader): `#define GP_SONG_COLS/ROWS/LEN`, ROIs emitted as brace macros `#define GP_SONG_SLOT_ROI {x0,y0,x1,y1}` (see lines 146-147), offset-search arrays `gp_song_dx[]/gp_song_dy[]`, per-template `gp_song_vec_&lt;i&gt;[LEN]` float arrays, and a `gp_song_template_t {setlist,index,roi_kind,song_id,vec*}` table.

**To emit digit templates + score ROIs in the same style:** add a block that writes `#define GP_DIGIT_COLS/ROWS/LEN`, a score-region ROI macro `#define GP_SCORE_ROI {..}` (and per-font ROIs since training vs career score boxes differ in position/font), per-digit-glyph templates via `_u8_rows(...)` (a `gp_digit_templates[10][LEN]` for each font — mirrors `gp_centroids`), and any integer per-digit match thresholds. Two fonts → two template banks (e.g. `GP_FONT_TRAIN` white-proportional, `GP_FONT_CAREER` green-segmented), selectable like `roi_kind`/`setlist` are today. Keep templates `uint8` + integer thresholds (exact) per the header's stated convention; the journal's port decision only allows floats for per-frame-normalized vectors.

**Firmware port style** — `firmware/marvin/default/src/game/gameplay_select.{h,c}`:
- Header declares pure, non-reentrant readers driven by `gameplay_metadata.h`: `gp_menu_for_screen`, `int gp_read_selection(frame,w,h,menu)`, `int gp_read_song(frame,w,h,gp_song_t*)` with an output struct.
- `.c` shows the integer-math idioms to reuse: `gp_edge(i,extent,n)` (splits a band into n spans by `round(i*extent/n)`), `gp_rect_mean_bgr(...)` (uint32 accumulators over a clamped rect), per-frame normalization (subtract mean, divide by spread), argmin/argmax over templates with `fabsf` L1, and an offset search (`gp_song_dx/dy`) with static scratch buffers. Uses soft-float only for the small normalized vectors; distances/indexing are integer. A `gp_read_score(frame,w,h,gp_score_t*)` would segment the score ROI into digit cells with `gp_edge`, fingerprint each cell, and nearest-template match against the emitted per-font digit banks — same shape as `gp_read_song`.

Current `gameplay_metadata.h`: 13 screens (`in_song` is index 1), 8 menus, song tables. **No digit/score/glyph tables exist yet** (grep clean).

## 4. DATA AVAILABILITY — the gating problem

### `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/` (the labelled corpus, 101 PNGs, 720×480)
Filename encodes the label (`screen__selection.png`), loaded by `corpus.py` / `screens.py`. **Exactly one gameplay frame:** `in_song__training.png`. It is **training mode** and shows a score of **1138** in the white proportional font (with a "2" multiplier). There is **no career-mode in-song frame** in this labelled set, and **no score label is encoded** anywhere — the corpus filename scheme only carries a screen id / menu selection, never a numeric value. So the proven-corpus path gives you a single white-font example and zero green-font examples, with no machine-readable score ground truth.

### `tools/marvin-perf/snapshots/` (186 PNGs, 720×480 RGB)
These are **raw device video-frame captures** (produced by `marvin-perf snapshot`, README line 48) — unlabelled, named only `snapshot-NNNN.png`. **The only non-PNG in the directory is `.DS_Store`. No manifest, JSON, CSV, or sidecar labels of any kind.** Sampling confirms they are a mixed session spanning menus and gameplay:
- `0001` main_menu; `0050` song_select (bonus list); `0075` song_select (bonus list); `0180` "You Rock!" end screen.
- **Career/quickplay in-song frames with legible scores:** `0100` = "3938", `0125` = "11437", `0150` = "19979" (green segmented digits + a "3" multiplier). These show both venues/backgrounds and both font renderings.

So the scores **are visually present and legible** in a good number of these frames, but **the ground truth is not recorded anywhere** — you would have to hand-label (read the digits off each frame) to build a corpus. There is also no index of which snapshot is which screen/mode.

### `tools/marvin-perf/captures/` (5 songs: hitme, rockroll, slowride, story, talkdirty)
Each dir has `manifest.json` + `perf.bin` (perf-log binary, schema v4/5); sibling `*-hard.csv` files. These are **fretboard sensor time series** — columns `timestamp,fb_seq,ph_green..ph_orange,fret_green..fret_orange,strum`. **No score column, no video, not GH3 screen data.** Not usable as score ground truth.

### Repo-wide search for score ground truth / digit labels
- The `score` grep hits in firmware (`results/`, `dashboard_feed`, `perf_log_records.h`, `console.c`) are the **marvin device's own trainer scoring**, unrelated to GH3 on-screen OCR.
- `firmware/marvin/data/games/gh3-wii/songs.csv` is the **song catalog** (metadata/BPM), not per-play scores.
- `spec.md` line 509 documents a proposed reference-data CSV schema `player,game,setlist,index,song,difficulty,part,score,accuracy_pct,notes_hit,notes_total,timestamp` — but **no file matching that schema exists** (grep for `accuracy_pct`/`notes_hit` in `*.csv` returns nothing). It is an aspirational schema only.

### Bottom line on data
- **Labelled score data: none exists.** Zero frames anywhere carry a machine-readable ground-truth score.
- **Unlabelled raw material: plentiful and legible.** ~186 raw gameplay/menu snapshots (a meaningful fraction are in-song with readable scores) plus one labelled training-mode in-song frame.
- **Font coverage from existing images:** career/green-segmented digits appear in multiple snapshots; the white/proportional training font appears in `in_song__training.png` (score 1138) and at least one snapshot (`0125`, "11437"). Both fonts are observable, but you must **hand-label** every frame's score/digits before any `score_eval` (exact-match + per-digit) can run — this is the primary prerequisite that gates the plan. A natural approach mirroring the existing corpus convention would be to curate score-bearing snapshots into a directory with the score encoded in the filename (e.g. `score__career__019979.png`) and add a `score_from_filename` parser paralleling `song_from_filename`.

**Key files:** `tools/gameplay/gameplay/{evaluate,perturb,export_c,metadata,corpus,cli}.py`; `firmware/marvin/default/src/game/{gameplay_metadata.h,gameplay_select.h,gameplay_select.c}`; corpus at `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/in_song__training.png`; raw frames at `tools/marvin-perf/snapshots/snapshot-*.png`.</result>

```text
# Plan: Gameplay score reader (gameplay phase 5)

## Context
Gameplay journal phase 5 (= marvin spec M9 Phase 3): read the open-ended on-screen **score** from
GH3 gameplay video frames. This is the one recognizer that can't be a closed-set template match
(scores are unbounded), so it needs per-digit glyph recognition — the piece the earlier phases
explicitly deferred. First pass targets the **training-mode white proportional font only** (career
green segmented LED font is a follow-up). Goal: a host-side `score.py` reader proven against a small
labelled corpus + synthetic slop, in the same idiom as the existing readers, ready to port to
firmware later (like phases 1–4).

## Findings so far
- Two distinct score fonts by mode:
  - **Training** (`snapshot-0121`): white, rounded **proportional** digits. Score up to **6 digits**.
  - **Career** (`snapshot-0174`): **green segmented "LED"** digits.
- Score is **right-aligned, grows leftward** (units digit anchored at right; higher digits extend left).
- Approx ROIs (720×480 raw frame): training white digits ~x152–197 (extend left to ~x140 for 6 digits), y≈318–342; career green digits ~x140–200, y≈317–331 (dimmer — needs its own threshold/font).

## Reader idiom to mirror (from songselect.py)
- Frozen dataclasses: `Config` (grid dims + `dx_search`/`dy_search` offset tuples), `Template` (label + `vec`), `Catalog` (templates + config + thresholds, built from corpus), `Result` (label + `dist` + `margin`).
- ROIs are `(x0,y0,x1,y1)` in canonical **720×480**; call `fingerprint._to_canonical(image)` first.
- Sampling: `_luma_grid` = ROI slice → luma (BGR weights) → `rows×cols` cell means → per-frame zero-mean/unit-std. Match = **L1 over normalized vectors, argmin**; `margin` = 2nd-best − best.
- Offset search: precompute one fingerprint per (roi, dx, dy), score each template as min over the offset grid (re-aligns per frame → robust to positional slop).
- Metadata holds only geometry (ROI constants); template `vec`s are built at catalog-build time from the corpus.
- CLI: reader hooks in `cmd_classify` by `screen_id`; debug subcommand mirrors `cmd_rows`.
- Corpus: `load_bgr` → uint8 HxWx3 **BGR**; `Sample(screen_id, path, image)`; filenames `<prefix>__<selection>.png`; corpus dir `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/` (override `$GAMEPLAY_CORPUS_DIR`).

## Data gap (gating)
- Corpus has **exactly one** gameplay frame: `in_song__training.png`. No score-labelled frames, no digit exemplars, no career `in_song` frame.
- `tools/marvin-perf/snapshots/` has 186 raw PNGs (unlabelled) — candidate source to harvest + hand-label gameplay frames.

## Decisions (from user)
- **Training white font only** this pass; structure config per-font so career green slots in later.
- **~8-frame handful** corpus; avoid bulk manual labeling. I read scores off upscaled crops; **user
  labels/confirms a few** to anchor trust.
- The 8 frames × up-to-6 digits yield enough exemplars to build 0–9 white templates. A small
  **marvin-perf score-crop capture** feature (user's idea) is the recommended *later* enrichment
  (real-slop data + self-supervised template refinement) — not required for this first pass.

## Approach

**Segmentation — fixed-pitch, right-anchored grid.** Score is right-aligned and grows left, so anchor
the rightmost digit cell at a fixed x and step left by a constant pitch for up to `N=6` cells. GH3
HUD score digits are tabular (fixed advance) so a fixed pitch segments cleanly and ports to integer
firmware trivially (mirrors `gp_edge`). First implementation step **validates pitch constancy** on the
labelled frames (overlay cells); if the white font isn't tabular, fall back to gap-based column
segmentation — but tabular is expected.

**Per-digit glyph match.** For each cell, build a low-res normalized luma fingerprint (reuse the
`songselect._luma_grid` body + `fingerprint._region_bounds`) and nearest-template match (L1 argmin)
against an **11-class bank: digits 0–9 + `blank`** (leading empty cells). A small per-cell
`dx`/`dy` offset search re-aligns per frame (the song reader proved this recovers positional slop).
Assemble non-blank cells left→right into the integer value; `margin` = 2nd-best − best per digit.

**Templates built from the labelled corpus.** At catalog-build time: for each labelled frame, segment
its ROI, assign each cell the known digit from the filename value (right-justified; leading cells =
`blank`), and average per class → the 0–9 + blank `vec`s. No hand-cropping of individual glyphs.

**Font/mode selection.** Single font this pass, keyed explicitly (`mode="training"`). Structure a
per-mode `SCORE_ROI` + `ScoreConfig` so career adds a second ROI + template bank later; color
(green-dominant ROI) is the natural auto-discriminator when career lands.
```

```bash
    green=((G>110)&(G-R>25)&(G-B>25)).sum()
    return white,green
rows=[]
for fn in sorted(glob.glob(f"{snaps}/snapshot-*.png")):
    w,g=stats(fn)
    if w>25 or g>25:
        kind="WHITE" if w>g else "green"
        rows.append((os.path.basename(fn),w,g,kind))
print(f"{'file':22} {'white':>6} {'green':>6}  kind")
for fn,w,g,k in rows:
    print(f"{fn:22} {w:6d} {g:6d}  {k}")
print("\nWHITE candidates:", [fn for fn,w,g,k in rows if k=='WHITE'])
PY
```

```text
1	"""song_select reader: which song is in the highlight slot, and which setlist.
2	
3	`song_select` is fixed-slot — the selected song sits in a fixed highlight slot
4	while the list scrolls under it. We identify the song by **matching the selected
5	title line's low-resolution bitmap against the known per-song templates**
6	(closed-set nearest-match, the same idea as the screen classifier; deliberately
7	*not* char-level OCR — we have a reference image of every song). The ROI is
8	registered on the highlighted title glyphs (right of the album-art thumbnail);
9	see `metadata.SONG_SLOT_ROI`.
10	
11	Two wrinkles, both from the corpus:
12	- Each setlist's first song (Slow Ride on main, Avalancha on bonus) sits one row
13	  lower (the list can't scroll up past it), so its template comes from
14	  `SONG_FIRST_ROI`; every other song uses `SONG_SLOT_ROI`. At read time we
15	  fingerprint both ROIs and compare each template against the ROI it was built
16	  from.
17	- main vs bonus setlists overlap by position, so we first read which setlist tab
18	  is lit and match only within that catalog.
19	
20	The slot fingerprint is a low-res grayscale grid over the ROI (fine enough to
21	separate ~40 short titles by their ink pattern), normalized per frame to cancel
22	the analog gain/offset slop. Integer-friendly for the firmware port.
23	"""
24	
25	from __future__ import annotations
26	
27	from collections import defaultdict
28	from dataclasses import dataclass
29	
30	import numpy as np
31	
32	from .corpus import Sample
33	from .fingerprint import _to_canonical
34	from .metadata import (
35	    SETLIST_BG_ROI,
36	    SONG_FIRST_ROI,
37	    SONG_SLOT_ROI,
38	    song_from_filename,
39	)
40	
41	# Luma weights (B, G, R) /256.
42	_LUMA_W = np.array([29, 150, 77], dtype=np.float64)
43	
44	FIRST = "first"
45	SLOT = "slot"
46	
47	
48	@dataclass(frozen=True)
49	class SongConfig:
50	    cols: int = 32  # horizontal cells across the title (captures the ink pattern)
51	    rows: int = 6   # vertical cells down the title line
52	    # Small read-time offset search (px) that re-aligns the slot before matching —
53	    # this is what makes the fine grid tolerant of the analog path's positional
54	    # slop (without it, a few-px shift drops translate robustness to ~70%).
55	    dx_search: tuple[int, ...] = (-6, -3, 0, 3, 6)
56	    dy_search: tuple[int, ...] = (-6, -3, 0, 3, 6)
57	
58	
59	DEFAULT_SONG_CONFIG = SongConfig()
60	
61	
62	@dataclass(frozen=True)
63	class SongTemplate:
64	    setlist: str
65	    index: int
66	    song_id: str
67	    roi_kind: str  # SLOT or FIRST
68	    vec: np.ndarray
69	
70	
71	@dataclass(frozen=True)
72	class SongCatalog:
73	    templates: list[SongTemplate]
74	    config: SongConfig
75	    setlist_warmth_threshold: float  # bg (R-B) above this => main (yellow), else bonus
76	
77	
78	@dataclass(frozen=True)
79	class SongResult:
80	    setlist: str
81	    index: int
82	    song_id: str
83	    dist: float
84	    margin: float  # 2nd-best dist - best dist (higher = more confident)
85	
86	
87	def _luma_grid(image: np.ndarray, roi: tuple[int, int, int, int], cfg: SongConfig) -> np.ndarray:
88	    """Per-frame-normalized low-res luma grid over an ROI -> length cols*rows."""
89	    img = _to_canonical(image)
90	    x0, y0, x1, y1 = roi
91	    patch = img[y0:y1, x0:x1].astype(np.float64)
92	    luma = patch @ _LUMA_W / 256.0  # (h, w)
93	    ys = np.linspace(0, luma.shape[0], cfg.rows + 1).round().astype(int)
94	    xs = np.linspace(0, luma.shape[1], cfg.cols + 1).round().astype(int)
95	    cells = np.empty((cfg.rows, cfg.cols), dtype=np.float64)
96	    for r in range(cfg.rows):
97	        for c in range(cfg.cols):
98	            cells[r, c] = luma[ys[r]:ys[r + 1], xs[c]:xs[c + 1]].mean()
99	    v = cells.reshape(-1)
100	    v -= v.mean()
101	    s = v.std()
102	    return v / s if s > 1e-6 else v
103	
104	
105	def _bg_warmth(image: np.ndarray) -> float:
106	    """Warmth (R - B) of the page background — median over the BG ROI is robust to
107	    the song text painted over it. High = yellow (main), low = white (bonus)."""
108	    img = _to_canonical(image)
109	    x0, y0, x1, y1 = SETLIST_BG_ROI
110	    patch = img[y0:y1, x0:x1].reshape(-1, 3).astype(np.float64)
111	    med = np.median(patch, axis=0)  # (B, G, R)
112	    return float(med[2] - med[0])
113	
114	
115	def build_song_catalog(samples: list[Sample], config: SongConfig = DEFAULT_SONG_CONFIG) -> SongCatalog:
116	    templates: list[SongTemplate] = []
117	    warmth: dict[str, list[float]] = defaultdict(list)
118	    for s in samples:
119	        if s.screen_id != "song_select":
120	            continue
121	        parsed = song_from_filename(s.path.name)
122	        if parsed is None:
123	            continue
124	        setlist, index, song_id = parsed
125	        roi_kind = FIRST if index == 0 else SLOT
126	        roi = SONG_FIRST_ROI if roi_kind == FIRST else SONG_SLOT_ROI
127	        templates.append(
128	            SongTemplate(setlist, index, song_id, roi_kind, _luma_grid(s.image, roi, config))
129	        )
130	        warmth[setlist].append(_bg_warmth(s.image))
131	    # Threshold midway between the two setlists' mean background warmth.
132	    main_w = np.mean(warmth["main"]) if warmth["main"] else 0.0
133	    bonus_w = np.mean(warmth["bonus"]) if warmth["bonus"] else 0.0
134	    threshold = float((main_w + bonus_w) / 2.0)
135	    return SongCatalog(templates=templates, config=config, setlist_warmth_threshold=threshold)
136	
137	
138	def read_setlist(image: np.ndarray, catalog: SongCatalog) -> str:
139	    """Which setlist is active ("main"/"bonus"), from the page background colour."""
140	    return "main" if _bg_warmth(image) >= catalog.setlist_warmth_threshold else "bonus"
141	
142	
143	def _shift(roi: tuple[int, int, int, int], dx: int, dy: int) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
144	    x0, y0, x1, y1 = roi
145	    return (x0 + dx, y0 + dy, x1 + dx, y1 + dy)
146	
147	
148	def read_song(image: np.ndarray, catalog: SongCatalog, setlist: str | None = None) -> SongResult:
149	    """Identify the selected song by nearest-template match.
150	
151	    Matches across the whole catalog (both setlists) by default — main/bonus
152	    bitmaps are distinct, so the setlist falls out of the winning song and we
153	    don't depend on the (less reliable) tab read. Pass `setlist` to restrict.
154	
155	    A small offset search per candidate ROI re-aligns the slot before scoring, so
156	    the fine grid tolerates the analog path's positional slop.
157	    """
158	    cfg = catalog.config
159	    cand = [t for t in catalog.templates if setlist is None or t.setlist == setlist]
160	
161	    # One fingerprint per (roi_kind, offset), reused across all templates.
162	    fps: dict[tuple[str, int, int], np.ndarray] = {}
163	    for dx in cfg.dx_search:
164	        for dy in cfg.dy_search:
165	            fps[(SLOT, dx, dy)] = _luma_grid(image, _shift(SONG_SLOT_ROI, dx, dy), cfg)
166	            fps[(FIRST, dx, dy)] = _luma_grid(image, _shift(SONG_FIRST_ROI, dx, dy), cfg)
167	
168	    def best_dist(t: SongTemplate) -> float:
169	        return min(
170	            float(np.abs(fps[(t.roi_kind, dx, dy)] - t.vec).sum())
171	            for dx in cfg.dx_search
172	            for dy in cfg.dy_search
173	        )
174	
175	    scored = sorted(((best_dist(t), t) for t in cand), key=lambda kv: kv[0])
176	    best_d, best = scored[0]
177	    second_d = scored[1][0] if len(scored) > 1 else best_d
178	    return SongResult(
179	        setlist=best.setlist, index=best.index, song_id=best.song_id,
180	        dist=best_d, margin=second_d - best_d,
181	    )
182
```

```text
1	"""Load the labelled GH3 screen corpus.
2	
3	The corpus is the renamed snapshot set at `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/`
4	(720x480 PNGs). Each image's screen-class label comes from its filename via
5	`screens.screen_id_for_filename`. Images are returned as uint8 HxWx3 arrays in
6	**BGR** order, matching marvin's native framebuffer layout (capture is BGR888
7	packed; see marvin journal 2026-05-02).
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import os
13	from dataclasses import dataclass
14	from pathlib import Path
15	
16	import numpy as np
17	from PIL import Image
18	
19	from .screens import screen_id_for_filename
20	
21	# tools/gameplay/gameplay/corpus.py -> repo root is parents[3].
22	_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
23	_DEFAULT_CORPUS_DIR = _REPO_ROOT / "firmware" / "marvin" / "docs" / "gh3_screens"
24	
25	
26	def corpus_dir() -> Path:
27	    """Resolve the corpus directory (overridable via $GAMEPLAY_CORPUS_DIR)."""
28	    env = os.environ.get("GAMEPLAY_CORPUS_DIR")
29	    return Path(env) if env else _DEFAULT_CORPUS_DIR
30	
31	
32	@dataclass(frozen=True)
33	class Sample:
34	    screen_id: str
35	    path: Path
36	    image: np.ndarray  # uint8, HxWx3, BGR
37	
38	
39	def load_bgr(path: str | Path) -> np.ndarray:
40	    """Load an image file as a uint8 HxWx3 BGR array."""
41	    with Image.open(path) as im:
42	        rgb = np.asarray(im.convert("RGB"), dtype=np.uint8)
43	    return rgb[:, :, ::-1].copy()  # RGB -> BGR
44	
45	
46	def load_corpus(directory: str | Path | None = None) -> list[Sample]:
47	    """Load every `*.png` in the corpus directory as labelled `Sample`s.
48	
49	    Sorted by filename for determinism. Raises FileNotFoundError if the
50	    directory is empty or missing.
51	    """
52	    d = Path(directory) if directory is not None else corpus_dir()
53	    files = sorted(d.glob("*.png"))
54	    if not files:
55	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no PNGs found in corpus dir {d}")
56	    return [
57	        Sample(screen_id=screen_id_for_filename(f.name), path=f, image=load_bgr(f))
58	        for f in files
59	    ]
```

```text
94	def selected_item_from_filename(filename: str) -> str | None:
95	    """The selected item id encoded in a corpus filename, or None.
96	
97	    `main_menu__co_op_career.png` -> `co_op_career`. Returns None for filenames
98	    with no `__selection` suffix (single-shot screens) or screens not modelled here.
99	    """
100	    stem = filename.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]

108	# ─── song_select (fixed-slot) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
109	#
110	# The selected song sits in a fixed highlight slot while the list scrolls under
111	# it, with one exception per setlist: the *first* song (Slow Ride on main,
112	# Avalancha on bonus) sits one row lower, because the list can't scroll up past
113	# the top. So 38/39 main + 24/25 bonus use SONG_SLOT_ROI; each setlist's song 0
114	# uses SONG_FIRST_ROI. Both ROIs cover the highlighted *title* line only (the
115	# selected title glyphs, right of the album-art thumbnail), which we match
116	# (bitmap, not OCR) against the per-song templates.
117	#
118	# ROIs in canonical 720x480 space, registered on the selected title: normal songs
119	# render the title at y≈246, the first song ~45 px lower at y≈291 (measured across
120	# the corpus). x0 starts right of the album art so only text is sampled. See
121	# docs/journal.md.
122	SONG_SLOT_ROI = (183, 233, 385, 266)
123	SONG_FIRST_ROI = (183, 282, 385, 315)
124	
125	# Which setlist is active is read from the *page background colour*, not the tabs:
126	# the "setlist"/"bonus" tabs are only on screen when the first song is selected
127	# (they scroll off for song 2+), but the page colour is always visible — the main
128	# setlist's parchment is yellow, the bonus page is whiter. A large background ROI
129	# (median is robust to the song text over it); warmth = R - B separates them
130	# (offset-invariant, gain-preserving, so it survives the analog slop).
131	SETLIST_BG_ROI = (60, 60, 330, 300)

133	
134	def song_from_filename(filename: str) -> tuple[str, int, str] | None:
135	    """Parse a song_select corpus filename into (setlist, index, song_id).
136	
137	    `song_select__04_rock_and_roll_all_nite.png` -> ("main", 4, "rock_and_roll_all_nite")
138	    `song_select__bonus_07_generation_rock.png`  -> ("bonus", 7, "generation_rock")
139	    Returns None for non-song_select filenames.
140	    """
141	    sel = selected_item_from_filename(filename)
142	    if sel is None:
143	        return None
144	    setlist = "main"
145	    if sel.startswith("bonus_"):
146	        setlist = "bonus"
147	        sel = sel[len("bonus_") :]
148	    head, _, song_id = sel.partition("_")
149	    if not head.isdigit() or not song_id:
150	        return None
151	    return setlist, int(head), song_id
```

```text
371	def song_eval(samples: list[Sample], seed: int = 1234) -> SongEvalResult:
372	    catalog = build_song_catalog(samples)
373	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
374	    n = song_ok = setlist_ok = setlist_slop_ok = 0
375	    slop_ok = slop_total = 0
```

```python
"""In-song score reader: per-digit glyph OCR of the open-ended score value.

Unlike the menu/song readers (closed-set template matches), the score is an
open-ended number, so it is read digit by digit. The score is right-aligned in a
fixed HUD box and grows leftward; GH3 renders tabular (fixed-advance) digits, so
the score ROI (`metadata.SCORE_ROI[mode]`) splits into `N_SCORE_DIGITS` equal
cells anchored at the right edge. Each cell is fingerprinted (low-res normalized
luma grid, the same idea as the song reader) and matched against a per-mode bank
of digit templates 0-9 plus a `BLANK` class for the unused leading cells. A small
whole-field offset search re-aligns the ROI before matching, so the fine cell
grid tolerates the analog path's positional slop (as it does for the song
reader). Non-blank cells, left to right, assemble the integer value.

Templates are built from the labelled score corpus: each frame's known value is
right-justified across the cells, giving every cell a digit (or blank) label, and
the per-class mean fingerprint is the template — no hand-cropping of glyphs.

Integer-friendly for the firmware port: fixed cells + argmin L1 over uint8-scale
vectors, exactly like `gp_read_song`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

from .corpus import Sample
from .metadata import N_SCORE_DIGITS, SCORE_ROI, score_from_filename
from .songselect import _luma_grid, _shift

BLANK = 10  # class label for an unused (empty) leading cell


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ScoreConfig:
    n_digits: int = N_SCORE_DIGITS
    cols: int = 6   # per-cell grid columns (captures the digit's ink pattern)
    rows: int = 12  # per-cell grid rows
    # Small whole-field offset search (px) that re-aligns the score box before
    # matching. Range is tight: the field is rigid (right edge is rock-steady in
    # the corpus) and the digit pitch is ~10 px, so a few px covers the slop
    # without letting a cell drift onto its neighbour.
    dx_search: tuple[int, ...] = (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2)
    dy_search: tuple[int, ...] = (-2, 0, 2)


DEFAULT_SCORE_CONFIG = ScoreConfig()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DigitTemplate:
    digit: int  # 0-9, or BLANK
    vec: np.ndarray


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ScoreCatalog:
    mode: str
    templates: list[DigitTemplate]  # one per class present (per-class mean)
    config: ScoreConfig


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ScoreResult:
    value: int
    digits: tuple[int, ...]  # per-cell class, left->right (BLANK for empty leading cells)
    dist: float              # worst (max) per-cell best-distance
    margin: float            # weakest (min) per-cell 2nd-best - best


def _cell_rois(roi: tuple[int, int, int, int], n: int) -> list[tuple[int, int, int, int]]:
    """Split a score ROI into `n` equal-width digit cells (left->right)."""
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = roi
    xs = np.linspace(x0, x1, n + 1).round().astype(int)
    return [(int(xs[i]), y0, int(xs[i + 1]), y1) for i in range(n)]


def _labels_for_value(value: int, n_digits: int) -> list[int]:
    """Right-justify `value` across `n_digits` cells -> per-cell class labels.

    Leading (unused) cells are BLANK; e.g. 1138 over 6 cells ->
    [BLANK, BLANK, 1, 1, 3, 8]. Scores never carry leading zeros.
    """
    s = str(value)
    pad = n_digits - len(s)
    return [BLANK] * pad + [int(c) for c in s]


def build_score_catalog(
    samples: list[Sample],
    mode: str = "training",
    config: ScoreConfig = DEFAULT_SCORE_CONFIG,
) -> ScoreCatalog:
    """Build per-mode digit templates (0-9 + BLANK) from labelled score frames.

    Each frame's value is right-justified over the cells to label every cell, and
    the per-class mean cell-fingerprint becomes that class's template.
    """
    roi = SCORE_ROI[mode]
    cells = _cell_rois(roi, config.n_digits)
    acc: dict[int, list[np.ndarray]] = defaultdict(list)
    for s in samples:
        parsed = score_from_filename(s.path.name)
        if parsed is None or parsed[0] != mode:
            continue
        _mode, value = parsed
        labels = _labels_for_value(value, config.n_digits)
        for cell, label in zip(cells, labels):
            acc[label].append(_luma_grid(s.image, cell, config))
    templates = [
        DigitTemplate(digit=cls, vec=np.mean(np.stack(vecs), axis=0))
        for cls, vecs in sorted(acc.items())
    ]
    return ScoreCatalog(mode=mode, templates=templates, config=config)


def read_score(image: np.ndarray, catalog: ScoreCatalog) -> ScoreResult:
    """Read the score by per-cell nearest-template match with a whole-field offset search.

    For each field offset, classify every cell (argmin L1 to the digit/blank
    templates) and sum the per-cell best distances; the offset with the smallest
    total wins, and its per-cell classes assemble the value.
    """
    cfg = catalog.config
    base = SCORE_ROI[catalog.mode]
    by_class = {t.digit: t.vec for t in catalog.templates}
    classes = sorted(by_class)

    def classify_cell(cell: tuple[int, int, int, int]) -> tuple[int, float, float]:
        fp = _luma_grid(image, cell, cfg)
        scored = sorted((float(np.abs(fp - by_class[c]).sum()), c) for c in classes)
        best_d, best_c = scored[0]
        second_d = scored[1][0] if len(scored) > 1 else best_d
        return best_c, best_d, second_d - best_d

    def field_at(dx: int, dy: int) -> tuple[float, list[tuple[int, float, float]]]:
        cells = _cell_rois(_shift(base, dx, dy), cfg.n_digits)
        per_cell = [classify_cell(c) for c in cells]
        return sum(d for _c, d, _m in per_cell), per_cell

    _total, per_cell = min(
        (field_at(dx, dy) for dx in cfg.dx_search for dy in cfg.dy_search),
        key=lambda t: t[0],
    )
    digits = tuple(c for c, _d, _m in per_cell)
    text = "".join(str(c) for c in digits if c != BLANK)
    value = int(text) if text else 0
    return ScoreResult(
        value=value,
        digits=digits,
        dist=max(d for _c, d, _m in per_cell),
        margin=min(m for _c, _d, m in per_cell),
    )

```

```bash
export UV_CACHE_DIR=$TMPDIR/uv-cache && uv run python 2>/dev/null - <<'PY'
import numpy as np
from collections import defaultdict
from gameplay.corpus import load_score_corpus
from gameplay.songselect import _luma_grid, _shift
from gameplay.score import ScoreConfig, _cell_rois, _labels_for_value, BLANK
from gameplay.metadata import score_from_filename, SCORE_ROI
samples=load_score_corpus()
ROI=SCORE_ROI["training"]

def build_exemplars(train, cfg):
    cells=_cell_rois(ROI,cfg.n_digits)
    acc=defaultdict(list)
    for s in train:
        val=score_from_filename(s.path.name)[1]
        for cell,lab in zip(cells,_labels_for_value(val,cfg.n_digits)):
            acc[lab].append(_luma_grid(s.image,cell,cfg))
    return acc

def read(image, acc, cfg, per_cell_offset, nn):
    classes=sorted(acc)
    # per class: either centroid or list of exemplars
    if nn:
        bank={c:np.stack(acc[c]) for c in classes}
    else:
        bank={c:np.mean(np.stack(acc[c]),0)[None] for c in classes}
    def cell_scores(cell):
        fp=_luma_grid(image,cell,cfg)
        out=[]
        for c in classes:
            d=np.abs(bank[c]-fp).sum(1).min()
            out.append((float(d),c))
        out.sort()
        return out
    if per_cell_offset:
        digits=[]
        for i in range(cfg.n_digits):
            best=None
            for dx in cfg.dx_search:
                for dy in cfg.dy_search:
                    cell=_cell_rois(_shift(ROI,dx,dy),cfg.n_digits)[i]
                    sc=cell_scores(cell)
                    if best is None or sc[0][0]<best[0][0]: best=sc
            digits.append(best[0][1])
    else:
        bestfield=None
        for dx in cfg.dx_search:
            for dy in cfg.dy_search:
                cells=_cell_rois(_shift(ROI,dx,dy),cfg.n_digits)
                scs=[cell_scores(c) for c in cells]
                tot=sum(s[0][0] for s in scs)
                if bestfield is None or tot<bestfield[0]: bestfield=(tot,scs)
        digits=[s[0][1] for s in bestfield[1]]
    text="".join(str(d) for d in digits if d!=BLANK)
    return int(text) if text else 0, tuple(digits)

def loo(cfg,pco,nn):
    ex=0;dc=0;dt=0
    for s in samples:
        val=score_from_filename(s.path.name)[1]
        others=[o for o in samples if o.path.name!=s.path.name]
        acc=build_exemplars(others,cfg)
        v,digs=read(s.image,acc,cfg,pco,nn)
        ex+=v==val
        truth=tuple(_labels_for_value(val,6))
        dc+=sum(1 for a,b in zip(digs,truth) if a==b);dt+=6
    return ex,dc,dt

cfg=ScoreConfig(cols=8,rows=14,dx_search=(-2,-1,0,1,2),dy_search=(-2,-1,0,1,2))
for pco in (False,True):
    for nn in (False,True):
        ex,dc,dt=loo(cfg,pco,nn)
        print(f"per_cell_offset={pco!s:5} nn={nn!s:5}  LOO {ex}/9  per-cell {dc}/{dt}")
PY
```

```bash
import numpy as np
from collections import defaultdict
from gameplay.corpus import load_score_corpus
from gameplay.songselect import _luma_grid, _shift
from gameplay.score import ScoreConfig, _cell_rois, _labels_for_value, BLANK, build_score_catalog
from gameplay.metadata import score_from_filename, SCORE_ROI
from gameplay import perturb
samples=load_score_corpus()
ROI=SCORE_ROI["training"]

def read(image, by_class, cfg, coarse, fine):
    classes=sorted(by_class)
    def cell_best(cell):
        fp=_luma_grid(image,cell,cfg)
        return min((float(np.abs(by_class[c]-fp).sum()),c) for c in classes)
    # stage 1: global coarse offset
    bestg=None
    for gx in coarse:
        for gy in coarse:
            cells=_cell_rois(_shift(ROI,gx,gy),cfg.n_digits)
            tot=sum(cell_best(c)[0] for c in cells)
            if bestg is None or tot<bestg[0]: bestg=(tot,gx,gy)
    _,gx,gy=bestg
    # stage 2: per-cell fine
    digits=[]
    for i in range(cfg.n_digits):
        best=None
        for dx in fine:
            for dy in fine:
                cell=_cell_rois(_shift(ROI,gx+dx,gy+dy),cfg.n_digits)[i]
                d,c=cell_best(cell)
                if best is None or d<best[0]: best=(d,c)
        digits.append(best[1])
    text="".join(str(d) for d in digits if d!=BLANK)
    return int(text) if text else 0

def evalcfg(cfg, coarse, fine, label):
    # LOO clean
    ex=0
    for s in samples:
        val=score_from_filename(s.path.name)[1]
        cat=build_score_catalog([o for o in samples if o.path.name!=s.path.name],config=cfg)
        by={t.digit:t.vec for t in cat.templates}
        ex+=read(s.image,by,cfg,coarse,fine)==val
    # slop (train-on-all)
    cat=build_score_catalog(samples,config=cfg); by={t.digit:t.vec for t in cat.templates}
    rng=np.random.default_rng(1234)
    cok=defaultdict(lambda:[0,0]); tot=0; ok=0
    for s in samples:
        val=score_from_filename(s.path.name)[1]
        for c,name,pimg in perturb.envelope(s.image,rng):
            r=read(pimg,by,cfg,coarse,fine)==val
            cok[c][0]+=r;cok[c][1]+=1;ok+=r;tot+=1
    cats=" ".join(f"{k}={cok[k][0]}/{cok[k][1]}" for k in sorted(cok))
    print(f"{label:40} LOO {ex}/9  slop {ok}/{tot} ({ok/tot:.0%})  [{cats}]")

cfg=ScoreConfig(cols=8,rows=14)
evalcfg(cfg, coarse=range(-8,9,2), fine=(-1,0,1), label="2stage coarse±8/2 fine±1")
evalcfg(cfg, coarse=range(-8,9,1), fine=(-1,0,1), label="2stage coarse±8/1 fine±1")
evalcfg(cfg, coarse=(0,), fine=range(-7,8,1), label="per-cell only ±7/1 (neighbor risk)")
```

That's the right call — and it simplifies both the algorithm and the firmware cost. You're correct that the translate/scale I was testing models *per-rig* calibration variance, not moment-to-moment jitter. On a fixed rig the field sits at the same pixels every frame, so searching every frame is wasted work.

Here's the design I'd switch to:

**Register once → cheap per-frame read**
- **Registration (once):** a wide search locks the field's true position for this rig — ideally per-cell (6 small offsets), since I found the only thing separating the clean 9/9 read from a ~6/9 read was small *per-digit* sub-pixel placement, which is itself fixed on a given rig. Store the 6 locked cell rects.
- **Per-frame read (continual):** sample those 6 fixed cells, argmin-classify each against the 0–9+blank templates. No search — a handful of rect-means + an L1 over 11 tiny templates. Microseconds, trivial to port.
- **What this reframes:** the ±2 px continual search goes away. The earlier translate/scale "failures" were an artifact of expecting a fixed tiny search to chase a moving field; under register-once we lock to each rig's actual position, so translate/scale become *registration targets*, not per-frame problems. Clean per-frame accuracy stays 9/9.

The one decision that shapes the firmware: **how registration is sourced on the real system.**

```bash
import numpy as np
from collections import defaultdict
from gameplay.corpus import load_score_corpus
from gameplay.songselect import _luma_grid
from gameplay.score import build_score_catalog, calibrate_score, _labels_for_value, BLANK, DEFAULT_SCORE_CONFIG
from gameplay.metadata import score_from_filename
from gameplay import perturb
samples=load_score_corpus()
truth={s.path.name:score_from_filename(s.path.name)[1] for s in samples}
cfg=DEFAULT_SCORE_CONFIG

def bank_nn(train):
    from gameplay.metadata import SCORE_ROI
    from gameplay.score import _cell_rois
    cells=_cell_rois(SCORE_ROI["training"],cfg.n_digits)
    acc=defaultdict(list)
    for s in train:
        val=truth[s.path.name]
        for cell,lab in zip(cells,_labels_for_value(val,cfg.n_digits)):
            acc[lab].append(_luma_grid(s.image,cell,cfg))
    return {c:np.stack(v) for c,v in acc.items()}

def read_nn(image,bank,calib):
    classes=sorted(bank); digs=[]
    ms=[]
    for cell in calib.cells:
        fp=_luma_grid(image,cell,cfg)
        scored=sorted((float(np.abs(bank[c]-fp).sum(1).min()),c) for c in classes)
        digs.append(scored[0][1]); ms.append(scored[1][0]-scored[0][0])
    text="".join(str(d) for d in digs if d!=BLANK)
    return (int(text) if text else 0), min(ms)

cat=build_score_catalog(samples)
calib=calibrate_score([s.image for s in samples],cat)

bank=bank_nn(samples)
clean=sum(read_nn(s.image,bank,calib)[0]==truth[s.path.name] for s in samples)
print(f"NN clean (locked): {clean}/9")
ex=0
for s in samples:
    b=bank_nn([o for o in samples if o.path.name!=s.path.name])
    ex+=read_nn(s.image,b,calib)[0]==truth[s.path.name]
print(f"NN LOO (locked geometry): {ex}/9")
rng=np.random.default_rng(1234)
cok=defaultdict(lambda:[0,0])
for s in samples:
    for cate,name,pimg in perturb.envelope(s.image,rng):
        if cate in("gain","offset","noise"):
            ok=read_nn(pimg,bank,calib)[0]==truth[s.path.name]
            cok[cate][0]+=ok;cok[cate][1]+=1
print("NN A2D:", {k:f"{cok[k][0]}/{cok[k][1]}" for k in sorted(cok)})
PY
```

```text
167	    p_nav.set_defaults(func=cmd_navigate)
```

```text
from __future__ import annotations

from gameplay.evaluate import song_eval
from gameplay.metadata import song_from_filename
from gameplay.songselect import build_song_catalog, read_song


def test_song_from_filename():
    assert song_from_filename("song_select__04_rock_and_roll_all_nite.png") == ("main", 4, "rock_and_roll_all_nite")
    assert song_from_filename("song_select__bonus_07_generation_rock.png") == ("bonus", 7, "generation_rock")
    assert song_from_filename("song_select__00_slow_ride.png") == ("main", 0, "slow_ride")
    assert song_from_filename("main_menu__career.png") is None


def test_catalog_has_all_64(corpus):
    cat = build_song_catalog(corpus)
    assert len(cat.templates) == 64
    assert sum(t.setlist == "main" for t in cat.templates) == 39
    assert sum(t.setlist == "bonus" for t in cat.templates) == 25


def test_song_match_clean_and_slop(corpus):
    res = song_eval(corpus)
    assert res.n_total == 64
    assert res.song_acc == 1.0, res.failures  # every song identified (match-all)
    assert res.margin_min > 0
    assert res.slop_acc >= 0.95, res.slop_acc


def test_first_song_uses_lower_roi(corpus):
    # Slow Ride / Avalancha are the per-setlist first songs (lower slot).
    cat = build_song_catalog(corpus)
    firsts = {(t.setlist, t.song_id): t.roi_kind for t in cat.templates if t.index == 0}
    assert firsts[("main", "slow_ride")] == "first"
    assert firsts[("bonus", "avalancha")] == "first"


def test_match_all_yields_correct_setlist(corpus):
    # Without being told the setlist, the match places each song in the right list.
    cat = build_song_catalog(corpus)
    for s in corpus:
        parsed = song_from_filename(s.path.name)
        if parsed is None:
            continue
        setlist, _i, song_id = parsed
        r = read_song(s.image, cat)
        assert (r.setlist, r.song_id) == (setlist, song_id), s.path.name
```

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from gameplay.evaluate import score_eval
from gameplay.metadata import N_SCORE_DIGITS, score_from_filename
from gameplay.score import (
    BLANK,
    _labels_for_value,
    build_score_catalog,
    calibrate_score,
    read_score,
)


def test_score_from_filename():
    assert score_from_filename("score__training__010584__snap0121.png") == ("training", 10584)
    assert score_from_filename("score__training__001138__snap0097.png") == ("training", 1138)
    assert score_from_filename("song_select__04_rock_and_roll_all_nite.png") is None
    assert score_from_filename("in_song__training.png") is None


def test_labels_right_justify():
    assert _labels_for_value(1138, 6) == [BLANK, BLANK, 1, 1, 3, 8]
    assert _labels_for_value(17728, 6) == [BLANK, 1, 7, 7, 2, 8]
    # A full-width value fills every cell.
    assert _labels_for_value(123456, 6) == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]


def test_corpus_covers_all_digits(score_corpus):
    # The handful of frames must expose every glyph 0-9 to build templates.
    cat = build_score_catalog(score_corpus)
    digits = {t.digit for t in cat.templates}
    assert set(range(10)) <= digits
    assert BLANK in digits  # leading cells of the shorter scores


def test_read_score_clean_exact(score_corpus):
    # Register once on the session, then every frame reads exactly (search-free).
    cat = build_score_catalog(score_corpus)
    calib = calibrate_score([s.image for s in score_corpus], cat)
    for s in score_corpus:
        value = score_from_filename(s.path.name)[1]
        r = read_score(s.image, cat, calib)
        assert r.value == value, (s.path.name, r.digits)
        assert len(r.digits) == N_SCORE_DIGITS


def test_score_eval_clean_and_slop(score_corpus):
    res = score_eval(score_corpus)
    assert res.n_total == len(score_corpus)
    assert res.exact_acc == 1.0, res.failures       # clean exact match on the handful
    assert res.digit_acc == 1.0                      # every cell classified correctly
    assert res.a2d_acc == 1.0                        # gain/offset/noise cancelled per-frame
    assert res.reg_acc == 1.0                        # auto-registration recovers position shifts
    assert res.margin_min > 0
```

Phase 5 (score reader, training white font) is built and green. Summary:

## What landed (host-side prototype, `tools/gameplay/`)
- **`gameplay/score.py`** — the reader. Fixed-pitch, right-anchored 6-cell segmentation → per-digit **1-NN glyph match** against 0–9 + blank. Split into **register-once** (`calibrate_score`, two-stage: wide whole-field search then small per-cell refine) + **search-free per-frame read** (`read_score`).
- **`gameplay/metadata.py`** — `SCORE_ROI["training"]=(139,315,199,333)`, `N_SCORE_DIGITS=6`, `score_from_filename`.
- **`gameplay/corpus.py`** — `load_score_corpus()`.
- **`gameplay/evaluate.py`** — `score_eval` (clean exact + per-digit + LOO + A2D-slop + re-registration), wired into `run_report`.
- **`gameplay/cli.py`** — `in_song` branch in `classify`; new `read-score` debug verb.
- **`data/scores/`** — 9 hand-labelled training-white frames (all 10 glyphs covered).
- **`tests/test_score.py`** — 5 new tests; full suite **56 passed**.

## Results (~9-frame corpus)
- **Clean 9/9 exact, 54/54 per-digit**
- **A2D slop (gain/offset/noise) 100%** — cancelled by per-frame normalization
- **Position re-registration 100%** on every shift
- **LOO 6/9** — the small-corpus ceiling (a held-out digit sometimes has one lookalike exemplar left), not an algorithm limit

## Key design decisions (recorded in the journal)
Your steers shaped it: **register-once** (position stable per rig) → cheap continual read; **no scale concern**, just position + A2D; the whole-field-first registration is what stops a cell aliasing onto its neighbor; 1-NN over exemplars because averaging blurred 8/3/0.

Two things worth your input before I go further:
- **Spot-check the labels** — the 9 ground-truth scores I read: 1138, 3938, 5327, 17728, 9056, 9906, 10584, 11437, 12236. Flag any misread.
- **Next step?** Options are (a) the **career green** font, (b) the **marvin-perf score-crop capture** to enrich templates / lift LOO, or (c) the **firmware port** (`gp_read_score`). No rush — and I haven't committed anything (per repo rule, that's on your say-so).

```text
=== README ===
# marvin-perf

Host-side decoder and analyzer for the marvin firmware **perf-log** wire format.

The firmware emits framed binary records (schema version 5) over its USB-device
CDC ACM port. This tool consumes that stream live, records it to disk, and
replays captures offline. Summary analyses (latency attribution, drop
accounting, stack high-water trends) are produced by the `serve` viewer, not a
standalone CLI verb.

Wire format source-of-truth lives in the firmware tree at
[`firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h`](../../firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h).
The Python schema mirror in [`marvin_perf/records.py`](marvin_perf/records.py)
must match it byte-for-byte; bump `EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` (Python side) and
`PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` (firmware side) together.

## Setup

All Python work runs through [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). First-time
bootstrap:

    cd tools/marvin-perf
    uv sync --group viewer   # include viewer deps for the serve command

`uv sync` creates `.venv/` and writes `uv.lock`. Subsequent invocations use the
existing venv automatically. Omit `--group viewer` if you only need the headless
CLI helpers (record, set-mask, set-overlay, snapshot, export-ml).

## Usage

    # Launch the visual review server (default when no subcommand is given)
    uv run marvin-perf
    uv run marvin-perf serve
    uv run marvin-perf serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765
    uv run marvin-perf serve --capture session.bin   # pre-load a capture on startup

    # Capture raw bytes from the marvin USB-device CDC port
    uv run marvin-perf record --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --out session.bin
    uv run marvin-perf record --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --out-dir session/   # perf.bin + manifest.json

    # Push a type-mask to a running device without attaching for capture
    uv run marvin-perf set-mask --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --types ALL

    # Toggle the per-fret target rings on the SENSING strip
    uv run marvin-perf set-overlay --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --on

    # Capture one full video frame from a running device and save it
    uv run marvin-perf snapshot --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --out snapshots/

    # Export a capture as a SensiML-format CSV for MPLAB ML training
    uv run marvin-perf export-ml session/ --out session.csv --labels actuator-fb

## Tests

    uv run pytest

Fixtures under [`tests/fixtures/`](tests/fixtures/) are hand-built byte streams
covering one frame per record type plus framing edge cases (FCS mismatch,
truncated payload, mid-stream join needing SOF resync).
```
