```text
1	"""Reassemble PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT band strips into a full frame and save it.
2	
3	The device answers a snapshot command with a top-to-bottom run of full-width
4	`STRIP` records (kind SNAPSHOT), all sharing one `frame_epoch`; the final band
5	sets `STRIP_FLAG_LAST`. This module groups bands by `frame_epoch`, pastes them
6	onto a canvas, and writes the result as a lossless `.png` (frame_epoch in a
7	tEXt chunk).
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
13	from pathlib import Path
14	
15	from .records import STRIP_BPP, Strip, StripKind
16	
17	
18	@dataclass(frozen=True)
19	class CompletedSnapshot:
20	    width: int
21	    height: int
22	    frame_epoch: int
23	    bgr: bytes  # width * height * 3, row-major, top-to-bottom
24	
25	    @property
26	    def n_bytes(self) -> int:
27	        return self.width * self.height * STRIP_BPP
28	
29	
30	class SnapshotError(Exception):
31	    pass
32	
33	
34	@dataclass
35	class _Pending:
36	    width: int
37	    bands: dict[int, Strip] = field(default_factory=dict)  # keyed by band y
38	    last_y: int | None = None  # y of the band flagged LAST
39	
40	
41	class SnapshotAssembler:
42	    """Feed decoded `Strip` records; get a `CompletedSnapshot` when done.
43	
44	    `add()` ignores non-SNAPSHOT strips and returns None until a snapshot's
45	    LAST band has arrived and every row from 0..height is covered, at which
46	    point it returns the assembled frame (and forgets that frame_epoch).
47	    """
48	
49	    def __init__(self) -> None:
50	        self._pending: dict[int, _Pending] = {}
51	
52	    def add(self, strip: Strip) -> CompletedSnapshot | None:
53	        if strip.kind != int(StripKind.SNAPSHOT):
54	            return None
55	        if strip.x != 0:
56	            raise SnapshotError(f"snapshot band at x={strip.x}, expected full-width")
57	
58	        epoch = strip.hdr.frame_epoch
59	        p = self._pending.get(epoch)
60	        if p is None:
61	            p = _Pending(width=strip.w)
62	            self._pending[epoch] = p
63	        elif strip.w != p.width:
64	            raise SnapshotError(
65	                f"snapshot band width {strip.w} != {p.width} (frame_epoch {epoch})"
66	            )
67	
68	        p.bands[strip.y] = strip
69	        if strip.is_last:
70	            p.last_y = strip.y
71	
72	        if p.last_y is None:
73	            return None
74	        return self._try_finalize(epoch, p)
75	
76	    def _try_finalize(self, epoch: int, p: _Pending) -> CompletedSnapshot | None:
77	        # Walk contiguous bands from y=0; bail (keep waiting) on any gap.
78	        canvas = bytearray()
79	        y = 0
80	        height = 0
81	        while y in p.bands:
82	            band = p.bands[y]
83	            canvas += band.bgr
84	            height = y + band.h
85	            y += band.h
86	        if p.last_y is None or height <= p.last_y:
87	            return None  # not yet contiguous through the LAST band
88	
89	        del self._pending[epoch]
90	        return CompletedSnapshot(
91	            width=p.width, height=height, frame_epoch=epoch, bgr=bytes(canvas)
92	        )
93	
94	
95	def save_snapshot(snap: CompletedSnapshot, out: str | Path) -> list[Path]:
96	    """Write the snapshot as a lossless PNG and return its path.
97	
98	    `out` may carry a .png suffix (or a stale .bgr/.json, stripped) or be a bare
99	    stem; the result is always `<stem>.png`. PNG is lossless for the packed RGB
100	    pixels, so no separate raw buffer is needed; `frame_epoch` rides along in a
101	    tEXt chunk rather than a sidecar JSON.
102	    """
103	    base = Path(out)
104	    if base.suffix.lower() in (".bgr", ".png", ".json"):
105	        base = base.with_suffix("")
106	    base.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
107	
108	    try:
109	        from PIL import Image, PngImagePlugin
110	    except ImportError as e:  # pragma: no cover - Pillow is a base dependency
111	        raise SnapshotError("Pillow is required to save snapshots as PNG") from e
112	
113	    # Pillow's "raw" decoder maps BGR → RGB without a manual per-pixel swap.
114	    img = Image.frombytes("RGB", (snap.width, snap.height), snap.bgr, "raw", "BGR")
115	    meta = PngImagePlugin.PngInfo()
116	    meta.add_text("frame_epoch", str(snap.frame_epoch))
117	
118	    png_path = base.with_suffix(".png")
119	    img.save(png_path, pnginfo=meta)
120	    return [png_path]
121
```

```text
1	"""In-song score reader: per-digit glyph OCR of the open-ended score value.
2	
3	Unlike the menu/song readers (closed-set template matches), the score is an
4	open-ended number, so it is read digit by digit. The score is right-aligned in a
5	fixed HUD box and grows leftward; GH3 renders tabular (fixed-advance) digits, so
6	the score ROI (`metadata.SCORE_ROI[mode]`) splits into `N_SCORE_DIGITS` equal
7	cells anchored at the right edge. Each cell is fingerprinted (low-res normalized
8	luma grid, the same idea as the song reader) and matched against a per-mode bank
9	of digit templates 0-9 plus a `BLANK` class for the unused leading cells.
10	Non-blank cells, left to right, assemble the integer value.
11	
12	Two stages, because the field position is fixed on a given rig but the analog
13	capture varies frame to frame:
14	
15	- **Registration (once).** A per-cell offset search over a wide range locks the
16	  exact rect of each of the `N_SCORE_DIGITS` cells for this rig (`calibrate_score`
17	  → `ScoreCalibration`). This is where positional slop is absorbed — the field
18	  sits at the same pixels every frame, so we find it once (at gameplay start,
19	  over a few frames) rather than searching continually.
20	- **Per-frame read (continual).** `read_score` samples the locked cells and
21	  argmin-classifies each — no search. Per-frame luma normalization cancels the
22	  A2D gain/offset/brightness drift, so the fixed cells read correctly frame to
23	  frame. Cheap: a handful of rect-means + an L1 over 11 tiny templates.
24	
25	Templates are built from the labelled score corpus: each frame's known value is
26	right-justified across the cells, giving every cell a digit (or blank) label, and
27	the per-class mean fingerprint is the template — no hand-cropping of glyphs.
28	
29	Integer-friendly for the firmware port: fixed cells + argmin L1 over uint8-scale
30	vectors, exactly like `gp_read_song`; registration reuses the same offset-search
31	idiom, run once instead of per frame.
32	"""
33	
34	from __future__ import annotations
35	
36	from dataclasses import dataclass
37	
38	import numpy as np
39	
40	from .corpus import Sample
41	from .metadata import N_SCORE_DIGITS, SCORE_ROI, score_from_filename
42	from .songselect import _luma_grid, _shift
43	
44	BLANK = 10  # class label for an unused (empty) leading cell
45	
46	
47	@dataclass(frozen=True)
48	class ScoreConfig:
49	    n_digits: int = N_SCORE_DIGITS
50	    cols: int = 8   # per-cell grid columns (captures the digit's ink pattern)
51	    rows: int = 14  # per-cell grid rows
52	    # Registration search ranges (px), used *once* to lock the cell rects; not on
53	    # the per-frame read path. Two stages: a wide *whole-field* search finds the
54	    # score box for this rig (all cells move together, so it can't alias a cell
55	    # onto a neighbouring digit), then a small *per-cell* search locks each digit's
56	    # sub-pixel placement (kept well under the ~10 px pitch to avoid that aliasing).
57	    gx_search: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(range(-8, 9))
58	    gy_search: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(range(-4, 5))
59	    fine: tuple[int, ...] = (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2)
60	
61	
62	DEFAULT_SCORE_CONFIG = ScoreConfig()
63	
64	
65	@dataclass(frozen=True)
66	class DigitTemplate:
67	    digit: int  # 0-9, or BLANK
68	    vec: np.ndarray
69	
70	
71	@dataclass(frozen=True)
72	class ScoreCatalog:
73	    mode: str
74	    templates: list[DigitTemplate]  # one per labelled cell exemplar (1-NN, not centroid)
75	    config: ScoreConfig
76	
77	
78	@dataclass(frozen=True)
79	class ScoreCalibration:
80	    mode: str
81	    cells: tuple[tuple[int, int, int, int], ...]  # locked per-cell ROIs (len n_digits)
82	
83	
84	@dataclass(frozen=True)
85	class ScoreResult:
86	    value: int
87	    digits: tuple[int, ...]  # per-cell class, left->right (BLANK for empty leading cells)
88	    dist: float              # worst (max) per-cell best-distance
89	    margin: float            # weakest (min) per-cell 2nd-best - best
90	
91	
92	def _cell_rois(roi: tuple[int, int, int, int], n: int) -> list[tuple[int, int, int, int]]:
93	    """Split a score ROI into `n` equal-width digit cells (left->right)."""
94	    x0, y0, x1, y1 = roi
95	    xs = np.linspace(x0, x1, n + 1).round().astype(int)
96	    return [(int(xs[i]), y0, int(xs[i + 1]), y1) for i in range(n)]
97	
98	
99	def _labels_for_value(value: int, n_digits: int) -> list[int]:
100	    """Right-justify `value` across `n_digits` cells -> per-cell class labels.
101	
102	    Leading (unused) cells are BLANK; e.g. 1138 over 6 cells ->
103	    [BLANK, BLANK, 1, 1, 3, 8]. Scores never carry leading zeros.
104	    """
105	    s = str(value)
106	    pad = n_digits - len(s)
107	    return [BLANK] * pad + [int(c) for c in s]
108	
109	
110	def build_score_catalog(
111	    samples: list[Sample],
112	    mode: str = "training",
113	    config: ScoreConfig = DEFAULT_SCORE_CONFIG,
114	) -> ScoreCatalog:
115	    """Build per-mode digit templates (0-9 + BLANK) from labelled score frames.
116	
117	    Each frame's value is right-justified over the cells to label every cell, and
118	    every labelled cell fingerprint is kept as its own template — matching is 1-NN
119	    over the exemplars (not a per-class centroid): the crisp digits blur together
120	    when averaged (8/3/0), so nearest-exemplar separates them cleanly.
121	    """
122	    roi = SCORE_ROI[mode]
123	    cells = _cell_rois(roi, config.n_digits)
124	    templates: list[DigitTemplate] = []
125	    for s in samples:
126	        parsed = score_from_filename(s.path.name)
127	        if parsed is None or parsed[0] != mode:
128	            continue
129	        _mode, value = parsed
130	        labels = _labels_for_value(value, config.n_digits)
131	        for cell, label in zip(cells, labels):
132	            templates.append(DigitTemplate(digit=label, vec=_luma_grid(s.image, cell, config)))
133	    return ScoreCatalog(mode=mode, templates=templates, config=config)
134	
135	
136	def calibrate_score(
137	    images: list[np.ndarray],
138	    catalog: ScoreCatalog,
139	) -> ScoreCalibration:
140	    """Lock each digit cell's rect for this rig (run once, e.g. at gameplay start).
141	
142	    Two stages, aggregating the summed best-template distance across the
143	    calibration `images` (so the lock reflects true position, not one frame's
144	    glyphs):
145	
146	    1. **Whole-field:** find the single (gx, gy) shift of the score box that
147	       minimizes the total over all cells. Moving every cell together can't align
148	       one onto a neighbouring digit, so the wide search is safe here.
149	    2. **Per-cell:** around that field offset, search a small range per cell for
150	       its best sub-pixel placement. Kept under half the digit pitch, so a cell
151	       can't drift to its neighbour.
152	
153	    The resulting per-cell rects are reused by every subsequent `read_score`.
154	    """
155	    cfg = catalog.config
156	    base = SCORE_ROI[catalog.mode]
157	    vecs = [t.vec for t in catalog.templates]
158	
159	    def cell_cost(cell: tuple[int, int, int, int]) -> float:
160	        total = 0.0
161	        for img in images:
162	            fp = _luma_grid(img, cell, cfg)
163	            total += min(float(np.abs(fp - v).sum()) for v in vecs)
164	        return total
165	
166	    # Stage 1: whole-field offset (all cells move together).
167	    best_field: tuple[float, int, int] | None = None
168	    for gx in cfg.gx_search:
169	        for gy in cfg.gy_search:
170	            cells = _cell_rois(_shift(base, gx, gy), cfg.n_digits)
171	            total = sum(cell_cost(c) for c in cells)
172	            if best_field is None or total < best_field[0]:
173	                best_field = (total, gx, gy)
174	    assert best_field is not None
175	    _t, gx, gy = best_field
176	
177	    # Stage 2: small per-cell refinement around the field offset.
178	    cells_out: list[tuple[int, int, int, int]] = []
179	    for i in range(cfg.n_digits):
180	        best: tuple[float, tuple[int, int, int, int]] | None = None
181	        for dx in cfg.fine:
182	            for dy in cfg.fine:
183	                cell = _cell_rois(_shift(base, gx + dx, gy + dy), cfg.n_digits)[i]
184	                c = cell_cost(cell)
185	                if best is None or c < best[0]:
186	                    best = (c, cell)
187	        assert best is not None
188	        cells_out.append(best[1])
189	    return ScoreCalibration(mode=catalog.mode, cells=tuple(cells_out))
190	
191	
192	def read_score(
193	    image: np.ndarray,
194	    catalog: ScoreCatalog,
195	    calibration: ScoreCalibration | None = None,
196	) -> ScoreResult:
197	    """Read the score from the locked cells — no offset search (search-free per frame).
198	
199	    Each cell is fingerprinted (per-frame normalized, so A2D gain/offset drift is
200	    cancelled) and argmin-classified against the digit/blank templates. Non-blank
201	    classes, left to right, assemble the integer value. `calibration` gives the
202	    locked per-cell rects from `calibrate_score`; if omitted the nominal ROI cells
203	    are used (convenient for a single well-registered frame / tests).
204	    """
205	    cfg = catalog.config
206	    if calibration is not None:
207	        cells = list(calibration.cells)
208	    else:
209	        cells = _cell_rois(SCORE_ROI[catalog.mode], cfg.n_digits)
210	    templates = catalog.templates
211	
212	    per_cell: list[tuple[int, float, float]] = []
213	    for cell in cells:
214	        fp = _luma_grid(image, cell, cfg)
215	        scored = sorted((float(np.abs(fp - t.vec).sum()), t.digit) for t in templates)
216	        best_d, best_c = scored[0]
217	        # margin = distance to the nearest exemplar of a *different* class.
218	        other = next((d for d, c in scored if c != best_c), best_d)
219	        per_cell.append((best_c, best_d, other - best_d))
220	
221	    digits = tuple(c for c, _d, _m in per_cell)
222	    text = "".join(str(c) for c in digits if c != BLANK)
223	    value = int(text) if text else 0
224	    return ScoreResult(
225	        value=value,
226	        digits=digits,
227	        dist=max(d for _c, d, _m in per_cell),
228	        margin=min(m for _c, _d, m in per_cell),
229	    )
230
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-09 17:08:59Z)**_

Excellent catch — you're exactly right. The red is the **registration mask** (the pixels I treat as static chrome to lock position). Because our samples only have ≤5-digit scores, the left of the digit row is always blank panel → low variance → the STD-based mask wrongly includes it as "chrome." A full 6-digit score would put a digit right there and corrupt registration.

The fix: **hard-exclude the entire digit row** (full width a max-length score can fill) from the registration mask — regardless of variance — and register only on chrome that a score can never overlap: the panel/ring below the digit line, the medallion ring, and the box borders. Let me redo the mask that way and re-validate.

```text
38	/* ─── Internal types ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
39	
40	/* Discriminated slot for the state queue. The drain task switches on
41	 * hdr.type and writes only the populated bytes. Sized to the largest
42	 * small record so all types fit in one slot — DETECTOR_CONFIG is by far
43	 * the largest at ~188 B; the others fit in 32-51 B. The slot grew with
44	 * v3; queue depth × slot size is still trivial against 240 MB DDR. */
45	typedef union
46	{
47	    perf_hdr_t                  hdr;
48	    perf_rec_session_t          session;
49	    perf_rec_stamp_t            stamp;
50	    perf_rec_detector_t         detector;
51	    perf_rec_timing_t           timing;
52	    perf_rec_drop_t             drop;
53	    perf_rec_task_highwater_t   hwm;
54	    perf_rec_task_runtime_t     runtime;
55	    perf_rec_detector_config_t  detector_config;
56	    perf_rec_actuator_t         actuator;
57	    perf_rec_fretboard_raw_t    fretboard_raw;
58	} perf_rec_state_slot_t;
59	
60	/* ─── Static storage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
61	
62	static QueueHandle_t s_state_q;
63	static StaticQueue_t s_state_q_buf;
64	static uint8_t       s_state_q_storage[PL_STATE_QUEUE_DEPTH * sizeof(perf_rec_state_slot_t)];
65	
66	/* Strip pool: data lives here from producer fill through drain write to the
67	 * sink — no copy at queue ops. Both queues carry uint8_t slot indices. The
68	 * "in-flight" queue holds full slots awaiting drain; the "free" queue holds
69	 * available slots for the producer to claim. */
70	static perf_rec_strip_t s_strip_pool[PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE];
71	
72	static QueueHandle_t s_strip_q;
73	static StaticQueue_t s_strip_q_buf;
74	static uint8_t       s_strip_q_storage[PL_STRIP_QUEUE_DEPTH * sizeof(uint8_t)];
75	
76	static QueueHandle_t s_strip_free_q;
77	static StaticQueue_t s_strip_free_q_buf;
78	static uint8_t       s_strip_free_q_storage[PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE * sizeof(uint8_t)];
79	
80	static StackType_t   s_drain_stack[PL_DRAIN_STACK_WORDS];
81	static StaticTask_t  s_drain_tcb;
82	
83	#define PL_TASK_SLOT_COUNT  18u  /* one per perf_task_id_t — IDLE + 9 MCC slots + OTHER + FRETBOARD_RX */
84	static TaskHandle_t  s_task_handles[PL_TASK_SLOT_COUNT];
85	
86	static volatile uint32_t s_drop_state;
87	static volatile uint32_t s_drop_strip;
88	static volatile uint32_t s_drop_sink;
89	
90	static volatile bool s_running;
91	
92	/* One-shot full-frame snapshot. The RX path latches s_snapshot_req; the drain
93	 * task copies the current frame into s_snapshot_staging (one coherent copy out
94	 * of the rotating nocache ring) and pages it out as full-width SNAPSHOT bands.
95	 * Staging is sized to the max capture (1280×720×3); the scratch strip record is
96	 * static because it's ~65 KB — far too large for the 2 KB drain stack. */
97	static volatile bool    s_snapshot_req;
98	static uint8_t          s_snapshot_staging[1280u * 720u * PERF_STRIP_BPP];
99	static perf_rec_strip_t s_snapshot_scratch;
100	
101	/* Boot with only the cheap diagnostic types enabled: DROP (1 Hz),
102	 * TASK_HIGHWATER (~6/s), TASK_RUNTIME (~6/s). The host viewer enables
103	 * higher-rate types (STAMP, DETECTOR, TIMING, STRIP) via
104	 * PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK once it's ready to consume them. SESSION is
105	 * always emitted regardless of mask.
106	 *
107	 * Why default-off for the high-rate types — and STRIP especially:
108	 * before a host attaches and clears the wire, every emitted record
109	 * burns producer CPU (queue ops, framing, Fletcher) only to be dropped
110	 * at the sink for lack of DTR. STRIP at 60 Hz is the worst case
111	 * (multiple MB/s of pixel data thrown away) but STAMP isn't free either
112	 * (~700/s of state-queue traffic). */
113	static volatile uint32_t s_enabled_mask =
114	    (1u << PERF_REC_DROP) |
115	    (1u << PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER) |
116	    (1u << PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME);
117	
118	static inline bool type_enabled(uint8_t type)
119	{
120	    if (type == PERF_REC_SESSION) { return true; }
121	    return (s_enabled_mask & (1u << type)) != 0u;
122	}
123	
124	/* Overlay sinks for the per-fret target rings (PERF_OVERLAY_* bits). Read
125	 * lock-free by the CV producer; set by PERF_CMD_SET_OVERLAY. Default: rings on
126	 * the viewer strips, capture buffer untouched. */
127	static volatile uint32_t s_overlay_flags = PERF_OVERLAY_STRIP;
128	
129	/* ─── Header fill ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
130	
131	static inline void hdr_fill(perf_hdr_t *h, uint8_t type, uint8_t flags,
132	                            uint32_t frame_epoch)
133	{
134	    h->magic       = PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC;
135	    h->type        = type;
136	    h->flags       = flags;
137	    h->frame_epoch = frame_epoch;
138	    h->ts_counter  = SYS_TIME_Counter64Get();
139	}
140	
141	/* ─── Record-size dispatch ───────────────────────────────────────────────── */
142	
143	static uint16_t record_size(const perf_rec_state_slot_t *r)
144	{
145	    switch (r->hdr.type)
146	    {
147	        case PERF_REC_SESSION:         return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_session_t);
148	        case PERF_REC_STAMP:           return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_stamp_t);
149	        case PERF_REC_DETECTOR:        return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_detector_t);
150	        case PERF_REC_TIMING:          return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_timing_t);
151	        case PERF_REC_DROP:            return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_drop_t);
152	        case PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER:  return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_task_highwater_t);
153	        case PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME:    return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_task_runtime_t);
154	        case PERF_REC_DETECTOR_CONFIG: return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_detector_config_t);
155	        case PERF_REC_ACTUATOR:        return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_actuator_t);
156	        case PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW:   return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_fretboard_raw_t);
157	        default:                       return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_hdr_t);
158	    }
159	}
160	
161	/* Variable-length: queue slot is max-sized, but on the wire we send only
162	 * HDR + body + the actually-used pixel bytes. */
163	static uint16_t strip_record_size(const perf_rec_strip_t *r)
164	{
165	    uint32_t pix = (uint32_t)r->w * (uint32_t)r->h * PERF_STRIP_BPP;
166	    if (pix > PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES) { pix = PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES; }
167	    return (uint16_t)(PERF_STRIP_HDR_BYTES + pix);
168	}
169	
170	/* ─── Drain task ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
171	
172	static void emit_session_record(void)
173	{
174	    perf_rec_session_t r;
175	    memset(&r, 0, sizeof(r));
176	    hdr_fill(&r.hdr, PERF_REC_SESSION, 0u, 0u);
177	    r.timer_freq_hz  = SYS_TIME_FrequencyGet();
178	    r.schema_version = (uint16_t)PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION;
179	    PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&r, (uint16_t)sizeof(r));
180	}
181	
182	static void emit_drop_record(void)
183	{
184	    perf_rec_drop_t r;
185	    memset(&r, 0, sizeof(r));
186	    hdr_fill(&r.hdr, PERF_REC_DROP, 0u, 0u);
187	    r.dropped_state = s_drop_state;
188	    r.dropped_strip = s_drop_strip;
189	    r.dropped_sink  = s_drop_sink;
190	    PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&r, (uint16_t)sizeof(r));
191	}
192	
193	static void sample_and_emit_hwms(void)
194	{
195	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < PL_TASK_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
196	    {
197	        TaskHandle_t h = s_task_handles[i];
198	        if (h == NULL) { continue; }
199	        uint32_t words = (uint32_t)uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark(h);
200	        PerfLog_EmitTaskHighwater((perf_task_id_t)i, words);
201	    }
202	}
203	
204	/* Map FreeRTOS eTaskState → wire enum. Same numeric ordering today, but
205	 * cast through this so a future RTOS-side enum reshuffle doesn't silently
206	 * skew the wire format. */
207	static perf_task_state_t map_task_state(eTaskState s)
208	{
209	    switch (s)
210	    {
211	        case eRunning:   return PERF_TASK_STATE_RUNNING;
212	        case eReady:     return PERF_TASK_STATE_READY;
213	        case eBlocked:   return PERF_TASK_STATE_BLOCKED;
214	        case eSuspended: return PERF_TASK_STATE_SUSPENDED;
215	        case eDeleted:   return PERF_TASK_STATE_DELETED;
216	        default:         return PERF_TASK_STATE_INVALID;
217	    }
218	}
219	
220	/* Sized to comfortably exceed total live task count: marvin owns ~7
221	 * (CV / detector-drain / timing / fretboard-link / video / perf-drain /
222	 * idle) plus MCC-driven tasks (XLCDC, MAXTOUCH, LEGATO, SYS_INPUT, USB
223	 * host EHCI/OHCI/HUB/CDC) — call it ≤ 20 today, bump if we ever overflow. */
224	#define PL_RUNTIME_TASK_BUF  24u
225	
226	static void sample_and_emit_runtimes(void)
227	{
228	    static TaskStatus_t buf[PL_RUNTIME_TASK_BUF];
229	    UBaseType_t n = uxTaskGetSystemState(buf, PL_RUNTIME_TASK_BUF, NULL);
230	
231	    uint64_t sum_all = 0u, sum_registered = 0u;
232	
233	    for (UBaseType_t k = 0u; k < n; k++)
234	    {
235	        const TaskStatus_t *t = &buf[k];
236	        sum_all += (uint64_t)t->ulRunTimeCounter;
237	
238	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < PL_TASK_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
239	        {
240	            if (s_task_handles[i] != t->xHandle) { continue; }
241	            sum_registered += (uint64_t)t->ulRunTimeCounter;
242	            PerfLog_EmitTaskRuntime((perf_task_id_t)i,
243	                                    map_task_state(t->eCurrentState),
244	                                    (uint8_t)t->uxCurrentPriority,
245	                                    (uint32_t)t->ulRunTimeCounter);
246	            break;
247	        }
248	    }
249	
250	    /* OTHER pseudo-slot: every cycle not accounted to a registered task
251	     * (including IDLE, which is registered). Lets the host close the
252	     * books — Σ per-window CPU% = 100. State/priority don't have a
253	     * single value here; emit READY/0 as harmless placeholders. */
254	    PerfLog_EmitTaskRuntime(PERF_TASK_OTHER,
255	                            PERF_TASK_STATE_READY,
256	                            0u,
257	                            (uint32_t)(sum_all - sum_registered));
258	}
259	
260	/* MCC tasks are created in SYS_Tasks() right before vTaskStartScheduler,
261	 * not at SYS_Initialize time — so the handles aren't lookup-able from
262	 * APP_Initialize where PerfLog_Start runs. Same goes for the FreeRTOS
263	 * idle task: xTaskGetIdleTaskHandle() returns NULL until vTaskStartScheduler
264	 * creates it. The drain task runs after the scheduler is up and all
265	 * SYS_Tasks() xTaskCreate calls have landed; it does both lookups here.
266	 *
267	 * Names match the pcName argument in default/tasks.c xTaskCreate calls.
268	 * If MCC ever renames one (regen risk), xTaskGetHandle returns NULL and
269	 * that slot stays unregistered — its CPU runtime falls into OTHER, and
270	 * the host viewer sees a flat-zero series for that task as a hint. */
271	static const struct
272	{
273	    perf_task_id_t id;
274	    const char    *name;
275	} s_mcc_task_names[] =
276	{
277	    { PERF_TASK_LEGATO,        "LEGATO_Tasks"        },
278	    { PERF_TASK_XLCDC,         "XLCDC_Tasks"         },
279	    { PERF_TASK_MAXTOUCH,      "DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks"  },
280	    { PERF_TASK_SYS_INPUT,     "SYS_INPUT_Tasks"     },
281	    { PERF_TASK_USB_DEVICE,    "USB_DEVICE_TASKS"    },
282	    { PERF_TASK_USB_HOST,      "USB_HOST_TASKS"      },
283	    { PERF_TASK_DRV_USB_UDPHS, "DRV_USB_UDPHS_TASKS" },
284	    { PERF_TASK_DRV_USB_HOST,  "DRV_USB_HOST_TASKS"  },
285	    { PERF_TASK_APP,           "APP_Tasks"           },
286	};
287	
288	static void register_post_scheduler_tasks(void)
289	{
290	    TaskHandle_t idle = xTaskGetIdleTaskHandle();
291	    if (idle != NULL)
292	    {
293	        PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_IDLE, idle);
294	    }
295	    else
296	    {
297	        LOG_WARN("PerfLog: idle task handle not available\r\n");
298	    }
299	
300	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < sizeof(s_mcc_task_names) / sizeof(s_mcc_task_names[0]); i++)
301	    {
302	        TaskHandle_t h = xTaskGetHandle(s_mcc_task_names[i].name);
303	        if (h != NULL)
304	        {
305	            PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(s_mcc_task_names[i].id, h);
306	        }
307	        else
308	        {
309	            LOG_WARN("PerfLog: MCC task '%s' not found\r\n", s_mcc_task_names[i].name);
310	        }
311	    }
312	}
313	
314	/* Stream the current video frame back as full-width SNAPSHOT bands. Runs in
315	 * the drain task: writes each band directly to the sink (bypassing the small
316	 * strip pool, which can't hold 16-45 bands), naturally paced by the wire. This
317	 * briefly monopolizes the drain (~0.4 s @480p, ~1 s @720p) — fine for an
318	 * on-demand debug capture. */
319	static void emit_snapshot(void)
320	{
321	    Video_FrameInfo vi;
322	    Video_GetFrameInfo(&vi);
323	    if (vi.buffer == NULL || vi.width == 0u || vi.height == 0u) { return; }
324	    if (vi.bytes_per_pixel != PERF_STRIP_BPP) { return; }
325	
326	    const uint16_t w      = vi.width;
327	    const uint16_t h      = vi.height;
328	    const uint32_t stride = (uint32_t)w * PERF_STRIP_BPP;
329	    const uint32_t frame_bytes = stride * (uint32_t)h;
330	    if (frame_bytes > sizeof(s_snapshot_staging)) { return; }
331	
332	    memcpy(s_snapshot_staging, vi.buffer, frame_bytes);
333	
334	    uint32_t band_rows = PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES / stride;
335	    if (band_rows == 0u) { return; }              /* frame too wide for a strip */
336	    if (band_rows > h)   { band_rows = h; }
337	
338	    for (uint16_t y = 0u; y < h; )
339	    {
340	        uint16_t bh = (uint16_t)(((uint32_t)(h - y) < band_rows) ? (h - y) : band_rows);
341	
342	        perf_rec_strip_t *r = &s_snapshot_scratch;
343	        memset(r, 0, PERF_STRIP_HDR_BYTES);
344	        hdr_fill(&r->hdr, PERF_REC_STRIP, 0u, vi.frame_count);
345	        r->x     = 0u;
346	        r->y     = y;
347	        r->w     = w;
348	        r->h     = bh;
349	        r->kind  = (uint8_t)PERF_STRIP_SNAPSHOT;
350	        r->flags = ((uint32_t)y + bh >= h) ? PERF_STRIP_FLAG_LAST : 0u;
351	        memcpy(r->bgr, &s_snapshot_staging[(uint32_t)y * stride], (uint32_t)bh * stride);
352	
353	        PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(r, strip_record_size(r));
354	        y = (uint16_t)(y + bh);
355	    }
356	}
357	
358	static void perf_log_drain_task(void *param)
359	{
360	    (void)param;
361	
362	    PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize();
363	    register_post_scheduler_tasks();
364	    s_running = true;
365	
366	    TickType_t last_drop = xTaskGetTickCount();
367	    bool prev_connected = false;
368	
369	    for (;;)
370	    {
371	        bool now_connected = PerfLogSinkCdc_IsConnected();
372	        if (now_connected && !prev_connected)
373	        {
374	            emit_session_record();
375	        }
376	        prev_connected = now_connected;
377	
378	        if (s_snapshot_req)
379	        {
380	            s_snapshot_req = false;
381	            emit_snapshot();
382	        }
383	
384	        perf_rec_state_slot_t srec;
385	        if (xQueueReceive(s_state_q, &srec,
386	                          pdMS_TO_TICKS(PL_DRAIN_RX_TIMEOUT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
387	        {
388	            PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&srec, record_size(&srec));
389	            /* Drain all currently queued state records before moving on.
390	             * Strips cost ~5 ms apiece on the wire, so a one-state-per-
391	             * iteration loop runs at ~50 Hz under load — well below the
392	             * ~700 stamps/s production rate. Same shape as the strip
393	             * drain below. */
394	            while (xQueueReceive(s_state_q, &srec, 0) == pdTRUE)
395	            {
396	                PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&srec, record_size(&srec));
397	            }
398	        }
399	
400	        /* Strip drain: dequeue slot index, write the slot's data via
401	         * pointer (no copy), return slot to the free pool. */
402	        uint8_t slot_idx;
403	        while (xQueueReceive(s_strip_q, &slot_idx, 0) == pdTRUE)
404	        {
405	            const perf_rec_strip_t *r = &s_strip_pool[slot_idx];
406	            PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(r, strip_record_size(r));
407	            (void)xQueueSend(s_strip_free_q, &slot_idx, 0);
408	        }
409	
410	        if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - last_drop) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(PL_DROP_REPORT_PERIOD_MS))
411	        {
412	            last_drop = xTaskGetTickCount();
413	            emit_drop_record();
414	            sample_and_emit_hwms();
415	            sample_and_emit_runtimes();
416	        }
417	    }
418	}
419	
420	/* ─── Init ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
421	
422	void PerfLog_Initialize(void)
423	{
424	    s_state_q = xQueueCreateStatic(PL_STATE_QUEUE_DEPTH,
425	                                   sizeof(perf_rec_state_slot_t),
426	                                   s_state_q_storage,
427	                                   &s_state_q_buf);
428	    configASSERT(s_state_q != NULL);
429	
430	    s_strip_q = xQueueCreateStatic(PL_STRIP_QUEUE_DEPTH,
431	                                   sizeof(uint8_t),
432	                                   s_strip_q_storage,
433	                                   &s_strip_q_buf);
434	    configASSERT(s_strip_q != NULL);
435	
436	    s_strip_free_q = xQueueCreateStatic(PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE,
437	                                        sizeof(uint8_t),
438	                                        s_strip_free_q_storage,
439	                                        &s_strip_free_q_buf);
440	    configASSERT(s_strip_free_q != NULL);
441	
442	    /* Seed the free list with all pool indices. */
443	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE; i++)
444	    {
445	        (void)xQueueSend(s_strip_free_q, &i, 0);
446	    }
447	}
448	
449	void PerfLog_Start(void)
450	{
451	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(perf_log_drain_task,
452	                                       "PerfDrain",
453	                                       PL_DRAIN_STACK_WORDS,
454	                                       NULL,
455	                                       PL_DRAIN_PRIORITY,
456	                                       s_drain_stack,
457	                                       &s_drain_tcb);
458	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_PERF_DRAIN, h);
459	    /* Idle handle isn't valid until vTaskStartScheduler creates the idle
460	     * task — registered from the drain task post-scheduler instead, see
461	     * register_post_scheduler_tasks. */
462	}
463	
464	void PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(perf_task_id_t id, TaskHandle_t handle)
465	{
466	    if ((unsigned)id >= PL_TASK_SLOT_COUNT) { return; }
467	    s_task_handles[id] = handle;
468	}
469	
470	bool PerfLog_IsRunning(void)
471	{
472	    return s_running;
473	}
474	
475	/* ─── Emit (task context) ────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
476	
477	/* Drop counters are RMW from both task (send_state, EmitPatch,
478	 * NoteSinkDrop) and ISR (EmitStampFromISR) contexts. ARM926 single-
479	 * issue makes a single 32-bit aligned store atomic, but the increment
480	 * is LDR/ADD/STR — an ISR firing between LDR and STR loses an increment.
481	 * Critical sections (which globally disable IRQs on this port) keep
482	 * the RMW indivisible. The counters are diagnostic, so the very brief
483	 * IRQ-off window is fine. */
484	static inline void counter_add_task(volatile uint32_t *p, uint32_t v)
485	{
486	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
487	    *p += v;
488	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
489	}
490	
491	static inline void counter_add_isr(volatile uint32_t *p, uint32_t v)
492	{
493	    UBaseType_t s = taskENTER_CRITICAL_FROM_ISR();
494	    *p += v;
495	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL_FROM_ISR(s);
496	}
497	
498	static inline void send_state(const perf_rec_state_slot_t *slot)
499	{
500	    if (s_state_q == NULL) { return; }
501	    if (!type_enabled(slot->hdr.type)) { return; }
502	    if (xQueueSend(s_state_q, slot, 0) != pdTRUE)
503	    {
504	        counter_add_task(&s_drop_state, 1u);
505	    }
506	}
507	
508	void PerfLog_EmitStamp(perf_stage_t stage, uint32_t frame_epoch, uint32_t aux)
509	{
510	    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
511	    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
512	    hdr_fill(&slot.stamp.hdr, PERF_REC_STAMP, 0u, frame_epoch);
513	    slot.stamp.stage_id = (uint8_t)stage;
514	    slot.stamp.aux      = aux;
515	    send_state(&slot);
516	}
517	
518	void PerfLog_EmitDetector(uint32_t frame_epoch,
519	                          const uint16_t hold_dist[FRET_COUNT],
520	                          const uint16_t edge_dist[FRET_COUNT],
521	                          uint8_t  pressed_mask,
522	                          uint8_t  edge_active_mask)
523	{
524	    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
525	    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
526	    hdr_fill(&slot.detector.hdr, PERF_REC_DETECTOR, 0u, frame_epoch);
527	    memcpy(slot.detector.hold_dist, hold_dist, sizeof(slot.detector.hold_dist));
528	    memcpy(slot.detector.edge_dist, edge_dist, sizeof(slot.detector.edge_dist));
529	    slot.detector.pressed_mask     = pressed_mask;
530	    slot.detector.edge_active_mask = edge_active_mask;
531	    send_state(&slot);
532	}
533	
534	void PerfLog_EmitTiming(uint32_t frame_epoch, const perf_timing_snapshot_t *s)
535	{
536	    if (s == NULL) { return; }
537	    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;

628	/* Claim a free strip pool slot and fill its header. Returns the slot pointer
629	 * (writing its index to *out_idx) or NULL when STRIP is masked off, the args
630	 * are invalid, or the pool is empty (drop counted). The caller fills r->bgr
631	 * then calls strip_slot_commit. No struct memcpy in the queue critical
632	 * section — only a 1-byte index transfer. */
633	static perf_rec_strip_t *strip_slot_claim(uint32_t frame_epoch, perf_strip_kind_t kind,
634	                                          uint16_t x, uint16_t y,
635	                                          uint16_t w, uint16_t h,
636	                                          uint8_t *out_idx)
637	{
638	    if (s_strip_q == NULL || s_strip_free_q == NULL) { return NULL; }
639	    if (!type_enabled(PERF_REC_STRIP)) { return NULL; }
640	    if (w == 0u || h == 0u) { return NULL; }
641	    if ((uint32_t)w * (uint32_t)h * PERF_STRIP_BPP > PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES) { return NULL; }
642	
643	    uint8_t slot_idx;
644	    if (xQueueReceive(s_strip_free_q, &slot_idx, 0) != pdTRUE)
645	    {
646	        counter_add_task(&s_drop_strip, 1u);
647	        return NULL;
648	    }
649	
650	    perf_rec_strip_t *r = &s_strip_pool[slot_idx];
651	    memset(r, 0, PERF_STRIP_HDR_BYTES);
652	    hdr_fill(&r->hdr, PERF_REC_STRIP, 0u, frame_epoch);
653	    r->x    = x;
654	    r->y    = y;
655	    r->w    = w;
656	    r->h    = h;
657	    r->kind = (uint8_t)kind;
658	    *out_idx = slot_idx;
659	    return r;
660	}
661	
662	static void strip_slot_commit(uint8_t slot_idx)
663	{
664	    if (xQueueSend(s_strip_q, &slot_idx, 0) != pdTRUE)
665	    {
666	        /* In-flight queue full (pool sized depth+2 makes this rare; only
667	         * possible if the drain task is blocked while strip_q is at depth
668	         * and the producer also holds a slot). Return slot to free pool. */
669	        (void)xQueueSend(s_strip_free_q, &slot_idx, 0);
670	        counter_add_task(&s_drop_strip, 1u);
671	    }
672	}
673	
674	/* Strip producer: claim a free slot, row-copy a w×h BGR888 region out of the
675	 * strided source frame directly into the slot, then enqueue the slot index.
676	 * Total pixel bytes (w*h*3) must fit the slot's bgr[] (PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES);
677	 * per-axis shape is unconstrained beyond that. Drop-on-pool-empty. */
678	void PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(uint32_t frame_epoch,
679	                                perf_strip_kind_t kind,
680	                                const uint8_t *frame, uint32_t frame_stride,
681	                                uint16_t x, uint16_t y,
682	                                uint16_t w, uint16_t h)
683	{
684	    if (frame == NULL) { return; }
685	
686	    uint8_t slot_idx;
687	    perf_rec_strip_t *r = strip_slot_claim(frame_epoch, kind, x, y, w, h, &slot_idx);
688	    if (r == NULL) { return; }
689	
690	    const uint32_t row_bytes = (uint32_t)w * PERF_STRIP_BPP;
691	    const uint8_t *src = frame + (uint32_t)y * frame_stride + (uint32_t)x * PERF_STRIP_BPP;
692	    uint8_t *dst = r->bgr;
693	    for (uint16_t row = 0u; row < h; row++)
694	    {
695	        memcpy(dst, src, row_bytes);
696	        src += frame_stride;
697	        dst += row_bytes;
698	    }
699	
700	    strip_slot_commit(slot_idx);
701	}
702	
703	void PerfLog_EmitStripPacked(uint32_t frame_epoch,
704	                             perf_strip_kind_t kind,
705	                             uint16_t x, uint16_t y,
706	                             uint16_t w, uint16_t h,
707	                             const uint8_t *pixels)
708	{
709	    if (pixels == NULL) { return; }
710	
711	    uint8_t slot_idx;
712	    perf_rec_strip_t *r = strip_slot_claim(frame_epoch, kind, x, y, w, h, &slot_idx);
713	    if (r == NULL) { return; }
714	
715	    memcpy(r->bgr, pixels, (uint32_t)w * (uint32_t)h * PERF_STRIP_BPP);
716	    strip_slot_commit(slot_idx);
717	}
718	
719	/* ─── Emit (ISR context) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
720	
721	void PerfLog_EmitStampFromISR(perf_stage_t stage,
722	                              uint32_t frame_epoch,

731	    slot.stamp.stage_id = (uint8_t)stage;
732	    slot.stamp.aux      = aux;

734	    {
735	        counter_add_isr(&s_drop_state, 1u);
736	    }
737	}
```

```text
1	#include "perf_log_rx.h"
2	#include "perf_log.h"
3	#include "perf_log_records.h"
4	
5	#include <stdint.h>
6	#include <stdbool.h>
7	#include <string.h>
8	
9	/* Largest command frame today is perf_cmd_set_mask_t (8 B payload). The
10	 * buffer is sized to allow a small amount of growth without re-tuning. */
11	#define PL_RX_PAYLOAD_MAX  64u
12	
13	typedef enum
14	{
15	    RX_WAIT_SOF_0 = 0,
16	    RX_WAIT_SOF_1,
17	    RX_WAIT_SOF_2,
18	    RX_WAIT_SOF_3,
19	    RX_READ_LEN_0,
20	    RX_READ_LEN_1,
21	    RX_READ_PAYLOAD,
22	    RX_READ_FCS_0,
23	    RX_READ_FCS_1,
24	} rx_state_t;
25	
26	static rx_state_t s_state;
27	static uint16_t   s_len;
28	static uint16_t   s_payload_idx;
29	static uint8_t    s_payload[PL_RX_PAYLOAD_MAX];
30	/* Streaming Fletcher-16 (mod 255). init from 0xFFFF: s1 = s2 = 0xFF. */
31	static uint8_t    s_fcs_s1;
32	static uint8_t    s_fcs_s2;
33	static uint16_t   s_fcs_rx;
34	static uint32_t   s_drops;
35	
36	static inline void fcs_byte(uint8_t b)
37	{
38	    s_fcs_s1 = (uint8_t)(((uint16_t)s_fcs_s1 + b) % 255u);
39	    s_fcs_s2 = (uint8_t)(((uint16_t)s_fcs_s2 + s_fcs_s1) % 255u);
40	}
41	
42	static void reset(void)
43	{
44	    s_state       = RX_WAIT_SOF_0;
45	    s_len         = 0u;
46	    s_payload_idx = 0u;
47	    s_fcs_s1      = 0xFFu;
48	    s_fcs_s2      = 0xFFu;
49	    s_fcs_rx      = 0u;
50	}
51	
52	static void drop_and_reset(void)
53	{
54	    s_drops++;
55	    reset();
56	}
57	
58	/* Resync helper: if we're past WAIT_SOF_0 and the byte we just rejected
59	 * happens to be the first SOF byte of a fresh frame, give it credit
60	 * rather than waiting another full frame for the sync window. */
61	static void resync(uint8_t b)
62	{
63	    drop_and_reset();
64	    if (b == PERF_LOG_SOF_0)
65	    {
66	        s_state = RX_WAIT_SOF_1;
67	    }
68	}
69	
70	static void dispatch_payload(void)
71	{
72	    if (s_len < sizeof(perf_cmd_hdr_t)) { return; }
73	
74	    perf_cmd_hdr_t hdr;
75	    memcpy(&hdr, s_payload, sizeof(hdr));
76	    if (hdr.magic != PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC) { return; }
77	
78	    switch (hdr.cmd_id)
79	    {
80	        case PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK:
81	            if (s_len == sizeof(perf_cmd_set_mask_t))
82	            {
83	                perf_cmd_set_mask_t cmd;
84	                memcpy(&cmd, s_payload, sizeof(cmd));
85	                PerfLog_SetEnabledMask(cmd.enabled_mask);
86	            }
87	            break;
88	
89	        case PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT:
90	            /* Header-only. Just latch the request; the drain task does the
91	             * staging copy + banded emit (heavy work stays out of this
92	             * USB-callback context). */
93	            PerfLog_RequestSnapshot();
94	            break;
95	
96	        case PERF_CMD_SET_OVERLAY:
97	            if (s_len == sizeof(perf_cmd_set_overlay_t))
98	            {
99	                perf_cmd_set_overlay_t cmd;
100	                memcpy(&cmd, s_payload, sizeof(cmd));
101	                PerfLog_SetOverlayFlags(cmd.flags);
102	            }
103	            break;
104	
105	        default:
106	            break;
107	    }
108	}
109	
110	void PerfLogRx_Initialize(void)
111	{
112	    reset();
113	    s_drops = 0u;
114	}
115	
116	void PerfLogRx_Feed(const uint8_t *bytes, uint32_t len)
117	{
118	    for (uint32_t i = 0u; i < len; i++)
119	    {
120	        uint8_t b = bytes[i];
121	        switch (s_state)
122	        {
123	            case RX_WAIT_SOF_0:
124	                if (b == PERF_LOG_SOF_0) { s_state = RX_WAIT_SOF_1; }
125	                break;
126	
127	            case RX_WAIT_SOF_1:
128	                if (b == PERF_LOG_SOF_1) { s_state = RX_WAIT_SOF_2; }
129	                else                     { resync(b); }
130	                break;
131	
132	            case RX_WAIT_SOF_2:
133	                if (b == PERF_LOG_SOF_2) { s_state = RX_WAIT_SOF_3; }
134	                else                     { resync(b); }
135	                break;
136	
137	            case RX_WAIT_SOF_3:
138	                if (b == PERF_LOG_SOF_3) { s_state = RX_READ_LEN_0; }
139	                else                     { resync(b); }
140	                break;
141	
142	            case RX_READ_LEN_0:
143	                s_len   = b;
144	                fcs_byte(b);
145	                s_state = RX_READ_LEN_1;
146	                break;
147	
148	            case RX_READ_LEN_1:
149	                s_len  |= (uint16_t)b << 8;
150	                fcs_byte(b);
151	                if (s_len == 0u || s_len > PL_RX_PAYLOAD_MAX) { drop_and_reset(); }
152	                else                                          { s_state = RX_READ_PAYLOAD; }
153	                break;
154	
155	            case RX_READ_PAYLOAD:
156	                s_payload[s_payload_idx++] = b;
157	                fcs_byte(b);
158	                if (s_payload_idx >= s_len) { s_state = RX_READ_FCS_0; }
159	                break;
160	
161	            case RX_READ_FCS_0:
162	                s_fcs_rx = b;
163	                s_state  = RX_READ_FCS_1;
164	                break;
165	
166	            case RX_READ_FCS_1:
167	                s_fcs_rx |= (uint16_t)b << 8;
168	                {
169	                    uint16_t fcs_calc = (uint16_t)(((uint16_t)s_fcs_s2 << 8) | s_fcs_s1);
170	                    if (s_fcs_rx == fcs_calc) { dispatch_payload(); reset(); }
171	                    else                      { drop_and_reset(); }
172	                }
173	                break;
174	
175	            default:
176	                drop_and_reset();
177	                break;
178	        }
179	    }
180	}
181	
182	uint32_t PerfLogRx_GetDropCount(void)
183	{
184	    return s_drops;
185	}
```

```text
1	#ifndef PERF_LOG_RECORDS_H
2	#define PERF_LOG_RECORDS_H
3	
4	#include <stdint.h>
5	
6	#include "game/fret.h"
7	
8	/* Perf-log wire format. Mirror this header byte-for-byte in the host
9	 * decoder (tools/marvin-perf). Bump PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION on
10	 * every layout change; the host refuses streams that don't match.
11	 *
12	 * All fields little-endian, naturally aligned, fixed width. Records
13	 * are framed on the wire by the drain task (SOF magic + length + CRC);
14	 * the structs below are the framed payload only. */
15	
16	#define PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION   5u
17	
18	#define PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC        0x4D56u   /* 'M','V' little-endian */
19	
20	/* SOF bytes: 0x55 0x4D 0x52 0x56 ("UMRV"). Distinct from the 16-bit
21	 * header magic so a mid-stream reader can resync on a 4-byte pattern. */
22	#define PERF_LOG_SOF_0            0x55u
23	#define PERF_LOG_SOF_1            0x4Du
24	#define PERF_LOG_SOF_2            0x52u
25	#define PERF_LOG_SOF_3            0x56u
26	
27	typedef enum
28	{
29	    PERF_REC_SESSION         = 0x01,
30	    PERF_REC_STAMP           = 0x02,
31	    PERF_REC_DETECTOR        = 0x03,
32	    PERF_REC_TIMING          = 0x04,
33	    PERF_REC_STRIP           = 0x05,
34	    PERF_REC_DROP            = 0x06,
35	    PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER  = 0x07,
36	    PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME    = 0x08,
37	    PERF_REC_DETECTOR_CONFIG = 0x09,
38	    PERF_REC_ACTUATOR        = 0x0A,
39	    PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW   = 0x0B,
40	} perf_rec_type_t;
41	
42	/* stage_id values for PERF_REC_STAMP. Producer call sites map 1:1. */
43	typedef enum
44	{
45	    PERF_STAGE_ISC_IRQ            = 0x10,
46	    PERF_STAGE_VIDEO_PUBLISH      = 0x11,
47	    PERF_STAGE_CV_START           = 0x20,
48	    PERF_STAGE_CV_END             = 0x21,
49	    PERF_STAGE_TP_TICK            = 0x30,
50	    PERF_STAGE_FBL_SEND           = 0x40,
51	    PERF_STAGE_CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE = 0x41,
52	    /* PERF_STAGE_FBL_READ_COMPLETE = 0x42 — slot reserved; per-Read emit
53	     * was tried during fretboard-RX bring-up but at the fretboard's 240 Hz
54	     * polling rate it doubled the timeline marker count and made Plotly's
55	     * SVG scatter freeze the live page. FRETBOARD_RAW records carry their
56	     * own ts_counter so the same Read-side timing is recoverable offline
57	     * without a per-Read stamp. Re-enable here only if a sub-frame USB
58	     * latency tuning task explicitly needs it. */
59	} perf_stage_t;
60	
61	#define PERF_FLAG_FROM_ISR        0x01u
62	
63	/* Common header on every record. 16 B. */
64	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
65	{
66	    uint16_t magic;           /* PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC */
67	    uint8_t  type;            /* perf_rec_type_t */
68	    uint8_t  flags;           /* PERF_FLAG_* */
69	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     /* Video_FrameInfo.frame_count at producer site */
70	    uint64_t ts_counter;      /* SYS_TIME raw counter; host divides by timer_freq_hz */
71	} perf_hdr_t;
72	
73	/* PERF_REC_SESSION — emitted once when the drain task starts. The host
74	 * decoder uses timer_freq_hz to convert ts_counter to seconds and
75	 * schema_version to refuse mismatched streams. */
76	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
77	{
78	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
79	    uint32_t   timer_freq_hz;
80	    uint16_t   schema_version;
81	    uint16_t   reserved;
82	    uint32_t   fw_git_short;  /* zero until we wire a build-time symbol */
83	    uint32_t   reserved2;
84	} perf_rec_session_t;
85	
86	/* PERF_REC_STAMP — single-point timestamp marker. aux is stage-specific:
87	 *   ISC_IRQ           : reserved (0)
88	 *   VIDEO_PUBLISH     : subscriber bitmask
89	 *   CV_START / CV_END : reserved (0)
90	 *   TP_TICK           : publish_mask (low 7 bits)
91	 *   FBL_SEND          : queued mask
92	 *   CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE: USB CDC result code */
93	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))

205	/* PERF_REC_STRIP — variable-size BGR888 region of interest, kind-tagged.

210	 * Future kinds (SCORE, MINIMAP, etc.) plug into the same record type —
211	 * adding one is an enum entry plus a producer; no schema bump.
212	 *
213	 * Wire payload size is HDR + 12 B body + w*h*PERF_STRIP_BPP bytes,
214	 * tightly packed. The queue slot is sized to PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES; the
215	 * drain task computes the on-wire length from (w, h) and frames only

220	    PERF_STRIP_STRIKE   = 1,

236	 *   2. UDPHS DMA single-transfer cap is
237	 *      DRV_USB_UDPHS_DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE × 64 KB
238	 *      (currently 2 × 64 KB = 128 KB; well above the LEN cap)

240	 * The u16 LEN field is the binding constraint. Set at 65000 to land just
241	 * under it with a small margin. Producers may use any (w, h) shape as
242	 * long as w * h * PERF_STRIP_BPP <= PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES.
243	 *
244	 * Practical strip-size envelope (pixel area = w*h ≤ ~21666):
245	 *   720×30  640×33  480×45  320×64  290×72

247	 * Buffer footprint scales with this:
248	 *   pool      = PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE × (28 + PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES)
249	 *   sink ring = SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH × round_up_64(36 + PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES)

251	 *
```

```text
40	# ─── Type-mask CLI parsing ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
41	
42	
43	def parse_types_arg(spec: str | None) -> int | None:
44	    """Resolve a `--types` spec to a u32 mask. Returns None if `spec` is None.
45	
46	    Accepts a comma-separated list of RecordType names plus the special tokens
47	    `ALL` (0xFFFFFFFF) and `MIN` (SESSION|DROP). Case-insensitive.
48	    """
49	    if spec is None:
50	        return None
51	    mask = 0
52	    for raw in spec.split(","):
53	        token = raw.strip().upper()
54	        if not token:
55	            continue
56	        if token == "ALL":
57	            return TYPE_MASK_ALL
58	        if token == "MIN":
59	            mask |= TYPE_MASK_MIN
60	            continue
61	        if token not in RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME:
62	            valid = ", ".join(sorted(RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME))
63	            raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
64	                f"unknown record type {token!r}; valid: {valid}, ALL, MIN"
65	            )
66	        mask |= 1 << RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME[token]
67	    return mask
68	
69	
70	def _types_help() -> str:
71	    bit_lines = ", ".join(
72	        f"{name}={int(rt)}" for name, rt in sorted(RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME.items())
73	    )
74	    return (
75	        "Comma-separated record types to enable on the device. "
76	        f"Names: {bit_lines}. Special: ALL (default), MIN (SESSION+DROP). "
77	        "SESSION is always emitted regardless of mask. Old firmware ignores the command."
78	    )

81	def _send_mask(ser: SerialSource, mask: int) -> None:
82	    payload = encode_set_mask_payload(mask)
83	    ser.send_command(frame_encode(payload))
84	    print(f"[mask] sent 0x{mask:08x}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)

90	def cmd_record(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
91	    """Pure pass-through to disk; no decode.
92	
93	    Two modes: `--out FILE.bin` writes a raw legacy file; `--out-dir DIR`
94	    writes a capture directory (DIR/perf.bin + manifest.json finalized on
95	    close).
96	    """
97	    if (args.out is None) == (args.out_dir is None):
98	        print("record: exactly one of --out or --out-dir is required", file=sys.stderr)
99	        return 2
100	
101	    if args.out_dir is not None:
102	        cap_dir = init_capture_dir(args.out_dir, exist_ok=False)
103	        bin_path = cap_dir / BIN_NAME
104	        label = f"capture {cap_dir.name}/"
105	    else:
106	        cap_dir = None
107	        bin_path = Path(args.out)
108	        label = f"recording {bin_path.name}"
109	
110	    mask = parse_types_arg(args.types)
111	    bytes_written = 0
112	    last_status = time.monotonic()
113	    with SerialSource(args.port) as ser, bin_path.open("wb") as fh:
114	        if mask is not None:
115	            _send_mask(ser, mask)
116	        try:
117	            for chunk in ser:
118	                fh.write(chunk)
119	                fh.flush()
120	                bytes_written += len(chunk)
121	                now = time.monotonic()
122	                if (now - last_status) >= 1.0:
123	                    print(f"{label}: {bytes_written} B", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
124	                    last_status = now
125	        except KeyboardInterrupt:
126	            print(f"\nstopped after {bytes_written} B", file=sys.stderr)
127	
128	    if cap_dir is not None:
129	        manifest = finalize_capture_dir(
130	            cap_dir,
131	            source=CaptureSource(kind="serial", port=args.port),
132	        )
133	        print(
134	            f"finalized {cap_dir}/manifest.json — {manifest.n_records} records, "
135	            f"types={manifest.producer_capabilities}",
136	            file=sys.stderr,
137	        )
138	    return 0
139

143	    if mask is None:
144	        print("set-mask: --types is required", file=sys.stderr)
145	        return 2
146	    with SerialSource(args.port) as ser:
147	        _send_mask(ser, mask)
148	    return 0

151	def cmd_set_overlay(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
152	    """Toggle the per-fret target rings on the SENSING strip."""
153	    flags = PERF_OVERLAY_STRIP if args.on else 0
154	    with SerialSource(args.port) as ser:
155	        ser.send_command(frame_encode(encode_set_overlay_payload(flags)))
156	    print(f"set-overlay: strip rings {'on' if args.on else 'off'}", file=sys.stderr)
157	    return 0

159	
160	def _idle_chunks(ser: SerialSource, idle_timeout_s: float):
161	    """Yield serial chunks until `idle_timeout_s` elapses with no new bytes.
162	
163	    Lets `iter_frames` terminate once the snapshot burst stops (or stalls),
164	    instead of blocking forever on the infinite SerialSource iterator.
165	    """
166	    deadline = time.monotonic() + idle_timeout_s
167	    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
168	        chunk = ser.read_chunk()
169	        if chunk:
170	            deadline = time.monotonic() + idle_timeout_s
171	            yield chunk
172	
173	
174	def _resolve_snapshot_out(out: str | None) -> Path:
175	    """Resolve the `--out` argument to a concrete .png path.
176	
177	    A value ending in `.png` is taken literally. Anything else (including the
178	    default when `--out` is omitted) is treated as a directory, and the next
179	    free `snapshot-NNNN.png` in it is chosen so rapid captures never clobber.
180	    """
181	    p = Path(out) if out else Path("snapshots")
182	    if p.suffix.lower() == ".png":
183	        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
184	        return p
185	
186	    p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
187	    nums = [
188	        int(m.group(1))
189	        for f in p.glob("snapshot-*.png")
190	        if (m := re.fullmatch(r"snapshot-(\d+)", f.stem))
191	    ]
192	    nxt = (max(nums) + 1) if nums else 1
193	    return p / f"snapshot-{nxt:04d}.png"
194	
195	
196	def cmd_snapshot(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
197	    """Trigger a full-frame snapshot and save it as a lossless PNG.
198	
199	    Sends PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT, reassembles the returned SNAPSHOT band strips into
200	    one frame, and writes a PNG. With `--out` omitted (or pointed at a
201	    directory) the filename auto-increments as `snapshot-NNNN.png` for quick
202	    repeated captures.
203	    """
204	    out_path = _resolve_snapshot_out(args.out)
205	
206	    assembler = SnapshotAssembler()
207	    with SerialSource(args.port) as ser:
208	        ser.send_command(frame_encode(encode_snapshot_payload()))
209	        print("[snapshot] requested; waiting for bands…", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
210	        snap = None
211	        for fb in iter_frames(_idle_chunks(ser, args.timeout)):
212	            rec = decode_record(fb.payload)
213	            if not isinstance(rec, Strip):
214	                continue
215	            snap = assembler.add(rec)
216	            if snap is not None:
217	                break
218	
219	    if snap is None:
220	        print(
221	            f"snapshot: no complete frame within {args.timeout:.1f}s idle timeout. "
222	            "Is marvin connected, HDMI locked, and the firmware schema current?",
223	            file=sys.stderr,
224	        )
225	        return 1
226	
227	    written = save_snapshot(snap, out_path)
228	    print(
229	        f"snapshot: {snap.width}×{snap.height} (frame_epoch {snap.frame_epoch}) → "
230	        + ", ".join(str(p) for p in written),
231	        file=sys.stderr,
232	    )
233	    return 0

236	def cmd_export_ml(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
237	    """Export a finished capture as a SensiML-format CSV for MPLAB ML.
238	
239	    One row per fretboard ADC sample (~240 Hz); each row carries the five
240	    raw 12-bit ADC values plus binary labels. With --labels=detector the
241	    labels are the five per-fret pressed bits from cv_marvin_v1's
242	    pressed_mask; with --labels=actuator they are the five frets plus a
243	    collapsed strum bit from the timing pipeline's intended_mask (the
244	    edge-ai distillation target); with --labels=actuator-fb the same labels
245	    come from the actuator bitmask the fretboard reports inside each frame
246	    (atomically paired with the ADC; preferred — adds an fb_seq column).
247	    """
248	    try:
249	        stats = export_sensiml_csv(
250	            args.capture, args.out, labels=args.labels, strict=args.strict
251	        )
252	    except ExportError as e:
253	        print(f"export-ml: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
254	        return 1
255	    if args.labels == "actuator-fb":
256	        print(
257	            f"wrote {args.out}: {stats.n_rows} rows over {stats.duration_s:.2f} s "
258	            f"({stats.n_strum_events} strum events, "
259	            f"{stats.n_fretboard_records} fretboard records, "
260	            f"{stats.n_seq_gaps} seq gaps, "
261	            f"{stats.n_skipped_unlabeled} skipped)",
262	            file=sys.stderr,
263	        )
264	    elif args.labels == "detector-fb":
265	        print(
266	            f"wrote {args.out}: {stats.n_rows} rows over {stats.duration_s:.2f} s "
267	            f"({stats.n_detector_records} detector records, "
268	            f"{stats.n_strum_events} strum events, "
269	            f"{stats.n_fretboard_records} fretboard records, "
270	            f"{stats.n_seq_gaps} seq gaps)",
271	            file=sys.stderr,
272	        )
273	    elif args.labels == "actuator":
274	        print(
275	            f"wrote {args.out}: {stats.n_rows} rows over {stats.duration_s:.2f} s "
276	            f"({stats.n_actuator_records} actuator records, "
277	            f"{stats.n_strum_events} strum events, "
278	            f"{stats.n_fretboard_records} fretboard records, "
279	            f"{stats.n_skipped_unlabeled} skipped)",
280	            file=sys.stderr,
281	        )
282	    else:
283	        print(
284	            f"wrote {args.out}: {stats.n_rows} rows over {stats.duration_s:.2f} s "
285	            f"({stats.n_detector_records} detector records, "
286	            f"{stats.n_fretboard_records} fretboard records, "
287	            f"{stats.n_skipped_unlabeled} skipped)",
288	            file=sys.stderr,
289	        )
290	    # Loud failure modes: a structurally-valid CSV with zero usable labels is
291	    # training-useless and easy to miss from a one-line summary. Surface as a
292	    # warning the user can't ignore, and exit non-zero so scripts notice.
293	    if args.labels == "actuator" and stats.n_rows > 0 and stats.n_actuator_records == 0:
294	        print(
295	            "WARNING: capture contains no ACTUATOR records — every row's "
296	            "fret_*/strum columns are all zeros. The CSV is unlabelled and "
297	            "not useful for training. Re-record with both ACTUATOR and "
298	            "FRETBOARD_RAW enabled in the Types panel (or "
299	            "--types ACTUATOR,FRETBOARD_RAW for `marvin-perf record`).",
300	            file=sys.stderr,
301	        )
302	        return 2
303	    if args.labels in ("detector", "detector-fb") and stats.n_rows > 0 and stats.n_detector_records == 0:
304	        print(
305	            "WARNING: capture contains no DETECTOR records — every row's "
306	            "fret columns are all zeros. The CSV is unlabelled and not "
307	            "useful for training. Re-record with both DETECTOR and "
308	            "FRETBOARD_RAW enabled in the Types panel (or "
309	            "--types DETECTOR,FRETBOARD_RAW for `marvin-perf record`).",
310	            file=sys.stderr,
311	        )
312	        return 2
313	    if args.labels == "actuator-fb" and stats.n_rows > 0 and stats.n_strum_events == 0:
314	        print(
315	            "WARNING: no strum events in the in-frame actuator bitmask — the "
316	            "fretboard reported no actuation. Either this isn't gameplay, or "
317	            "the firmware predates schema v4 (frames carry no applied_mask).",
318	            file=sys.stderr,
319	        )
320	        return 2
321	    if stats.n_rows == 0:
322	        print(
323	            "WARNING: capture contains no FRETBOARD_RAW records — output "
324	            "CSV has only the header row. Re-record with FRETBOARD_RAW "
325	            "enabled.",

349	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
350	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
351	        prog="marvin-perf",
352	        description="marvin perf-log: visual review server + headless capture helpers.",
353	    )
354	    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="command")
355	
356	    p_record = sub.add_parser("record", help="Capture raw bytes (no decode).")
357	    p_record.add_argument("--port", required=True)
358	    p_record.add_argument("--out", help="Write a bare .bin (legacy)")
```

```text
1	"""Reassemble PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT band strips into a full frame and save it.
2	
3	The device answers a snapshot command with a top-to-bottom run of full-width
4	`STRIP` records (kind SNAPSHOT), all sharing one `frame_epoch`; the final band
5	sets `STRIP_FLAG_LAST`. This module groups bands by `frame_epoch`, pastes them
6	onto a canvas, and writes the result as a lossless `.png` (frame_epoch in a
7	tEXt chunk).
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
13	from pathlib import Path
14	
15	from .records import STRIP_BPP, Strip, StripKind
16	
17	
18	@dataclass(frozen=True)
19	class CompletedSnapshot:
20	    width: int
21	    height: int
22	    frame_epoch: int
23	    bgr: bytes  # width * height * 3, row-major, top-to-bottom
24	
25	    @property
26	    def n_bytes(self) -> int:
27	        return self.width * self.height * STRIP_BPP
28	
29	
30	class SnapshotError(Exception):
31	    pass
32	
33	
34	@dataclass
35	class _Pending:
36	    width: int
37	    bands: dict[int, Strip] = field(default_factory=dict)  # keyed by band y
38	    last_y: int | None = None  # y of the band flagged LAST
39	
40	
41	class SnapshotAssembler:
42	    """Feed decoded `Strip` records; get a `CompletedSnapshot` when done.
43	
44	    `add()` ignores non-SNAPSHOT strips and returns None until a snapshot's
45	    LAST band has arrived and every row from 0..height is covered, at which
46	    point it returns the assembled frame (and forgets that frame_epoch).
47	    """
48	
49	    def __init__(self) -> None:
50	        self._pending: dict[int, _Pending] = {}
51	
52	    def add(self, strip: Strip) -> CompletedSnapshot | None:
53	        if strip.kind != int(StripKind.SNAPSHOT):
54	            return None
55	        if strip.x != 0:
56	            raise SnapshotError(f"snapshot band at x={strip.x}, expected full-width")
57	
58	        epoch = strip.hdr.frame_epoch
59	        p = self._pending.get(epoch)
60	        if p is None:
61	            p = _Pending(width=strip.w)
62	            self._pending[epoch] = p
63	        elif strip.w != p.width:
64	            raise SnapshotError(
65	                f"snapshot band width {strip.w} != {p.width} (frame_epoch {epoch})"
66	            )
67	
68	        p.bands[strip.y] = strip
69	        if strip.is_last:
70	            p.last_y = strip.y
71	
72	        if p.last_y is None:
73	            return None
74	        return self._try_finalize(epoch, p)
75	
76	    def _try_finalize(self, epoch: int, p: _Pending) -> CompletedSnapshot | None:
77	        # Walk contiguous bands from y=0; bail (keep waiting) on any gap.
78	        canvas = bytearray()
79	        y = 0
80	        height = 0
81	        while y in p.bands:
82	            band = p.bands[y]
83	            canvas += band.bgr
84	            height = y + band.h
85	            y += band.h
86	        if p.last_y is None or height <= p.last_y:
87	            return None  # not yet contiguous through the LAST band
88	
89	        del self._pending[epoch]
90	        return CompletedSnapshot(
91	            width=p.width, height=height, frame_epoch=epoch, bgr=bytes(canvas)
92	        )
93	
94	
95	def save_snapshot(snap: CompletedSnapshot, out: str | Path) -> list[Path]:
96	    """Write the snapshot as a lossless PNG and return its path.
97	
98	    `out` may carry a .png suffix (or a stale .bgr/.json, stripped) or be a bare
99	    stem; the result is always `<stem>.png`. PNG is lossless for the packed RGB
100	    pixels, so no separate raw buffer is needed; `frame_epoch` rides along in a
101	    tEXt chunk rather than a sidecar JSON.
102	    """
103	    base = Path(out)
104	    if base.suffix.lower() in (".bgr", ".png", ".json"):
105	        base = base.with_suffix("")
106	    base.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
107	
108	    try:
109	        from PIL import Image, PngImagePlugin
110	    except ImportError as e:  # pragma: no cover - Pillow is a base dependency
111	        raise SnapshotError("Pillow is required to save snapshots as PNG") from e
112	
113	    # Pillow's "raw" decoder maps BGR → RGB without a manual per-pixel swap.
114	    img = Image.frombytes("RGB", (snap.width, snap.height), snap.bgr, "raw", "BGR")
115	    meta = PngImagePlugin.PngInfo()
116	    meta.add_text("frame_epoch", str(snap.frame_epoch))
117	
118	    png_path = base.with_suffix(".png")
119	    img.save(png_path, pnginfo=meta)
120	    return [png_path]
121
```

```text
1	"""Wire-frame parser for the perf-log USB CDC stream.
2	
3	Wire layout (mirrors firmware perf_log_sink_cdc.c):
4	
5	    SOF(4)  | LEN(u16 LE) | PAYLOAD(LEN bytes) | FCS(u16 LE)
6	
7	FCS is Fletcher-16 (mod 255, init 0xFFFF) computed over `LEN || PAYLOAD`
8	(NOT including SOF). USB hardware already CRCs the wire; the framing
9	checksum is just for resync alignment + firmware-bug detection.
10	
11	This module is purely byte-level. It does not understand record types — that's
12	decode.py's job. It exists to (a) resync after mid-stream join or byte loss,
13	(b) reject corrupt frames, and (c) yield validated payloads upward.
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
19	from dataclasses import dataclass
20	
21	from .records import MAX_RECORD_BYTES, SOF_BYTES
22	
23	
24	# ─── Fletcher-16 (mod 255, init 0xFFFF) ──────────────────────────────────────
25	
26	
27	def fletcher16(data: bytes | memoryview, init: int = 0xFFFF) -> int:
28	    """Fletcher-16 with mod 255. Mirrors firmware perf_log_sink_cdc.c.
29	
30	    Detection: single-byte changes, adjacent swaps, most non-adjacent swaps.
31	    Strong enough for framing-layer alignment + firmware-bug detection on
32	    top of USB's wire-level CRC. ~3× cheaper than CRC-16 in C and Python.
33	    """
34	    s1 = init & 0xFF
35	    s2 = (init >> 8) & 0xFF
36	    for b in data:
37	        s1 = (s1 + b) % 255
38	        s2 = (s2 + s1) % 255
39	    return (s2 << 8) | s1
40	
41	
42	def frame_encode(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
43	    """SOF + LEN(u16LE) + payload + Fletcher-16(u16LE).
44	
45	    Mirror of the device-side framer; FCS covers LEN || PAYLOAD (not SOF).
46	    """
47	    length = len(payload)
48	    if length > 0xFFFF:
49	        raise ValueError(f"payload too large: {length} bytes")
50	    len_bytes = bytes((length & 0xFF, (length >> 8) & 0xFF))
51	    fcs = fletcher16(len_bytes + payload)
52	    fcs_bytes = bytes((fcs & 0xFF, (fcs >> 8) & 0xFF))
53	    return SOF_BYTES + len_bytes + payload + fcs_bytes
54	
55	
56	# ─── Frame iterator ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
57	
58	
59	@dataclass(frozen=True)
60	class FrameBytes:
61	    """A successfully-parsed wire frame's payload + provenance."""
62	
63	    payload: bytes
64	    bytes_skipped_before: int  # diagnostic: bytes dropped resyncing to this frame
65	    framed: bytes = b""        # full SOF+LEN+payload+CRC for re-emission to disk
66	
67	
68	class FrameError(Exception):
69	    """Wire-level frame error (FCS mismatch, length out of range)."""
70	
71	
72	class FrameStats:
73	    """Mutable counters surfaced by `iter_frames` for the CLI."""
74	
75	    def __init__(self) -> None:
76	        self.frames_ok: int = 0
77	        self.bytes_resync_dropped: int = 0
78	        self.fcs_mismatches: int = 0
79	        self.bad_lengths: int = 0
80	
81	
82	def iter_frames(
83	    chunks: Iterable[bytes],
84	    stats: FrameStats | None = None,
85	) -> Iterator[FrameBytes]:
86	    """Consume an iterable of byte chunks, yield validated frame payloads.
87	
88	    The iterator handles arbitrary chunk boundaries (a frame may straddle as
89	    many chunks as it likes), resyncs on the 4-byte SOF after byte loss, and
90	    drops frames whose FCS does not match. Counters are accumulated into
91	    `stats` if supplied.
92	    """
93	    if stats is None:
94	        stats = FrameStats()
95	
96	    buf = bytearray()
97	    skipped_since_last_ok = 0
98	
99	    for chunk in chunks:
100	        if not chunk:
101	            continue
102	        buf.extend(chunk)
103	
104	        while True:
105	            sof_idx = buf.find(SOF_BYTES)
106	            if sof_idx < 0:
107	                # No SOF in buffer. Drop everything but the last 3 bytes (a
108	                # SOF could still be straddling the boundary).
109	                if len(buf) > 3:
110	                    skipped_since_last_ok += len(buf) - 3
111	                    stats.bytes_resync_dropped += len(buf) - 3
112	                    del buf[: len(buf) - 3]
113	                break
114	
115	            if sof_idx > 0:
116	                skipped_since_last_ok += sof_idx
117	                stats.bytes_resync_dropped += sof_idx
118	                del buf[:sof_idx]
119	
120	            # buf now starts with SOF. Need 4 (SOF) + 2 (LEN) before we can
121	            # bound the frame.
122	            if len(buf) < 6:
123	                break
124	
125	            length = buf[4] | (buf[5] << 8)
126	
127	            # Sanity-bound the length. A bogus LEN (e.g. mid-payload bytes
128	            # that happened to align with SOF) will trip this; treat the SOF
129	            # as a false positive and step past it.
130	            if length < 16 or length > MAX_RECORD_BYTES:
131	                stats.bad_lengths += 1
132	                skipped_since_last_ok += 1
133	                stats.bytes_resync_dropped += 1
134	                del buf[0]
135	                continue
136	
137	            total = 6 + length + 2
138	            if len(buf) < total:
139	                break
140	
141	            payload = bytes(buf[6 : 6 + length])
142	            fcs_observed = buf[6 + length] | (buf[6 + length + 1] << 8)
143	            fcs_expected = fletcher16(buf[4 : 6 + length])
144	
145	            if fcs_observed != fcs_expected:
146	                # Bad FCS. Likely a false-positive SOF in the middle of an
147	                # earlier frame; step past one byte and rescan.
148	                stats.fcs_mismatches += 1
149	                skipped_since_last_ok += 1
150	                stats.bytes_resync_dropped += 1
151	                del buf[0]
152	                continue
153	
154	            # Good frame — capture the full framed bytes, consume, yield.
155	            framed = bytes(buf[:total])
156	            del buf[:total]
157	            stats.frames_ok += 1
158	            yield FrameBytes(
159	                payload=payload,
160	                bytes_skipped_before=skipped_since_last_ok,
161	                framed=framed,
162	            )
163	            skipped_since_last_ok = 0
164
```

```text
1	"""Byte sources feeding `framing.iter_frames`.
2	
3	Each source is an iterable of `bytes` chunks. Chunk size is not load-bearing —
4	the framer handles arbitrary boundaries.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	from collections.abc import Iterator
10	from contextlib import AbstractContextManager
11	from pathlib import Path
12	
13	
14	# ─── File source ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
15	
16	
17	class FileSource(AbstractContextManager["FileSource"]):
18	    """Iterate over fixed-size chunks from a captured `.bin` file."""
19	
20	    def __init__(self, path: str | Path, chunk_bytes: int = 64 * 1024) -> None:
21	        self.path = Path(path)
22	        self.chunk_bytes = chunk_bytes
23	        self._fh: BinaryIO | None = None
24	
25	    def __enter__(self) -> "FileSource":
26	        self._fh = self.path.open("rb")
27	        return self
28	
29	    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:
30	        if self._fh is not None:
31	            self._fh.close()
32	            self._fh = None
33	
34	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[bytes]:
35	        if self._fh is None:
36	            raise RuntimeError("FileSource must be used as a context manager")
37	        while True:
38	            chunk = self._fh.read(self.chunk_bytes)
39	            if not chunk:
40	                return
41	            yield chunk
42	
43	
44	# ─── Serial source ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
45	
46	
47	class SerialSource(AbstractContextManager["SerialSource"]):
48	    """Read bytes from the marvin USB-device CDC ACM port via pyserial.
49	
50	    The firmware sink is DTR-gated (`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:216`); pyserial raises
51	    DTR by default on open, which triggers the firmware to re-emit a SESSION
52	    record. CDC ACM ignores baud rate; we still pass one because pyserial
53	    requires it.
54	    """
55	
56	    def __init__(
57	        self,
58	        port: str,
59	        *,
60	        baudrate: int = 921600,
61	        chunk_bytes: int = 4096,
62	        read_timeout_s: float = 0.1,
63	    ) -> None:
64	        self.port = port
65	        self.baudrate = baudrate
66	        self.chunk_bytes = chunk_bytes
67	        self.read_timeout_s = read_timeout_s
68	        self._ser: object | None = None
69	
70	    def __enter__(self) -> "SerialSource":
71	        # Imported lazily so file-only workflows do not require pyserial.
72	        import serial  # noqa: WPS433  (intentional lazy import)
73	
74	        self._ser = serial.Serial(
75	            port=self.port,
76	            baudrate=self.baudrate,
77	            timeout=self.read_timeout_s,
78	            dsrdtr=False,
79	        )
80	        # Make DTR explicit — some platforms default it off.
81	        try:
82	            self._ser.dtr = True  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
83	        except (OSError, AttributeError):
84	            pass
85	        return self
86	
87	    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:
88	        if self._ser is not None:
89	            try:
90	                self._ser.close()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
91	            finally:
92	                self._ser = None
93	
94	    def send_command(self, framed: bytes) -> int:
95	        """Write pre-framed command bytes to the device.
96	
97	        Caller frames via `framing.frame_encode`. Returns bytes written.
98	        """
99	        if self._ser is None:
100	            raise RuntimeError("SerialSource must be used as a context manager")
101	        return self._ser.write(framed)  # type: ignore[attr-defined,no-any-return]
102	
103	    def read_chunk(self) -> bytes:
104	        """One read of whatever has arrived; possibly empty on timeout.
105	
106	        Lets a caller drive the framer with its own deadline/idle logic
107	        (e.g. `snapshot`) instead of the infinite `__iter__` loop.
108	        """
109	        if self._ser is None:
110	            raise RuntimeError("SerialSource must be used as a context manager")
111	        ser = self._ser
112	        n = max(1, getattr(ser, "in_waiting", 0))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
113	        return ser.read(min(n, self.chunk_bytes))  # type: ignore[attr-defined,no-any-return]
114	
115	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[bytes]:
116	        if self._ser is None:
117	            raise RuntimeError("SerialSource must be used as a context manager")
118	        ser = self._ser
119	        while True:
120	            # `read` with timeout returns whatever has arrived (possibly empty
121	            # on timeout). `in_waiting` lets us drain the OS buffer in one go
122	            # when bytes are already queued.
123	            n = max(1, getattr(ser, "in_waiting", 0))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
124	            chunk: bytes = ser.read(min(n, self.chunk_bytes))  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
125	            if chunk:
126	                yield chunk
127	
128	
129
```
