```text
1	# marvin-perf
2	
3	Host-side decoder and analyzer for the marvin firmware **perf-log** wire format.
4	
5	The firmware emits framed binary records (schema version 5) over its USB-device
6	CDC ACM port. This tool consumes that stream live, records it to disk, and
7	replays captures offline. Summary analyses (latency attribution, drop
8	accounting, stack high-water trends) are produced by the `serve` viewer, not a
9	standalone CLI verb.
10	
11	Wire format source-of-truth lives in the firmware tree at
12	[`firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h`](../../firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h).
13	The Python schema mirror in [`marvin_perf/records.py`](marvin_perf/records.py)
14	must match it byte-for-byte; bump `EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` (Python side) and
15	`PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` (firmware side) together.
16	
17	## Setup
18	
19	All Python work runs through [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). First-time
20	bootstrap:
21	
22	    cd tools/marvin-perf
23	    uv sync --group viewer   # include viewer deps for the serve command
24	
25	`uv sync` creates `.venv/` and writes `uv.lock`. Subsequent invocations use the
26	existing venv automatically. Omit `--group viewer` if you only need the headless
27	CLI helpers (record, set-mask, set-overlay, snapshot, export-ml).
28	
29	## Usage
30	
31	    # Launch the visual review server (default when no subcommand is given)
32	    uv run marvin-perf
33	    uv run marvin-perf serve
34	    uv run marvin-perf serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765
35	    uv run marvin-perf serve --capture session.bin   # pre-load a capture on startup
36	
37	    # Capture raw bytes from the marvin USB-device CDC port
38	    uv run marvin-perf record --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --out session.bin
39	    uv run marvin-perf record --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --out-dir session/   # perf.bin + manifest.json
40	
41	    # Push a type-mask to a running device without attaching for capture
42	    uv run marvin-perf set-mask --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --types ALL
43	
44	    # Toggle the per-fret target rings on the SENSING strip
45	    uv run marvin-perf set-overlay --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --on
46	
47	    # Capture one full video frame from a running device and save it
48	    uv run marvin-perf snapshot --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --out snapshots/
49	
50	    # Export a capture as a SensiML-format CSV for MPLAB ML training
51	    uv run marvin-perf export-ml session/ --out session.csv --labels actuator-fb
52	
53	## Tests
54	
55	    uv run pytest
56	
57	Fixtures under [`tests/fixtures/`](tests/fixtures/) are hand-built byte streams
58	covering one frame per record type plus framing edge cases (FCS mismatch,
59	truncated payload, mid-stream join needing SOF resync).
60
```

189	    return TaskHighwater(hdr=hdr, task_id=task_id, words=words)

192	def _decode_task_runtime(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> TaskRuntime:
193	    _check(payload, TaskRuntime.SIZE, "TaskRuntime")
194	    task_id, state, priority, _reserved, run_time_counter, _reserved2 = (
195	        TaskRuntime._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
196	    )
197	    return TaskRuntime(
198	        hdr=hdr,
199	        task_id=task_id,
200	        state=state,
201	        priority=priority,
202	        run_time_counter=run_time_counter,
203	    )
204	
205	
206	def _decode_strip(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Strip:
207	    if len(payload) < STRIP_HDR_BYTES:
208	        raise DecodeError(
209	            f"Strip: payload {len(payload)} < header {STRIP_HDR_BYTES}"
210	        )
211	    x, y, w, h, kind, flags, _reserved = _STRIP_BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
212	    expected_pixels = w * h * STRIP_BPP
213	    if expected_pixels > STRIP_MAX_BYTES:
214	        raise DecodeError(
215	            f"Strip: w*h*bpp {expected_pixels} > max {STRIP_MAX_BYTES}"
216	        )
217	    expected_total = STRIP_HDR_BYTES + expected_pixels
218	    if len(payload) != expected_total:
219	        raise DecodeError(
220	            f"Strip: payload {len(payload)} != expected {expected_total} "
221	            f"({w}×{h}×{STRIP_BPP})"
222	        )
223	    bgr = bytes(payload[STRIP_HDR_BYTES:expected_total])
224	    return Strip(hdr=hdr, x=x, y=y, w=w, h=h, kind=kind, flags=flags, bgr=bgr)
225	
226	
227	_DISPATCH = {
228	    RecordType.SESSION: _decode_session,
229	    RecordType.STAMP: _decode_stamp,
230	    RecordType.DETECTOR: _decode_detector,
231	    RecordType.TIMING: _decode_timing,
232	    RecordType.DROP: _decode_drop,
233	    RecordType.TASK_HIGHWATER: _decode_task_highwater,
234	    RecordType.TASK_RUNTIME: _decode_task_runtime,
235	    RecordType.STRIP: _decode_strip,
236	    RecordType.DETECTOR_CONFIG: _decode_detector_config,
237	    RecordType.ACTUATOR: _decode_actuator,
238	    RecordType.FRETBOARD_RAW: _decode_fretboard_raw,
239	}
240	
241	
242	def decode_record(payload: bytes) -> Record:
243	    """Decode an FCS-validated frame payload into a typed Record dataclass.
244	
245	    Caller (framing.iter_frames) has already verified FCS and length sanity.
246	    Unknown record types are surfaced as UnknownRecord so a forward-schema
247	    firmware does not crash an older host.
248	    """
249	    if len(payload) < HDR_SIZE:
250	        raise DecodeError(f"payload {len(payload)} < HDR_SIZE {HDR_SIZE}")
251	    hdr = Header.unpack(payload)
252	    if hdr.magic != PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC:
253	        raise DecodeError(f"bad magic 0x{hdr.magic:04x}")
254	
255	    decoder = _DISPATCH.get(hdr.type)
256	    if decoder is None:
257	        return UnknownRecord(hdr=hdr, raw=payload)
258	    return decoder(hdr, payload)
259

15	 * USB-device CDC sink. Drop-on-full, never block. The pipeline must
16	 * remain unaffected if perf-log vanishes.

18	 * All emit calls take ≈O(memcpy) and never lock. The ISR variants use
19	 * xQueueSendFromISR; the task variants use xQueueSend with zero block
20	 * time. Choose by call site — passing the wrong one will not corrupt
21	 * state but may misuse the higher_priority_task_woken pathway. */

5	firmware-emitted captures become available (post-producer-wiring), drop them
6	into tests/fixtures/ as `.bin` files and add a parametrized test asserting the

8	code with the host CRC keeps the algorithm under test.

191	def build_strip_payload(
192	    *,
193	    frame_epoch: int = 1,
194	    kind: int = int(StripKind.SENSING),
195	    x: int = 240,
196	    y: int = 295,
197	    w: int = 4,
198	    h: int = 2,
199	    flags: int = 0,
200	    fill: int = 0x55,
201	) -> bytes:
202	    body = _STRIP_BODY.pack(x, y, w, h, kind, flags, b"\x00\x00")
203	    bgr = bytes((fill,) * (w * h * STRIP_BPP))
204	    return build_header(RecordType.STRIP, frame_epoch=frame_epoch) + body + bgr
205	
206	
207	# ─── Frame wrapper (SOF + LEN + payload + FCS) ───────────────────────────────
208	
209	
210	def wrap_frame(payload: bytes, *, corrupt_fcs: bool = False) -> bytes:
211	    length = len(payload)
212	    length_bytes = struct.pack("<H", length)
213	    fcs = fletcher16(length_bytes + payload)
214	    if corrupt_fcs:
215	        fcs ^= 0xFFFF
216	    return SOF_BYTES + length_bytes + payload + struct.pack("<H", fcs)

20	/* USB-device CDC ACM sink. The MCC config provides USB_DEVICE_Initialize

22	 * machine: open the device handle, register event handlers, attach
23	 * on VBUS, and provide a write API for the perf-log drain task.
24	 *
25	 * Single producer (the drain task). Not thread-safe by design: a second
26	 * writer would race on s_tx_head and could allocate the same ring slot
27	 * twice. */
28	
29	/* Header(6) + max payload (sizeof perf_rec_strip_t) + CRC(2), padded up
30	 * to a cache-line multiple so UDPHS DMA can't share a line with whatever
31	 * sits next to us in BSS. Derived from PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES so the two
32	 * constants can't drift — a too-small sink buffer silently rejects
33	 * larger strips at the size check, accumulating dropped_sink. */
34	#define SINK_FRAME_BYTES_RAW  (6u + PERF_STRIP_HDR_BYTES + PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES + 2u)
35	#define SINK_FRAME_BYTES_MAX  ((SINK_FRAME_BYTES_RAW + 63u) & ~63u)

38	 * permit N concurrent in-flight writes:

40	 *   - CDC per-instance queueSizeWrite                       (usb_device_init_data.c via MCC yml)
41	 *   - USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED minus RX/notif use (configuration.h via MCC yml)
42	 * MCC config has all three sized for N=3; bump together if changed. */
43	#define SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH    3u
44	
45	#define SINK_OPEN_RETRY_MS    50u
46	#define SINK_CONFIG_WAIT_MS   100u
47	#define SINK_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS 100u

50	static volatile bool           s_is_configured;

60	/* Counting semaphore: tokens = ring slots free for the producer to fill.
61	 * Init = SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH (all slots free). Take before claiming a
62	 * slot; ISR gives one back per WRITE_COMPLETE. */
63	static SemaphoreHandle_t s_tx_credits;
64	static StaticSemaphore_t s_tx_credits_buf;

66	/* Staging ring for outgoing frames. UDPHS DMAs from these addresses;

68	 * multiple of CACHE_LINE_SIZE keeps every inner buffer line-aligned
69	 * so the driver's cache-maintenance ops don't collide with neighbors.
70	 * s_tx_head advances one slot per accepted submission; producer is the
71	 * single drain task so no lock is needed. */
72	static uint8_t CACHE_ALIGN s_tx_ring[SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH][SINK_FRAME_BYTES_MAX];
73	static uint32_t s_tx_head;

78	#define SINK_RX_BUF_BYTES  512u
79	static uint8_t CACHE_ALIGN s_rx_buf[SINK_RX_BUF_BYTES];

81	static void prime_rx_read(void)

83	    USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE th = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
84	    (void)USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0, &th,
85	                              s_rx_buf, SINK_RX_BUF_BYTES);

88	/* Fletcher-16 (mod 255, init 0xFFFF). USB hardware already CRCs every
89	 * bulk packet on the wire, so this checksum's job is *framing-layer*
90	 * detection only — false SOF matches during resync, firmware bugs that
91	 * write a wrong LEN or a partial frame. Fletcher catches single-byte
92	 * changes, adjacent swaps, and most non-adjacent swaps with ~1/65536
93	 * accidental-match rate against random byte streams — plenty for that
94	 * job, at ~2 cycles/byte vs ~6 for a table-driven CRC-16. Block-mod
95	 * pattern from RFC 1146 / Wikipedia: defer the modulo until uint32
96	 * could overflow, which gives ~5800 iterations between reductions. */
97	static uint16_t fletcher16(uint16_t init, const uint8_t *p, uint16_t len)
98	{
99	    uint32_t s1 = (uint32_t)(init & 0xFFu);
100	    uint32_t s2 = (uint32_t)((init >> 8) & 0xFFu);
101	
102	    while (len > 0u)
103	    {
104	        uint16_t blk = (len > 5802u) ? 5802u : len;
105	        len = (uint16_t)(len - blk);
106	        do
107	        {
108	            s1 += *p++;
109	            s2 += s1;
110	            blk--;
111	        } while (blk > 0u);
112	        s1 %= 255u;
113	        s2 %= 255u;
114	    }
115	
116	    return (uint16_t)((s2 << 8) | s1);
117	}

196	{

198	
199	    switch (event)

201	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_RESET:
202	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_DECONFIGURED:
203	            s_is_configured = false;

214	                LOG_INFO("PERF: USB device CDC configured\r\n");
215	                prime_rx_read();
216	            }
217	            break;
218	        }
219	
220	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_POWER_DETECTED:
221	            (void)USB_DEVICE_Attach(s_dev_handle);
222	            break;
223	
224	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_POWER_REMOVED:
225	            (void)USB_DEVICE_Detach(s_dev_handle);

227	            break;
228	
229	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_SUSPENDED:
230	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_RESUMED:
231	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_SOF:
232	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_ERROR:
233	        default:
234	            break;
235	    }
236	}

238	/* ─── Public sink interface ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */
239	
240	void PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize(void)
241	{
242	    s_tx_credits = xSemaphoreCreateCountingStatic(SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH,
243	                                                  SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH,
244	                                                  &s_tx_credits_buf);
245	    configASSERT(s_tx_credits != NULL);
246	
247	    PerfLogRx_Initialize();
248	
249	    /* Open may fail until USB_DEVICE_Initialize finishes its own first
250	     * task tick — retry until success. Drain task is alive at this
251	     * point so vTaskDelay is fine. */
252	    while (s_dev_handle == USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID)
253	    {
254	        s_dev_handle = USB_DEVICE_Open(USB_DEVICE_INDEX_0,
255	                                       DRV_IO_INTENT_READWRITE);
256	        if (s_dev_handle == USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID)
257	        {
258	            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(SINK_OPEN_RETRY_MS));
259	        }
260	    }
261	
262	    USB_DEVICE_EventHandlerSet(s_dev_handle, device_event_handler, 0u);
263	
264	    /* Cold-boot-with-cable case: by the time we register the handler the
265	     * UDPHS driver may have already raced past the VBUS edge it needed
266	     * to fire POWER_DETECTED, or the host may have seen a brief pull-up
267	     * assertion during early boot and given up retrying. Force a clean
268	     * detach→short delay→attach edge so the host sees an unambiguous
269	     * device-arrival on the bus. Hot-plug after this point is unaffected
270	     * because POWER_REMOVED/POWER_DETECTED still drive Detach/Attach. */
271	    (void)USB_DEVICE_Detach(s_dev_handle);
272	    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(100));
273	    (void)USB_DEVICE_Attach(s_dev_handle);
274	
275	    LOG_INFO("PERF: USB device opened, waiting for host enumeration\r\n");
276	}
277	
278	bool PerfLogSinkCdc_IsConnected(void)
279	{
280	    return s_is_configured && s_cls.dtr;
281	}
282	
283	void PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(const void *payload, uint16_t len)
284	{
285	    if (!s_is_configured || !s_cls.dtr)
286	    {
287	        PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop((uint32_t)len);
288	        return;
289	    }
290	
291	    uint16_t total = (uint16_t)(6u + len + 2u);
292	    if (total > SINK_FRAME_BYTES_MAX)
293	    {
294	        PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop((uint32_t)len);
295	        return;
296	    }
297	
298	    /* Wait for a free ring slot. With N=3 against the lower CDC layer's
299	     * 3-deep transfer queue, this only blocks when the host has stalled
300	     * — under load the producer pipelines at the rate ISR returns
301	     * credits. Timeout drops the record and lets the next sink state-
302	     * machine pass observe DECONFIGURED if the host went away. */
303	    if (xSemaphoreTake(s_tx_credits,
304	                       pdMS_TO_TICKS(SINK_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS)) != pdTRUE)
305	    {
306	        PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop((uint32_t)len);
307	        return;
308	    }
309	
310	    uint8_t *frame = s_tx_ring[s_tx_head];
311	
312	    frame[0] = 0x55u;
313	    frame[1] = 0x4Du;
314	    frame[2] = 0x52u;
315	    frame[3] = 0x56u;
316	    frame[4] = (uint8_t)(len & 0xFFu);
317	    frame[5] = (uint8_t)((len >> 8) & 0xFFu);
318	    memcpy(&frame[6], payload, len);
319	
320	    uint16_t fcs = fletcher16(0xFFFFu, &frame[4], (uint16_t)(2u + len));
321	    frame[6u + len]      = (uint8_t)(fcs & 0xFFu);
322	    frame[6u + len + 1u] = (uint8_t)((fcs >> 8) & 0xFFu);
323	
324	    USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE th = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
325	    USB_DEVICE_CDC_RESULT r = USB_DEVICE_CDC_Write(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0,
326	                                                  &th,
327	                                                  frame, total,
328	                                                  USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_FLAGS_DATA_COMPLETE);
329	    if (r != USB_DEVICE_CDC_RESULT_OK)
330	    {
331	        /* Submission rejected: ISR won't fire for this slot, so hand
332	         * the credit back ourselves. Slot stays free; head doesn't
333	         * advance. */
334	        (void)xSemaphoreGive(s_tx_credits);
335	        PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop((uint32_t)len);
336	        return;
337	    }
338	
339	    s_tx_head = (s_tx_head + 1u) % SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH;
340	}

# Plan: marvin-perf full-rate score-block capture

## Context
The gameplay score reader (phase 5) works, but its digit templates are built from only ~9
hand-picked frames, so held-out accuracy is 10/16 (all misses low-margin →8 confusions from
sparse per-digit exemplars). We need many more exemplars of each glyph, tear-free. Rather than
hand-label lots of full frames, capture just the **scoring block** (`SCORE_BLOCK_ROI =
(114,309,210,414)`, 96×105 px) at full frame rate to disk, so a short play sweeps every digit
0–9 many times. The block also happens to be the reader's registration fiducial. Scores climb
monotonically within a play, which (plus a visual read) lets the frames be auto-labelled cheaply
downstream — no bulk manual labelling.

10	/* Video pipeline: HDMI source → TC358743 bridge → CSI-2 → CSI2DC → ISC →
11	 * DDR. This module is the capture *producer*: it owns its own FreeRTOS task
12	 * (tc358743, isc_capture, capture state machine) and fans completed frames out
13	 * to subscribers from the ISC IRQ via xQueueSendFromISR.
14	 *
15	 * Display (the HEO hardware layer that scans a captured frame to the LCD) is
16	 * owned by the compositor (ui_manager), NOT here — capture and display are fully
17	 * independent (the detector/gameplay consume frames whether or not HEO is shown).
18	 * The module notifies the compositor through two registered callbacks so the
19	 * compositor can own all HEO/BASE register writes while keeping the timing this
20	 * task/IRQ already has:
21	 *   - a display-reconcile callback, called each task tick with the current source
22	 *     validity + size, so the compositor can (re)bind/unbind HEO in task context;
23	 *   - a frame-latch callback, called from the ISC IRQ with the freshest completed
24	 *     buffer address, so the compositor can latch HEO to the newest ring slot.
25	 *
26	 * Defaults at Initialize: capture disabled, no callbacks. */
27	
28	void Video_Initialize(void);
29	
30	/* Capture chain control. ENABLE: arm ISC + bridge stream when source
31	 * is locked, re-arm on every lost/regain cycle. DISABLE: stop ISC +
32	 * stream and stay off regardless of lock state. */
33	void Video_CaptureEnable(void);
34	void Video_CaptureDisable(void);
35	
36	/* Register the compositor's HEO hooks (see the module note above). Both are
37	 * optional (NULL = no display). Set before the video task starts.
38	 *   frame-latch: fires in ISC IRQ context with the just-completed buffer address.
39	 *   reconcile:   fires each task tick with (source_valid, src_w, src_h). */
40	void Video_SetFrameLatchCallback(void (*cb)(uint32_t buffer_addr));
41	void Video_SetDisplayReconcileCallback(void (*cb)(bool source_valid,
42	                                                  uint16_t src_w, uint16_t src_h));
43	
44	/* Frame metadata delivered to subscribers on every captured frame. */
45	typedef struct
46	{
47	    void    *buffer;          /* pointer to most-recent complete frame in DDR */
48	    uint32_t frame_count;     /* monotonic since last ISC start */
49	    uint16_t width;
50	    uint16_t height;
51	    uint16_t bytes_per_pixel;
52	} Video_FrameInfo;
53	
54	/* Subscribe a queue to frame-ready events. The video module sends a
55	 * Video_FrameInfo from the ISC frame-done IRQ via xQueueSendFromISR
56	 * each time a frame completes to DDR — fanned out to every subscribed
57	 * queue. Create the queue with:
58	 *   QueueHandle_t q = xQueueCreate(N, sizeof(Video_FrameInfo));
59	 *
60	 * Per-subscriber depth chooses the back-pressure policy. Depth 1 means
61	 * "process most recent frame, drop the rest" — when a frame arrives and
62	 * the queue is full, the IRQ's xQueueSendFromISR returns errQUEUE_FULL
63	 * and the frame is dropped for that subscriber. Deeper queues preserve
64	 * frames at the cost of memory and added latency. Each subscriber chooses
65	 * independently.
66	 *
67	 * The Video_FrameInfo.buffer pointer reflects the buffer that *just*
68	 * completed (one of the descriptor-ring slots). With NUM_BUFFERS > 2 a
69	 * subscriber can hold the pointer for multiple frame-times before the
70	 * ring laps it; with NUM_BUFFERS = 2 the buffer is overwritten on the
71	 * second-next frame.
72	 *
73	 * Returns false if the subscriber table is full. Calling with a queue
74	 * already in the table is a no-op success. Up to VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS
75	 * concurrent subscribers (currently 4). */
76	bool Video_SubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q);
77	
78	/* Remove a queue from the subscriber list. Returns false if not found. */
79	bool Video_UnsubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q);
80	
81	/* Synchronous read of the current frame state. Doesn't block. May
82	 * report frame_count = 0 / buffer = NULL if capture has never armed. */
83	void Video_GetFrameInfo(Video_FrameInfo *info);

85	/* Detected active-picture rectangle within the captured frame.

87	 * A component→HDMI source (the Wii bridge) frames its active raster with dead
88	 * black bars whose thickness varies by console/converter, so the active area is
89	 * detected at runtime — the union of the bright-pixel bounds over the first
90	 * frames after capture arms, locked once it clears a minimum size. Detection is
91	 * one-shot per capture arm (reset on re-arm / source-size change).
92	 *
93	 * Returns true with the locked rect (x,y = top-left offset, w,h = size, all in
94	 * source pixels) once detected; false until then, filling *x=*y=0 and *w/*h =
95	 * the full frame — a safe full-frame fallback so callers always get a usable
96	 * rect. Any NULL out-param is skipped. */
97	bool Video_GetActiveRect(uint16_t *x, uint16_t *y, uint16_t *w, uint16_t *h);

1	"""Reassemble PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT band strips into a full frame and save it.
2	
3	The device answers a snapshot command with a top-to-bottom run of full-width
4	`STRIP` records (kind SNAPSHOT), all sharing one `frame_epoch`; the final band
5	sets `STRIP_FLAG_LAST`. This module groups bands by `frame_epoch`, pastes them
6	onto a canvas, and writes the result as a lossless `.png` (frame_epoch in a
7	tEXt chunk).
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
13	from pathlib import Path
14	
15	from .records import STRIP_BPP, Strip, StripKind
16	
17	
18	@dataclass(frozen=True)
19	class CompletedSnapshot:
20	    width: int
21	    height: int
22	    frame_epoch: int
23	    bgr: bytes  # width * height * 3, row-major, top-to-bottom
24	
25	    @property
26	    def n_bytes(self) -> int:
27	        return self.width * self.height * STRIP_BPP
28	
29	
30	class SnapshotError(Exception):
31	    pass
32	
33	
34	@dataclass
35	class _Pending:
36	    width: int
37	    bands: dict[int, Strip] = field(default_factory=dict)  # keyed by band y
38	    last_y: int | None = None  # y of the band flagged LAST
39	
40	
41	class SnapshotAssembler:
42	    """Feed decoded `Strip` records; get a `CompletedSnapshot` when done.
43	
44	    `add()` ignores non-SNAPSHOT strips and returns None until a snapshot's
45	    LAST band has arrived and every row from 0..height is covered, at which
46	    point it returns the assembled frame (and forgets that frame_epoch).
47	    """
48	
49	    def __init__(self) -> None:
50	        self._pending: dict[int, _Pending] = {}
51	
52	    def add(self, strip: Strip) -> CompletedSnapshot | None:
53	        if strip.kind != int(StripKind.SNAPSHOT):
54	            return None
55	        if strip.x != 0:
56	            raise SnapshotError(f"snapshot band at x={strip.x}, expected full-width")
57	
58	        epoch = strip.hdr.frame_epoch
59	        p = self._pending.get(epoch)
60	        if p is None:
61	            p = _Pending(width=strip.w)
62	            self._pending[epoch] = p
63	        elif strip.w != p.width:
64	            raise SnapshotError(
65	                f"snapshot band width {strip.w} != {p.width} (frame_epoch {epoch})"
66	            )
67	
68	        p.bands[strip.y] = strip
69	        if strip.is_last:
70	            p.last_y = strip.y
71	
72	        if p.last_y is None:
73	            return None
74	        return self._try_finalize(epoch, p)
75	
76	    def _try_finalize(self, epoch: int, p: _Pending) -> CompletedSnapshot | None:
77	        # Walk contiguous bands from y=0; bail (keep waiting) on any gap.
78	        canvas = bytearray()
79	        y = 0
80	        height = 0
81	        while y in p.bands:
82	            band = p.bands[y]
83	            canvas += band.bgr
84	            height = y + band.h
85	            y += band.h
86	        if p.last_y is None or height <= p.last_y:
87	            return None  # not yet contiguous through the LAST band
88	
89	        del self._pending[epoch]
90	        return CompletedSnapshot(
91	            width=p.width, height=height, frame_epoch=epoch, bgr=bytes(canvas)
92	        )
93	
94	
95	def save_snapshot(snap: CompletedSnapshot, out: str | Path) -> list[Path]:
96	    """Write the snapshot as a lossless PNG and return its path.
97	
98	    `out` may carry a .png suffix (or a stale .bgr/.json, stripped) or be a bare
99	    stem; the result is always `<stem>.png`. PNG is lossless for the packed RGB
100	    pixels, so no separate raw buffer is needed; `frame_epoch` rides along in a
101	    tEXt chunk rather than a sidecar JSON.
102	    """
103	    base = Path(out)
104	    if base.suffix.lower() in (".bgr", ".png", ".json"):
105	        base = base.with_suffix("")
106	    base.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
107	
108	    try:
109	        from PIL import Image, PngImagePlugin
110	    except ImportError as e:  # pragma: no cover - Pillow is a base dependency
111	        raise SnapshotError("Pillow is required to save snapshots as PNG") from e
112	
113	    # Pillow's "raw" decoder maps BGR → RGB without a manual per-pixel swap.
114	    img = Image.frombytes("RGB", (snap.width, snap.height), snap.bgr, "raw", "BGR")
115	    meta = PngImagePlugin.PngInfo()
116	    meta.add_text("frame_epoch", str(snap.frame_epoch))
117	
118	    png_path = base.with_suffix(".png")
119	    img.save(png_path, pnginfo=meta)
120	    return [png_path]
121
```

227:#### 4.2.2 Detector model

240:    uint32_t frame_epoch;     // master sync token (§4.6.4)
252:Fields are fixed-width, naturally aligned, little-endian — this is also the on-disk record layout for the state log (§4.6.5). `frame_epoch` is the master clock for cross-detector and cross-recording sync.
254:#### 4.2.4 Bus mechanics
261:#### 4.2.5 Reference-detector responsibilities
269:#### 4.2.6 Open questions surfaced here
271:- Initial CV algorithm — pixel-mean threshold per ROI, edge-trough, optical-flow-based, or learned. (Defer; bring up the simplest first to validate end-to-end.)
274:### 4.3 Fretboard link ✅
278:Direct **FLEXCOM1 USART** link between marvin and the fretboard MCU — a plain UART wire, no USB. marvin's `PA28` (FLEXCOM1_IO0, `GUITAR_TX`) and `PA29` (FLEXCOM1_IO1, `GUITAR_RX`) connect to the fretboard's SERCOM1 (`PB01` RX / `PB00` TX). Both ends run **500 000 baud, 8N1**. The FLEXCOM1 USART runs in Harmony ring-buffer mode so RX never drops bytes between reads. (Was FLEXCOM2 until the console moved onto FLEXCOM2 — see §4.9.)
281:- **Fretboard → marvin:** raw ADC stream (5 channels × 16-bit) at 240 Hz, in a 17-byte start/end-bracketed frame (`0x03 … 0xFC`, with `sample_seq` + `applied_mask`). The FLEXCOM1 RX ring fills continuously from its ISR; a persistent read-threshold notification wakes `fretboard_rx_task`, which drains the ring, resyncs on the frame markers, and republishes each valid frame as a `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` perf-log record (default-disabled, host enables via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`). This is the on-board capture path until the SD-card recorder lands; it's also the substrate for the future `adc_fretboard` detector (§4.2).
283:- **Fauxmote link (T1S build only):** with the guitar node on T1S, FLEXCOM1 is free, so in the T1S build marvin brings up a link to the fauxmote board (ESP32 Wiimote emulator, §7 top-level SPEC) on FLEXCOM1 (`net/fauxmote/fauxmote_link.c`, `Fauxmote_Initialize`). It mirrors every gameplay bitmask — `FretboardLink_Send` taps `Fauxmote_SendGuitarMask` — and is inspected/controlled via the `fauxmote` console command (§4.9).
285:### 4.4 Timing pipeline 🚧
297:### 4.5 UI / operator surface 🚧
311:**Presentation layer (decided 2026-06-25).** For the *presentation* half of Q5: keep **Legato as the renderer**, add a thin marvin **compositor over the GFX Canvas component** — pre-render panels into static non-cached RAM surfaces and multiplex the two free LCDC overlay layers (`OVR1`/`OVR2`) across them for instant reveal/slide without redrawing what's behind. Authoritative design in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md). This does not dictate per-screen *authoring* (MGS vs. custom widgets).
313:**Fonts — DejaVu Sans Mono only (decided 2026-06-30).** For licensing reasons the UI uses **only the DejaVu Sans Mono family** (`DejaVuSansMono_*`, `DejaVuSansMonoBold_*`). Any new text — labels, widgets, dynamic strings — must use a DejaVu Sans Mono face; do **not** introduce other faces (e.g. the figma-imported Menlo / NotoSans assets MGS may pull in). The DejaVu mono faces are subsetted with `0x20–0x7E`, `0xA0–0xFF`, and `0x2605` (★), so Latin-1 plus the tier star are available. Some legacy MGS-imported faces remain in the generated font set and are a known cleanup item — migrate them to DejaVu over time.
315:### 4.6 Reference-data recording & export 🚧
317:#### 4.6.1 Goals (in priority order)
325:#### 4.6.2 Transport — SD card
349:#### 4.6.3 Format — detector-state + sparse keyframes
356:    ├── manifest.json          // session metadata, calibration snapshot, detector versions
358:    ├── commands.bin           // emitted fret/strum commands with frame_epoch
359:    ├── adc_raw.bin            // raw fretboard ADC stream with frame_epoch interleave
361:        ├── 000000.bgr         // raw BGR888 keyframe (no encoder), filename = frame_epoch
367:- **`commands.bin`** — fret/strum bitmask + direction + emit timestamp + frame_epoch, ~16 B per emit. Sparse.
368:- **`adc_raw.bin`** — fretboard 17-byte frames at 240 Hz with `frame_epoch` annotation = ~4.1 KB/s. Modest. Until the SD recorder lands, the same data is available live as `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` records (28 B framed) in any marvin-perf capture (default-disabled; enable with `set-mask`).
372:Filename convention: directory name is ISO-8601 timestamp at session start (UTC); keyframe filenames are zero-padded `frame_epoch` so chronological order matches lexical order.
374:#### 4.6.4 Sync token — `frame_epoch`
376:A 32-bit counter incremented by the video task on every captured ISC frame (rolls over after ~830 days @ 60 Hz). Every record in a session — `state.bin`, `commands.bin`, `adc_raw.bin`, keyframe filenames, off-board detector data — is keyed by `frame_epoch`. This is the master clock for the entire system, including any later-added detectors that record independently and need to align their data with marvin's.
378:For records that don't fall on a frame boundary (ADC samples emitted between video frames), the most-recent `frame_epoch` is used and the sub-frame offset is captured by `timestamp_us`.
380:#### 4.6.5 manifest.json
402:#### 4.6.6 On-device buffering
404:A FreeRTOS task (`record_task`) owns SD writes. State / command / ADC streams are small and write through directly. Keyframes are larger — a single keyframe at 1.04 MB cannot block the video pipeline, so the record task receives a **frame buffer pointer** (the same DDR buffer the ISC writes into; refcounted by the video task) and writes from DDR while the next frame is being captured into another buffer. We need ≥ 3 capture frame buffers (one capturing, one displaying, one being recorded) when recording is active; today the video task already has multiple frames pre-allocated — exact count is verified during implementation.
408:#### 4.6.7 Off-board detectors recording independently
412:- Subscribe to marvin's `frame_epoch` over a chosen link (UART/Ethernet/etc.).
413:- Record its own observations (e.g. its own sensor data + its own detector output) in its own format, *keyed by marvin's `frame_epoch`*.
414:- Be aligned post-hoc against marvin's reference recording during training.
416:The spec does not constrain how off-board detectors store their data — only the sync contract (`frame_epoch` timeline) is canonical.
418:#### 4.6.8 On-demand full-frame snapshot (USB CDC) ✅
420:Independent of the SD recording path above (M4, not started), marvin can export a single full-resolution frame on demand over the existing perf-log USB CDC link. The host sends `PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT`; the perf-drain task copies the current frame once into a staging buffer and streams it back as a top-to-bottom run of full-width `PERF_STRIP_SNAPSHOT` band records (each ≤ `PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES`), all sharing one `frame_epoch`, the last flagged `PERF_STRIP_FLAG_LAST`. Bands are written straight to the sink (bypassing the small strip pool) and paced by the wire; emit is not gated by the STRIP type mask. `marvin-perf snapshot` reassembles and saves the frame (`.bgr` + sidecar `.json`, plus `.png` via Pillow). This is the offline-study on-ramp for the game-state work (§4.8) — no in-runtime role.
422:### 4.7 System services 🚧
428:- **Config persistence** ✅ implemented on **QSPI NOR flash**, not the SD card (resolves Q9). `flash/settings.c` maintains a power-fail-safe 256-byte-slot ring-log (`MVST` magic + CRC), exposing `Settings_Load/Get/Save/SetBacklight`. Today it persists the backlight brightness, which is restored at splash (`ui_manager.c`); the `settings` console command dumps/saves/wipes/stress-tests the store. Loads at first use, before the scheduler if needed, and survives with no card present; absent/invalid record → compiled-in defaults. Additional fields (calibration values, mode toggles, recording stride) extend the same record.
432:### 4.8 Game-state awareness & control 🚧
434:Note on numbering: this subsystem is logically a peer of §4.2–§4.6 (a video-frame consumer that emits typed events plus a controller that issues actuator commands). It lives at §4.8 only to avoid renumbering existing sections referenced from the journal and milestones.
436:#### 4.8.1 Role
443:This is *not* the gameplay note-detection path (§4.2). cv_marvin_v1 plays notes during gameplay; the game-state module decides *what to play* at the session level (which song, which difficulty, which mode) and gets us there from any starting screen.
445:Recognition is bootstrapped offline: the on-demand snapshot path (§4.6.8) collects a corpus of real GH3 screens, detection algorithms are prototyped host-side in Python (`tools/gameplay/`) against that corpus, and only the proven GH3-specific logic is ported into the firmware `gameplay_engine` module. Per Q10, the approach favors fixed-region/color/glyph matching over general CV — GH3's screens, fonts, and layouts are static.
451:#### 4.8.2 Module shape
459:#### 4.8.3 Game catalog & menu metadata
463:- **Recognizer templates.** Per-state visual signatures used by the CV recognizer — could be small reference images (template matching), color histograms, or text regions for OCR. Format chosen with the recognizer algorithm (open Q10).
477:`setlist` is the string `main`/`bonus` (the same key the art filenames use); `title`/`artist`/`album`/`genre`/`difficulty` are CSV-quoted (may contain commas; any may be empty); `bpm`/`length_s`/`year` are integers, `0` when unknown. Rows may be sparse or out of order — only `(setlist, index)` is the key. `title`/`artist`/`album` come from the `SONGS` table in `tools/fetch_gh3_cover_art.py`, whose `--catalog` mode also fills `year`/`genre` from MusicBrainz; `bpm`/`length_s`/`difficulty` are reserved-but-blank (GH3 surfaces no per-song difficulty — the only authentic signal is the career tier, deferred).
487:#### 4.8.4 Interaction with other subsystems
490:- **Timing pipeline (§4.4):** during gameplay the timing pipeline drives the actuators from detector-state. Outside gameplay it's idle, and the game-state controller drives actuators directly. Coordination and arbitration between the two is open Q11.
495:#### 4.8.5 Open questions surfaced here
499:- **Q10** — Recognizer algorithm: template matching vs simple OCR vs region/color heuristics vs a small CNN. Trade-off is robustness vs CPU cost vs metadata authoring effort.
502:#### 4.8.6 Performance results & player profiles 🚧

204	## 4. Subsystems
205	
206	### 4.1 Video capture & display ✅
207	
208	Working end-to-end. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md) and [`display_path.md`](display_path.md) for register-level detail. The video task (`video.c`, FreeRTOS) owns the capture pipeline and a frame queue that other tasks subscribe to. Display intent and capture intent are decoupled (commit `e28c497`); a software scaler can be inserted between capture and display when source ≠ panel native.
209	
210	**What this subsystem owns:**
211	- TC358743 init, source detection, EDID, format negotiation.
212	- ISC DMA configuration and frame buffer rotation in DDR.
213	- XLCDC overlay window placement (pillarbox/letterbox) for the active source.
214	- Frame-ready notification to subscribers (CV detect, recording, UI overlay).
215	
216	**What it doesn't own:**
217	- CV processing (§4.2).
218	- Recording / export (§4.6).
219	- UI widgets / chrome (§4.5) — only the pixel composition for the live-view layer.
220	
221	### 4.2 CV detection pipeline + detector-state bus 🚧
222

The renamed detail labels (Title/Artist/Album/Genre/Tier/Duration/Status) already used stable `LABEL_DASHBOARD_SONG_*` names, so only the new widgets needed wiring — dashboard code had no references to the removed decorative names.
8:- **Both time markers are runtime `leFixedString`s** (set up in `song_detail_init` alongside the Status label). `STOP_TIME` tracks the committed selection: `ScreenDashboard_ApplySelection` rewrites it with the song's `m:ss` (same `SongDetail_Duration` string shown in the DURATION field), "-" when unknown. `START_TIME` counts up with elapsed play time (see below); it resets to "0:00" on a fresh selection.
13:- **Tier string is stars-only** (separate ask): `SongDetail_TierText` drops the " TIER n" suffix — main-setlist songs show just ★×tier, bonus still "BONUS". Shared helper, so song-select dialog and dashboard both change.

31:- **Follow-up — `health` now shows a recent-window `cpu%`, not cumulative-since-boot.** The old table used `ulRunTimeCounter / total_since_boot`, a lifetime average with no decay — it buried *current* load under startup (e.g. VideoTask's boot-time active-area scan reading as a steady "13%" long after it had latched). `HealthMonitor_Report` now snapshots, waits `HM_REPORT_WINDOW_MS` (500 ms), snapshots again, and reports each task's share of *that* window (the supervisor's delta math, on demand). `health` takes ~½ s to answer and shows what tasks are doing *now*. (Separately noted: `detect_active` has a silent, no-give-up failure path — `frame_edges`-false re-scans the border every tick forever with no log; a bounded/observable fix is still pending.)
59:- **Supervisor** (prio 6 — above every app task, which top out at 5): samples the run-time-stats counters every 1 s and logs `RUNAWAY '<task>'` when one task eats the CPU while idle ~0%. It runs at higher priority than any spinner and uses its **own lock-free snapshot buffer** (never shares the heartbeat's mutex — a starved health task holding that mutex would otherwise deadlock the reporter exactly when needed), so it can name the culprit *during* the wedge. Also emits a `SUP: idle/top/isr%` summary every 10 s.
96:- **Observer hook added:** `GameplayEngine_GetLatest(game_state_t*)` — synchronous snapshot of the last classification, retained every classify (paired with `RequestObservation()` for a fresh read after each command). `game_state_t.selection` is the cursor index (static menus) / `gp_song_templates[]` index (song_select).

12:  - **Partial-repaint gotcha (fill-end artifacts):** `AaCorners_RenderRoundImage` re-blends existing pixels toward the backdrop and writes at full-rect coordinates via `_Unsafe` pixel ops (relative to the current frame/damage rect, no bounds check). `panel_aa` is safe because a panel repaints its whole rect. But the stock `setValue` damages only the delta strip between old/new value, so a mid-bar update leaves the frame rect a sliver — the corner writes land outside that tile (garbage) and, over many updates, erode the AA bands into the fill (visible in the first/last ~10%). Fix + smoothness in one: the bar is no longer driven by the stock value at all. `ProgressBarAA_SetPermille` stores a 0-1000 fill fraction and invalidates the *whole* widget; `aa_paint` lets the stock skin draw only the (square) track — the widget value stays 0 so the stock fill is skipped — then draws the fill itself as a `RectFill` of the exact pixel width, then rounds the corners. Full-widget repaint every change keeps the corner writes in-bounds and idempotent, and the pixel-width fill removes the 100-step quantization.
26:**2026-07-05 — `detect_active` no longer burns CPU while the source is dark.** Follow-on to the `cpu%` work below: VideoTask's active-area detector re-scanned the frame border **every 20 ms tick** while unlatched, and each *failed* scan (dark border) walked the whole band on uncached DDR (~2.6 ms) → ~13% whenever the source was dark (notably: booting while the Wii is asleep). Two fixes, and crucially **it still never gives up** — abandoning detection would permanently mis-frame a source that starts dark and later brightens:

# marvin-perf: scoping a `score-capture` (region-stream) verb

All paths absolute. Line refs are from the current tree.

## 1. End-to-end `snapshot` flow

`cmd_snapshot` is the model to copy. File: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/cli.py`.

**Resolve output path** (`_resolve_snapshot_out`, cli.py:174-193): if `--out` ends in `.png` it is used verbatim (parent `mkdir`); otherwise it is a directory and the next free `snapshot-NNNN.png` is chosen by globbing `snapshot-*.png`, regexing the numeric stem, and taking `max+1` (or 1). Note it computes **one** name — it does not stream-increment. Auto-increment across a run is done by re-calling it per frame in a loop (see §2).

**Send → drain → assemble → save** (`cmd_snapshot`, cli.py:196-233):
```python
out_path = _resolve_snapshot_out(args.out)
assembler = SnapshotAssembler()
with SerialSource(args.port) as ser:
    ser.send_command(frame_encode(encode_snapshot_payload()))   # cli.py:208
    snap = None
    for fb in iter_frames(_idle_chunks(ser, args.timeout)):     # cli.py:211
        rec = decode_record(fb.payload)
        if not isinstance(rec, Strip):
            continue
        snap = assembler.add(rec)
        if snap is not None:
            break                                               # stops at first complete frame
```
- `encode_snapshot_payload()` (records.py:411-413) packs the header-only `<HBB>` command (magic `0x4D43`, cmd_id `0x02`, reserved 0). `frame_encode` (framing.py:42-53) wraps it in `SOF|LEN|payload|FCS`. `ser.send_command` writes the bytes (transport.py:94-101).
- `iter_frames` (framing.py:82-163) consumes byte chunks, resyncs on the 4-byte SOF, validates Fletcher-16, and yields validated `FrameBytes` payloads. `decode_record` (decode.py:242-258) turns a payload into a typed `Strip`.
- **How it decides capture is done — idle timeout:** `_idle_chunks(ser, args.timeout)` (cli.py:160-171) is the terminator. It calls `ser.read_chunk()` (transport.py:103-113, one non-blocking-ish read, possibly empty on the 0.1 s serial timeout) and yields non-empty chunks, resetting a `deadline = now + idle_timeout` on every byte. When `idle_timeout_s` elapses with no new bytes, the generator returns, `iter_frames` ends, and the `for` loop exits. `--timeout` defaults to 5.0 s (cli.py:392-398). So `snapshot` stops either at the first completed frame (break) **or** when the stream goes idle.

**Save** (`save_snapshot`, snapshot.py:95-120): strips a stale `.bgr/.png/.json` suffix, `mkdir` parent, builds a Pillow `Image.frombytes("RGB", (w,h), bgr, "raw", "BGR")` (BGR→RGB without manual swap), stashes `frame_epoch` in a PNG tEXt chunk, writes `<stem>.png`, returns `[png_path]`.

**Subparser registration** (`build_parser`, cli.py:381-399): `--port` (required), `--out` (default None), `--timeout` (float, default 5.0), `set_defaults(func=cmd_snapshot)`. Dispatch is `args.func(args)` in `main` (cli.py:442-447).

**How other verbs send commands:** `set-mask` → `_send_mask` (cli.py:81-84) does `ser.send_command(frame_encode(encode_set_mask_payload(mask)))`. `set-overlay` (cli.py:151-157) does the same with `encode_set_overlay_payload`. `record` (cli.py:90-138) optionally sends a mask then loops `for chunk in ser:` (the infinite iterator) writing to disk until `KeyboardInterrupt`. The **Ctrl-C pattern** you want for `score-capture` is exactly `record`'s: wrap the drain loop in `try/except KeyboardInterrupt` and print a summary (cli.py:116-126).

## 2. What a new `score-capture` verb needs

It is a hybrid of `snapshot` (assemble region strips → PNG) and `record` (run continuously until Ctrl-C / a count). Concretely:

**a) A start/stop command.** The current firmware SNAPSHOT command is one-shot and header-only, and takes **no parameters** — see the firmware contract at `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h:418-422` ("current frame, full resolution; needs no parameters") and the handler `perf_log_rx.c:89-94` which just calls `PerfLog_RequestSnapshot()`. There is **no existing continuous or sub-region command** on the device, and I found no `96×105` / "scoring block" region defined in firmware (the grep hits in `game/gameplay_metadata.h` are unrelated image data). So a real `score-capture` needs a **new firmware command** (e.g. `PERF_CMD_SCORE_CAPTURE` with a start/stop flag, and implicitly the fixed 96×105 rect), mirrored host-side. Host-side that means:
   - Add `PERF_CMD_SCORE_CAPTURE = 0x04` to the `PERF_CMD_*` block in records.py:22-24 (mirroring the firmware `perf_cmd_t` enum, records.h:387-392).
   - Add an `encode_score_capture_payload(start: bool)` next to `encode_snapshot_payload` (records.py:408-413), packing `<HBB>` + a flag byte (or reuse header-only for "start" and a second cmd/flag for "stop"). Framing is identical: `frame_encode(...)` then `ser.send_command(...)`.
   - Stop: on Ctrl-C / count reached, send the stop command before closing the port (mirroring how `_send_mask` sends inline).

   If instead the plan is host-driven repeated one-shots (no firmware change), `score-capture` could loop sending `encode_snapshot_payload()` and crop each returned full frame to the 96×105 rect — but that is not "continuous full-rate" and the task explicitly says a fixed sub-region streamed at full rate, so the new-command path is the intended one.

**b) Receive a continuous run of SNAPSHOT-like strips grouped by frame_epoch.** Same drain machinery, but the terminator changes. Do **not** `break` on the first completed frame. Instead loop over `iter_frames(...)` feeding a multi-frame assembler; each time the assembler returns a completed region frame, save it and keep going. For the byte source you want continuous reading — either `for chunk in ser` (infinite, like `record`) guarded by `KeyboardInterrupt`, or keep `_idle_chunks(ser, timeout)` as a safety net so a stalled stream still terminates. `_idle_chunks` already resets its deadline on every byte (cli.py:166-170), so at full rate it never trips.

**c) Save one PNG per completed region frame with auto-increment.** `_resolve_snapshot_out` computes a single name, so calling it once per completed frame inside the loop gives natural auto-increment (`snapshot-0001`, `-0002`, …). Better: add a sibling resolver (e.g. `_resolve_score_out`) that uses a `score-NNNN.png` prefix and its own directory (default `./scores/`), and to avoid re-globbing every frame, resolve the base once and increment an in-memory counter. Reuse `save_snapshot` unchanged for the actual PNG write (it already stamps `frame_epoch` and is dimension-agnostic).

**d) Stop on Ctrl-C or --count.** Add `--count` (int, default None) and a `--timeout`/idle arg to the subparser. In the loop: `saved += 1` per completed frame; `if args.count and saved >= args.count: break`. Wrap the whole drain in `try/except KeyboardInterrupt` and print a summary like `record` (cli.py:125-126). New subparser block mirrors cli.py:381-399 with `--port` (required), `--out` (default None → `scores/`), `--count`, `--timeout`, `set_defaults(func=cmd_score_capture)`.

## 3. Can `SnapshotAssembler` be reused/extended?

File: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/snapshot.py`. **It cannot be reused as-is for two reasons, but is a good template:**

- **`x != 0` guard.** `SnapshotAssembler.add` raises `SnapshotError` on any strip with `strip.x != 0` (snapshot.py:55-56) — it hard-assumes full-width, x-anchored-at-0 bands. A 96×105 scoring block will have `x != 0` and `w < full`. The finalizer also pastes bands by simple vertical concatenation assuming full-width rows (`canvas += band.bgr`, snapshot.py:81-85, height derived purely from y+h), so it produces a `width = p.width` image with no horizontal offset handling. For a sub-region where every band is the same sub-width this still works if you drop the `x!=0` check and treat `p.width` as the region width — but you must also validate `x`/region consistency. (The decoder itself, `_decode_strip` at decode.py:206-224, is fully dimension-agnostic and already accepts any `x,y,w,h`, so no change there.)

- **Multi-frame streams.** `SnapshotAssembler` already keys pending frames by `frame_epoch` in a dict (`self._pending`, snapshot.py:50-74) and deletes the epoch on finalize (snapshot.py:89), so structurally it *can* handle many epochs over its lifetime — `add()` returns a `CompletedSnapshot` each time a frame completes and you keep calling it. The one-per-`break` behavior is in `cmd_snapshot` (cli.py:216-217), not the assembler. So a streaming caller can reuse the same instance across frames.

**Recommendation:** cleanest is a small new `ScoreRegionAssembler` (or a `full_width: bool` / `expected_rect` parameter on the existing class) that (1) drops the `x!=0` raise and instead validates each band shares the region's `(x, w)`, (2) optionally filters on a specific `StripKind` for the score stream, and (3) keeps the epoch-keyed multi-frame logic. `CompletedSnapshot` and `save_snapshot` can be reused verbatim — they only care about `width/height/frame_epoch/bgr`. If the firmware sends the scoring block as one strip per frame (96×105×3 = 30 240 B, well under `STRIP_MAX_BYTES` 65 000, records.py:46), the assembler collapses to "one strip = one frame, emit on LAST flag," which is even simpler and argues for a purpose-built tiny assembler over bending `SnapshotAssembler`.

## 4. Schema-version mirror bump + test-fixture conventions

- **`EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION`** lives at records.py:17 (`= 5`) and mirrors firmware `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION 5u` at `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h:16`. The module docstring (records.py:1-7) and README.md:11-15 both state the rule: bump both sides together whenever the wire layout changes. **Adding a new host→device *command* (a `PERF_CMD_*` id) does not by itself change any *record* wire layout**, so strictly it may not require a schema bump — the existing SET_OVERLAY command was added at cmd_id 0x03 without needing new record structs. A bump is required only if `score-capture` introduces a new **record type** or changes an existing struct. If a new `StripKind` (e.g. `SCORE`) is added to the `StripKind` enum (records.py:63-66) that is also arguably a wire-contract change worth a coordinated bump. Decide with the firmware author; the mirror discipline is "match firmware byte-for-byte and bump in lockstep."

README.md:57-59 notes real `.bin` captures would go under `tests/fixtures/` once firmware emits them, but that directory does not yet exist.
  - `build_strip_payload` (conftest.py:191-204) already takes `x, y, w, h, kind, flags, fill` — so it can build **sub-region** (x≠0) and **SCORE-kind** strips today with no change. Tests would add a `frame_epoch` per frame and multiple bands.
  - `test_snapshot.py` is the pattern to copy for a new assembler: `_band(...)` helper (test_snapshot.py:21-36) wraps `build_strip_payload` → `decode_record` → `Strip`; tests assert in-order assembly, out-of-order contiguity waiting, non-matching-kind ignoring, width-mismatch raising, and PNG round-trip losslessness/epoch tEXt (test_snapshot.py:38-102). A `score-capture` assembler would get parallel tests plus a **multi-epoch** test (feed two frames, assert two `CompletedSnapshot`s).
  - `test_cli.py:49-74` covers `_resolve_snapshot_out` (explicit `.png`, dir auto-increment, default dir, gap-skipping). A `_resolve_score_out` would get the analogous four tests.
  - No test currently exercises `cmd_snapshot` end-to-end over a serial port (serial is mocked/absent); the seam that is tested is the pure functions (`_resolve_*`, assembler, `save_*`). Follow that seam: keep the new verb's testable logic (payload encode, assembler, out-resolver) as free functions.

**Files to touch for the feature (for reference, no changes made):** `records.py` (new `PERF_CMD_*`, `encode_score_capture_payload`, maybe a `StripKind`), `snapshot.py` (new/extended assembler; reuse `save_snapshot`), `cli.py` (`cmd_score_capture`, `_resolve_score_out`, subparser in `build_parser`), `README.md` (verb list at lines 26-27 and 47-48), `tests/test_snapshot.py` + `tests/test_cli.py` (or new test module), and the firmware side (`perf_log_records.h` command enum + `perf_log_rx.c` dispatch + producer) which is where the real continuous sub-region capture must be implemented.

- **`EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION`** lives at records.py:17 (`= 5`) and mirrors firmware `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION 5u` at `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h:16`. The module docstring (records.py:1-7) and README.md:11-15 both state the rule: bump both sides together whenever the wire layout changes. **Adding a new host→device *command* (a `PERF_CMD_*` id) does not by itself change any *record* wire layout**, so strictly it may not require a schema bump — the existing SET_OVERLAY command was added at cmd_id 0x03 without needing new record structs. A bump is required only if `score-capture` introduces a new **record type** or changes an existing struct. If a new `StripKind` (e.g. `SCORE`) is added to the `StripKind` enum (records.py:63-66) that is also arguably a wire-contract change worth a coordinated bump. Decide with the firmware author; the mirror discipline is "match firmware byte-for-byte and bump in lockstep."

- **Test-fixture conventions** (`/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/marvin-perf/tests/`):
  - Fixtures are **built in code**, not stored — `conftest.py` (top docstring, lines 1-9) exposes per-type `build_*_payload` helpers and `wrap_frame` (conftest.py:210-216) which does `SOF + LEN + payload + Fletcher-16`. README.md:57-59 notes real `.bin` captures would go under `tests/fixtures/` once firmware emits them, but that directory does not yet exist.
  - `build_strip_payload` (conftest.py:191-204) already takes `x, y, w, h, kind, flags, fill` — so it can build **sub-region** (x≠0) and **SCORE-kind** strips today with no change. Tests would add a `frame_epoch` per frame and multiple bands.
  - `test_snapshot.py` is the pattern to copy for a new assembler: `_band(...)` helper (test_snapshot.py:21-36) wraps `build_strip_payload` → `decode_record` → `Strip`; tests assert in-order assembly, out-of-order contiguity waiting, non-matching-kind ignoring, width-mismatch raising, and PNG round-trip losslessness/epoch tEXt (test_snapshot.py:38-102). A `score-capture` assembler would get parallel tests plus a **multi-epoch** test (feed two frames, assert two `CompletedSnapshot`s).
  - `test_cli.py:49-74` covers `_resolve_snapshot_out` (explicit `.png`, dir auto-increment, default dir, gap-skipping). A `_resolve_score_out` would get the analogous four tests.
  - No test currently exercises `cmd_snapshot` end-to-end over a serial port (serial is mocked/absent); the seam that is tested is the pure functions (`_resolve_*`, assembler, `save_*`). Follow that seam: keep the new verb's testable logic (payload encode, assembler, out-resolver) as free functions.

**Files to touch for the feature (for reference, no changes made):** `records.py` (new `PERF_CMD_*`, `encode_score_capture_payload`, maybe a `StripKind`), `snapshot.py` (new/extended assembler; reuse `save_snapshot`), `cli.py` (`cmd_score_capture`, `_resolve_score_out`, subparser in `build_parser`), `README.md` (verb list at lines 26-27 and 47-48), `tests/test_snapshot.py` + `tests/test_cli.py` (or new test module), and the firmware side (`perf_log_records.h` command enum + `perf_log_rx.c` dispatch + producer) which is where the real continuous sub-region capture must be implemented.</result>

# Scoping: perf-log region-stream ("scoring block") variant

All paths absolute; line numbers from the files as read.

## 1. Snapshot request→emit flow and how coherence (tear-freeness) is guaranteed

**Request latch (from USB RX callback context):**
- `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_rx.c:89-94` — `PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT` is header-only; the handler just calls `PerfLog_RequestSnapshot()`. RX runs in the CDC `READ_COMPLETE` ISR/callback path (`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:173-183` → `PerfLogRx_Feed`), so it deliberately offloads all heavy work.
- `perf_log.c:748-751` — `PerfLog_RequestSnapshot()` sets `volatile bool s_snapshot_req = true`. That's the whole cross-context handoff.

**Drain-task pickup:**
- `perf_log.c:378-382` — the drain loop polls `s_snapshot_req` at the top of each iteration, clears it, and calls `emit_snapshot()` inline (before servicing the state/strip queues).

**emit_snapshot() — `perf_log.c:319-356`:**
```c
Video_FrameInfo vi;
Video_GetFrameInfo(&vi);                 // 320-323 sanity checks buffer/w/h
if (vi.bytes_per_pixel != PERF_STRIP_BPP) return;   // 324 (BPP must be 3)
...
memcpy(s_snapshot_staging, vi.buffer, frame_bytes);  // 332  ← the ONE coherent copy
uint32_t band_rows = PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES / stride;  // 334  full-width band height
for (uint16_t y = 0; y < h; ) {
    bh = min(h-y, band_rows);
    hdr_fill(&r->hdr, PERF_REC_STRIP, 0u, vi.frame_count);  // 344 frame_epoch = frame_count
    r->x=0; r->y=y; r->w=w; r->h=bh;                        // 346-349  x always 0, full width
    r->kind = PERF_STRIP_SNAPSHOT;                          // 349
    r->flags = (y+bh >= h) ? PERF_STRIP_FLAG_LAST : 0;      // 350
    memcpy(r->bgr, &s_snapshot_staging[y*stride], bh*stride);
    PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(r, strip_record_size(r));    // 353 write straight to sink
}
```

**Why it's tear-free — the crux:**
- The framebuffer is a **4-slot uncached ring in `.region_nocache`**: `isc_capture.c:24` `ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS 4u`, `isc_capture.c:34-36` (`.region_nocache`, aligned 32). Uncached means CPU reads see ISC DMA writes with no cache maintenance (`isc_capture.c:31-32`).
- `Video_GetFrameInfo` (`video.c:480-488`) returns `s_latest_buffer` = the **just-completed** ring slot (set in the frame-done IRQ, `video.c:93`; the completed-slot arithmetic is `isc_capture.c:56-60`). So `vi.buffer` is a *completed* frame, **not** the live DMA target — but the ISC keeps advancing through the other 3 slots and will **lap** (~4 frames ≈ 66 ms @60 Hz) and overwrite it.
- Coherence is therefore achieved **entirely by the single up-front `memcpy` at line 332**: the whole frame is copied into the private cached BSS buffer `s_snapshot_staging` (`perf_log.c:98`, sized `1280*720*3`) in one shot — fast enough to finish before the ring laps. The slow, wire-paced banded emit (comment `perf_log.c:314-318`: "~0.4 s @480p, ~1 s @720p") then reads only from `s_snapshot_staging`, never the live ring. Tearing would only occur if you read the ring *during* the slow emit — which it never does.

## 2. What a region-stream variant would take

### (a) Copy only a fixed sub-region — **already fully supported, no wire change**
- `perf_rec_strip_t` already carries per-record `x, y, w, h` (`perf_log_records.h:262-263`). Sub-windowing is a first-class feature, not a snapshot-only assumption.
- `PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame` (`perf_log.c:678-701`) already row-copies an arbitrary `w×h` window at offset `(x,y)` out of a strided frame: `src = frame + y*frame_stride + x*BPP` (line 691), looping `h` rows of `w*BPP`. The existing SENSING/STRIKE producers use exactly this at non-zero offsets (`cv_marvin_v1.c:423-425`, `:450-452`).
- Your scoring block **96×105×3 = 30,240 bytes** is < `PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES` (65000, `perf_log_records.h:255`) and < the single-strip area cap → **one region frame fits in exactly one STRIP record.** No banding, no staging buffer, no reassembly needed. It also passes `strip_slot_claim`'s size guard (`perf_log.c:641`).

### (b) Stream continuously at frame rate (start/stop)
The natural design mirrors the existing SENSING strip, which is already a tear-free 60 Hz sub-region stream:
- **Producer hook:** a frame subscriber already runs per-frame. Both `cv_marvin_v1.c:397-453` (the CV loop) and `game/gameplay_engine.c:91` (`Video_SubscribeFrames`) receive each completed frame. Because `PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame` copies immediately on frame receipt — right after completion, well inside the ~66 ms lap window — each emitted region strip is inherently coherent, exactly like today's SENSING/STRIKE strips. The scoring block is a §4.8 game-state concern, so `gameplay_engine.c` is the most natural home.
- **Start/stop control:** add `PERF_CMD_REGION_STREAM` carrying an enable flag (and optionally x/y/w/h, though the block is fixed). Handler sets a `volatile bool s_region_stream_on` (+ optional coords) analogous to `s_snapshot_req`/`s_overlay_flags` (`perf_log.c:97`, `:127`). The per-frame producer checks the flag (lock-free load, like `PerfLog_GetOverlayFlags()` at `cv_marvin_v1.c:445`) and, when set, calls `PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_SCORE, frame.buffer, fstride, 114, 309, 96, 105)`.
- **Go through the normal strip pool, NOT the snapshot path.** `emit_snapshot()` monopolizes the drain (comment `perf_log.c:314-318`); a continuous stream must not. The pool path (`strip_slot_claim`/`strip_slot_commit`, `perf_log.c:633-672`; drained at `perf_log.c:403-408`) is drop-on-full (`PL_STRIP_QUEUE_DEPTH 4`, pool 6), so region frames naturally interleave with state records and drop under back-pressure instead of stalling the pipeline. It is also STRIP-mask-gated (`strip_slot_claim` line 639), so it costs nothing until the host enables it.

### (c) Tag/deliver so the host can reassemble — **use a NEW strip kind, do not reuse SNAPSHOT**
- Reusing `PERF_STRIP_SNAPSHOT` is unsafe: the host `SnapshotAssembler.add()` **explicitly rejects `x != 0`** and requires full-width bands — `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/snapshot.py:54-56` (`raise SnapshotError(... expected full-width)`), and it groups/reassembles bands by `frame_epoch`.
- Add a new kind, e.g. `PERF_STRIP_SCORE = 3`, to the enum at `perf_log_records.h:217-222`. Per the record-format doc (`perf_log_records.h:205-216` and spec §4.6.8 note: *"Future kinds (SCORE, MINIMAP, etc.) plug into the same record type — adding one is an enum entry plus a producer; no schema bump"*), and the host decoder keeps `kind` as an int for forward-compat (`records.py:258`). So the raw STRIP decode already handles it.
- Delivery is trivial on the host: since each region frame is a **single** STRIP record tagged with `frame_epoch` (=`frame_count`) and `kind=SCORE`, no assembler is needed — each decoded `Strip` with `kind==SCORE` *is* a complete region frame. A thin consumer keyed on the new kind (parallel to `SnapshotAssembler`, but pass-through) is all that's required host-side; the `Strip` struct/decoder (`records.py:247-271`) needs no change beyond adding `SCORE = 3` to `StripKind` (`records.py:63-66`).

## 3. Schema-version bump convention
- Firmware: `#define PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION 5u` at `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h:16`. Header rule (`:9-14`): *"Bump PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION on every layout change; the host refuses streams that don't match."* Emitted in the SESSION record (`perf_log.c:178`).
- Python mirror: `EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 5` at `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py:17`, with the comment *"bump EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION here whenever PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION is bumped on the firmware side."* The host refuses on mismatch (SESSION `schema_version`).
- **Applicability to this change:** adding only a new *strip kind* is documented as **not** requiring a bump (kind is forward-compat int). However, adding a new **command** (`PERF_CMD_REGION_STREAM`) to `perf_cmd_t` (`perf_log_records.h:387-392`, mirrored `records.py:22-24`) and any new command payload struct is a wire-format addition — bump **both** `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` (→6) and `EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` (→6) together, add the encoder in `records.py` (alongside `encode_snapshot_payload`, `records.py:411-413`, and `encode_set_overlay_payload`, `:419-422`), and add the `StripKind.SCORE` entry.

## 4. Concurrency & bandwidth concerns
- **Bandwidth is comfortable.** 96×105×3 = 30,240 B/frame × 60 Hz ≈ **1.8 MB/s**. The strip cap note (`perf_log_records.h:250-254`) states the wire sustains ~3.9 MB/s (60 fps × 65 KB), so a single scoring block at 60 Hz is <½ that ceiling. Framed overhead is small (SOF 4 + LEN 2 + FCS 2 + HDR 16 + body 12 = 36 B/record).
- **Drain task:** must use the pooled strip path (`perf_log.c:403-408`), NOT `emit_snapshot`'s direct-write monopolization. The drain already writes one strip per loop iteration and interleaves state records (`perf_log.c:384-408`). Region strips will contend with SENSING/STRIKE (also 60 Hz) if both are enabled — pool depth is 6 (`PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE`, `perf_log.c:30`) and queue depth 4 (`PL_STRIP_QUEUE_DEPTH`, `:23`), drop-on-full via `s_drop_strip`. Consider that concurrent SCORE + SENSING + STRIKE = 3 strips/frame competing for 4 queue slots; region-stream should probably be mutually exclusive with, or accounted against, the other STRIP producers, or bump pool/queue depth.
- **Sink throughput:** CDC ACM ring is 3-deep (`SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH 3`, `perf_log_sink_cdc.c:43`), single-producer (drain only, `:26-27`), credit-metered by a counting semaphore returned per `WRITE_COMPLETE` ISR (`:164-171`, `:303-308`). Writes block up to `SINK_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS=100` then drop (`:303-308`). The dwDTERate 921600 (`:54`) is cosmetic — it's USB HS bulk, real throughput is far higher. Each 30 KB region record is a single `USB_DEVICE_CDC_Write` well under the `SINK_FRAME_BYTES_MAX` cap derived from `PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES` (`:34-35`), so no per-record fragmentation.
- **Interaction with normal perf records:** the drain drains all queued state records each iteration before/after strips (`perf_log.c:384-408`); at full region rate the ~5 ms/strip wire cost (comment `:390-393`) means the drain still services state at ~50 Hz. STAMP/DETECTOR/TIMING remain on the state queue (depth 1024) and are unaffected in ordering, though sustained 1.8 MB/s of SCORE strips will raise `dropped_sink`/`dropped_strip` if the host under-consumes. Gating SCORE behind its own start/stop (default off) keeps the idle/normal path at zero cost, matching the existing default-off high-rate-type philosophy (`perf_log.c:101-116`).

**Net:** the wire format and producer machinery already support everything except (1) a new `PERF_STRIP_SCORE` kind, (2) a new `PERF_CMD_REGION_STREAM` start/stop command + payload + flag, (3) a per-frame producer call in `gameplay_engine.c` (or `cv_marvin_v1.c`) gated on the flag, and (4) host-side: `StripKind.SCORE`, a command encoder, schema bump to 6 on both sides, and a trivial pass-through consumer (each record = one complete region frame; no reassembly).

**Why it's tear-free — the crux:**
- The framebuffer is a **4-slot uncached ring in `.region_nocache`**: `isc_capture.c:24` `ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS 4u`, `isc_capture.c:34-36` (`.region_nocache`, aligned 32). Uncached means CPU reads see ISC DMA writes with no cache maintenance (`isc_capture.c:31-32`).
- `Video_GetFrameInfo` (`video.c:480-488`) returns `s_latest_buffer` = the **just-completed** ring slot (set in the frame-done IRQ, `video.c:93`; the completed-slot arithmetic is `isc_capture.c:56-60`). So `vi.buffer` is a *completed* frame, **not** the live DMA target — but the ISC keeps advancing through the other 3 slots and will **lap** (~4 frames ≈ 66 ms @60 Hz) and overwrite it.
- Coherence is therefore achieved **entirely by the single up-front `memcpy` at line 332**: the whole frame is copied into the private cached BSS buffer `s_snapshot_staging` (`perf_log.c:98`, sized `1280*720*3`) in one shot — fast enough to finish before the ring laps. The slow, wire-paced banded emit (comment `perf_log.c:314-318`: "~0.4 s @480p, ~1 s @720p") then reads only from `s_snapshot_staging`, never the live ring. Tearing would only occur if you read the ring *during* the slow emit — which it never does.

## 2. What a region-stream variant would take

### (a) Copy only a fixed sub-region — **already fully supported, no wire change**
- `perf_rec_strip_t` already carries per-record `x, y, w, h` (`perf_log_records.h:262-263`). Sub-windowing is a first-class feature, not a snapshot-only assumption.
- `PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame` (`perf_log.c:678-701`) already row-copies an arbitrary `w×h` window at offset `(x,y)` out of a strided frame: `src = frame + y*frame_stride + x*BPP` (line 691), looping `h` rows of `w*BPP`. The existing SENSING/STRIKE producers use exactly this at non-zero offsets (`cv_marvin_v1.c:423-425`, `:450-452`).
- Your scoring block **96×105×3 = 30,240 bytes** is &lt; `PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES` (65000, `perf_log_records.h:255`) and &lt; the single-strip area cap → **one region frame fits in exactly one STRIP record.** No banding, no staging buffer, no reassembly needed. It also passes `strip_slot_claim`'s size guard (`perf_log.c:641`).

### (b) Stream continuously at frame rate (start/stop)
The natural design mirrors the existing SENSING strip, which is already a tear-free 60 Hz sub-region stream:
- **Producer hook:** a frame subscriber already runs per-frame. Both `cv_marvin_v1.c:397-453` (the CV loop) and `game/gameplay_engine.c:91` (`Video_SubscribeFrames`) receive each completed frame. Because `PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame` copies immediately on frame receipt — right after completion, well inside the ~66 ms lap window — each emitted region strip is inherently coherent, exactly like today's SENSING/STRIKE strips. The scoring block is a §4.8 game-state concern, so `gameplay_engine.c` is the most natural home.
- **Start/stop control:** add `PERF_CMD_REGION_STREAM` carrying an enable flag (and optionally x/y/w/h, though the block is fixed). Handler sets a `volatile bool s_region_stream_on` (+ optional coords) analogous to `s_snapshot_req`/`s_overlay_flags` (`perf_log.c:97`, `:127`). The per-frame producer checks the flag (lock-free load, like `PerfLog_GetOverlayFlags()` at `cv_marvin_v1.c:445`) and, when set, calls `PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_SCORE, frame.buffer, fstride, 114, 309, 96, 105)`.
- **Go through the normal strip pool, NOT the snapshot path.** `emit_snapshot()` monopolizes the drain (comment `perf_log.c:314-318`); a continuous stream must not. The pool path (`strip_slot_claim`/`strip_slot_commit`, `perf_log.c:633-672`; drained at `perf_log.c:403-408`) is drop-on-full (`PL_STRIP_QUEUE_DEPTH 4`, pool 6), so region frames naturally interleave with state records and drop under back-pressure instead of stalling the pipeline. It is also STRIP-mask-gated (`strip_slot_claim` line 639), so it costs nothing until the host enables it.

### (c) Tag/deliver so the host can reassemble — **use a NEW strip kind, do not reuse SNAPSHOT**
- Reusing `PERF_STRIP_SNAPSHOT` is unsafe: the host `SnapshotAssembler.add()` **explicitly rejects `x != 0`** and requires full-width bands — `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/snapshot.py:54-56` (`raise SnapshotError(... expected full-width)`), and it groups/reassembles bands by `frame_epoch`.
- Add a new kind, e.g. `PERF_STRIP_SCORE = 3`, to the enum at `perf_log_records.h:217-222`. Per the record-format doc (`perf_log_records.h:205-216` and spec §4.6.8 note: *"Future kinds (SCORE, MINIMAP, etc.) plug into the same record type — adding one is an enum entry plus a producer; no schema bump"*), and the host decoder keeps `kind` as an int for forward-compat (`records.py:258`). So the raw STRIP decode already handles it.
- Delivery is trivial on the host: since each region frame is a **single** STRIP record tagged with `frame_epoch` (=`frame_count`) and `kind=SCORE`, no assembler is needed — each decoded `Strip` with `kind==SCORE` *is* a complete region frame. A thin consumer keyed on the new kind (parallel to `SnapshotAssembler`, but pass-through) is all that's required host-side; the `Strip` struct/decoder (`records.py:247-271`) needs no change beyond adding `SCORE = 3` to `StripKind` (`records.py:63-66`).

## 3. Schema-version bump convention
- Firmware: `#define PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION 5u` at `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h:16`. Header rule (`:9-14`): *"Bump PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION on every layout change; the host refuses streams that don't match."* Emitted in the SESSION record (`perf_log.c:178`).
- Python mirror: `EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 5` at `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py:17`, with the comment *"bump EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION here whenever PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION is bumped on the firmware side."* The host refuses on mismatch (SESSION `schema_version`).
- **Applicability to this change:** adding only a new *strip kind* is documented as **not** requiring a bump (kind is forward-compat int). However, adding a new **command** (`PERF_CMD_REGION_STREAM`) to `perf_cmd_t` (`perf_log_records.h:387-392`, mirrored `records.py:22-24`) and any new command payload struct is a wire-format addition — bump **both** `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` (→6) and `EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` (→6) together, add the encoder in `records.py` (alongside `encode_snapshot_payload`, `records.py:411-413`, and `encode_set_overlay_payload`, `:419-422`), and add the `StripKind.SCORE` entry.

## 4. Concurrency &amp; bandwidth concerns
- **Bandwidth is comfortable.** 96×105×3 = 30,240 B/frame × 60 Hz ≈ **1.8 MB/s**. The strip cap note (`perf_log_records.h:250-254`) states the wire sustains ~3.9 MB/s (60 fps × 65 KB), so a single scoring block at 60 Hz is &lt;½ that ceiling. Framed overhead is small (SOF 4 + LEN 2 + FCS 2 + HDR 16 + body 12 = 36 B/record).
- **Drain task:** must use the pooled strip path (`perf_log.c:403-408`), NOT `emit_snapshot`'s direct-write monopolization. The drain already writes one strip per loop iteration and interleaves state records (`perf_log.c:384-408`). Region strips will contend with SENSING/STRIKE (also 60 Hz) if both are enabled — pool depth is 6 (`PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE`, `perf_log.c:30`) and queue depth 4 (`PL_STRIP_QUEUE_DEPTH`, `:23`), drop-on-full via `s_drop_strip`. Consider that concurrent SCORE + SENSING + STRIKE = 3 strips/frame competing for 4 queue slots; region-stream should probably be mutually exclusive with, or accounted against, the other STRIP producers, or bump pool/queue depth.
- **Sink throughput:** CDC ACM ring is 3-deep (`SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH 3`, `perf_log_sink_cdc.c:43`), single-producer (drain only, `:26-27`), credit-metered by a counting semaphore returned per `WRITE_COMPLETE` ISR (`:164-171`, `:303-308`). Writes block up to `SINK_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS=100` then drop (`:303-308`). The dwDTERate 921600 (`:54`) is cosmetic — it's USB HS bulk, real throughput is far higher. Each 30 KB region record is a single `USB_DEVICE_CDC_Write` well under the `SINK_FRAME_BYTES_MAX` cap derived from `PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES` (`:34-35`), so no per-record fragmentation.
- **Interaction with normal perf records:** the drain drains all queued state records each iteration before/after strips (`perf_log.c:384-408`); at full region rate the ~5 ms/strip wire cost (comment `:390-393`) means the drain still services state at ~50 Hz. STAMP/DETECTOR/TIMING remain on the state queue (depth 1024) and are unaffected in ordering, though sustained 1.8 MB/s of SCORE strips will raise `dropped_sink`/`dropped_strip` if the host under-consumes. Gating SCORE behind its own start/stop (default off) keeps the idle/normal path at zero cost, matching the existing default-off high-rate-type philosophy (`perf_log.c:101-116`).

**Net:** the wire format and producer machinery already support everything except (1) a new `PERF_STRIP_SCORE` kind, (2) a new `PERF_CMD_REGION_STREAM` start/stop command + payload + flag, (3) a per-frame producer call in `gameplay_engine.c` (or `cv_marvin_v1.c`) gated on the flag, and (4) host-side: `StripKind.SCORE`, a command encoder, schema bump to 6 on both sides, and a trivial pass-through consumer (each record = one complete region frame; no reassembly).</result>
