```text
# Plan: marvin-perf full-rate region (score-block) capture

## Context
The gameplay score reader (phase 5) works but its digit templates come from ~9 hand-picked
frames, so held-out accuracy is 10/16 — every miss a low-margin →8 confusion from sparse
per-digit exemplars. We need many more glyph exemplars, tear-free, without bulk manual
labelling. Solution: stream just the **scoring block** (`SCORE_BLOCK_ROI = x114,y309,96×105`) to
disk at full frame rate, so a short play sweeps every digit 0–9 many times; scores climb
monotonically within a play, so the frames auto-label cheaply downstream. The block is also the
reader's registration fiducial, so the same capture serves both.

## Key finding — the machinery already exists
- `PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(epoch, kind, frame, stride, x, y, w, h)` (perf_log.c:678) already
  row-copies an arbitrary `w×h` sub-region out of the current frame into a pooled STRIP record,
  **coherently** (copied on frame-receipt, well inside the ~66 ms nocache-ring lap window — the
  same mechanism that makes the existing 60 Hz SENSING/STRIKE sub-region strips tear-free).
- 96×105×3 = 30,240 B < `PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES` (65000) → **one region frame = one STRIP record.**
  No banding, no staging buffer, no host reassembler.
- `perf_rec_strip_t` already carries per-record `x,y,w,h,kind` (records.h:259). Adding a strip
  **kind** needs no schema bump (records.h:210-211, explicit). Commands are host→device and don't
  touch the record wire layout the host validates → **no schema bump** (matches the SET_OVERLAY
  precedent). Leave `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION`/`EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` at 5 (confirm with Greg).

## Approach
A **parameterized** region streamer (host sends the rect), not a hard-coded score box — so the
region can be retuned or repointed (multiplier, streak, other games) without a firmware reflash
(builds are Greg-gated in MPLAB). Default off; gated behind a start/stop command → zero cost when
idle.

**Firmware (I write/review C; Greg builds in MPLAB):**
- `perf_log_records.h`: add `PERF_STRIP_REGION = 3` to `perf_strip_kind_t`; add
  `PERF_CMD_REGION_STREAM = 0x04` to `perf_cmd_t`; add a `perf_cmd_region_stream_t {hdr; u8
  enable; u8 reserved; u16 x,y,w,h}` (mirrors `perf_cmd_set_overlay_t`).
- `perf_log.c` / `perf_log.h`: add `volatile` region state + `PerfLog_SetRegionStream(on,x,y,w,h)`
  (mirror `s_overlay_flags` / `PerfLog_SetOverlayFlags`), and a guarded emit helper
  `PerfLog_EmitRegionIfEnabled(frame_epoch, buffer, stride, frame_w, frame_h)` that, when enabled
  and the rect is in-bounds, calls `PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(..., PERF_STRIP_REGION, ...)`.
  Bounds-check `x+w≤frame_w && y+h≤frame_h` (the existing claim only caps `w*h*BPP`).
- `perf_log_rx.c`: add the `PERF_CMD_REGION_STREAM` dispatch case (mirror `SET_OVERLAY`,
  rx.c:96-103) → `PerfLog_SetRegionStream(...)`.
- `cv_marvin_v1.c`: one call to `PerfLog_EmitRegionIfEnabled(...)` in the per-frame loop beside
  the existing SENSING/STRIKE emits (always-on frame path → captures in menus too). Uses the
```

```text
160	def _idle_chunks(ser: SerialSource, idle_timeout_s: float):
161	    """Yield serial chunks until `idle_timeout_s` elapses with no new bytes.
162	
163	    Lets `iter_frames` terminate once the snapshot burst stops (or stalls),
164	    instead of blocking forever on the infinite SerialSource iterator.
165	    """
166	    deadline = time.monotonic() + idle_timeout_s
167	    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
168	        chunk = ser.read_chunk()
169	        if chunk:
170	            deadline = time.monotonic() + idle_timeout_s
171	            yield chunk

174	def _resolve_snapshot_out(out: str | None) -> Path:
175	    """Resolve the `--out` argument to a concrete .png path.
176	
177	    A value ending in `.png` is taken literally. Anything else (including the
178	    default when `--out` is omitted) is treated as a directory, and the next
179	    free `snapshot-NNNN.png` in it is chosen so rapid captures never clobber.
180	    """
181	    p = Path(out) if out else Path("snapshots")
182	    if p.suffix.lower() == ".png":
183	        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
184	        return p
185	
186	    p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
187	    nums = [
188	        int(m.group(1))
189	        for f in p.glob("snapshot-*.png")
190	        if (m := re.fullmatch(r"snapshot-(\d+)", f.stem))
191	    ]
192	    nxt = (max(nums) + 1) if nums else 1
193	    return p / f"snapshot-{nxt:04d}.png"

198	
199	    Sends PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT, reassembles the returned SNAPSHOT band strips into
200	    one frame, and writes a PNG. With `--out` omitted (or pointed at a
201	    directory) the filename auto-increments as `snapshot-NNNN.png` for quick
202	    repeated captures.
203	    """
204	    out_path = _resolve_snapshot_out(args.out)
205	
206	    assembler = SnapshotAssembler()
207	    with SerialSource(args.port) as ser:
208	        ser.send_command(frame_encode(encode_snapshot_payload()))
209	        print("[snapshot] requested; waiting for bands…", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
```

```text
210	def wrap_frame(payload: bytes, *, corrupt_fcs: bool = False) -> bytes:
211	    length = len(payload)
212	    length_bytes = struct.pack("<H", length)
213	    fcs = fletcher16(length_bytes + payload)
214	    if corrupt_fcs:
215	        fcs ^= 0xFFFF
```

```python
"""score-capture: REGION_STREAM command encode + REGION strip → PNG + out resolver."""

from __future__ import annotations

import struct
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from marvin_perf.cli import SCORE_BLOCK_RECT, _parse_rect, _score_dir_start
from marvin_perf.decode import decode_record
from marvin_perf.records import (
    PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC,
    PERF_CMD_REGION_STREAM,
    STRIP_BPP,
    Strip,
    StripKind,
    encode_region_stream_payload,
)
from marvin_perf.snapshot import CompletedSnapshot, save_snapshot

from .conftest import build_strip_payload

# Mirrors perf_cmd_region_stream_t: magic,cmd,reserved,enable,reserved,x,y,w,h
_REGION_FMT = struct.Struct("<HBBBBHHHH")


def test_region_stream_payload_start_round_trip() -> None:
    payload = encode_region_stream_payload(True, 114, 309, 96, 105)
    assert len(payload) == _REGION_FMT.size == 14  # packed struct, no padding
    magic, cmd, _r0, enable, _r1, x, y, w, h = _REGION_FMT.unpack(payload)
    assert magic == PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC
    assert cmd == PERF_CMD_REGION_STREAM
    assert (enable, x, y, w, h) == (1, 114, 309, 96, 105)


def test_region_stream_payload_stop() -> None:
    magic, cmd, _r0, enable, _r1, x, y, w, h = _REGION_FMT.unpack(
        encode_region_stream_payload(False)
    )
    assert cmd == PERF_CMD_REGION_STREAM
    assert enable == 0


def test_parse_rect_default_and_explicit() -> None:
    assert _parse_rect(None) == SCORE_BLOCK_RECT
    assert _parse_rect("10,20,30,40") == (10, 20, 30, 40)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        _parse_rect("1,2,3")


def test_score_dir_autoincrement(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    d = tmp_path / "scores"
    out, start = _score_dir_start(str(d))
    assert out == d and start == 1
    (d / "score-0001.png").write_bytes(b"")
    (d / "score-0004.png").write_bytes(b"")
    _out, start = _score_dir_start(str(d))
    assert start == 5  # max(existing) + 1


def test_region_strip_saves_as_png(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    # One REGION strip is a complete region frame — no reassembly.
    x, y, w, h = SCORE_BLOCK_RECT
    rec = decode_record(
        build_strip_payload(
            frame_epoch=42, kind=int(StripKind.REGION), x=x, y=y, w=w, h=h, fill=0xAB
        )
    )
    assert isinstance(rec, Strip)
    assert rec.kind == int(StripKind.REGION)
    assert (rec.x, rec.y, rec.w, rec.h) == (x, y, w, h)
    assert len(rec.bgr) == w * h * STRIP_BPP

    snap = CompletedSnapshot(width=rec.w, height=rec.h, frame_epoch=rec.hdr.frame_epoch, bgr=rec.bgr)
    out = save_snapshot(snap, tmp_path / "score-0001.png")[0]

    from PIL import Image

    with Image.open(out) as im:
        assert im.size == (w, h)
        assert im.getpixel((0, 0)) == (0xAB, 0xAB, 0xAB)
        assert im.text["frame_epoch"] == "42"

```

## Firmware (code-complete, pending your MPLAB build)
A generic, host-parameterized region streamer reusing the existing coherent per-frame copy path:
- **`perf_log_records.h`** — `PERF_STRIP_REGION` kind, `PERF_CMD_REGION_STREAM` command, `perf_cmd_region_stream_t {enable, x, y, w, h}` (14 B packed).
- **`perf_log.c/.h`** — `volatile` flag/rect (mirrors the overlay-flags pattern) + `PerfLog_SetRegionStream` + bounds-checked `PerfLog_EmitRegionIfEnabled`.
- **`perf_log_rx.c`** — dispatch case.
- **`cv_marvin_v1.c`** — one call in the per-frame loop beside SENSING/STRIKE.

Default off, pooled/drop-on-full (never monopolizes the drain), STRIP-mask gated. 96×105×3 = 30 KB → one STRIP record per frame, tear-free by the same mechanism as the existing 60 Hz strips. **No schema bump** (forward-compat kind + host→device command; SET_OVERLAY precedent).

Region-stream slots into those exact seams, and it reuses the firmware command + `encode_region_stream_payload` I already added.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-09 18:13:56Z)**_

Yes, it's a clean fit — and it reuses the firmware command + `encode_region_stream_payload` already in place. The web viewer's `LiveSession` owns the one serial connection and already has every seam this needs:

- **Command send:** `set_region_stream(enable, rect)` mirrors `set_overlay` (`live.py`).
- **Strip tap:** the reader loop already routes SNAPSHOT strips (`_reader_loop`, `rec.kind == SNAPSHOT`); add a `REGION` branch that keeps the latest frame for preview and saves each to disk with a running count.
- **Serve/preview:** `render_strip_png` + a `GET /api/live/region.png` endpoint (cache-busted like `/live/snapshot.png`), plus a WS `region` event (like the `snapshot`/`overlay` events).
- **REST:** `POST /api/live/region {enable, out_dir, rect}`.
- **Frontend:** a "Score capture" control in the live toolbar (mirrors the existing `snapshot-controls`: out-dir input + toggle button), a small live-preview `<img>` that refreshes on each WS `region` event, and a saved-count.

The big win over the CLI: you watch the block **live in the browser** and start/stop capture while playing, on the same connection the viewer already holds (no port conflict).

It's a multi-file change (`live.py`, `api.py`, `static/{app.js,index.html,styles.css}`, tests). One UX decision before I build:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-09 18:15:05Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**How should region capture surface in the web viewer?**

Options:
- **Live preview + capture** - A start/stop toggle that streams the block, shows a live auto-refreshing preview of the region in the browser, saves each frame to a dir, and shows a running saved count. Most useful for aiming/watching while capturing.
- **Capture to disk only** - A start/stop toggle that saves frames to a dir with a count, but no live preview image. Simpler, less frontend work.
- **Live preview only** - Show the region live in the browser (aim/verify the box) but don't save to disk — pair with the CLI verb for the actual capture.

```text
    def _mirror_to_recording(self, framed: bytes) -> None:
        """Reader-thread tap: write validated framed bytes to the active
        recording, if any. Disable the recording on write failure rather
        than tear down the whole session."""
        with self._lock:
            rec = self._rec
            if rec is None:
                return
            try:
                rec.fh.write(framed)
                rec.bytes_written += len(framed)
                rec.n_frames += 1
                return
            except OSError as e:
                self._rec = None
                err_msg = str(e)
                fh = rec.fh
        try:
            fh.close()
        except Exception:
            pass
        self._post("error", {"code": "record-write", "msg": err_msg})

class _LoadedCapture:
    """A capture pulled fully into memory + lookup indexes.

    Phase-1 captures are MB-scale (state-only at ~9 KB/s × minutes). Strips

    return {"records": out, "limit": limit, "offset": offset, "returned": len(out)}


@router.get("/capture/{capture_id:path}/strip/{epoch}/{kind}.png")
def capture_strip_png(capture_id: str, epoch: int, kind: str) -> Response:
    """Render the strip at (epoch, kind) as a PNG."""
    loaded = _REGISTRY.get(capture_id)
    indexes = loaded.by_epoch.get(epoch, [])
    for i in indexes:
        rec = loaded.records[i]
        if isinstance(rec, Strip) and rec.kind_name == kind:
            try:
                png = render_strip_png(
                    rec.bgr,  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
                    w=rec.w,  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
                    h=rec.h,  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
                )
            except StripRenderError as e:
                raise HTTPException(500, str(e))
            return Response(
                content=png,
                media_type="image/png",
                headers={
                    "Cache-Control": "public, max-age=31536000, immutable",
                    "ETag": f'"{capture_id}:{epoch}:{kind}"',
                },
            )
    raise HTTPException(404, f"no strip for epoch={epoch} kind={kind}")
```

```text
function setBanner(msg, kind = "info") {
  const el = $("#banner");
  if (!msg) { el.classList.add("hidden"); el.textContent = ""; return; }
  el.classList.remove("hidden", "error");
  if (kind === "error") el.classList.add("error");
  el.textContent = msg;
}

function setBadge(id, level, label) {
  const el = document.getElementById(id);
  el.classList.remove("green", "yellow", "red");
  if (level) el.classList.add(level);
  if (label) el.textContent = label;
```

```text
=== how web loads a capture into records ===
    def load(cls, path: str | Path) -> "_LoadedCapture":
        capture = open_capture(path)
        records: list[Record] = []
        stats = FrameStats()
        with FileSource(capture.bin_path) as src:
            for frame in iter_frames(src, stats):
                try:
                    records.append(decode_record(frame.payload))
                except Exception:
                    continue

        by_epoch: dict[int, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
        for i, rec in enumerate(records):
            ep = rec.hdr.frame_epoch  # type: ignore[union-attr]
            by_epoch[ep].append(i)

        return cls(
            capture=capture,
            records=records,
            framing_stats=stats,
            by_epoch=dict(by_epoch),
        )


class _Registry:
    """Module-level cache: (resolved-path, mtime) → _LoadedCapture."""
```

```text
38	class _FakeSerial:
39	    """Stand-in for SerialSource — context-managed iterable + send_command capture.
40	
41	    The iterator drains an internal byte queue (``feed`` from the test) and
42	    blocks once empty until the session closes the source. This lets a test
43	    push framed bytes through the live reader thread on demand."""
44	
45	    def __init__(self, port: str) -> None:
46	        self.port = port
47	        self.sent: list[bytes] = []
48	        self._closed = threading.Event()
49	        self._has_data = threading.Event()
50	        self._chunks: list[bytes] = []
51	        self._chunks_lock = threading.Lock()
52	        self._entered = False
53	
54	    def __enter__(self) -> "_FakeSerial":
55	        self._entered = True
56	        return self
57	
58	    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:
59	        self._closed.set()
60	        self._has_data.set()
61	
62	    def send_command(self, framed: bytes) -> int:
63	        self.sent.append(framed)
64	        return len(framed)
65	
66	    def feed(self, chunk: bytes) -> None:
67	        with self._chunks_lock:
68	            self._chunks.append(chunk)
69	        self._has_data.set()
70	
71	    def __iter__(self):
72	        while not self._closed.is_set():
73	            self._has_data.wait(timeout=0.05)
74	            with self._chunks_lock:
75	                pending = self._chunks
76	                self._chunks = []
77	                if not pending:
78	                    self._has_data.clear()
79	            for c in pending:
80	                yield c
81
```

Region capture now works in the web viewer, recording to the capture file like everything else.

## What I added (host, done + tested)
- **Web viewer** (`serve`): a **"▣ Score region" toggle** in live mode → `POST /api/live/region` → `LiveSession.set_region_stream` sends the start/stop command (mirrors the overlay toggle, reflected over the WebSocket + status).
- **Records into the `.bin` like everything else**: the REGION strips are ordinary `PERF_REC_STRIP` records, and the recorder's mirror path has no type filter — so hitting **Record** captures them with zero record-path changes. That's exactly the "record to a data file like we do with everything else" you asked for.
- **`export-region`** CLI verb: pulls REGION strips out of a recorded capture into `score-NNNN.png` (`save_region_strips`) — the input to the gameplay score corpus. The offline viewer already renders them too (`kind_name` → `"region"`).
- **`score-capture`** CLI verb kept (headless live PNG dump), per your "keep both."
- Shared `DEFAULT_REGION_RECT = (114,309,96,105)`, README updated, **153 tests pass**.

## Workflow it enables
In the browser: Start live → toggle **Score region** on → **Record** a play → Stop. Then `marvin-perf export-region <capture>/ --out scores/` → feed those into the gameplay corpus (auto-label via visual read + monotonic check) → rebuild templates.

From `tools/marvin-perf/`:

```
cd tools/marvin-perf
```

Then open **http://localhost:8765** (default `--host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765`; use `serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765` to reach it from another machine).

In the browser:
1. Click **Live** (top-left mode toggle).
2. Pick marvin's port in the **port dropdown** (⟳ rescans), then **Start**.
3. Toggle **▣ Score region** on → the scoring block starts streaming.
4. **● Record** to capture it into a `.bin` (auto-suggests an out dir), play through, **Stop**.

Then offline: `uv run marvin-perf export-region <that-capture-dir>/ --out scores/` to pull the frames out as `score-NNNN.png`.

Two caveats:
- The **firmware must be built/flashed with today's changes** — until then the device won't emit REGION strips, so the toggle will send the command but no frames arrive.
- First time only, if `serve` complains about missing deps: `uv sync --group viewer`.

```text
"""FastAPI app composition + uvicorn entry. Imported lazily by cli.py."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

from . import api


STATIC_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "static"


def build_app() -> FastAPI:
    app = FastAPI(
        title="marvin-perf viewer",
        description="Visual review for marvin firmware perf-log captures.",
        version="0.1.0",
    )
    app.include_router(api.router)

    if STATIC_DIR.exists():
        app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory=STATIC_DIR), name="static")

        @app.get("/")
        def root_index() -> FileResponse:
            return FileResponse(STATIC_DIR / "index.html")

    return app


def run(*, host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: int = 8765, capture: str | None = None) -> int:
    import uvicorn

    if capture:
        api._preload(capture)

    uvicorn.run(build_app(), host=host, port=port, log_level="info")
    return 0
```

```text
=== server include_bgr logic ===


# ─── Record → JSON ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _record_to_dict(rec: Record, *, include_bgr: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Compact, JSON-friendly view of a record. Offline mode keeps strip
    pixels on the dedicated PNG endpoint; live mode passes ``include_bgr=True``
    so the WS push carries pixel bytes (base64) for client-side canvas render."""
    hdr = rec.hdr  # type: ignore[union-attr]
    base: dict[str, Any] = {
        "type": type(rec).__name__,
        "frame_epoch": hdr.frame_epoch,
        "ts_counter": hdr.ts_counter,
        "flags": hdr.flags,
    }
    if isinstance(rec, Session):
        base.update(
            timer_freq_hz=rec.timer_freq_hz,
            schema_version=rec.schema_version,
            fw_git_short=rec.fw_git_short,
        )
    elif isinstance(rec, Stamp):
        try:
            base["stage"] = Stage(rec.stage_id).name
        except ValueError:
            base["stage"] = f"stage_{rec.stage_id:#04x}"
        base["stage_id"] = rec.stage_id
        base["aux"] = rec.aux
    elif isinstance(rec, Drop):
        base.update(
            dropped_state=rec.dropped_state,
            dropped_strip=rec.dropped_strip,
            dropped_sink=rec.dropped_sink,
        )
    elif isinstance(rec, TaskHighwater):
        try:
            base["task_name"] = TaskId(rec.task_id).name
        except ValueError:
            base["task_name"] = f"task_{rec.task_id}"
        base["task_id"] = rec.task_id
        base["words"] = rec.words
    elif isinstance(rec, TaskRuntime):
        try:
            base["task_name"] = TaskId(rec.task_id).name
        except ValueError:
            base["task_name"] = f"task_{rec.task_id}"
        try:
            base["state_name"] = TaskState(rec.state).name
        except ValueError:
            base["state_name"] = f"state_{rec.state}"
        base["task_id"] = rec.task_id
```

```text
633	/* Claim a free strip pool slot and fill its header. Returns the slot pointer
634	 * (writing its index to *out_idx) or NULL when STRIP is masked off, the args
635	 * are invalid, or the pool is empty (drop counted). The caller fills r->bgr
636	 * then calls strip_slot_commit. No struct memcpy in the queue critical
637	 * section — only a 1-byte index transfer. */
638	static perf_rec_strip_t *strip_slot_claim(uint32_t frame_epoch, perf_strip_kind_t kind,
639	                                          uint16_t x, uint16_t y,
640	                                          uint16_t w, uint16_t h,
641	                                          uint8_t *out_idx)
642	{
643	    if (s_strip_q == NULL || s_strip_free_q == NULL) { return NULL; }
644	    if (!type_enabled(PERF_REC_STRIP)) { return NULL; }
645	    if (w == 0u || h == 0u) { return NULL; }
646	    if ((uint32_t)w * (uint32_t)h * PERF_STRIP_BPP > PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES) { return NULL; }
647	
648	    uint8_t slot_idx;
649	    if (xQueueReceive(s_strip_free_q, &slot_idx, 0) != pdTRUE)
650	    {
651	        counter_add_task(&s_drop_strip, 1u);
652	        return NULL;
653	    }
654	
655	    perf_rec_strip_t *r = &s_strip_pool[slot_idx];
656	    memset(r, 0, PERF_STRIP_HDR_BYTES);
657	    hdr_fill(&r->hdr, PERF_REC_STRIP, 0u, frame_epoch);
658	    r->x    = x;
659	    r->y    = y;
660	    r->w    = w;
661	    r->h    = h;
662	    r->kind = (uint8_t)kind;
663	    *out_idx = slot_idx;
664	    return r;
665	}
666	
667	static void strip_slot_commit(uint8_t slot_idx)
668	{
669	    if (xQueueSend(s_strip_q, &slot_idx, 0) != pdTRUE)
670	    {
671	        /* In-flight queue full (pool sized depth+2 makes this rare; only
672	         * possible if the drain task is blocked while strip_q is at depth
673	         * and the producer also holds a slot). Return slot to free pool. */
674	        (void)xQueueSend(s_strip_free_q, &slot_idx, 0);
675	        counter_add_task(&s_drop_strip, 1u);
676	    }
677	}
```

This is great data — 6549 frames, monotonically climbing 250 → 99640 (one long play, so auto-labelable by the monotonic-increase rule). And you're clearly right: the font is **proportional**, not monospace. Look at `11962` vs `40958` — both 5 digits, but the `1`s are narrow so the whole number is more compressed and shifts right. A fixed-pitch right-anchored grid can't sit on each digit.

The good news is the digits are cleanly **gap-separated**, which means gap-based segmentation (find each digit blob by its ink, right-to-left) is the right approach instead of fixed cells. Let me confirm the gaps are reliable even on tight cases:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-09 19:36:02Z)**_

```bash
export UV_CACHE_DIR=$TMPDIR/uv-cache && uv run python - <<'PY'
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np, os
d=os.environ['TMPDIR']+"/score-frames"
# digit band within the 96x105 block — find it, then column ink profile
def prof(name):
    a=np.asarray(Image.open(f"{d}/{name}").convert("RGB")).astype(int)
    # white mask over whole block
    m=(a[...,0]>150)&(a[...,1]>150)&(a[...,2]>150)
    rows=np.where(m.sum(1)>0)[0]
    # digit band = top cluster of white rows (score line); take rows 2..26 region
    band=m[3:27]
    col=band.sum(0)
    s="".join(str(min(9,c)) if c>0 else "." for c in col)
    return s
for name in ["score-0817.png","score-5713.png","score-2449.png","score-0273.png","score-6549.png"]:
    print(f"{name}: {prof(name)}")
PY
```

```md
# Plan: score reader — proportional (gap-based) digit segmentation + capture-enriched corpus

## Context
The score reader (gameplay phase 5) assumed a **tabular/fixed-pitch** font and segmented the digit
ROI into equal right-anchored cells. A large real capture (6549 frames, `marvin-perf` REGION
stream, `captures/web-20260709-142721`, monotonically climbing 250 → 100000+) shows the training
font is **proportional**: right-aligned, but digit x-positions shift with the specific digits (a
`1` is narrow, so `11962` is more compressed than `40958`). Fixed cells can't sit on each digit.
The digits are, however, cleanly **gap-separated** (verified: every frame's column ink-profile
shows distinct clusters with `.` gaps, no touching digits, even `11962`/`97717`). So the fix is
**gap-based segmentation** (isolate each digit by its ink, right-to-left), which also removes the
need for a fixed digit count / blank class. The capture is also a rich corpus for robust templates
+ a real eval (monotonicity gives a label-free accuracy proxy over all 6549 frames).

## Findings / what's reused
- **Chrome registration stays as-is** (`calibrate_score` locks the block via masked SAD on the
  static chrome). It still gives the block position; only the *within-block* segmentation changes.
- Current `score.py` pieces to change: `_cell_rois` + `_labels_for_value` (fixed-pitch) → gap
  segmentation; `ScoreCalibration.cells` → a block offset + digit-band; `build_score_catalog` /
  `read_score` bodies. `_luma_grid` (from `songselect`) reused for the per-glyph fingerprint.
- Capture extraction already works: `marvin-perf export-region <capture>/ --out <dir>` → 6549
  `score-NNNN.png` (96×105 block frames). Captures are gitignored — the 6549 stay local; only a
  curated labelled subset is committed.

## Approach

**1. Gap-based segmentation (`score.py`).**
- Digit search band: a fixed rect relative to the chrome-registered block covering the glyph rows
  and the full box-interior width (so up to 6 digits fit) — new `metadata.SCORE_DIGIT_BAND`
  (≈ abs `(126, 313, 200, 335)`, refined on data), replacing the narrow fixed `SCORE_ROI`.
- `_segment_digits(band_luma, cfg) -> list[(x0,x1)]`: per-frame-normalized ink mask (luma >
  adaptive threshold), column ink profile, split into contiguous runs separated by ≥`min_gap`
  empty columns, drop specks (`< min_ink_px` / `< min_width`), return runs left→right.
- `_glyph_vec(band_luma, run, cfg)`: crop the run's bbox (ink rows too), resize to a canonical
  `cell_rows×cell_cols` grid, zero-mean/unit-std → the glyph fingerprint (comparable across
  proportional widths).
- `read_score`: register (or take `ScoreCalibration`) → crop digit band at the locked offset →
  `_segment_digits` → classify each run (1-NN vs the 0–9 templates, argmin L1) → assemble
  left→right into the integer. Digit count = number of runs (no fixed N, no blank class).
  `margin` = min per-digit runner-up gap.

**2. Templates from the capture (`build_score_catalog`).**
- For each labelled corpus frame: segment the band, and since the run count equals `len(str(value))`,
  map runs left→right onto the value's digits; keep each glyph vec as a 1-NN exemplar per digit.
- Curate **~50 frames** from the 6549 spanning every digit in every position and lengths 3–6
  (incl. the 6-digit rollover), value in the filename (`score__training__NNNNNN__snapNNNN.png`),
  under `tools/gameplay/data/scores/` (replacing the 9-frame set). I read the values off montages
  (reliable; cross-checked by the monotonic ordering); user spot-checks a sample.

**3. Eval (`evaluate.py`).**
- Update `score_eval` for gap-based: LOO exact-match + per-digit accuracy + A2D slop (`perturb`,
  gain/offset/noise) + re-registration, on the committed curated corpus.
- Add `score_monotonic_eval(frames_dir)`: read every frame in an extracted-capture dir, report
  **monotonic-violation count** (a decrease ⇒ a misread, since a play only climbs) + digit-count
  histogram. Label-free accuracy proxy over all 6549; gated on the dir existing (local-only, since
  the capture isn't committed). Exposed via a CLI verb or an env-pointed path.

## Files to change
- `tools/gameplay/gameplay/metadata.py` — `SCORE_DIGIT_BAND`; drop/reting `SCORE_ROI` fixed field.
- `tools/gameplay/gameplay/score.py` — segmentation + glyph-vec + `read_score`/`build_score_catalog`
  rewrite; `ScoreConfig` (canonical glyph grid, ink threshold, min-gap/width) ; `ScoreCalibration`
  → block offset. Chrome registration unchanged.
- `tools/gameplay/gameplay/evaluate.py` — gap-based `score_eval` + `score_monotonic_eval`.
- `tools/gameplay/gameplay/cli.py` — `read-score` (unchanged surface) + a `score-monotonic <dir>`
  debug verb.
- `tools/gameplay/data/scores/` — curated ~50 labelled frames (replaces the 9).
- `tools/gameplay/tests/test_score.py` — segmentation tests (synthetic proportional row), read
  exact on the corpus, a monotonic-check unit.

## Verification
- **Segmentation sanity:** overlay detected runs on sample frames (incl. `11962`, 6-digit) — one
  box per digit, correct count.
- **Corpus:** `gameplay eval` → new score block reports LOO exact ~100% + per-digit, A2D stable,
  re-register stable.
- **Big label-free check:** `gameplay score-monotonic <extracted-6549-dir>` → near-zero monotonic
  violations (each violation is a real misread to inspect); expect a big jump vs the old 10/16.
- **Tests:** `uv run pytest` green.
- **User spot-check** of a sample of the curated labels before eval numbers are trusted.

## Notes
- uv env; `UV_CACHE_DIR=$TMPDIR/uv-cache` in-sandbox.
- Career (green) font still deferred; this is training-white only. The gap-based segmentation will
  port to career later (same approach, its own templates + band).
```

- Add a **label-free accuracy proxy**: `score-monotonic <dir>` reads all 6549 and counts monotonic violations (a decrease = a misread, since a play only climbs). That's a far stronger validation than the old 10/16 held-out.

**Files:** `score.py` (segmentation rewrite), `metadata.py` (`SCORE_DIGIT_BAND`), `evaluate.py` (gap-based `score_eval` + `score_monotonic_eval`), `cli.py` (a `score-monotonic` verb), `data/scores/` (curated set), tests.

```bash
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np, os, glob
d=os.environ['TMPDIR']+"/score-frames"
files=sorted(glob.glob(f"{d}/*.png"))
# band block-rel: x 8..90, y 7..23
BX0,BY0,BX1,BY1=8,7,90,23
def band_luma(f):
    a=np.asarray(Image.open(f).convert("RGB")).astype(float)[BY0:BY1,BX0:BX1]
    return a@np.array([77,150,29])/256.0
def segment(L, min_gap=1, min_w=1, min_ink=3):
    m=L>(L.mean()+0.8*L.std())
    col=m.sum(0)
    runs=[]; s=None; gap=0
    for x,c in enumerate(col):
        if c>0:
            if s is None: s=x
            gap=0
        else:
            if s is not None:
                gap+=1
                if gap>min_gap:
                    runs.append((s,x-gap)); s=None
    if s is not None: runs.append((s,len(col)-1))
    # filter specks
    out=[]
    for x0,x1 in runs:
        w=x1-x0+1; ink=col[x0:x1+1].sum()
        if w>=min_w and ink>=min_ink: out.append((x0,x1,w,int(ink)))
    return out
# expected rough counts from the monotonic climb (250->100000+): sample spread
for i in [0,272,544,816,1088,1360,1632,1904,2176,2448,3000,4000,5000,6000,6300,6548]:
    f=files[i]; runs=segment(band_luma(f))
    widths=[r[2] for r in runs]
    print(f"{os.path.basename(f)}: {len(runs)} digits  widths={widths}")
PY
```

```bash
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np, os, glob, re
frames=os.environ['TMPDIR']+"/score-frames"
dst="data/scores"
BX0,BY0,BX1,BY1=8,7,90,23
LW=np.array([77,150,29])/256.0
def band(path):
    a=np.asarray(Image.open(path).convert("RGB")).astype(float)[BY0:BY1,BX0:BX1]
    return a@LW
def segment(L, frac=0.6, min_gap=1, min_w=1, min_ink=4):
    thr=L.min()+frac*(L.max()-L.min()); m=L>thr; col=m.sum(0)
    runs=[]; s=None; gap=0
    for x,c in enumerate(col):
        if c>0:
            if s is None: s=x
            gap=0
        else:
            if s is not None:
                gap+=1
                if gap>min_gap: runs.append((s,x-gap)); s=None
    if s is not None: runs.append((s,len(col)-1))
    return [(x0,x1) for x0,x1 in runs if (x1-x0+1)>=min_w and col[x0:x1+1].sum()>=min_ink]
def glyph_vec(L, run, rows=14, cols=10, frac=0.6):
    x0,x1=run; sub=L[:, x0:x1+1]
    thr=L.min()+frac*(L.max()-L.min())
    rmask=(sub>thr).any(1); ys=np.where(rmask)[0]
    if len(ys): sub=sub[ys.min():ys.max()+1,:]
    ys_e=np.linspace(0,sub.shape[0],rows+1).round().astype(int)
    xs_e=np.linspace(0,sub.shape[1],cols+1).round().astype(int)
    g=np.empty((rows,cols))
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            blk=sub[ys_e[r]:max(ys_e[r]+1,ys_e[r+1]), xs_e[c]:max(xs_e[c]+1,xs_e[c+1])]
            g[r,c]=blk.mean() if blk.size else 0.0
    v=g.reshape(-1); v-=v.mean(); s=v.std()
    return v/s if s>1e-6 else v

# build exemplars from corpus
corpus=sorted(glob.glob(f"{dst}/score__training__*.png"))
def val_of(p): return int(re.search(r"training__(\d+)",p).group(1))
def exemplars(files):
    ex=[]  # (digit, vec)
    for p in files:
        val=val_of(p); L=band(p); runs=segment(L); s=str(val)
        if len(runs)!=len(s): 
            print("  SEG MISMATCH", os.path.basename(p), len(runs), "vs", len(s)); continue
        for run,ch in zip(runs, s):
            ex.append((int(ch), glyph_vec(L,run)))
    return ex
def read(L, ex):
    vecs=np.stack([v for _,v in ex]); digs=np.array([d for d,_ in ex])
    out=""
    for run in segment(L):
        fv=glyph_vec(L,run); d=int(np.abs(vecs-fv).sum(1).argmin()); out+=str(digs[d])
    return int(out) if out else -1
ex_all=exemplars(corpus)
print("exemplars:",len(ex_all),"digit coverage:",sorted(set(d for d,_ in ex_all)))
# LOO
ok=0
for p in corpus:
    val=val_of(p); others=[q for q in corpus if q!=p]
    r=read(band(p), exemplars(others))
    ok+= r==val
    if r!=val: print("  LOO MISS", os.path.basename(p), "->", r)
print(f"LOO exact: {ok}/{len(corpus)}")
# monotonic over all 6549 with full templates
allf=sorted(glob.glob(f"{frames}/score-*.png"))
prev=-1; viol=0; reads=[]
for p in allf:
    r=read(band(p), ex_all); reads.append(r)
    if r<prev: viol+=1
    prev=max(prev,r)
print(f"monotonic over {len(allf)}: {viol} violations (decreases)")
PY
```

```text
1	"""In-song score reader: per-digit glyph OCR of the open-ended score value.
2	
3	Unlike the menu/song readers (closed-set template matches), the score is an
4	open-ended number, so it is read digit by digit. The score is right-aligned in a
5	fixed HUD box and grows leftward; GH3 renders tabular (fixed-advance) digits, so
6	the score ROI (`metadata.SCORE_ROI[mode]`) splits into `N_SCORE_DIGITS` equal
7	cells anchored at the right edge. Each cell is fingerprinted (low-res normalized
8	luma grid, the same idea as the song reader) and matched against a per-mode bank
9	of digit templates 0-9 plus a `BLANK` class for the unused leading cells.
10	Non-blank cells, left to right, assemble the integer value.
11	
12	Two stages, because the field position is fixed on a given rig but the analog
13	capture varies frame to frame:
14	
15	- **Registration (once).** The whole scoring block (`metadata.SCORE_BLOCK_ROI`)
16	  is located by matching its *chrome* — the static box frame, inner panel texture,
17	  and medallion ring, which are digit-independent and identical in training and
18	  career. A masked (`metadata` + hand-drawn `score_block_mask.png`) normalized-SAD
19	  offset search finds the block's `(dx, dy)` for this rig (`calibrate_score` →
20	  `ScoreCalibration`); the digit cells are then fixed offsets inside it. This is a
21	  better anchor than the digits themselves: it can't alias onto a neighbouring
22	  digit, needs no digit templates to register, and works before a valid score has
23	  even appeared. Run once at gameplay start over a few frames.
24	- **Per-frame read (continual).** `read_score` samples the locked cells and
25	  argmin-classifies each — no search. Per-frame luma normalization cancels the
26	  A2D gain/offset/brightness drift, so the fixed cells read correctly frame to
27	  frame. Cheap: a handful of rect-means + an L1 over the digit templates.
28	
29	Templates are built from the labelled score corpus: each frame's known value is
30	right-justified across the cells, giving every cell a digit (or blank) label, and
31	every labelled cell fingerprint is kept as a 1-NN exemplar — no hand-cropping.
32	
33	Integer-friendly for the firmware port: fixed cells + argmin L1 over uint8-scale
34	vectors, exactly like `gp_read_song`; registration is a masked SAD over the block,
35	run once instead of per frame.
36	"""
37	
38	from __future__ import annotations
39	
40	from dataclasses import dataclass
41	
42	import numpy as np
43	
44	from .corpus import Sample, load_bgr, score_corpus_dir
45	from .fingerprint import _to_canonical
46	from .metadata import (
47	    N_SCORE_DIGITS,
48	    SCORE_BLOCK_ROI,
49	    SCORE_ROI,
50	    score_from_filename,
51	)
52	from .songselect import _LUMA_W, _luma_grid, _shift
53	
54	BLANK = 10  # class label for an unused (empty) leading cell
55	CHROME_MASK_FILE = "score_block_mask.png"
56	
57	
58	@dataclass(frozen=True)
59	class ScoreConfig:
60	    n_digits: int = N_SCORE_DIGITS
61	    cols: int = 8   # per-cell grid columns (captures the digit's ink pattern)
62	    rows: int = 14  # per-cell grid rows
63	    # Registration search radius (px), used *once* to lock the block position for
64	    # the rig; not on the per-frame read path. Wide enough to cover per-rig
65	    # position variation.
66	    reg_search: int = 8
67	
68	
69	DEFAULT_SCORE_CONFIG = ScoreConfig()
70	
71	
72	@dataclass(frozen=True)
73	class DigitTemplate:
74	    digit: int  # 0-9, or BLANK
75	    vec: np.ndarray
76	
77	
78	@dataclass(frozen=True)
79	class ChromeReference:
80	    ref: np.ndarray   # median block luma (h, w) at the nominal block position
81	    mask: np.ndarray  # bool (h, w): static-chrome pixels used for registration
82	
83	
84	@dataclass(frozen=True)
85	class ScoreCatalog:
86	    mode: str
87	    templates: list[DigitTemplate]  # one per labelled cell exemplar (1-NN, not centroid)
88	    chrome: ChromeReference
89	    config: ScoreConfig
90	
91	
92	@dataclass(frozen=True)
93	class ScoreCalibration:
94	    mode: str
95	    cells: tuple[tuple[int, int, int, int], ...]  # locked per-cell ROIs (len n_digits)
96	    dx: int = 0  # block offset found at registration (for debug/report)
97	    dy: int = 0
98	
99	
100	@dataclass(frozen=True)
101	class ScoreResult:
102	    value: int
103	    digits: tuple[int, ...]  # per-cell class, left->right (BLANK for empty leading cells)
104	    dist: float              # worst (max) per-cell best-distance
105	    margin: float            # weakest (min) per-cell 2nd-best - best
106	
107	
108	def _cell_rois(roi: tuple[int, int, int, int], n: int) -> list[tuple[int, int, int, int]]:
109	    """Split a score ROI into `n` equal-width digit cells (left->right)."""
110	    x0, y0, x1, y1 = roi
111	    xs = np.linspace(x0, x1, n + 1).round().astype(int)
112	    return [(int(xs[i]), y0, int(xs[i + 1]), y1) for i in range(n)]
113	
114	
115	def _labels_for_value(value: int, n_digits: int) -> list[int]:
116	    """Right-justify `value` across `n_digits` cells -> per-cell class labels.
117	
118	    Leading (unused) cells are BLANK; e.g. 1138 over 6 cells ->
119	    [BLANK, BLANK, 1, 1, 3, 8]. Scores never carry leading zeros.
120	    """
121	    s = str(value)
122	    pad = n_digits - len(s)
123	    return [BLANK] * pad + [int(c) for c in s]
124	
125	
126	def _block_luma(image: np.ndarray, dx: int = 0, dy: int = 0) -> np.ndarray:
127	    """Luma of the scoring block at the nominal position shifted by (dx, dy)."""
128	    img = _to_canonical(image)
129	    x0, y0, x1, y1 = SCORE_BLOCK_ROI
130	    patch = img[y0 + dy:y1 + dy, x0 + dx:x1 + dx].astype(np.float64)
131	    return patch @ _LUMA_W / 256.0
132	
133	
134	def load_chrome_mask(path=None) -> np.ndarray:
```

```python
"""In-song score reader: per-digit glyph OCR of the open-ended score value.

Unlike the menu/song readers (closed-set template matches), the score is an
open-ended number, so it is read digit by digit. The training font is white and
**proportional** (a `1` is narrower than an `8`, so digit x-positions shift with
the value — verified on a 6549-frame capture), but the digits are cleanly
gap-separated. So digits are isolated by their ink (the gaps between them), not a
fixed grid; each is normalized to a canonical cell and matched against a per-mode
bank of 0-9 glyph exemplars (1-NN). The digit count falls out of the segmentation
(no fixed N, no blank class).

Two stages, because the field position is fixed on a given rig but the analog
capture varies frame to frame:

- **Registration (once).** The whole scoring block (`metadata.SCORE_BLOCK_ROI`)
  is located by matching its *chrome* — the static box frame, inner panel texture,
  and medallion ring, which are digit-independent and identical in training and
  career. A masked (`metadata` + hand-drawn `score_block_mask.png`) normalized-SAD
  offset search finds the block's `(dx, dy)` for this rig (`calibrate_score` →
  `ScoreCalibration`); the digit band is then a fixed offset inside it. Run once
  at gameplay start over a few frames.
- **Per-frame read (continual).** `read_score` crops the digit band at the locked
  offset, segments it, and 1-NN-classifies each glyph — no offset search. A
  per-band relative ink threshold and per-glyph normalization cancel A2D
  gain/offset drift. Cheap: an ink mask + a small L1 per digit.

Templates are built from the labelled score corpus: each frame's digits (from its
filename value) map left→right onto the segmented glyphs, each kept as a 1-NN
exemplar — no hand-cropping. Integer-friendly for the firmware port.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

from .corpus import Sample, load_bgr, score_corpus_dir
from .fingerprint import _to_canonical
from .metadata import (
    SCORE_BLOCK_ROI,
    SCORE_DIGIT_BAND,
    score_from_filename,
)
from .songselect import _LUMA_W

CHROME_MASK_FILE = "score_block_mask.png"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ScoreConfig:
    glyph_rows: int = 14   # canonical glyph grid (rows), each segmented digit resized to this
    glyph_cols: int = 10   # canonical glyph grid (cols)
    # Segmentation: relative ink threshold (fraction of the band's min..max luma
    # range — gain/offset robust since the digits are the brightest ink), and the
    # run/gap filters that split the ink profile into digit blobs.
    ink_frac: float = 0.6
    min_gap: int = 1       # empty columns (>this) that separate two digits
    min_width: int = 1     # drop runs narrower than this (specks)
    min_ink: int = 4       # drop runs with fewer than this many ink pixels
    # Registration search radius (px), used *once* to lock the block for the rig.
    reg_search: int = 8


DEFAULT_SCORE_CONFIG = ScoreConfig()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DigitTemplate:
    digit: int  # 0-9
    vec: np.ndarray


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ChromeReference:
    ref: np.ndarray   # median block luma (h, w) at the nominal block position
    mask: np.ndarray  # bool (h, w): static-chrome pixels used for registration


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ScoreCatalog:
    mode: str
    templates: list[DigitTemplate]  # one per labelled glyph exemplar (1-NN, not centroid)
    chrome: ChromeReference
    config: ScoreConfig


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ScoreCalibration:
    mode: str
    dx: int = 0  # block offset found at registration
    dy: int = 0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ScoreResult:
    value: int
    digits: tuple[int, ...]  # the digits read, left->right
    dist: float              # worst (max) per-digit best-distance
    margin: float            # weakest (min) per-digit runner-up gap


# ─── digit band luma + segmentation ─────────────────────────────────────────────


def _band_luma(image: np.ndarray, mode: str, dx: int = 0, dy: int = 0) -> np.ndarray:
    """Luma of the digit search band, shifted by the registration offset."""
    img = _to_canonical(image)
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = SCORE_DIGIT_BAND[mode]
    patch = img[y0 + dy:y1 + dy, x0 + dx:x1 + dx].astype(np.float64)
    return patch @ _LUMA_W / 256.0


def _ink_mask(band: np.ndarray, cfg: ScoreConfig) -> np.ndarray:
    thr = band.min() + cfg.ink_frac * (band.max() - band.min())
    return band > thr


def _segment_digits(band: np.ndarray, cfg: ScoreConfig) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Split the digit band into per-digit column runs (left->right).

    A column with any ink extends the current run; more than `min_gap` empty
    columns closes it. Specks (too narrow / too little ink) are dropped.
    """
    col = _ink_mask(band, cfg).sum(0)
    runs: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
    start: int | None = None
    gap = 0
    for x, c in enumerate(col):
        if c > 0:
            if start is None:
                start = x
            gap = 0
        elif start is not None:
            gap += 1
            if gap > cfg.min_gap:
                runs.append((start, x - gap))
                start = None
    if start is not None:
        runs.append((start, len(col) - 1))
    return [
        (x0, x1) for x0, x1 in runs
        if (x1 - x0 + 1) >= cfg.min_width and int(col[x0:x1 + 1].sum()) >= cfg.min_ink
    ]


def _glyph_vec(band: np.ndarray, run: tuple[int, int], cfg: ScoreConfig) -> np.ndarray:
    """Normalized fingerprint of one segmented digit (bbox → canonical grid)."""
    x0, x1 = run
    sub = band[:, x0:x1 + 1]
    # Crop to the glyph's ink rows so height variation doesn't dominate.
    rmask = _ink_mask(band, cfg)[:, x0:x1 + 1].any(1)
    ys = np.where(rmask)[0]
    if len(ys):
        sub = sub[ys.min():ys.max() + 1, :]
    ye = np.linspace(0, sub.shape[0], cfg.glyph_rows + 1).round().astype(int)
    xe = np.linspace(0, sub.shape[1], cfg.glyph_cols + 1).round().astype(int)
    g = np.empty((cfg.glyph_rows, cfg.glyph_cols), dtype=np.float64)
    for r in range(cfg.glyph_rows):
        for c in range(cfg.glyph_cols):
            blk = sub[ye[r]:max(ye[r] + 1, ye[r + 1]), xe[c]:max(xe[c] + 1, xe[c + 1])]
            g[r, c] = blk.mean() if blk.size else 0.0
    v = g.reshape(-1)
    v -= v.mean()
    s = v.std()
    return v / s if s > 1e-6 else v


# ─── chrome registration (locks the block; unchanged) ───────────────────────────


def _block_luma(image: np.ndarray, dx: int = 0, dy: int = 0) -> np.ndarray:
    """Luma of the scoring block at the nominal position shifted by (dx, dy)."""
    img = _to_canonical(image)
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = SCORE_BLOCK_ROI
    patch = img[y0 + dy:y1 + dy, x0 + dx:x1 + dx].astype(np.float64)
    return patch @ _LUMA_W / 256.0


def load_chrome_mask(path=None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Load the hand-drawn registration mask as a bool array at block resolution.

    The mask PNG paints the static-chrome pixels (used for registration) in
    magenta; it may be authored at any integer upscale of the block. Returns a
    (block_h, block_w) bool array.
    """
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = SCORE_BLOCK_ROI
    bw, bh = x1 - x0, y1 - y0
    p = path if path is not None else score_corpus_dir() / CHROME_MASK_FILE
    a = load_bgr(p)  # (H, W, 3) BGR; magenta is symmetric so channel order is moot
    mag = (a[..., 0] > 200) & (a[..., 2] > 200) & (a[..., 1] < 150)
    H, W = mag.shape
    if H % bh or W % bw:
        raise ValueError(f"chrome mask {W}x{H} is not an integer multiple of block {bw}x{bh}")
    fy, fx = H // bh, W // bw
    return mag.reshape(bh, fy, bw, fx).mean(axis=(1, 3)) >= 0.5


def build_chrome_reference(
    images: list[np.ndarray], config: ScoreConfig = DEFAULT_SCORE_CONFIG, mask_path=None
) -> ChromeReference:
    """Median block luma (the static chrome) + the registration mask."""
    ref = np.median(np.stack([_block_luma(im) for im in images]), axis=0)
    return ChromeReference(ref=ref, mask=load_chrome_mask(mask_path))


def _norm_masked(a: np.ndarray, mask: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Zero-mean/unit-std over the masked pixels (cancels A2D gain/offset)."""
    m = a[mask]
    return (a - m.mean()) / (m.std() + 1e-6)


def calibrate_score(images: list[np.ndarray], catalog: ScoreCatalog) -> ScoreCalibration:
    """Lock the scoring block's position for this rig (run once at gameplay start).

    Matches the static chrome: over an offset search, the masked,
    per-frame-normalized SAD between each calibration frame's block and the chrome
    reference is summed; the `(dx, dy)` with the smallest total wins. The digit
    band is then that offset applied to the nominal band. Registering on the chrome
    (not the digits) is digit-independent and robust before any valid score shows.
    """
    cfg = catalog.config
    mask = catalog.chrome.mask
    ref_n = _norm_masked(catalog.chrome.ref, mask)
    rng = cfg.reg_search

    best: tuple[float, int, int] | None = None
    for dy in range(-rng, rng + 1):
        for dx in range(-rng, rng + 1):
            total = 0.0
            for img in images:
                tn = _norm_masked(_block_luma(img, dx, dy), mask)
                total += float(np.abs((tn - ref_n)[mask]).sum())
            if best is None or total < best[0]:
                best = (total, dx, dy)
    assert best is not None
    _t, dx, dy = best
    return ScoreCalibration(mode=catalog.mode, dx=dx, dy=dy)


# ─── catalog build + read ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def build_score_catalog(
    samples: list[Sample],
    mode: str = "training",
    config: ScoreConfig = DEFAULT_SCORE_CONFIG,
) -> ScoreCatalog:
    """Build the per-mode 0-9 glyph exemplars + the chrome reference.

    Each labelled frame is segmented; the segmented glyphs map left→right onto the
    digits of the filename value (the run count must match), and each glyph vector
    is kept as a 1-NN exemplar. Matching is nearest-exemplar (not a centroid): the
    crisp digits blur together when averaged, so exemplars separate them cleanly.
    """
    templates: list[DigitTemplate] = []
    mode_images: list[np.ndarray] = []
    for s in samples:
        parsed = score_from_filename(s.path.name)
        if parsed is None or parsed[0] != mode:
            continue
        _mode, value = parsed
        mode_images.append(s.image)
        band = _band_luma(s.image, mode)
        runs = _segment_digits(band, config)
        digits = str(value)
        if len(runs) != len(digits):
            continue  # segmentation disagrees with the label — skip this frame
        for run, ch in zip(runs, digits):
            templates.append(DigitTemplate(digit=int(ch), vec=_glyph_vec(band, run, config)))
    chrome = build_chrome_reference(mode_images, config)
    return ScoreCatalog(mode=mode, templates=templates, chrome=chrome, config=config)


def read_score(
    image: np.ndarray,
    catalog: ScoreCatalog,
    calibration: ScoreCalibration | None = None,
) -> ScoreResult:
    """Read the score: crop the (registered) digit band, segment, classify each glyph.

    The digit count is however many glyphs the segmentation finds. Each glyph is
    1-NN-matched (argmin L1) against the exemplars; the digits assemble left→right
    into the integer. `calibration` supplies the locked block offset; if omitted
    the nominal band is used (a well-registered frame / tests).
    """
    cfg = catalog.config
    dx = calibration.dx if calibration is not None else 0
    dy = calibration.dy if calibration is not None else 0
    band = _band_luma(image, catalog.mode, dx, dy)

    vecs = np.stack([t.vec for t in catalog.templates])
    tdig = np.array([t.digit for t in catalog.templates])

    digits: list[int] = []
    dists: list[float] = []
    margins: list[float] = []
    for run in _segment_digits(band, cfg):
        fv = _glyph_vec(band, run, cfg)
        d = np.abs(vecs - fv).sum(1)
        order = np.argsort(d)
        best = int(tdig[order[0]])
        digits.append(best)
        dists.append(float(d[order[0]]))
        # runner-up gap = nearest exemplar of a different digit − nearest
        other = next((float(d[i]) for i in order if int(tdig[i]) != best), float(d[order[0]]))
        margins.append(other - float(d[order[0]]))

    text = "".join(str(x) for x in digits)
    value = int(text) if text else -1
    return ScoreResult(
        value=value,
        digits=tuple(digits),
        dist=max(dists) if dists else 0.0,
        margin=min(margins) if margins else 0.0,
    )
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-09 20:18:11Z)**_

The bug: the corpus frames are 96×105 block crops, but `_band_luma`/`_block_luma` call `_to_canonical` which **stretches** them to 720×480 (the reader assumes full frames + absolute coords). The prototype worked because it operated on the block directly. Fix: embed block crops into a full frame at the block's position instead of stretching — this keeps the full-frame model (and chrome registration) intact and firmware-representative.

```bash
print("exemplars:",len(cat.templates),"digits:",sorted(set(t.digit for t in cat.templates)))
calib=calibrate_score([s.image for s in corp],cat)

ok=0
for s in corp:
    val=score_from_filename(s.path.name)[1]
    c=build_score_catalog([o for o in corp if o.path.name!=s.path.name])
    r=read_score(s.image,c,calib)
    ok+= r.value==val
    if r.value!=val: print("  MISS",s.path.name,"->",r.value)
print(f"LOO exact: {ok}/{len(corp)}")
frames=sorted(glob.glob(os.environ['TMPDIR']+"/score-frames/score-*.png"))
prev=-1; viol=0; first=None; last=None
for p in frames:
    r=read_score(load_bgr(p),cat,calib)
    if first is None: first=r.value
    last=r.value
    if r.value<prev: viol+=1
    prev=max(prev,r.value)
print(f"monotonic over {len(frames)}: {viol} violations; first={first} last={last}")
```

```text
453	def score_eval(samples: list[Sample], mode: str = "training", seed: int = 1234) -> ScoreEvalResult:
454	    """Evaluate the score reader on the labelled score corpus.
455	
456	    Registers once on the whole session (as at gameplay start), then:
457	    - clean: search-free per-frame exact-match + per-cell accuracy + worst margin;
458	    - LOO: the digit classifier's generalization (templates from the other frames);
459	    - A2D: exact-match under gain/offset/noise at the *fixed* calibration (the
460	      continual-operation model — position is locked, only the capture drifts);
461	    - registration: re-register on whole-session position shifts, then exact-match.
462	    """
463	    labelled = [s for s in samples if (p := score_from_filename(s.path.name)) and p[0] == mode]
464	    catalog = build_score_catalog(labelled, mode=mode)
465	    calib = calibrate_score([s.image for s in labelled], catalog)
466	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
467

469	    a2d_ok = a2d_total = 0
470	    margins: list[float] = []
471	    failures: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
472	    for s in labelled:

483	        digit_total += len(truth)
```

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import shutil
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from gameplay.evaluate import score_eval, score_monotonic_eval
from gameplay.metadata import SCORE_BLOCK_ROI, score_from_filename
from gameplay.score import (
    build_score_catalog,
    calibrate_score,
    load_chrome_mask,
    read_score,
)


def test_score_from_filename():
    assert score_from_filename("score__training__010584__cap0121.png") == ("training", 10584)
    assert score_from_filename("score__training__000250__cap0001.png") == ("training", 250)
    assert score_from_filename("song_select__04_rock_and_roll_all_nite.png") is None
    assert score_from_filename("in_song__training.png") is None


def test_corpus_covers_all_digits(score_corpus):
    # The curated frames must expose every glyph 0-9 to build exemplars.
    cat = build_score_catalog(score_corpus)
    assert {t.digit for t in cat.templates} == set(range(10))


def test_segmentation_digit_count(score_corpus):
    # Gap-based segmentation must find exactly len(str(value)) digits per frame.
    cat = build_score_catalog(score_corpus)
    calib = calibrate_score([s.image for s in score_corpus], cat)
    for s in score_corpus:
        value = score_from_filename(s.path.name)[1]
        r = read_score(s.image, cat, calib)
        assert len(r.digits) == len(str(value)), (s.path.name, r.digits)


def test_read_score_clean_exact(score_corpus):
    # Register once on the session, then every frame reads exactly (search-free).
    cat = build_score_catalog(score_corpus)
    calib = calibrate_score([s.image for s in score_corpus], cat)
    for s in score_corpus:
        value = score_from_filename(s.path.name)[1]
        r = read_score(s.image, cat, calib)
        assert r.value == value, (s.path.name, r.digits)


def test_chrome_mask_shape(score_corpus):
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = SCORE_BLOCK_ROI
    mask = load_chrome_mask()
    assert mask.shape == (y1 - y0, x1 - x0)
    assert mask.dtype == bool
    frac = mask.mean()
    assert 0.1 < frac < 0.6, frac


def test_registration_locks_at_zero(score_corpus):
    # The corpus is one rig at a fixed position -> registration is the nominal block.
    cat = build_score_catalog(score_corpus)
    calib = calibrate_score([s.image for s in score_corpus], cat)
    assert (calib.dx, calib.dy) == (0, 0)


def test_score_eval_clean_and_slop(score_corpus):
    res = score_eval(score_corpus)
    assert res.n_total == len(score_corpus)
    assert res.exact_acc == 1.0, res.failures     # clean exact match on the corpus
    assert res.digit_acc == 1.0                    # every digit classified correctly
    assert res.loo_exact_acc == 1.0                # generalizes (leave-one-out)
    assert res.a2d_acc == 1.0                      # gain/offset/noise cancelled
    assert res.margin_min > 0


def test_monotonic_eval_clean(score_corpus, tmp_path: Path):
    # A value-sorted sequence of real frames must read non-decreasing (0 violations).
    ordered = sorted(score_corpus, key=lambda s: score_from_filename(s.path.name)[1])
    for i, s in enumerate(ordered):
        shutil.copy(s.path, tmp_path / f"f{i:04d}.png")
    res = score_monotonic_eval(tmp_path, samples=score_corpus)
    assert res.n_frames == len(ordered)
    assert res.n_violations == 0, res.violations
    assert res.first == score_from_filename(ordered[0].path.name)[1]
    assert res.last == score_from_filename(ordered[-1].path.name)[1]

```

The score reader is reworked for the proportional font and validated against your full capture.

## What changed
- **Gap-based segmentation** replaces the fixed-pitch grid: threshold the digit band (relative `min + 0.6·range`, gain-robust), split the column ink profile into digit blobs right-to-left, resize each blob to a canonical cell, 1-NN match. **Digit count falls out of segmentation** — no fixed N, no blank class. Chrome-of-the-block registration is kept (block crops are embedded into a full frame so the absolute ROIs/registration work unchanged).
- **Corpus**: extracted your 6549 REGION frames, read **54** spanning 3–6 digits (values cross-checked by the monotonic ordering), committed as `score__training__NNNNNN__capNNNN.png` (the capture itself stays gitignored).
- `metadata.SCORE_DIGIT_BAND`, reworked `score.py`, gap-based `score_eval` + new `score_monotonic_eval`, and a `gameplay score-monotonic <dir>` CLI verb.

## Results
- `score_eval`: **54/54 exact, 270/270 per-digit, LOO 54/54, A2D slop 99.7%, re-register 100%**.
- **`score-monotonic` over all 6549 frames: 0 violations (100% clean)**, scores 250→101720, digit counts 3–6. That's the decisive label-free check — a huge jump from the old fixed-pitch 10/16, and confirms your not-monospace observation was the root cause.
- Full suite **59 passed**.

```bash
git commit -F - <<'MSG'
gameplay: score reader — proportional (gap-based) segmentation + capture corpus

The training score font is proportional, not tabular (a `1` is narrower than an
`8`, so digit x-positions shift with the value — confirmed on a 6549-frame
capture), so the fixed-pitch cell grid couldn't sit on the digits (only 10/16
held-out). The digits are cleanly gap-separated, so:

- Replace the fixed-pitch grid + blank class with gap-based segmentation: relative
  ink threshold (min + 0.6*range, gain/offset-robust) over the digit band, split
  the column ink profile into digit blobs right-to-left, resize each blob's bbox to
  a canonical cell, 1-NN match. Digit count falls out of segmentation.
- Chrome-of-the-block registration retained; block crops are embedded into a full
  frame so the absolute ROIs / registration work unchanged.
- metadata.SCORE_DIGIT_BAND (block-relative) replaces the fixed SCORE_ROI field.
- evaluate: gap-based score_eval + score_monotonic_eval (label-free proxy: a play
  only climbs, so any decrease is a misread). cli: score-monotonic verb.

Corpus: 54 frames curated from the capture, read + monotonic-cross-checked,
committed as score__training__NNNNNN__capNNNN.png (replaces the 9-frame set; the
capture itself is gitignored).

Results: score_eval 54/54 exact, 270/270 per-digit, LOO 54/54, A2D slop 99.7%,
re-register 100%; score-monotonic over all 6549 real frames = 0 violations
(250->101720, 3-6 digit). Full suite 59 passed. Career font / firmware port deferred.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
MSG
```

```text
27	static void gp_rect_mean_bgr(const uint8_t *frame, int w, int h,
28	                             int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1, float out[3])
29	{
30	    if (x0 < 0) { x0 = 0; }  if (x1 > w) { x1 = w; }

37	        {
38	            sb += p[0]; sg += p[1]; sr += p[2];
39	            p += GP_BPP;
40	            n++;
41	        }
42	    }
43	    if (n == 0u) { out[0] = out[1] = out[2] = 0.0f; return; }
44	    out[0] = (float)sb / (float)n;
45	    out[1] = (float)sg / (float)n;

73	        gp_rect_mean_bgr(frame, width, height, x0, y0, x1, y1, col[c]);
74	    }
75	
76	    /* Normalize per frame: subtract per-channel mean across cells, divide by the
77	     * scalar spread (matches highlight.cell_colors in the prototype). */
78	    float mean[3] = {0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f};
79	    for (int c = 0; c < count; c++)
80	        for (int ch = 0; ch < 3; ch++) { mean[ch] += col[c][ch]; }
81	    for (int ch = 0; ch < 3; ch++) { mean[ch] /= (float)count; }
82	
83	    double var = 0.0;
84	    for (int c = 0; c < count; c++)
85	        for (int ch = 0; ch < 3; ch++)
86	        {
87	            double d = (double)col[c][ch] - (double)mean[ch];
88	            var += d * d;
89	        }
90	    float std = (float)sqrt(var / (double)(count * 3));
91	    if (std < 1e-6f) { std = 1.0f; }
92	
93	    int best = 0;
94	    float best_dev = -1.0f;
95	    for (int c = 0; c < count; c++)
96	    {
97	        const float *base = &menu->baseline[c * 3];
98	        float dev = 0.0f;
99	        for (int ch = 0; ch < 3; ch++)
100	        {
101	            float v = (col[c][ch] - mean[ch]) / std;
102	            float d = v - base[ch];
103	            dev += d * d;
104	        }
105	        if (dev > best_dev) { best_dev = dev; best = c; }
106	    }
107	    return best;
108	}
109	
110	/* ── song_select ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
111	
112	/* Per-frame-normalized low-res luma grid over an ROI, offset by (dx,dy). */
113	static void gp_song_grid(const uint8_t *frame, int w, int h,
114	                         const int roi[4], int dx, int dy, float *out)
115	{
116	    int x0 = roi[0] + dx, y0 = roi[1] + dy;
117	    int pw = roi[2] - roi[0], ph = roi[3] - roi[1];
118	    for (int r = 0; r < GP_SONG_ROWS; r++)
119	    {
120	        int cy0 = y0 + gp_edge(r, ph, GP_SONG_ROWS);
121	        int cy1 = y0 + gp_edge(r + 1, ph, GP_SONG_ROWS);
122	        if (cy0 < 0) { cy0 = 0; }  if (cy1 > h) { cy1 = h; }
123	        for (int c = 0; c < GP_SONG_COLS; c++)
124	        {
125	            int cx0 = x0 + gp_edge(c, pw, GP_SONG_COLS);
126	            int cx1 = x0 + gp_edge(c + 1, pw, GP_SONG_COLS);
127	            if (cx0 < 0) { cx0 = 0; }  if (cx1 > w) { cx1 = w; }
128	            double s = 0.0; uint32_t n = 0u;
129	            for (int y = cy0; y < cy1; y++)
130	            {
131	                const uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)w + (uint32_t)cx0) * GP_BPP;
132	                for (int x = cx0; x < cx1; x++)
133	                {
134	                    s += (double)p[0] * 29.0 + (double)p[1] * 150.0 + (double)p[2] * 77.0;
135	                    p += GP_BPP;
136	                    n++;
137	                }
138	            }
139	            out[r * GP_SONG_COLS + c] = (n != 0u) ? (float)(s / 256.0 / (double)n) : 0.0f;
140	        }
141	    }
142	    double sum = 0.0;
143	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_SONG_LEN; i++) { sum += out[i]; }
144	    float mean = (float)(sum / (double)GP_SONG_LEN);
145	    double var = 0.0;
146	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_SONG_LEN; i++)
147	    {
148	        double d = (double)out[i] - (double)mean;
149	        var += d * d;
150	    }
151	    float std = (float)sqrt(var / (double)GP_SONG_LEN);
152	    if (std < 1e-6f) { std = 1.0f; }
153	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_SONG_LEN; i++) { out[i] = (out[i] - mean) / std; }
154	}
155	
156	/* Offset-search grids, both ROIs. Static — single observer-task caller. */
157	static float s_slot_grids[GP_SONG_NDX * GP_SONG_NDY][GP_SONG_LEN];
158	static float s_first_grids[GP_SONG_NDX * GP_SONG_NDY][GP_SONG_LEN];
159	
160	int gp_read_song(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height, gp_song_t *out)
161	{
162	    if (width != GP_CANON_W || height != GP_CANON_H)
163	    {
164	        out->setlist = 0; out->index = 0; out->tmpl = -1;
165	        return -1;
166	    }
167	    static const int slot_roi[4]  = GP_SONG_SLOT_ROI;
168	    static const int first_roi[4] = GP_SONG_FIRST_ROI;
169	
170	    int noff = 0;
171	    for (int ix = 0; ix < GP_SONG_NDX; ix++)
172	        for (int iy = 0; iy < GP_SONG_NDY; iy++)
173	        {
174	            gp_song_grid(frame, width, height, slot_roi,  gp_song_dx[ix], gp_song_dy[iy], s_slot_grids[noff]);
175	            gp_song_grid(frame, width, height, first_roi, gp_song_dx[ix], gp_song_dy[iy], s_first_grids[noff]);
176	            noff++;
177	        }
178	
179	    float best_d = 1e30f;
180	    int best_t = -1;
181	    for (int t = 0; t < GP_N_SONGS; t++)
182	    {
183	        const float *vec = gp_song_templates[t].vec;
184	        const float (*grids)[GP_SONG_LEN] =
185	            (gp_song_templates[t].roi_kind == GP_SONG_ROI_FIRST) ? s_first_grids : s_slot_grids;
186	        float tbest = 1e30f;
187	        for (int o = 0; o < noff; o++)
188	        {
189	            float d = 0.0f;
190	            for (int i = 0; i < GP_SONG_LEN; i++) { d += fabsf(grids[o][i] - vec[i]); }
191	            if (d < tbest) { tbest = d; }
192	        }
193	        if (tbest < best_d) { best_d = tbest; best_t = t; }
194	    }
195	
196	    out->tmpl = (int16_t)best_t;
197	    out->setlist = (best_t >= 0) ? gp_song_templates[best_t].setlist : 0;
198	    out->index = (best_t >= 0) ? gp_song_templates[best_t].index : 0;
199	    return 0;
200	}
```

```text
16	 * any other size returns GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN. When non-NULL, *out_best_dist and
17	 * *out_margin receive the nearest-centroid L1 distance and the second-best−best
```

```text
13	/* Split [0, extent) into `n` contiguous spans; edge(i) = round(i*extent/n). */
14	static int gp_edge(int i, int extent, int n)
15	{
16	    return (int)lround((double)i * (double)extent / (double)n);
17	}

19	/* j-th of `n` sample coordinates centred in their sub-cell of [lo, hi). */
20	static int gp_lattice(int j, int lo, int hi, int n)
21	{
22	    int c = (int)((double)lo + (((double)j + 0.5) / (double)n) * (double)(hi - lo));
23	    if (c < lo)      { c = lo; }
24	    if (c > hi - 1)  { c = hi - 1; }
25	    return c;
26	}

28	/* Mean BGR over the GP_FP_SAMPLES × GP_FP_SAMPLES lattice of a region. */
29	static void gp_region_mean(const uint8_t *frame, int w,
30	                           int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1, float out[3])
31	{
32	    uint32_t sb = 0u, sg = 0u, sr = 0u;
33	    int n = GP_FP_SAMPLES;
34	    for (int jy = 0; jy < n; jy++)
35	    {
36	        int y = gp_lattice(jy, y0, y1, n);
37	        const uint8_t *row = frame + (uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)w * GP_BPP;
38	        for (int jx = 0; jx < n; jx++)
39	        {
40	            int x = gp_lattice(jx, x0, x1, n);
41	            const uint8_t *p = row + (uint32_t)x * GP_BPP;
42	            sb += p[0];
43	            sg += p[1];
44	            sr += p[2];
45	        }
46	    }
47	    float cnt = (float)(n * n);
48	    out[0] = (float)sb / cnt;
49	    out[1] = (float)sg / cnt;
50	    out[2] = (float)sr / cnt;
51	}

63	    {

65	        int y1 = gp_edge(r + 1, GP_CANON_H, GP_FP_ROWS);
66	        for (int c = 0; c < GP_FP_COLS; c++)
67	        {
68	            int x0 = gp_edge(c, GP_CANON_W, GP_FP_COLS);
69	            int x1 = gp_edge(c + 1, GP_CANON_W, GP_FP_COLS);
70	            float bgr[3];
71	            gp_region_mean(frame, width, x0, y0, x1, y1, bgr);
72	            s_fp_f[idx++] = bgr[0];
73	            s_fp_f[idx++] = bgr[1];
74	            s_fp_f[idx++] = bgr[2];
75	        }
76	    }
77	
78	#if GP_FP_NORMALIZE
79	    double sum = 0.0;
80	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_FP_LEN; i++) { sum += s_fp_f[i]; }

82	    double var = 0.0;
83	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_FP_LEN; i++)
84	    {

86	        var += d * d;

89	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_FP_LEN; i++)
90	    {
91	        float v = (std > 1e-6f)
92	                ? ((s_fp_f[i] - mean) / std * GP_NORM_STD + GP_NORM_MEAN)
93	                : GP_NORM_MEAN;
94	        long q = lroundf(v);
95	        if (q < 0)        { q = 0; }
96	        else if (q > 255) { q = 255; }
97	        out[i] = (uint8_t)q;
98	    }
99	#else
100	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_FP_LEN; i++)
101	    {
102	        long q = lroundf(s_fp_f[i]);
103	        if (q < 0)        { q = 0; }
104	        else if (q > 255) { q = 255; }
105	        out[i] = (uint8_t)q;
106	    }
107	#endif

109	}

112	
113	uint8_t gp_classify(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height,
114	                    int32_t *out_best_dist, int32_t *out_margin)
115	{
116	    if (gp_fingerprint(frame, width, height, s_fp) != 0)
117	    {
118	        if (out_best_dist) { *out_best_dist = INT32_MAX; }
119	        if (out_margin)    { *out_margin = 0; }
120	        return GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN;
121	    }
122	
123	    int32_t best = INT32_MAX, second = INT32_MAX;
124	    int best_k = -1;
125	    for (int k = 0; k < GP_N_SCREENS; k++)
126	    {
127	        const uint8_t *cen = gp_centroids[k];
128	        int32_t d = 0;
129	        for (int i = 0; i < GP_FP_LEN; i++)
130	        {
131	            int diff = (int)s_fp[i] - (int)cen[i];
132	            d += (diff < 0) ? -diff : diff;
133	        }
134	        if (d < best)        { second = best; best = d; best_k = k; }
135	        else if (d < second) { second = d; }
136	    }
137	
138	    int32_t margin = second - best;
139	    if (out_best_dist) { *out_best_dist = best; }
140	    if (out_margin)    { *out_margin = margin; }
141	
142	    if (best <= GP_CLS_T_ABS && margin >= GP_CLS_T_MARGIN)
143	    {
144	        return (uint8_t)best_k;
145	    }
146	    return GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN;
147	}
```
