134	    thr = band.min() + cfg.ink_frac * (band.max() - band.min())
135	    return band > thr
136	
137	
138	def _segment_digits(band: np.ndarray, cfg: ScoreConfig) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
139	    """Split the digit band into per-digit column runs (left->right).
140	
141	    A column with any ink extends the current run; more than `min_gap` empty
142	    columns closes it. Specks (too narrow / too little ink) are dropped.
143	    """
144	    col = _ink_mask(band, cfg).sum(0)
145	    runs: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
146	    start: int | None = None
147	    gap = 0
148	    for x, c in enumerate(col):
149	        if c > 0:
150	            if start is None:
151	                start = x
152	            gap = 0
153	        elif start is not None:
154	            gap += 1
155	            if gap > cfg.min_gap:
156	                runs.append((start, x - gap))
157	                start = None
158	    if start is not None:
159	        runs.append((start, len(col) - 1))
160	    return [
161	        (x0, x1) for x0, x1 in runs
162	        if (x1 - x0 + 1) >= cfg.min_width and int(col[x0:x1 + 1].sum()) >= cfg.min_ink
163	    ]
164	
165	
166	def _glyph_vec(band: np.ndarray, run: tuple[int, int], cfg: ScoreConfig) -> np.ndarray:
167	    """Normalized fingerprint of one segmented digit (bbox → canonical grid)."""
168	    x0, x1 = run
169	    sub = band[:, x0:x1 + 1]
170	    # Crop to the glyph's ink rows so height variation doesn't dominate.
171	    rmask = _ink_mask(band, cfg)[:, x0:x1 + 1].any(1)
172	    ys = np.where(rmask)[0]
173	    if len(ys):
174	        sub = sub[ys.min():ys.max() + 1, :]
175	    ye = np.linspace(0, sub.shape[0], cfg.glyph_rows + 1).round().astype(int)
176	    xe = np.linspace(0, sub.shape[1], cfg.glyph_cols + 1).round().astype(int)
177	    g = np.empty((cfg.glyph_rows, cfg.glyph_cols), dtype=np.float64)
178	    for r in range(cfg.glyph_rows):
179	        for c in range(cfg.glyph_cols):
180	            blk = sub[ye[r]:max(ye[r] + 1, ye[r + 1]), xe[c]:max(xe[c] + 1, xe[c + 1])]
181	            g[r, c] = blk.mean() if blk.size else 0.0
182	    v = g.reshape(-1)
183	    v -= v.mean()
184	    s = v.std()
185	    return v / s if s > 1e-6 else v
186	
187	
188	# ─── chrome registration (locks the block; unchanged) ───────────────────────────
```

271	    digits of the filename value (the run count must match), and each glyph vector

282	        mode_images.append(s.image)
283	        band = _band_luma(s.image, mode)

285	        digits = str(value)
286	        if len(runs) != len(digits):
287	            continue  # segmentation disagrees with the label — skip this frame
288	        for run, ch in zip(runs, digits):
289	            templates.append(DigitTemplate(digit=int(ch), vec=_glyph_vec(band, run, config)))

302	    1-NN-matched (argmin L1) against the exemplars; the digits assemble left→right
303	    into the integer. `calibration` supplies the locked block offset; if omitted
304	    the nominal band is used (a well-registered frame / tests).

308	    dy = calibration.dy if calibration is not None else 0
309	    band = _band_luma(image, catalog.mode, dx, dy)
310

312	    tdig = np.array([t.digit for t in catalog.templates])
313

315	    dists: list[float] = []
316	    margins: list[float] = []

318	        fv = _glyph_vec(band, run, cfg)
319	        d = np.abs(vecs - fv).sum(1)
320	        order = np.argsort(d)

325	        other = next((float(d[i]) for i in order if int(tdig[i]) != best), float(d[order[0]]))
326	        margins.append(other - float(d[order[0]]))

1	"""In-song score reader: per-digit glyph OCR of the open-ended score value.
2	
3	Unlike the menu/song readers (closed-set template matches), the score is an
4	open-ended number, so it is read digit by digit. The training font is white and
5	**proportional** (a `1` is narrower than an `8`, so digit x-positions shift with
6	the value — verified on a 6549-frame capture), but the digits are cleanly
7	gap-separated. So digits are isolated by their ink (the gaps between them), not a
8	fixed grid; each is normalized to a canonical cell and matched against a per-mode
9	bank of 0-9 glyph exemplars (1-NN). The digit count falls out of the segmentation
10	(no fixed N, no blank class).
11	
12	Two stages, because the field position is fixed on a given rig but the analog
13	capture varies frame to frame:
14	
15	- **Registration (once).** The whole scoring block (`metadata.SCORE_BLOCK_ROI`)
16	  is located by matching its *chrome* — the static box frame, inner panel texture,
17	  and medallion ring, which are digit-independent and identical in training and
18	  career. A masked (`metadata` + hand-drawn `score_block_mask.png`) normalized-SAD
19	  offset search finds the block's `(dx, dy)` for this rig (`calibrate_score` →
20	  `ScoreCalibration`); the digit band is then a fixed offset inside it. Run once
21	  at gameplay start over a few frames.
22	- **Per-frame read (continual).** `read_score` crops the digit band at the locked
23	  offset, segments it, and 1-NN-classifies each glyph — no offset search. A
24	  per-band relative ink threshold and per-glyph normalization cancel A2D
25	  gain/offset drift. Cheap: an ink mask + a small L1 per digit.
26	
27	Templates are built from the labelled score corpus: each frame's digits (from its
28	filename value) map left→right onto the segmented glyphs, each kept as a 1-NN
29	exemplar — no hand-cropping. Integer-friendly for the firmware port.
30	"""

#include "game/gameplay_score.h"
#include "game/gameplay_metadata.h"

#include <math.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

#define GP_BPP             3
#define GP_SCORE_MAX_RUNS  16   /* raw runs before filtering (>= any digit count) */

/* Split [0, extent) into `n` spans; edge(i) = round(i*extent/n). Matches the
 * prototype's np.linspace bin edges and gameplay_select.c's gp_edge. */
static int gp_edge(int i, int extent, int n)
{
    return (int)lround((double)i * (double)extent / (double)n);
}

/* Digit-band scratch (one mode's band), row-major. */
static uint8_t  s_ink[GP_SCORE_BAND_MAX_H * GP_SCORE_BAND_MAX_W];  /* 1 = pixel above ink threshold */
static uint16_t s_col_ink[GP_SCORE_BAND_MAX_W];                   /* ink-pixel count per column */
static uint8_t  s_glyph[GP_SCORE_LEN];                            /* one digit's coverage mask (0-255) */
static uint16_t s_runs[GP_SCORE_MAX_RUNS][2];                     /* [x0, x1] inclusive column runs */

/* Fill s_ink (0/1) over the band rect: luma = (B*29+G*150+R*77)/256, ink where
 * luma > min + INK_FRAC*(max-min) (relative → gain/offset robust). bw/bh out. */
static void band_ink(const uint8_t *frame, int w, int h,
                     const uint16_t band[4], int *bw, int *bh)
{
    int x0 = band[0], y0 = band[1], x1 = band[2], y1 = band[3];
    int W = x1 - x0, H = y1 - y0;
    *bw = W;
    *bh = H;

    float lo = 1e30f, hi = -1e30f;
    static float lum[GP_SCORE_BAND_MAX_H * GP_SCORE_BAND_MAX_W];
    for (int r = 0; r < H; r++)
    {
        int fy = y0 + r;
        for (int c = 0; c < W; c++)
        {
            int fx = x0 + c;
            float v = 0.0f;
            if (fx >= 0 && fx < w && fy >= 0 && fy < h)
            {
                const uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)fy * (uint32_t)w + (uint32_t)fx) * GP_BPP;
                v = (float)((double)p[0] * 29.0 + (double)p[1] * 150.0 + (double)p[2] * 77.0) / 256.0f;
            }
            lum[r * W + c] = v;
            if (v < lo) { lo = v; }
            if (v > hi) { hi = v; }
        }
    }
    float thr = lo + GP_SCORE_INK_FRAC * (hi - lo);
    for (int i = 0; i < W * H; i++) { s_ink[i] = (lum[i] > thr) ? 1u : 0u; }
}

/* Per-cell ink coverage (0-255) of one digit run [x0,x1] (inclusive), cropped to
 * its ink rows and resized to GLYPH_ROWS x GLYPH_COLS. Mirrors score.py _glyph_cov. */
static void glyph_cov(int bw, int bh, int x0, int x1)
{
    /* Ink rows spanned by this run. */
    int ry0 = -1, ry1 = -1;
    for (int r = 0; r < bh; r++)
    {
        for (int c = x0; c <= x1; c++)
        {
            if (s_ink[r * bw + c]) { if (ry0 < 0) { ry0 = r; } ry1 = r; break; }
        }
    }
    if (ry0 < 0) { ry0 = 0; ry1 = bh - 1; }
    int rh = ry1 - ry0 + 1, rw = x1 - x0 + 1;

    for (int gr = 0; gr < GP_SCORE_GLYPH_ROWS; gr++)
    {
        int ya = gp_edge(gr, rh, GP_SCORE_GLYPH_ROWS);
        int yb = gp_edge(gr + 1, rh, GP_SCORE_GLYPH_ROWS);
        if (yb <= ya) { yb = ya + 1; }
        for (int gc = 0; gc < GP_SCORE_GLYPH_COLS; gc++)
        {
            int xa = gp_edge(gc, rw, GP_SCORE_GLYPH_COLS);
            int xb = gp_edge(gc + 1, rw, GP_SCORE_GLYPH_COLS);
            if (xb <= xa) { xb = xa + 1; }
            uint32_t sum = 0u, n = 0u;
            for (int r = ry0 + ya; r < ry0 + yb; r++)
                for (int c = x0 + xa; c < x0 + xb; c++)
                {
                    sum += s_ink[r * bw + c];
                    n++;
                }
            /* coverage fraction → 0-255, rounded */
            s_glyph[gr * GP_SCORE_GLYPH_COLS + gc] =
                (n != 0u) ? (uint8_t)((sum * 255u + n / 2u) / n) : 0u;
        }
    }
}

int gp_read_score(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height,
                  uint8_t mode, gp_score_t *out)
{
    out->value = -1; out->ndigits = 0; out->dist = 0; out->margin = 0;
    if (width != GP_CANON_W || height != GP_CANON_H) { return -1; }
    if (mode >= GP_N_SCORE_MODES) { return -1; }
    const gp_score_mode_t *M = &gp_score_modes[mode];

    int bw = 0, bh = 0;
    band_ink(frame, width, height, M->band, &bw, &bh);

    for (int c = 0; c < bw; c++)
    {
        uint16_t cnt = 0;
        for (int r = 0; r < bh; r++) { if (s_ink[r * bw + c]) { cnt++; } }
        s_col_ink[c] = cnt;
    }

    /* Segment: contiguous ink columns split by > MIN_GAP empty columns (mirrors
     * score.py _segment_digits), then drop specks. */
    int nruns = 0;
    int start = -1, gap = 0;
    for (int c = 0; c < bw; c++)
    {
        if (s_col_ink[c] > 0)
        {
            if (start < 0) { start = c; }
            gap = 0;
        }
        else if (start >= 0)
        {
            gap++;
            if (gap > GP_SCORE_MIN_GAP)
            {
                if (nruns < GP_SCORE_MAX_RUNS) { s_runs[nruns][0] = (uint16_t)start; s_runs[nruns][1] = (uint16_t)(c - gap); nruns++; }
                start = -1;
            }
        }
    }
    if (start >= 0 && nruns < GP_SCORE_MAX_RUNS)
    {
        s_runs[nruns][0] = (uint16_t)start; s_runs[nruns][1] = (uint16_t)(bw - 1); nruns++;
    }

    int32_t value = 0;
    int ndigits = 0;
    int32_t worst_dist = 0;
    int32_t min_margin = INT32_MAX;

    for (int ri = 0; ri < nruns && ndigits < GP_SCORE_MAX_DIGITS; ri++)
    {
        int x0 = s_runs[ri][0], x1 = s_runs[ri][1];
        uint32_t ink = 0;
        for (int k = x0; k <= x1; k++) { ink += s_col_ink[k]; }
        if ((x1 - x0 + 1) < GP_SCORE_MIN_WIDTH || ink < (uint32_t)GP_SCORE_MIN_INK) { continue; }

        glyph_cov(bw, bh, x0, x1);

        /* argmin integer L1 over the 10 per-digit coverage templates (row == digit);
         * margin = gap to the runner-up digit. */
        int32_t best = INT32_MAX, second = INT32_MAX;
        int best_digit = 0;
        for (int d = 0; d < GP_SCORE_NDIGITS; d++)
        {
            const uint8_t *tmpl = M->tmpl[d];
            int32_t l1 = 0;
            for (int i = 0; i < GP_SCORE_LEN; i++) { l1 += abs((int)s_glyph[i] - (int)tmpl[i]); }
            if (l1 < best) { second = best; best = l1; best_digit = d; }
            else if (l1 < second) { second = l1; }
        }

        value = value * 10 + best_digit;
        ndigits++;
        if (best > worst_dist) { worst_dist = best; }
        if (second - best < min_margin) { min_margin = second - best; }
    }

    out->ndigits = (uint8_t)ndigits;
    out->value = (ndigits > 0) ? value : -1;
    out->dist = worst_dist;
    out->margin = (ndigits > 0) ? min_margin : 0;
    return 0;
}

Root cause: `heartbeat_write()` (and `results.c` `Results_Append`) declared `SYS_FS_FSTAT st;` **uninitialized** before `SYS_FS_FileStat`. Per the SYS_FS contract (`sys_fs.h:1374`) the caller must set `lfname = NULL`; uninitialized, `st.lfname` held stack garbage → non-NULL → `FATFS_stat` wrote through it → abort. Explains the **random timing** exactly: crash only when that stack slot happened to hold an unmapped value (otherwise a silent harmless-looking write). `art.c`/`storage.c` already `memset`+`lfname=NULL` before `SYS_FS_DirRead` (the codebase knew the contract; these two sites missed it). **Fix:** `memset(&st,0,sizeof st)` before `SYS_FS_FileStat` in both `health_monitor.c` and `results.c`. Done — the score matcher is now the simple version you wanted, end to end.

## What changed (host + firmware)
- **Feature**: per-glyph **ink coverage** (0–255 per cell) instead of normalized grayscale — keeps the thin closed-loop strokes that were the only real confusion (8→5/3, 0→3).
- **Matcher**: **10 per-digit averaged templates + integer L1 argmin**, replacing the 270-exemplar float 1-NN. No soft-float, no per-frame normalization.
- **`score.py`**, **`export_c.py`** (emits a `[10][140]` uint8 array per mode), **`gameplay_score.c`** (integer coverage + L1) all reworked; still mode-parameterized for career.

## Results
- **eval 54/54 exact, LOO 54/54, monotonic 0 violations over all 6549 frames** — identical accuracy to the heavy version.
- **Header 554 KB → 157 KB** (score data: 1.4 KB vs ~400 KB).
- Host↔firmware **cross-check passes** (`gp_read_score` == `read_score` on all 54 frames); `gameplay_score.c` compiles clean `-Wall -Wextra`; full suite **60 passed**.

You were right — it wasn't a hard OCR problem. The diagnosis (binary mask only ever confused the closed-loop digits) pinpointed the one thing to fix, and coverage-instead-of-binary closed the gap while staying a plain integer mask match.

Crystal clear, and exactly as you said:
- **1x** = no digit (the dim brown portrait medallion) — e.g. frames 250, 97390.
- **2x** = **gold/yellow** "2" (frame 99440).
- **3x** = **green** "3" (frame 3862).
- **4x** = **purple/magenta** "4" (most frames).

So color alone should separate 2/3/4, and 1x = "no bright saturated digit." No segmentation, no glyph match — just the dominant color in the medallion. Let me measure the color signatures on representative frames to nail a simple integer rule and the ROI:

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>

```bash
export UV_CACHE_DIR=$TMPDIR/uv-cache && uv run python - <<'PY'
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np, os
d=os.environ['TMPDIR']+"/score-frames"
# block-rel ROI over the medallion/multiplier (center-lower); block is 96x105
ROI=(38,44,82,96)  # x0,y0,x1,y1
label={1:"1x",328:"3x",655:"4x",6214:"2x",5560:"1x",5887:"1x",982:"4x"}
def stats(num):
    a=np.asarray(Image.open(f"{d}/score-{num:04d}.png").convert("RGB")).astype(int)
    x0,y0,x1,y1=ROI; s=a[y0:y1,x0:x1].reshape(-1,3)
    R,G,B=s[:,0],s[:,1],s[:,2]
    mx=s.max(1); mn=s.min(1); sat=mx-mn
    # bright, saturated pixels only
    bright=(mx>110)&(sat>40)
    purple=bright&(R>G+25)&(B>G+25)          # magenta: R&B > G
    green =bright&(G>R+20)&(G>B+20)
    yellow=bright&(R>B+40)&(G>B+40)&(R>G-40)  # R&G high, B low
    n=len(R)
    return dict(brightfrac=round(bright.mean(),3),
                purple=int(purple.sum()), green=int(green.sum()), yellow=int(yellow.sum()),
                meanRGB=tuple(int(v) for v in s[bright].mean(0)) if bright.any() else (0,0,0))
for num in sorted(label):
    print(f"score-{num:04d} ({label[num]}): {stats(num)}")
PY

from PIL import Image

from collections import Counter
d=os.environ['TMPDIR']+"/score-frames"; files=sorted(glob.glob(f"{d}/score-*.png"))
ROI=(38,44,82,96)
def mult(path):
    a=np.asarray(Image.open(path).convert("RGB")).astype(int)
    x0,y0,x1,y1=ROI; s=a[y0:y1,x0:x1].reshape(-1,3)
    R,G,B=s[:,0],s[:,1],s[:,2]; mx=s.max(1); sat=mx-s.min(1)

    return {p:4,g:3,y:2}[best]

```md
# Plan: in-song multiplier reader (color classifier) → dashboard 1X/2X/3X/4X buttons

## Context
Next gameplay-telemetry value after the score: the GH3 score **multiplier**, shown as a big glyph
in the scoring-block medallion. Four states: **1x = no digit** (dim portrait), **2x = gold**,
**3x = green**, **4x = purple**. Verified on the 6549-frame capture — color alone separates them
cleanly (hundreds of colored pixels vs ~0), and the classifier's output climbs 1→2→3→4 / resets to
1 with only **1 anomalous transition in 6548**. So no OCR/segmentation: a **color-count classifier**
over one medallion ROI. Display on the existing `Marvin_BUTTON_DASHBOARD_ROBOT_{1,2,3,4}X` buttons
(highlight the active one — the `ApplyFret` pattern). Mode-independent (colors identical in
training/career), so one classifier, no per-mode data.

## Approach

def classify(a,roi,mincount):
    p,g,y,_=counts(a,roi); best=max(p,g,y)
    if best<mincount: return 1

PY

d=os.environ['TMPDIR']+"/score-frames"

# Plan: in-song streak reader (odometer OCR + monotonic/carry tracker) → dashboard STREAK label

## Context
Last gameplay-telemetry value in the GH3 scoring block: the **note-streak counter**, a 3-tumbler
mechanical odometer to the right of the multiplier medallion. It only appears once the streak is
~25+, and the tumblers **roll** into place — the units rolls constantly, the tens/hundreds roll at
carries — so any single frame can show one or more mid-roll (unreadable) digits. Per the user's rule:
assume the count is **monotonic increasing** within a run (until a miss/reset); if a digit can't be
read, hold its last value — unless a higher place rolled (a carry), in which case lower places are 0.
Goal: read the streak and show it live on the dashboard `Marvin_LABEL_DASHBOARD_ROBOT_Streak` label
(value; the `..._STREAK` caption stays "STREAK"), mirroring the score.

Confirmed geometry from the 6549-frame capture (block-relative x, strip near block bottom):
- **note icon** ~36–46 (ignored), **hundreds** center ~54, **tens** center ~67, **units** center ~84.
- **units** cell is always the bright **dark-on-light** tumbler; **hundreds/tens** are **white-on-dark**
  (same polarity as the score). Verified on frames 656=`050`, 3001=`17·`(units rolling), 5001=`295`,
  400=`03·`(units washed). Presence is a clean signal: strip max-luma ~75 & bright-frac 0 when absent
  vs max-luma ~175 & bright-frac ~0.07–0.11 when shown.

This mirrors the completed score/multiplier work: host prototype in `tools/gameplay/` → pure-C reader
→ engine `Observe` → dashboard feed. `DashboardFeed_PostStreak(uint16_t)` + `DASH_EVT_STREAK` stubs
already exist — only the apply path is unwired.

## Approach

Split into a **stateless per-frame raw read** (cross-checkable C==Python) and a **stateful tracker**
(monotonic/carry) layered on top — same split used for score (stateless) vs the play loop's resets.

**1. Digit templates — polarity-normalized coverage (host).** Reuse the score reader's per-cell
**ink-coverage** idea (0–255 coverage map, integer L1 argmin over 10 templates), but extract coverage
per-cell by polarity: white-on-dark cells → ink = bright pixels; the units light cell → ink = dark
pixels. One coverage-normalized template set of 10 digits serves all three cells. Because the streak
has **no filename ground truth** (unlike the score), build the templates from a **small hand-labeled
odometer corpus** — read ~20–40 strip crops from the capture montages (enough to cover digits 0–9 in
both polarities). **This labeling + a leave-one-out check is the feasibility gate**; if per-cell
reads aren't clean I'll report back before wiring firmware.

**2. Reader `read_streak(image) -> (present, digits[3], known[3])` (host `score.py`+`metadata.py`).**
- `STREAK_ROI`/three cell columns + note-icon exclusion as metadata constants (abs 720×480, derived
  from the block-rel centers above via `SCORE_BLOCK_ROI`).
- **Presence:** bright-pixel fraction over the strip vs a threshold (`STREAK_PRESENT_MIN`).
- Per cell: extract polarity-correct coverage → L1 argmin over the 10 templates. Flag the cell
  **rolling/unknown** when the best distance exceeds `STREAK_UNK_MAX` or the best/2nd-best margin is
  too small (mid-roll matches nothing cleanly). Reuse `_ensure_full_frame` so block-crop or full frame
  both work.

**3. Stateful tracker `StreakTracker` (host) — the monotonic/carry rule.** Holds `last_val` and
`last_digits[3]`; `reset()` at song start / when presence is lost. Per frame, top-down over places:
a known digit that increased vs last marks a **carry** → all lower places forced to 0; an unknown
digit is **held** from last unless a higher place carried (→0). Compose the value, then enforce
**non-decreasing** (a present-frame value below `last_val` with no reset is distrusted → keep
`last_val`). Absent → treat as reset (streak <25, not shown) → report 0/blank. Validate over the full
6549-frame sequence: monotonic within runs, resets at song boundaries, matches hand-read spot checks.

**4. Firmware `game/gameplay_score.{h,c}`.** `gp_read_streak(frame,w,h, gp_streak_raw_t *out)` —
stateless, fills `{present, digit[3], known[3]}` using the same integer coverage + L1 over
`export_c`-emitted `GP_STREAK_*` (ROI, cell columns, thresholds, `gp_streak_tmpl[10][GP_...]`). A small
**stateful tracker** (static state in `gameplay_engine`, or a tiny `gameplay_streak` helper) applies the
monotonic/carry combine → `game_state_t.streak` (new `uint16_t`); reset entry called at song start.
Log `GAME: in_song / score N x<m> streak<s>`.

**5. Dashboard.** Producer: `game_controller.play_until_done` → `DashboardFeed_PostStreak(gs.streak)`,
plus a reset to 0 at song start beside the existing score/mult/playtime resets, and reset the engine's
streak tracker there. Consumer (`dashboard_feed.c`): wire `DASH_EVT_STREAK` →
`ScreenDashboard_ApplyStreak(uint16_t)`, a new writer that sets `Marvin_LABEL_DASHBOARD_ROBOT_Streak`
via a static `leFixedString` (blank when 0/absent) — a direct copy of `ScreenDashboard_ApplyScore`
(`s_score_buf`/`s_score_str` pattern at screen_dashboard.c:97,164,370).

## Files to change
- `tools/gameplay/gameplay/{metadata.py, score.py, export_c.py}` — `STREAK_*` geometry/thresholds,
  `read_streak` + `StreakTracker`, streak→metadata header block; regenerates `gameplay_metadata.h`.
- `tools/gameplay/tests/test_firmware_classify.py` — `streak` driver mode + cross-check
  (`gp_read_streak` raw == `read_streak` on all corpus frames; C==Python, no labels needed).
- new host asset: a small labeled odometer corpus (montage-read) + template builder, under the
  gameplay tool (gitignored capture stays out of the repo; committed templates go in the header).
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/game/gameplay_score.{h,c}` — `gp_read_streak` + tracker helper.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/game/gameplay_engine.{c,h}` — `game_state_t.streak` + in_song read + tracker/reset.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/game/game_controller.c` — `PostStreak` + reset at song start.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/dashboard_feed.c` — apply `DASH_EVT_STREAK`.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/dashboard/screen_dashboard.{c,h}` — `ScreenDashboard_ApplyStreak`.
- journals (gameplay + marvin).

## Verification
- Host: `uv run pytest` green incl. the new C==Python cross-check; LOO on the hand-labeled corpus;
  a consistency run over the 6549-frame capture (streak monotonic within runs, resets at boundaries,
  matches hand-read spot checks). **Go/no-go on reader accuracy before firmware wiring.**
- Firmware (Greg's MPLAB build): on a training run the ROBOT streak label tracks the on-screen
  odometer, stays put through single-digit rolls, jumps correctly at carries, blanks/zeros on
  miss/reset and at song start; `GAME` log shows `streak<s>`. Lands "code-complete pending Greg's build".

## Notes / out of scope
- `DashboardFeed_PostStreak` + `DASH_EVT_STREAK` already exist (stubs) — just wire the apply.
- Static allocation only (templates in the generated header; tracker state static). No malloc.
- Career-font score mode still deferred. Streak is the last scoring-block element.

156	# The score is an *open-ended* value, so unlike the menu/song readers it needs
157	# per-digit glyph recognition rather than a whole-field template match. The
158	# training font is white and *proportional* (not tabular — a `1` is narrower than
159	# an `8`, so digit x-positions shift with the value; verified on a 6549-frame
160	# capture). The digits are cleanly gap-separated, so they are segmented by their
161	# ink (gaps between digits) rather than a fixed grid, then each is matched against
162	# 0-9. Per gameplay mode, because the font/box differs (training = white
163	# proportional; career = green segmented, added later).
164	#
165	# The digit search band, relative to the chrome-registered block: the glyph rows,
166	# spanning the full box interior so up to 6 digits fit (score can exceed 99999).
167	# Canonical 720x480 space. See docs/journal.md.
168	SCORE_DIGIT_BAND: dict[str, tuple[int, int, int, int]] = {
169	    "training": (122, 316, 204, 332),
170	}
171	
172	# The whole scoring block. This is the marvin-perf capture region *and* the
173	# registration fiducial: its chrome (the ornate box frame, inner panel texture,
174	# and medallion ring) is static — independent of the score digits and identical
175	# in training and career (verified: both modes' chrome registers to the same
176	# position) — so the block is located once by matching that chrome, and the digit
177	# cells sit at fixed offsets inside it. Fits both modes' full scoring display
178	# (score + multiplier + streak). Canonical 720x480 space.
179	SCORE_BLOCK_ROI = (114, 309, 210, 414)
180	# Inner box rectangle whose static chrome drives registration (the mask keeps the
181	# low-variation chrome pixels inside this rect, excluding the digit/multiplier/
182	# medallion-interior regions that change). Canonical 720x480 space.
183	SCORE_CHROME_BOX = (127, 311, 190, 397)
184	
185	# ─── score multiplier (colour-count classifier) ────────────────────────────────
186	#
187	# The multiplier glyph in the medallion has a fixed colour per value: 2x = gold,
188	# 3x = green, 4x = purple/magenta; 1x shows no digit (the dim portrait). So it's
189	# read by *colour*, not shape — count bright, saturated purple/green/yellow pixels
190	# in a small patch over the digit and take the argmax (or 1x if none clears a
191	# floor). A 16x24 patch is enough (we need only the hue), ~6x smaller than the
192	# glyph. Mode-independent (colours identical in training/career). 720x480 space.
193	SCORE_MULT_ROI = (164, 367, 180, 391)
194	SCORE_MULT_BRIGHT_MIN = 110   # a pixel counts only if max(R,G,B) exceeds this
195	SCORE_MULT_SAT_MIN = 40       # ...and (max-min) exceeds this (saturated)
196	SCORE_MULT_MIN_COUNT = 30     # fewer than this of the winning colour => 1x
197	
198	
199	def score_from_filename(filename: str) -> tuple[str, int] | None:
200	    """Parse a score corpus filename into (mode, value).
201	
202	    `score__training__010584__snap0121.png` -> ("training", 10584).
203	    Returns None for non-score filenames.
204	    """
205	    stem = filename.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
206	    if stem.endswith(".png"):
207	        stem = stem[: -len(".png")]
208	    parts = stem.split("__")
209	    if len(parts) < 3 or parts[0] != "score" or not parts[2].isdigit():
210	        return None
211	    return parts[1], int(parts[2])

132	def _band_luma(image: np.ndarray, mode: str, dx: int = 0, dy: int = 0) -> np.ndarray:
133	    """Luma of the digit search band, shifted by the registration offset."""
134	    img = _ensure_full_frame(image)

140	def _ink_mask(band: np.ndarray, cfg: ScoreConfig) -> np.ndarray:
141	    thr = band.min() + cfg.ink_frac * (band.max() - band.min())
142	    return band > thr

145	def _segment_digits(band: np.ndarray, cfg: ScoreConfig) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
146	    """Split the digit band into per-digit column runs (left->right).
147	
148	    A column with any ink extends the current run; more than `min_gap` empty
149	    columns closes it. Specks (too narrow / too little ink) are dropped.
150	    """
151	    col = _ink_mask(band, cfg).sum(0)
152	    runs: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
153	    start: int | None = None
154	    gap = 0
155	    for x, c in enumerate(col):
156	        if c > 0:
157	            if start is None:
158	                start = x
159	            gap = 0
160	        elif start is not None:
161	            gap += 1
162	            if gap > cfg.min_gap:
163	                runs.append((start, x - gap))
164	                start = None
165	    if start is not None:
166	        runs.append((start, len(col) - 1))
167	    return [
168	        (x0, x1) for x0, x1 in runs
169	        if (x1 - x0 + 1) >= cfg.min_width and int(col[x0:x1 + 1].sum()) >= cfg.min_ink
170	    ]

173	def _glyph_cov(band: np.ndarray, run: tuple[int, int], cfg: ScoreConfig) -> np.ndarray:
174	    """Ink-coverage fingerprint of one segmented digit (bbox → canonical grid).
175	
176	    Each cell holds the fraction of its pixels above the band's relative ink
177	    threshold, quantized to uint8 0-255. Coverage (not a 1-bit mask) keeps the
178	    thin/antialiased strokes that separate look-alike digits (8 vs 5/3); the
179	    relative threshold makes it gain/offset robust. Matching is then a plain
180	    integer L1 over 10 per-digit templates — no float normalization.
181	    """
182	    x0, x1 = run
183	    mask = _ink_mask(band, cfg)[:, x0:x1 + 1]
184	    ys = np.where(mask.any(1))[0]
185	    if len(ys):
186	        mask = mask[ys.min():ys.max() + 1, :]
187	    m = mask.astype(np.float64)
188	    ye = np.linspace(0, m.shape[0], cfg.glyph_rows + 1).round().astype(int)
189	    xe = np.linspace(0, m.shape[1], cfg.glyph_cols + 1).round().astype(int)
190	    g = np.empty((cfg.glyph_rows, cfg.glyph_cols), dtype=np.float64)
191	    for r in range(cfg.glyph_rows):
192	        for c in range(cfg.glyph_cols):
193	            blk = m[ye[r]:max(ye[r] + 1, ye[r + 1]), xe[c]:max(xe[c] + 1, xe[c + 1])]
194	            g[r, c] = blk.mean() if blk.size else 0.0
195	    return np.round(g.reshape(-1) * 255.0).astype(np.uint8)

201	def _block_luma(image: np.ndarray, dx: int = 0, dy: int = 0) -> np.ndarray:
202	    """Luma of the scoring block at the nominal position shifted by (dx, dy)."""
203	    img = _ensure_full_frame(image)
204	    x0, y0, x1, y1 = SCORE_BLOCK_ROI
205	    patch = img[y0 + dy:y1 + dy, x0 + dx:x1 + dx].astype(np.float64)

209	def load_chrome_mask(path=None) -> np.ndarray:
210	    """Load the hand-drawn registration mask as a bool array at block resolution.
211	
212	    The mask PNG paints the static-chrome pixels (used for registration) in
213	    magenta; it may be authored at any integer upscale of the block. Returns a
214	    (block_h, block_w) bool array.
215	    """
216	    x0, y0, x1, y1 = SCORE_BLOCK_ROI
217	    bw, bh = x1 - x0, y1 - y0
218	    p = path if path is not None else score_corpus_dir() / CHROME_MASK_FILE
219	    a = load_bgr(p)  # (H, W, 3) BGR; magenta is symmetric so channel order is moot
220	    mag = (a[..., 0] > 200) & (a[..., 2] > 200) & (a[..., 1] < 150)
221	    H, W = mag.shape
222	    if H % bh or W % bw:
223	        raise ValueError(f"chrome mask {W}x{H} is not an integer multiple of block {bw}x{bh}")
224	    fy, fx = H // bh, W // bw
225	    return mag.reshape(bh, fy, bw, fx).mean(axis=(1, 3)) >= 0.5
226

228	def build_chrome_reference(
229	    images: list[np.ndarray], config: ScoreConfig = DEFAULT_SCORE_CONFIG, mask_path=None
230	) -> ChromeReference:
231	    """Median block luma (the static chrome) + the registration mask."""
232	    ref = np.median(np.stack([_block_luma(im) for im in images]), axis=0)

236	def _norm_masked(a: np.ndarray, mask: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
237	    """Zero-mean/unit-std over the masked pixels (cancels A2D gain/offset)."""
238	    m = a[mask]
239	    return (a - m.mean()) / (m.std() + 1e-6)

242	def calibrate_score(images: list[np.ndarray], catalog: ScoreCatalog) -> ScoreCalibration:
243	    """Lock the scoring block's position for this rig (run once at gameplay start).
244	
245	    Matches the static chrome: over an offset search, the masked,
246	    per-frame-normalized SAD between each calibration frame's block and the chrome
247	    reference is summed; the `(dx, dy)` with the smallest total wins. The digit
248	    band is then that offset applied to the nominal band. Registering on the chrome
249	    (not the digits) is digit-independent and robust before any valid score shows.
250	    """
251	    cfg = catalog.config
252	    mask = catalog.chrome.mask
253	    ref_n = _norm_masked(catalog.chrome.ref, mask)
254	    rng = cfg.reg_search
255	
256	    best: tuple[float, int, int] | None = None
257	    for dy in range(-rng, rng + 1):
258	        for dx in range(-rng, rng + 1):
259	            total = 0.0
260	            for img in images:
261	                tn = _norm_masked(_block_luma(img, dx, dy), mask)
262	                total += float(np.abs((tn - ref_n)[mask]).sum())
263	            if best is None or total < best[0]:
264	                best = (total, dx, dy)
265	    assert best is not None
266	    _t, dx, dy = best
267	    return ScoreCalibration(mode=catalog.mode, dx=dx, dy=dy)

273	def build_score_catalog(
274	    samples: list[Sample],
275	    mode: str = "training",
276	    config: ScoreConfig = DEFAULT_SCORE_CONFIG,
277	) -> ScoreCatalog:
278	    """Build the per-mode 0-9 coverage templates + the chrome reference.
279	
280	    Each labelled frame is segmented; the glyphs map left→right onto the digits of
281	    the filename value (the run count must match). One template per digit — the
282	    mean ink-coverage over its exemplars (uint8) — since the fixed font's glyphs
283	    are consistent enough that a single averaged coverage mask separates all ten.
284	    """
285	    acc: dict[int, list[np.ndarray]] = defaultdict(list)
286	    mode_images: list[np.ndarray] = []
287	    for s in samples:
288	        parsed = score_from_filename(s.path.name)
289	        if parsed is None or parsed[0] != mode:
290	            continue
291	        _mode, value = parsed
292	        mode_images.append(s.image)
293	        band = _band_luma(s.image, mode)
294	        runs = _segment_digits(band, config)
295	        digits = str(value)
296	        if len(runs) != len(digits):
297	            continue  # segmentation disagrees with the label — skip this frame
298	        for run, ch in zip(runs, digits):
299	            acc[int(ch)].append(_glyph_cov(band, run, config))
300	    templates = [
301	        DigitTemplate(digit=d, vec=np.round(np.mean(np.stack(v), axis=0)).astype(np.uint8))
302	        for d, v in sorted(acc.items())
303	    ]
304	    chrome = build_chrome_reference(mode_images, config)
305	    return ScoreCatalog(mode=mode, templates=templates, chrome=chrome, config=config)
306	
307	
308	def read_score(
309	    image: np.ndarray,
310	    catalog: ScoreCatalog,
311	    calibration: ScoreCalibration | None = None,
312	) -> ScoreResult:
313	    """Read the score: crop the (registered) digit band, segment, classify each glyph.
314	
315	    The digit count is however many glyphs the segmentation finds. Each glyph's
316	    coverage mask is matched (argmin integer L1) against the 10 per-digit
317	    templates; the digits assemble left→right into the integer. `calibration`
318	    supplies the locked block offset; if omitted the nominal band is used.
319	    """
320	    cfg = catalog.config
321	    dx = calibration.dx if calibration is not None else 0
322	    dy = calibration.dy if calibration is not None else 0
323	    band = _band_luma(image, catalog.mode, dx, dy)
324	
325	    vecs = np.stack([t.vec.astype(np.int32) for t in catalog.templates])
326	    tdig = np.array([t.digit for t in catalog.templates])
327	
328	    digits: list[int] = []
329	    dists: list[float] = []
330	    margins: list[float] = []
331	    for run in _segment_digits(band, cfg):
332	        fv = _glyph_cov(band, run, cfg).astype(np.int32)
333	        d = np.abs(vecs - fv).sum(1)
334	        order = np.argsort(d)
335	        best = int(tdig[order[0]])
336	        digits.append(best)
337	        dists.append(float(d[order[0]]))
338	        # runner-up gap = nearest exemplar of a different digit − nearest
339	        other = next((float(d[i]) for i in order if int(tdig[i]) != best), float(d[order[0]]))
340	        margins.append(other - float(d[order[0]]))
341	
342	    text = "".join(str(x) for x in digits)
343	    value = int(text) if text else -1
344	    return ScoreResult(
345	        value=value,
346	        digits=tuple(digits),
347	        dist=max(dists) if dists else 0.0,
348	        margin=min(margins) if margins else 0.0,
349	    )
350	
351	
352	def read_multiplier(image: np.ndarray) -> int:
353	    """Classify the score multiplier (1..4) by the medallion glyph's colour.
354	
355	    2x = gold, 3x = green, 4x = purple; 1x shows no digit (dim portrait). Count
356	    bright, saturated pixels of each hue in the small `SCORE_MULT_ROI` patch and
357	    take the argmax — 1x if none clears `SCORE_MULT_MIN_COUNT`. Colour-only (no
358	    shape/segmentation), so a small patch suffices; works on a block crop or a
359	    full frame. Mode-independent.
360	    """
361	    img = _ensure_full_frame(image)
362	    x0, y0, x1, y1 = SCORE_MULT_ROI
363	    s = img[y0:y1, x0:x1].reshape(-1, 3).astype(np.int32)  # BGR
364	    b, g, r = s[:, 0], s[:, 1], s[:, 2]
365	    mx = s.max(1)
366	    bright = (mx > SCORE_MULT_BRIGHT_MIN) & ((mx - s.min(1)) > SCORE_MULT_SAT_MIN)
367	    purple = int((bright & (r > g + 25) & (b > g + 25)).sum())
368	    green = int((bright & (g > r + 20) & (g > b + 20)).sum())
369	    yellow = int((bright & (r > b + 40) & (g > b + 40)).sum())
370	    best = max(purple, green, yellow)
371	    if best < SCORE_MULT_MIN_COUNT:
372	        return 1
373	    if purple >= green and purple >= yellow:
374	        return 4
375	    if green >= yellow:
376	        return 3
377	    return 2
378

50	    """Load an image file as a uint8 HxWx3 BGR array."""
51	    with Image.open(path) as im:

53	    return rgb[:, :, ::-1].copy()  # RGB -> BGR

55	
56	def load_corpus(directory: str | Path | None = None) -> list[Sample]:
57	    """Load every `*.png` in the corpus directory as labelled `Sample`s.
58	
59	    Sorted by filename for determinism. Raises FileNotFoundError if the
60	    directory is empty or missing.
61	    """
62	    d = Path(directory) if directory is not None else corpus_dir()
63	    files = sorted(d.glob("*.png"))
64	    if not files:
65	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no PNGs found in corpus dir {d}")
66	    return [
67	        Sample(screen_id=screen_id_for_filename(f.name), path=f, image=load_bgr(f))
68	        for f in files
69	    ]

71	
72	def load_score_corpus(directory: str | Path | None = None) -> list[Sample]:
73	    """Load the labelled score frames (`score__<mode>__<value>__*.png`).
74	
75	    Labelled by numeric value in the filename (see `metadata.score_from_filename`),
76	    so these are returned as `in_song` samples; the score value is parsed from the
77	    path by the score reader/eval. Returns [] if the directory is missing/empty
78	    (the score corpus is optional relative to the screen corpus).
79	    """
80	    d = Path(directory) if directory is not None else score_corpus_dir()
81	    files = sorted(d.glob("score__*.png"))

export UV_CACHE_DIR="$TMPDIR/uv-cache"
uv run python - <<'PY'
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np, glob, os
from collections import defaultdict
LW=np.array([0.114,0.587,0.299])  # BGR luma (b,g,r)
def load_bgr(p):
    rgb=np.asarray(Image.open(p).convert("RGB"),np.uint8); return rgb[:,:,::-1].copy()
def luma(bgr): return bgr.astype(np.float64)@LW

# block-rel cells (in 96x105 crop): (col0,col1) ; rows fixed
ROWS=(81,100)
CELLS={"h":(50,60,False),"t":(63,74,False),"u":(76,92,True)}  # (c0,c1,is_light)
GR,GC=16,10
FRAC=0.55
def cov(cellluma,is_light):
    b=cellluma
    lo,hi=b.min(),b.max()
    if is_light: ink=b < lo+(1-FRAC)*(hi-lo)
    else:        ink=b > lo+FRAC*(hi-lo)
    ys=np.where(ink.any(1))[0]; xs=np.where(ink.any(0))[0]
    if len(ys)==0 or len(xs)==0: return np.zeros(GR*GC,np.uint8)
    m=ink[ys.min():ys.max()+1, xs.min():xs.max()+1].astype(float)
    ye=np.linspace(0,m.shape[0],GR+1).round().astype(int)
    xe=np.linspace(0,m.shape[1],GC+1).round().astype(int)
    g=np.empty((GR,GC))
    for r in range(GR):
        for c in range(GC):
            blk=m[ye[r]:max(ye[r]+1,ye[r+1]), xe[c]:max(xe[c]+1,xe[c+1])]
            g[r,c]=blk.mean() if blk.size else 0
    return np.round(g.reshape(-1)*255).astype(np.uint8)

def cellcov(img,cell):
    c0,c1,light=cell
    L=luma(img)[ROWS[0]:ROWS[1], c0:c1]
    return cov(L,light)

# load corpus
files=sorted(glob.glob("data/streak/streak__*.png"))
data=[]  # (label(h,t,u each int or None), {cellname:covvec})
for f in files:
    lab=f.split("streak__")[1].split("__")[0]
    img=load_bgr(f)
    covs={k:cellcov(img,v) for k,v in CELLS.items()}
    dig={"h":lab[0],"t":lab[1],"u":lab[2]}
    dig={k:(int(v) if v!='x' else None) for k,v in dig.items()}
    data.append((dig,covs))
print("corpus",len(data))

# gather exemplars per digit (pool all cells)
def build(exclude=None):
    acc=defaultdict(list)
    for i,(dig,covs) in enumerate(data):
        if i==exclude: continue
        for k in CELLS:
            d=dig[k]
            if d is not None: acc[d].append(covs[k])
    return {d:np.round(np.mean(np.stack(v),0)).astype(np.int32) for d,v in acc.items()}

# LOO: for each frame, rebuild templates without it, classify each known cell
tmpl_all=build()
digs=sorted(tmpl_all)
print("digits with templates:",digs)
ok=tot=0; bad=[]
dists=[]; margins=[]
for i,(dig,covs) in enumerate(data):
    T=build(exclude=i)
    keys=sorted(T); M=np.stack([T[d] for d in keys])
    for k in CELLS:
        d=dig[k]
        if d is None: continue
        fv=covs[k].astype(np.int32)
        dd=np.abs(M-fv).sum(1); order=np.argsort(dd)
        pred=keys[order[0]]; best=dd[order[0]]
        other=next(dd[j] for j in order if keys[j]!=pred)
        dists.append(best); margins.append(other-best)
        tot+=1
        if pred==d: ok+=1
        else: bad.append((os.path.basename(files[i]),k,d,pred,int(best),int(other-best)))
print(f"LOO per-cell accuracy: {ok}/{tot} = {ok/tot:.3f}")
print("dist: median %.0f p90 %.0f max %.0f"%(np.percentile(dists,50),np.percentile(dists,90),max(dists)))
print("margin: median %.0f p10 %.0f min %.0f"%(np.percentile(margins,50),np.percentile(margins,10),min(margins)))
print("misses:")
for b in bad: print("  ",b)
PY

def load_bgr(p):
    rgb=np.asarray(Image.open(p).convert("RGB"),np.uint8); return rgb[:,:,::-1].copy()
def luma(bgr): return bgr.astype(np.float64)@LW
# tuned cells (c0,c1,r0,r1,is_light)

GR,GC=16,10; FRAC=0.5
def cov(L,light):
    lo,hi=L.min(),L.max()
    ink=(L<lo+(1-FRAC)*(hi-lo)) if light else (L>lo+FRAC*(hi-lo))
    ys=np.where(ink.any(1))[0]; xs=np.where(ink.any(0))[0]
    if not len(ys) or not len(xs): return np.zeros(GR*GC,np.uint8)
    m=ink[ys.min():ys.max()+1,xs.min():xs.max()+1].astype(float)
    ye=np.linspace(0,m.shape[0],GR+1).round().astype(int)
    xe=np.linspace(0,m.shape[1],GC+1).round().astype(int)
    g=np.empty((GR,GC))
    for r in range(GR):
        for c in range(GC):
            blk=m[ye[r]:max(ye[r]+1,ye[r+1]),xe[c]:max(xe[c]+1,xe[c+1])]
            g[r,c]=blk.mean() if blk.size else 0
    return np.round(g.reshape(-1)*255).astype(np.uint8)
def cellcov(img,cell):

    covs={k:cellcov(img,v) for k,v in CELLS.items()}
    dig={k:(int(d) if d!='x' else None) for k,d in zip("htu",lab)}
    data.append((dig,covs))

def bank(exclude,polarity):  # polarity: cells with matching is_light
    cellset=[k for k in CELLS if CELLS[k][4]==polarity]
    acc=defaultdict(list)
    for i,(dig,covs) in enumerate(data):
        if i==exclude: continue
        for k in cellset:
            if dig[k] is not None: acc[dig[k]].append(covs[k])
    return {d:np.round(np.mean(np.stack(v),0)).astype(np.int32) for d,v in acc.items()}

for mode in ["separate","pooled"]:
    ok=tot=0; conf_ok=conf_tot=0; bad=[]
    for i,(dig,covs) in enumerate(data):
        for k in CELLS:
            d=dig[k]
            if d is None: continue
            light=CELLS[k][4]
            if mode=="separate":
                T=bank(i,light)
            else:
                a=bank(i,False); b=bank(i,True)
                T={dd:np.round((a.get(dd,b.get(dd)).astype(float))).astype(np.int32) for dd in set(a)|set(b)}
                # pooled: average both polarities where available
                T={}
                acc=defaultdict(list)
                for kk in CELLS:
                    for j,(dg,cv) in enumerate(data):
                        if j==i: continue
                        if dg[kk] is not None: acc[dg[kk]].append(cv[kk])
                T={dd:np.round(np.mean(np.stack(v),0)).astype(np.int32) for dd,v in acc.items()}
            keys=sorted(T); M=np.stack([T[x] for x in keys])
            fv=covs[k].astype(np.int32); dd=np.abs(M-fv).sum(1); o=np.argsort(dd)
            pred=keys[o[0]]; best=dd[o[0]]; other=next(dd[j] for j in o if keys[j]!=pred); margin=other-best
            tot+=1; ok+= (pred==d)
            confident = best<9000 and margin>1500
            if confident: conf_tot+=1; conf_ok+=(pred==d)
            if pred!=d: bad.append((k,d,pred,int(best),int(margin)))
    print(f"[{mode}] raw {ok}/{tot}={ok/tot:.3f}  confident {conf_ok}/{conf_tot}={conf_ok/max(1,conf_tot):.3f}")
    from collections import Counter
    print("   miss by cell:",Counter(b[0] for b in bad))
    print("   sample misses:",bad[:8])

            return s.val   # reject; hold (don't commit digits)
        s.dg=nd; s.val=v; return v

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-10 04:19:13Z)**_

The tracker works well — most anchors exact, resets correctly, never goes backward. The weak spot is **carry lag** (e.g. `98` held through `101`–`112` before catching up): when a tens 9→0 wrap coincides with an unreadable hundreds, the naive carry logic stalls. There's a cleaner formulation that uses the monotonic prior directly: **constrained search** — pick the value in `[last, last+MAXJUMP]` whose digits best match the confident reads. That handles carries (099→100) natively. Let me test it.

173	    }
174	
175	    out->ndigits = (uint8_t)ndigits;
176	    out->value = (ndigits > 0) ? value : -1;
177	    out->dist = worst_dist;
178	    out->margin = (ndigits > 0) ? min_margin : 0;
179	    return 0;
180	}
181	
182	/* Multiplier: count bright, saturated purple/green/yellow pixels in the medallion
183	 * ROI (independent tests, mirroring score.py read_multiplier), argmax → 4/3/2, or
184	 * 1x if the winner is below the floor. Colour only — no shape/segmentation. */
185	int gp_read_multiplier(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height)
186	{
187	    if (width != GP_CANON_W || height != GP_CANON_H) { return 1; }
188	    static const int roi[4] = GP_MULT_ROI;
189	    int x0 = roi[0], y0 = roi[1], x1 = roi[2], y1 = roi[3];
190	
191	    int purple = 0, green = 0, yellow = 0;
192	    for (int y = y0; y < y1; y++)
193	    {
194	        const uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)width + (uint32_t)x0) * GP_BPP;
195	        for (int x = x0; x < x1; x++, p += GP_BPP)
196	        {
197	            int B = p[0], G = p[1], R = p[2];
198	            int mx = R > G ? R : G; if (B > mx) { mx = B; }
199	            int mn = R < G ? R : G; if (B < mn) { mn = B; }
200	            if (mx <= GP_MULT_BRIGHT_MIN || (mx - mn) <= GP_MULT_SAT_MIN) { continue; }
201	            if (R > G + 25 && B > G + 25) { purple++; }
202	            if (G > R + 20 && G > B + 20) { green++; }
203	            if (R > B + 40 && G > B + 40) { yellow++; }
204	        }
205	    }
206	    int best = purple;
207	    if (green > best) { best = green; }
208	    if (yellow > best) { best = yellow; }
209	    if (best < GP_MULT_MIN_COUNT) { return 1; }
210	    if (purple >= green && purple >= yellow) { return 4; }
211	    if (green >= yellow) { return 3; }
212	    return 2;
213	}
214

10	 * digits are segmented by their ink gaps (not a fixed grid), each resized to a
11	 * canonical cell + per-glyph normalized, then 1-NN-matched against the mode's
12	 * 0-9 exemplars. Pure (no FreeRTOS/video), so it compiles + cross-checks on a
13	 * host. Not reentrant (static scratch); only the single observer task calls it.
14	 *
15	 * `mode` selects the glyph set / digit band (GP_SCORE_MODE_*); training is the
16	 * only mode with data today (career green font appends later, no API change). */

21	    uint8_t ndigits;  /* number of segmented digits */
22	    int32_t dist;     /* worst per-digit L1 to its template (diagnostic) */
23	    int32_t margin;   /* weakest per-digit runner-up L1 gap (confidence) */
24	} gp_score_t;
25	
26	int gp_read_score(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height,
27	                  uint8_t mode, gp_score_t *out);

30	 * (2x gold / 3x green / 4x purple; 1x = no digit). Colour-count over a small
31	 * fixed ROI — no segmentation, mode-independent. Returns 1 on a bad frame size. */

10	/* Game-state observer — see firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md §4.8 (M9).
11	 *
12	 * A video-frame consumer (not a detector): it classifies which GH3 screen the
13	 * captured frame shows and publishes typed game_state_t events on its own bus
14	 * (xGameStateQueue), kept separate from the detector-state bus per the §4.2
15	 * multi-detector decision. The recognizer data (region grid, per-class
16	 * centroids, thresholds) is the host-proven metadata frozen into
17	 * game/gameplay_metadata.h by `gameplay export-c`.
18	 *
19	 * Phase 1 (this module): screen classification only. Selection/song readers
20	 * (Phase 2) and the navigator/controller (Phase 3, M10) build on this. */
21	
22	typedef struct
23	{
24	    uint32_t frame_epoch;   /* master sync token, = Video_FrameInfo.frame_count */
25	    uint64_t timestamp_us;  /* monotonic, marvin-local */
26	    uint8_t  screen;        /* GP_SCREEN_* index, or GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN */
27	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
28	    int32_t  best_dist;     /* L1 to the nearest centroid */
29	    int32_t  margin;        /* second-best − best (confidence) */
30	    int16_t  selection;     /* static-list cell, song-template index, or -1 (none) */
31	    int32_t  score;         /* in-song score read (training font), or -1 (not in_song) */
32	    uint8_t  multiplier;    /* in-song score multiplier 1..4, or 0 (not in_song) */
33	} game_state_t;
34	
35	/* Brings up the game-state bus queue and the observer task. The observer
36	 * subscribes to the video frame queue from inside its task, so call this after
37	 * Video_Initialize. The task idles (draining frames, ~0 CPU) until a
38	 * GameplayEngine_Observe() request arrives. */
39	void GameplayEngine_Initialize(void);
40	
41	/* Game-state event bus. Consumers (operator UI, the controller at M10) read
42	 * here. Returns NULL until GameplayEngine_Initialize has run. */
43	QueueHandle_t GameplayEngine_BusQueue(void);
44	
45	/* Synchronous observation: request a classification of a fresh frame and block
46	 * until the result arrives, or timeout_ms elapses. On success writes the
47	 * {screen, selection, …} into *out and returns true; returns false on timeout or
48	 * a NULL out. This is the only way to read screen state — there is no retained
49	 * "current screen" to poll, so a read never returns stale state.
50	 *
51	 * The classified frame is guaranteed to have been captured after the request
52	 * (the task skips the in-hand frame, which predates it). The sole requester is
53	 * the game controller; do not call concurrently from multiple tasks.
54	 *
55	 * NOTE: GH3 menus take several frames to transition (cursor animation, fades, a
56	 * `loading` screen), so the controller settles/re-observes rather than trusting
57	 * one read the instant after actuating. */
58	bool GameplayEngine_Observe(game_state_t *out, uint32_t timeout_ms);

25	/* Observation is a synchronous request/response: the task idles (draining frames,
26	 * ~0 CPU) until GameplayEngine_Observe() posts a request, then classifies exactly
27	 * one fresh frame and hands the result back through s_resp_queue. There is no
28	 * free-running scan and no retained "latest" to poll — a read blocks for a frame
29	 * captured after the request, so it can never return stale state. The song_select
30	 * match is heavy soft-float (no FPU, ~tens of ms) and must never run unasked — a
31	 * continuous scan once pegged prio-4 and froze the UI. */

33	static QueueHandle_t s_bus_queue;

48	static volatile bool s_req_pending;

52	    return (idx < GP_N_SCREENS) ? gp_screen_ids[idx] : "unknown";
53	}

55	/* Read the selection for the classified screen: static-list cell index, the
56	 * song-template index on song_select, or -1 where there's no selection concept
57	 * (gameplay / loading / unknown). `name`/`name2` receive log-friendly labels. */
58	static int16_t read_selection(const uint8_t *frame, int w, int h, uint8_t screen,
59	                              const char **name, const char **name2)
60	{
61	    *name = NULL;
62	    *name2 = NULL;
63	    const gp_menu_layout_t *menu = gp_menu_for_screen(screen);
64	    if (menu != NULL)
65	    {
66	        int cell = gp_read_selection(frame, w, h, menu);
67	        if (cell >= 0 && cell < menu->count) { *name = menu->items[cell]; }
68	        return (int16_t)cell;
69	    }
70	    if (screen == GP_SCREEN_song_select)
71	    {
72	        gp_song_t song;
73	        if (gp_read_song(frame, w, h, &song) == 0 && song.tmpl >= 0)
74	        {
75	            *name = (song.setlist == GP_SETLIST_BONUS) ? "bonus" : "main";
76	            *name2 = gp_song_templates[song.tmpl].song_id;
77	            return song.tmpl;
78	        }
79	    }
80	    return -1;
81	}
82	
83	static void game_task(void *param)
84	{
85	    (void)param;
86	
87	    QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(GAME_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,
88	                                              sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
89	                                              s_frame_queue_storage,
90	                                              &s_frame_queue_buf);
91	    configASSERT(frames != NULL);
92	    bool subscribed = Video_SubscribeFrames(frames);
93	    configASSERT(subscribed);
94	
95	    LOG_INFO("GAME: gameplay_engine started\r\n");
96	
97	    uint8_t   last_screen = GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN;
98	    int16_t   last_sel    = -2;  /* != any real selection or -1, so first read logs */
99	    bool      armed       = false;  /* pre-request frame discarded; next one is fresh */
100	
101	    for (;;)
102	    {
103	        Video_FrameInfo frame;
104	        if (xQueueReceive(frames, &frame, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) { continue; }
105	
106	        /* Drain every frame so the queue never backs up. Classify only while a
107	         * request is pending — no free-running scan. */
108	        if (!s_req_pending) { armed = false; continue; }
109	
110	        /* The frame in hand when the request arrived predates it; skip it so the
111	         * classified frame is guaranteed to have been captured after the request. */
112	        if (!armed) { armed = true; continue; }
113	
114	        /* A bad frame leaves the request pending so the next valid one serves it. */
115	        if (frame.buffer == NULL)                          { continue; }
116	        if (frame.bytes_per_pixel != GAME_BYTES_PER_PIXEL) { continue; }
117	
118	        TickType_t now = xTaskGetTickCount();
119	        const uint8_t *buf = (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer;
120	        int w = (int)frame.width, h = (int)frame.height;
121	
122	        int32_t best_dist = 0, margin = 0;
123	        uint8_t screen = gp_classify(buf, w, h, &best_dist, &margin);
124	
125	        const char *sel_name = NULL, *sel_name2 = NULL;
126	        int16_t sel = read_selection(buf, w, h, screen, &sel_name, &sel_name2);
127	
128	        /* In-song: read the open-ended score (training font) + multiplier. Sentinels
129	         * (-1 / 0) elsewhere. */
130	        int32_t score = -1;
131	        uint8_t multiplier = 0;
132	        if (screen == GP_SCREEN_in_song)
133	        {
134	            gp_score_t sc;
135	            if (gp_read_score(buf, w, h, GP_SCORE_MODE_TRAINING, &sc) == 0) { score = sc.value; }
136	            multiplier = (uint8_t)gp_read_multiplier(buf, w, h);
137	        }
138	
139	        game_state_t ev;
140	        memset(&ev, 0, sizeof(ev));
141	        ev.frame_epoch  = frame.frame_count;
142	        ev.timestamp_us = (uint64_t)now * GAME_US_PER_TICK;
143	        ev.screen       = screen;
144	        ev.best_dist    = best_dist;
145	        ev.margin       = margin;
146	        ev.selection    = sel;
147	        ev.score        = score;
148	        ev.multiplier   = multiplier;
149	
150	        /* Answer the requester first (clear pending before the send so a follow-up
151	         * Observe that wakes on the response can't have its new request cleared). */
152	        armed = false;
153	        taskENTER_CRITICAL();
154	        s_req_pending = false;
155	        taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
156	        (void)xQueueSend(s_resp_queue, &ev, 0);
157	
158	        if (screen != last_screen || sel != last_sel)
159	        {
160	            (void)xQueueSend(s_bus_queue, &ev, 0);
161	
162	            if (sel_name2 != NULL)  /* song_select: "<setlist> #<idx> <song>" */
163	            {
164	                LOG_INFO("GAME: %s / %s #%d %s\r\n",
165	                         screen_name(screen), sel_name,
166	                         (int)gp_song_templates[sel].index, sel_name2);
167	            }
168	            else if (sel_name != NULL)  /* static-list: "<screen> / <item>" */
169	            {
170	                LOG_INFO("GAME: %s / %s\r\n", screen_name(screen), sel_name);
171	            }
172	            else if (screen == GP_SCREEN_in_song)  /* "in_song / score N x<mult>" */
173	            {
174	                LOG_INFO("GAME: %s / score %ld x%u\r\n",
175	                         screen_name(screen), (long)score, (unsigned)multiplier);
176	            }
177	            else
178	            {
179	                LOG_INFO("GAME: %s\r\n", screen_name(screen));
180	            }
181	            last_screen = screen;
182	            last_sel    = sel;
183	        }
184	    }
185	}

200	                            NULL, GAME_TASK_PRIORITY, s_task_stack, &s_task_tcb);
201	}

208	bool GameplayEngine_Observe(game_state_t *out, uint32_t timeout_ms)
209	{
210	    if (out == NULL) { return false; }
211	
212	    /* Discard any stale response (e.g. from a prior timed-out request), then post
213	     * the request and block for the result. */
214	    game_state_t drain;
215	    while (xQueueReceive(s_resp_queue, &drain, 0) == pdTRUE) { }
216	
217	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
218	    s_req_pending = true;
219	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
220	
221	    return (xQueueReceive(s_resp_queue, out, pdMS_TO_TICKS(timeout_ms)) == pdTRUE);
222	}

```python
"""Streak odometer reader + tracker.

Two halves, mirroring the firmware split:
- `read_streak` (stateless CV) is checked against the labelled corpus: every frame
  reads as present, and *confident* per-wheel reads are almost always correct — the
  few that aren't are what the tracker's monotonic/carry logic exists to absorb.
- `StreakTracker` (stateful reconcile) is checked on synthetic read sequences that
  isolate its rules: seeding, holding an unreadable wheel, carrying (099→100),
  rejecting a backward/implausible read, and resetting after a run of absent reads.

The end-to-end validation over the full 6549-frame capture (monotonic within the
run, single reset, 46/47 hand-read anchors exact) is recorded in the journal — that
capture is gitignored, so CI relies on the committed corpus + these synthetic cases.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from gameplay.corpus import load_streak_corpus
from gameplay.metadata import streak_from_filename
from gameplay.score import (
    StreakRaw,
    StreakTracker,
    build_streak_catalog,
    read_streak,
)


def _raw(present=True, h=(0, False), t=(0, False), u=(0, False)) -> StreakRaw:
    """StreakRaw helper: each place is (digit, known)."""
    return StreakRaw(present, (h[0], t[0], u[0]), (h[1], t[1], u[1]))


# ─── stateless reader against the labelled corpus ───────────────────────────────


def test_labeled_frames_all_present():
    cat = build_streak_catalog(load_streak_corpus())
    for s in load_streak_corpus():
        assert read_streak(s.image, cat).present, s.path.name


def test_confident_reads_mostly_correct():
    corpus = load_streak_corpus()
    cat = build_streak_catalog(corpus)
    ok = tot = 0
    for s in corpus:
        lab = streak_from_filename(s.path.name)
        r = read_streak(s.image, cat)
        for i in range(3):
            if lab[i] is not None and r.known[i]:
                tot += 1
                ok += r.digits[i] == lab[i]
    # In-sample confident accuracy is ~95%; the tracker tolerates the rest. Guard
    # against a regression that would break the monotonic reconciliation.
    assert tot > 0 and ok / tot >= 0.90, f"{ok}/{tot}"


# ─── stateful tracker logic ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_tracker_seeds_from_two_confident_wheels():
    tr = StreakTracker()
    # hundreds=1, tens=0 confident; units unknown → seed to the smallest matching = 100.
    assert tr.update(_raw(h=(1, True), t=(0, True), u=(0, False))) == 100
    assert tr.seen


def test_tracker_needs_two_wheels_to_seed():
    tr = StreakTracker()
    assert tr.update(_raw(h=(1, True))) == 0  # one confident wheel is not enough
    assert not tr.seen


def test_tracker_holds_when_unreadable():
    tr = StreakTracker()
    tr.update(_raw(h=(1, True), t=(0, True)))          # seed 100
    assert tr.update(_raw()) == 100                     # all wheels unreadable → hold


def test_tracker_carries_over_hundred():
    tr = StreakTracker()
    tr.update(_raw(h=(0, True), t=(9, True), u=(9, True)))   # seed 99
    assert tr.val == 99
    got = tr.update(_raw(h=(1, True), t=(0, True), u=(0, True)))  # 099 → 100
    assert got == 100


def test_tracker_rejects_backward_read():
    tr = StreakTracker()
    tr.update(_raw(h=(1, True), t=(0, True), u=(0, True)))   # seed 100
    # A confident read of 50 (out of the forward window) must not move the value back.
    assert tr.update(_raw(h=(0, True), t=(5, True), u=(0, True))) == 100


def test_tracker_advances_within_window():
    tr = StreakTracker()
    tr.update(_raw(h=(1, True), t=(0, True), u=(0, True)))   # seed 100
    assert tr.update(_raw(h=(1, True), t=(0, True), u=(5, True))) == 105


def test_tracker_resets_after_absent_run():
    tr = StreakTracker()
    tr.update(_raw(h=(1, True), t=(0, True), u=(0, True)))   # seed 100
    for _ in range(StreakTracker().cfg.absent_reset):
        tr.update(_raw(present=False))
    assert tr.val == 0 and not tr.seen

```

=== gameplay journal top 60 ===
# gameplay — Working Journal

Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for the GH3
game-state engine prototype. Newest entries at the top. This subproject is the **offline
host-side prototype** for marvin's game-state observer/controller (spec §4.8, M9/M10): we
prove the detection algorithms in Python against the real-screen corpus, then port the
proven, simple GH3-specific logic to a firmware `gameplay_engine` module.

Orienting docs (read alongside this journal):
- `firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md` §4.8 — what the game-state subsystem is.
- `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md` — screen catalog + menu graph (canonical screen names).
- `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/` — the labelled 720×480 PNG corpus (101 screens, 13 classes).

---

## Current focus

**Porting to marvin firmware (`gameplay_engine`, spec §4.8) — started.** The offline
prototype is complete (phases 1–4); now freezing the proven algorithms into firmware. Phased
because the firmware is built/flashed by Greg in MPLAB (I write + syntax-review C only), and
because M9 (observer) and M10 (controller) are separate milestones:

- **Phase 0 — metadata exporter (done, host-side).** `gameplay export-c` emits the proven
  recognizer data as a single generated C header (`gameplay_metadata.h`): classifier config +
  per-class `uint8` centroids + thresholds + screen-id table; static-list menu geometry +
  per-cell baselines; song config/ROIs + 64 per-song templates + catalog + setlist warmth
  threshold. Plain PODs + flat arrays; floats only for the normalized baselines/song vectors
  (soft-float on the ARM926, tiny vectors). Generated output compiles clean under
  `cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra`; the header lands in the firmware tree at Phase 1.
  - **SD-card data split (marvin journal 2026-06-22, spec §4.8.3):** this generated header stays the
    compile-time source of truth for the algorithm-coupled recognizer data — it does **not** move to
    SD. Two host-side follow-ups for when the SD catalog/artwork loaders are built: (1) emit a
    `metadata_version` `#define` here whose value is reused in `/marvin/games/<game>/songs.json` so the
    UI can detect a stale catalog after a template-set regen; (2) a small tool that produces
    target-sized JPEG/PNG album art named `<setlist>-<NN>.{jpg,png}` (the recognizer's `(setlist,index)`
    key) from source covers. Both deferred until that firmware work starts (post-M4).
- **Phase 1 — screen-classifier observer (M9 v0) — done (firmware code-complete, pending Greg's
  MPLAB build).** New marvin `game/` module: `gameplay_metadata.h` (generated), `gameplay_classify.{h,c}`
  (pure FreeRTOS-free classify math), `gameplay_engine.{h,c}` (`game_task` subscribing to the video
  frame queue, classify → publish `game_state_t` on `xGameStateQueue` on screen change). Wired into
  `app.c` + `user.cmake`; no MCC regen. The pure unit compiles under `cc -Wall -Wextra`, and
  `test_firmware_classify.py` proves the C decision matches the Python `classify_image` on real
  corpus frames. Soft-float normalization as decided. See marvin journal 2026-06-15 for detail.
- **Phase 2 — selection + song readers — done (firmware code-complete, builds in MPLAB per
  Greg; no hardware test yet).** `game/gameplay_select.{h,c}` (pure): static-list highlight
  (`gp_read_selection`) + `song_select` (`gp_read_song`, offset search). `gameplay_engine.c`
  reads the selection each (rate-limited ~5 Hz, with a one-shot force trigger for post-actuation
closed-loop reads) frame and logs on screen-*or*-selection change
  (`GAME: <screen> / <item>` etc.); `game_state_t` gained a `selection` field. Host cross-check
  extended to both readers (match the prototype on real frames). Song match densely re-reads its
  ROI across the offset search — rate limit bounds the cost; subsample later if needed.
- **Phase 3 — navigator/controller (M10)** — port `navgraph` + `NavController`; wire as the
  third `FretboardLink` producer behind the `actuator_mode` arbiter (marvin journal 2026-05-21
  anticipated this). `MenuInput`→bitmask: GREEN=bit0, RED=bit1, strums=bits5/6; `PLUS`/pause
  needs the `+/-` protocol extension the nav doc flagged (off the practice-run path).
  **Post-actuation settle:** after sending inputs the controller must let the screen transition
  before observing — GH3 menus animate (cursor slide, fades, `loading`), so a delay + a
  poll-until-expected (with timeout) is required, not a single immediate `RequestObservation`.
  The observer exposes background 5 Hz + a force trigger; the settle/poll policy is the
  controller's. (Mirrors the prototype `NavController`'s re-observe-until-match loop.)

33:**2026-07-05 — Dashboard live-telemetry feed: fret activity → dashboard, single-consumer event flow.** The dashboard ROBOT fret buttons were static; wired them to track the actual guitar mask, structured as the general flow that score/multiplier/streak will also ride. New `ui/dashboard_feed.{c,h}`: a **single tagged event queue** (`dashboard_evt_t` = {type, union}) with **one consumer task** (prio 2, UI band) that blocks on the queue, coalesces last-per-type on drain, and applies to widgets. Design decided w/ Greg:
171:## Decision log
189:| 2026-06-24 | **Legato CPU-render scratch buffer must live in non-cached DDR (`.region_nocache`) — fixed a GFX2D cache-coherency bleed; grew `ram_nocache` 16→32 MB.** Symptom (found during song-list bring-up): dashboard content streakily "bled through" an opaque overlay widget, intermittently, only where CPU-rendered text was. Active render path is **CPU software** (`leRenderer_FillArea` → `_RGBBlendFill`; glyphs too) into a **scratch buffer**, then **`DRV_GFX2D_Blit`** (the SAM9X75 2D engine) copies scratch→framebuffer. The framebuffer is non-cached (`FB_CACHE_NC` → `.region_nocache`) but the Legato scratch was **cacheable**: `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` was an empty no-op `#define` and `LE_COHERENT_ATTR = CACHE_ALIGN` (alignment only). The blit's `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr` of the cached scratch is insufficient on ARM926 → the 2D engine reads stale CPU-cached lines → streaky, cache-line-granularity bleed. **Fix:** define `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR = __attribute__((section(".region_nocache")))` in **`user.cmake`** (the `#ifndef` guard in the generated `legato_renderer.c` lets the `-D` win → survives MGS regen, no generated-tree patch); MCC grew `ram_nocache` 16→32 MB to host it (ddram.ld + plib_mmu.c + `DDRAM_NO_CACHE_SIZE`). **Confirmed on hardware** (commits `d36640f` + `c0f316c`). **Two upstream Microchip Legato/gfx bugs to file:** (1) with "Cacheable Frame Buffers" **off**, the generator non-caches the framebuffer but leaves the Legato render scratch cacheable (`LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` empty) — the gap that bit us; (2) `DRV_GFX2D_Fill` omits the `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr` that `DRV_GFX2D_Blit` has (latent — bites any GPU-fill config, e.g. `LE_WIDGET_BUFFER_ENABLE=1`). | Root-caused by elimination, not by reading (every software-logic path traced correct): a bare opaque magenta fill still bled, hiding the dashboard cleared it, and non-cached scratch fixed it → it's the cached-scratch ↔ 2D-engine coherency, below the software layer. Non-cached is the correct policy on this SoC — Microchip already chose it for the framebuffer (`FB_CACHE_NC`) rather than trusting cache maintenance for a DMA-/GPU-read buffer; the scratch is the same kind of buffer and should match. Adding cache maintenance to `DRV_GFX2D_Fill` would *not* fix this (Fill isn't on the path; the on-path `Blit` already invalidates and still leaked). System-wide rule for this board: any buffer the 2D engine or display DMA reads must be non-cached (or carry correct, sufficient maintenance — which the cacheable path here does not). |
192:| 2026-06-24 | **Results stored as flat CSV (`<card>/players/results.csv`); built `results` module on the SD/RTC layer ahead of the gameplay write path.** New in-tree `results/results.{h,c}` (added via `user.cmake`): `Results_Append(record)` (mount-on-demand, header-if-new, RTC UTC timestamp, CSV-quoted song), `Results_TopN(setlist,index,difficulty,…)` (streaming line scan + quote-aware `csv_split` + bounded score-descending insert, all static buffers), and `Results_Set/GetPlayer` (operator string, default "p1"). Console gains `player`, `scores <set> <idx> [diff]`, and `results add …` (synthetic-row injection for testing). Paths build from `Storage_MountPoint()` so files land at the card root next to `sdtest.bin`. **Code-complete; pending Greg's MPLAB build + on-hardware test.** | Same substrate-before-consumer play as `storage`/`time`: the writer + on-device reader + display validate the CSV format decision (spec §4.8.6) against synthetic rows **now**, entirely on the proven SD/FatFs/RTC stack — no gameplay dependency. CSV chosen so on-device high-score display parses with comma-split + `atol` into static buffers (no malloc, no JSON tokenizer, fits `FF_FS_MAX_FILES=1`) while the card still opens in pandas/Excel. The gameplay engine wires in later as a one-line `Results_Append` once M9 Phase 3 score readers exist; player-id scheme (operator string vs profiles) is the remaining Q12 open item. |
196:| 2026-06-22 | **SD-card data architecture decided (spec §4.6.2 layout, §4.7, §4.8.3, new §4.8.6/§4.8.7).** The flash-vs-SD line is drawn by *what the data is coupled to*. **Flash (compile-time):** recognizer signatures (centroids, menu baselines, song bitmap templates, thresholds) **and** the menu graph — all *algorithm-coupled* (only valid with the exact grid/sampling/normalization compiled into `gameplay_classify.c`/`gameplay_select.c`), generated by `tools/gameplay/gameplay/export_c.py` into `gameplay_metadata.h`. **Recognition never reads the SD card.** **SD (FAT32, `/marvin/`):** `config.json` (resolves Q9 — config on SD, not flash); `games/<game>/songs.json` song-catalog *labels* keyed by the recognizer's `(setlist,index)` (`gp_song_t`), carrying a `metadata_version` stamp so the UI can warn on a stale catalog; `games/<game>/art/<setlist>-<NN>.{jpg,png}` album artwork (named by the same key, decoded once at startup into a static DDR cache via Legato's already-enabled JPEG/PNG decoders — no new library); `players/results.jsonl` append-only per-player results; and `recordings/`. **Rejected: moving recognition data to SD** — it's an algorithm-coupled build artifact, not user-meaningful, and a stale SD blob would silently misclassify; keeping it compile-time removes that failure mode entirely. New open Qs: Q12 (results timestamps — enable SAM9X75 RTC for wall-clock vs `session`+`frame_epoch`; player identity) and Q13 (artwork target dimensions + cache pixel format). **Doc-only change; no firmware** — all loaders/writers build on the M4 FAT mount (results also need M9 Phase 3 score readers). | This is the design Greg raised (song metadata + artwork + per-player results on SD; could recognition be data-driven from a file?). Recognition turned out to already be data-driven, but coupled to the C algorithm, so the right split is the one spec §4.8.3 always anticipated: compile-time tables for the algorithm-coupled graph/signatures, SD for the user-meaningful, independently-changing data. Keying catalog/artwork/results by the stable `(setlist,index)` the recognizer emits means a missing/stale card degrades gracefully (Unknown song / placeholder) and never breaks recognition. Legato's runtime JPEG+PNG decoders are already enabled (`legato_config.h`), so no TJpgDec; the internal RTC exists (32.768 kHz + VDDBU backup on the Hybrid board) but is currently disabled, so wall-clock timestamps are an opt-in cost (MCC regen + backup-cell), not assumed. |
255:| 2026-05-20 | Non-detector vision tasks (menu navigation, score reading, etc.) are video-frame consumers, not detectors — `detector_state_t` stays narrow to fret-press shape | Forcing menu/score readers through `detector_state_t` would either abuse `fret[]` as untyped data or push the canonical record toward a tagged-union shape that hurts the recording layout. Cheaper to keep two separate concepts: (a) "video frame consumer" — anyone subscribing to the video module's frame queue, output type and downstream consumers are theirs to define; (b) "detector" — narrow note-timing emitter onto `xDetectorStateQueue`. cv_marvin_v1 happens to be both. Implication: `Video_SubscribeFrames` needs to go from single- to multi-subscriber before the second video CV task lands. |
257:| 2026-05-20 | `Video_SubscribeFrames` is multi-subscriber (max 4), each subscriber chooses its own queue depth + back-pressure policy | Need parallel video CV tasks (note detector + recording + future menu/score readers) on one capture pipeline. Static array of 4 `QueueHandle_t` slots; ISR fans out one `xQueueSendFromISR` per subscribed slot. Aligned-pointer slot reads/writes are atomic on Cortex-A5 so the IRQ can scan without locking; `taskENTER_CRITICAL` only needed in `Subscribe`/`Unsubscribe` to prevent two task-side writers racing on the same empty slot. Producer always uses `xQueueSendFromISR` (drop-on-full); consumer chooses queue depth — depth 1 = "newest only", deeper = "preserve every frame". |

12	  - **Partial-repaint gotcha (fill-end artifacts):** `AaCorners_RenderRoundImage` re-blends existing pixels toward the backdrop and writes at full-rect coordinates via `_Unsafe` pixel ops (relative to the current frame/damage rect, no bounds check). `panel_aa` is safe because a panel repaints its whole rect. Two fixes, and crucially **it still never gives up** — abandoning detection would permanently mis-frame a source that starts dark and later brightens:
27	- **Rate-limit:** `detect_active` self-caps to `VIDEO_ACTIVE_SCAN_MS` (100 ms, ~10 Hz) while unlatched instead of every tick. Trade-off: 16-frame accumulation now takes ~1.6 s after the source brightens (was ~0.3 s) — full-frame fallback shows briefly on wake, then snaps to the crop.
28	- **Dark-gate:** a cheap `frame_has_light()` (coarse grid, stride 64, returns on first bright sample) runs before the heavy border scan; an all-dark frame skips it → ~0 cost. So an asleep/dimmed Wii = near-idle, and detection resumes automatically the instant it brightens. Files: `video/video.c`. Build clean.

New `ui/dashboard_feed.{c,h}`: a **single tagged event queue** (`dashboard_evt_t` = {type, union}) with **one consumer task** (prio 2, UI band) that blocks on the queue, coalesces last-per-type on drain, and applies to widgets.
