34	- **Hard constraint honored:** the actuation path (timing/gameplay/fretboard link) must never be delayed. Producers post with `xQueueSend(…,0)` (non-blocking, drop-on-full) — `FretboardLink_Send` (the convergence point for all producers) gets one `DashboardFeed_PostFret(v)` line, mirroring its existing `Fauxmote_SendGuitarMask` fan-out. One store-class op, no lock, no Legato touch.
35	- **Consumer is the sole dashboard widget writer, under a render lock.** Legato here is **single-threaded** — no `LEGATO_USE_OSAL`, no renderer lock, no `leTimer`; `_LEGATO_Tasks` runs `leUpdate` (events + one-pass paint) then `vTaskDelay(10ms)`. So *any* widget/damage edit from another task races the renderer. **First cut got this wrong** (consumer mutated widgets from its own prio-2 task): frets never showed and the SONG card updated one selection behind — the classic dropped-damage signature — and it likely contributed to a hard freeze. Fix: `UiManager_RenderLock()/Unlock()` — suspend `LEGATO_Tasks`+`SYS_INPUT_Tasks` and gate on `leRenderer_IsIdle()` (reliable now that scratch is sized to one full-screen pass, §13), so the edit can't corrupt an in-flight paint. The consumer wraps its coalesced apply in it. Held ~microseconds; never touches the actuation tasks (prio 4–5). Note this corrected a wrong assumption in an earlier draft of this entry that the old off-thread path was safe — the old `dash_selection_changed` actually ran **in-context** (from the SELECT button callback inside `leUpdate`), which is why it worked.
36	- **Same-class pre-existing race also fixed:** `dash_game_status` wrote the Status label from the game-controller task (prio 4) via `lestring_set_utf8` → `setFromChar`, which **does** invalidate — an off-thread invalidate that fires during gameplay (NAVIGATING→PLAYING…) alongside the fret traffic. Routed it through the feed too (`DASH_EVT_STATUS`, string copied into the event; `ScreenDashboard_ApplyStatus`). No off-thread invalidate remains.
37	- **Fret visual:** the classic skin fills a button with `LE_SCHM_BACKGROUND` when pressed (state ≠ UP) and `LE_SCHM_BASE` when up, so each fret scheme already encodes lit/unlit — no new schemes. Two non-obvious requirements to make it show (both needed): (1) the buttons must be **toggleable**, else `setPressed(TRUE)` just fires a click and leaves state UP; (2) **explicit `invalidate`** after `setPressed`, because `setPressed` only self-invalidates for image/bevel/pressed-offset buttons — for a plain scheme-filled button the UP↔TOGGLED colour swap wouldn't repaint. `ScreenDashboard_ApplyFret(mask)` does both, per bit (`TIMING_BIT_*`), touching only buttons whose state changed (cached `s_last_mask`); buttons also set `IGNOREEVENTS` (status display, not input).
38	- **Lifecycle:** `DashboardFeed_Init()` (queue) pre-scheduler in `UiManager_Initialize` so producers can post immediately; `DashboardFeed_Start()` (task) at end of `ui_boot_task` (post-reveal), so the consumer never touches the widget tree during build/paint/reveal. Buffered events apply on first run.

43	**2026-07-04 — Navigation is now fully closed-loop; observation made synchronous; timing pipeline no longer observes screens.** A real misfire (after the Wii remote woke, the exit from `practice_end_menu` strummed down 1 + GREEN → RESTART instead of down 4 → QUIT) traced to two gaps: (1) `observe()` was `RequestObservation()` + a fixed 140 ms delay + `GetLatest()`, which returned the last *retained* classification whether or not a fresh one had completed — so right after the remote woke, the "check" read stale screen/selection; (2) `select_to()` read the cursor once then strummed the delta and pressed GREEN with no re-check, so a stale/wrong read fired GREEN on the wrong row. The retained-`latest`/`GetLatest` design (and the dormant `SetObserveEnabled` master gate) were vestiges of the removed background scan.
44	- **Fix (decided w/ Greg):**
45	  - **Observation is synchronous request/response.** `GameplayEngine_Observe(out, timeout)` posts a request and blocks until the task classifies a frame *captured after the request* (the task keeps draining every frame at ~0 CPU, and skips the in-hand pre-request frame for a freshness guarantee), then returns the result via a depth-1 response queue. Deleted `RequestObservation`, `GetLatest`, `s_have_latest`/`s_latest`, `s_force_observe`, and the dead `SetObserveEnabled`/`ObserveEnabled`/`s_observe_enabled` master gate. A read can no longer return stale state; there is no ambient "current screen" to poll.

The streak counter is complete end-to-end. Summary of what landed:

## Streak counter reader — done (host proven, firmware code-complete pending your MPLAB build)

**The problem, per your guidance:** a 3-tumbler odometer that only appears at ~25+, where **all three wheels roll** (units constantly, tens/hundreds at carries), so any frame can show unreadable wheels. Handled with monotonic-increasing + carry inference.

**Design (two halves, mirroring score/multiplier):**
- **Stateless read** — presence from the units wheel's mean luma (cleanly bimodal: ~29 absent vs ~106+ shown). Three fixed cells with *different polarity* — units dark-on-light (the highlighted wheel), tens/hundreds white-on-dark — each → coverage grid → integer-L1 over a **per-polarity 0-9 bank**. A wheel that fails the confidence gate is flagged unreadable.
- **Stateful tracker** — each present frame picks the value in `[last, last+30]` whose digits match the most *confident* wheels. Carries fall out for free (099→100), backward/implausible reads rejected, ≥2 agreeing wheels seed, absent-run resets. This constrained-search form replaced a hold/carry heuristic that lagged ~10 at missed carries.

**Validation (the go/no-go gate)** over the full 6549-frame capture: **46/47 hand-read anchors exact, 0 non-reset decreases, single clean reset, max 304** — monotonic and correct despite ~95% per-cell confident accuracy (the ~5% wrong is exactly what the tracker absorbs). _**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-10 16:13:26Z)**_

All three changes are in, tests green (71 passed), header regenerated.

## What changed

**1. Streak blanks when it disappears.** The real gap was song-end: `play_until_done` broke out of its loop without clearing the label, so it lingered on the last value. Now it posts `PostStreak(0)` on every exit (song end / stop). Mid-song misses (odometer hidden) already blank via the tracker's absent-reset, which I dropped from 3→2 polls (~600 ms) since the presence signal is cleanly bimodal — verified the full-capture run is still perfect (1 reset, 0 non-reset decreases, max 304).

**2. Peak streak + final score tracked per playthrough.** `play_until_done` now keeps `peak_streak` (persists across mid-song misses — it's a max over the whole run) and `final_score`, and logs `GC: result score N, peak streak M`. That's exactly where the future `Results_Append` (spec §4.8.6) will persist them; the values are ready, the write path just isn't wired yet.

**3. Reset on request, not on reaching gameplay.** Moved the score / multiplier / streak resets to the top of `run()` — they now zero out the instant Play is requested, before the Wii-connect and menu navigation, so the dashboard clears immediately rather than several seconds later. `play_until_done` keeps only the playtime-bar reset (it owns `play_start`).

Score is intentionally left showing the final total on the end screen (only streak blanks on exit) — say the word if you'd rather it clear too. Firmware side is code-complete pending your MPLAB build; nothing committed.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-10 16:27:43Z)**_

Good news: it's grounded in a request/response design, so the answer is clear.

## Not every frame — it's sampled at ~3.3 Hz

The gameplay engine is **not** a free-running per-frame processor. `game_task` drains every captured frame (~50 Hz) at ~0 CPU, and only actually *reads* anything when the controller asks via `GameplayEngine_Observe`. During a song, [game_controller.c:321](firmware/marvin/default/src/game/game_controller.c#L321) polls once per `GC_PLAY_POLL_MS = 300 ms` → **~3.3 observations/second**. Each observation classifies exactly one fresh frame; the other ~47 frames/sec are dropped untouched.

So score/multiplier/streak are computed ~3–4× per second, not 50×.

## Per-observation cost (in_song)

Each observe runs, in order:

| Step | Work | Est. |
|---|---|---|
| `gp_classify` (always) | 12×8 region grid, 5×5 lattice = 2400 sampled px → 288-vec, soft-float normalize, L1 vs 13 centroids | dominant of the small ones |
| `read_selection` | in_song has no menu/song → returns immediately | ~0 |
| `gp_read_score` | 82×16 band luma + segment + ≤6 digits × (140-cell grid + 10-template L1) | ~10k int ops + ~1.3k luma |
| `gp_read_multiplier` | 16×24 ROI, integer color counts | ~4k int ops |
| `gp_read_streak` | presence + 3 cells × (~140 px luma + 160-cell grid + 10-template L1) | ~6k int ops + ~0.6k luma |

The three value readers together are ~**20k integer ops + a few thousand soft-float luma conversions** over tiny ROIs — on the SAM9X75's ARM926 that's **sub-millisecond, realistically tens to low-hundreds of µs**. Even at a generous 1 ms/observe × 3.3 Hz that's **~0.3% CPU**.

For scale: the one genuinely heavy vision op is the **song_select** bitmap match (~190 ms soft-float, per the `GC_OBS_TIMEOUT_MS` comment at [game_controller.c:44](firmware/marvin/default/src/game/game_controller.c#L44)) — and that runs only on the song-select menu, **never in_song**. The in-song readers are cheap by comparison, which is why they can ride the same 3 Hz poll with no budget concern.

## Want real numbers?

These are analytical estimates. Two ways to get measured values on-target:
- **`health` command** — the per-task cpu% window (from the 2026-07-05 work) would show `GameEngine`'s actual share during a playthrough.
- A quick **cycle-count** bracket around the in_song read block, logged — I can add it behind a debug flag if you want the exact µs for each of the three reads.

Either is a small addition if you'd like the hard numbers rather than the estimate.

You're right — I overcomplicated it. The presence detector already tells us the odometer is gone; the fix is just to reset to 0 the moment it's absent, not wait.     lo,hi=L.min(),L.max(); ink=L>lo+FRAC*(hi-lo)
    ys=np.where(ink.any(1))[0]; xs=np.where(ink.any(0))[0]
    if not len(ys) or not len(xs): return np.zeros(GR*GC)
    m=ink[ys.min():ys.max()+1,xs.min():xs.max()+1].astype(float)
    ye=np.linspace(0,m.shape[0],GR+1).round().astype(int); xe=np.linspace(0,m.shape[1],GC+1).round().astype(int)
    g=np.empty((GR,GC))
    for r in range(GR):
        for c in range(GC):
            b=m[ye[r]:max(ye[r]+1,ye[r+1]),xe[c]:max(xe[c]+1,xe[c+1])]; g[r,c]=b.mean() if b.size else 0
    return np.round(g.reshape(-1)*255)
def covF(i): return covL(luma_of(load(i))[R0:R1,C0:C1])
# corpus-averaged note template
from gameplay.corpus import streak_corpus_dir
cf=sorted(glob.glob(str(streak_corpus_dir())+"/streak__*.png"))
tmpl=np.round(np.mean([covL(luma_of(np.asarray(Image.open(p).convert("RGB")))[R0:R1,C0:C1]) for p in cf],axis=0))
def sad(i): return int(np.abs(covF(i)-tmpl).sum())
# separation over full capture, classified by the units-mean present proxy (ground-ish)
um=np.array([luma_of(load(i))[83:97,78:88].mean() for i in range(len(F))])
THR=2000
locked=np.array([sad(i)<THR for i in range(len(F))])
present_proxy=um>90
# how many locked frames vs proxy; and SAD stats on locked runs
print("THR",THR)
print("locked frames:",int(locked.sum()),"  units-present frames:",int(present_proxy.sum()))
# slide frames (present_proxy True but not locked) — should be the transition
slide=present_proxy&~locked
print("present-but-not-locked (slide/overshoot):",int(slide.sum()))
# locked-but-absent (false positives) — should be ~0
fp=locked&~present_proxy
print("locked-but-units-dark (false lock):",int(fp.sum()))
PY

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-10 17:39:12Z)**_

Firmware compiles now, but the note-icon presence disagrees C-vs-Python on cap0420 (C=absent, Python=present). Since presence is an absolute SAD vs a fixed threshold (unlike the digit argmin, which has big margins), it's sensitive to the C `float` vs Python `float64` luma precision. Let me confirm that's the cause and measure the gap:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-10 17:39:31Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>

```bash
cd /Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/gameplay
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$TMPDIR/uv-cache"
uv run python - <<'PY'
import numpy as np
from gameplay.corpus import load_streak_corpus
from gameplay.score import build_streak_catalog
from gameplay.metadata import STREAK_NOTE_CELL, STREAK_GLYPH_ROWS as GR, STREAK_GLYPH_COLS as GC, STREAK_INK_FRAC as FRAC
LW=np.array([29,150,77])
corpus=load_streak_corpus(); cat=build_streak_catalog(corpus)
def cov(img, dtype):
    x0,y0,x1,y1=STREAK_NOTE_CELL
    L=(img[y0:y1,x0:x1].astype(dtype)@LW.astype(dtype))/dtype(256.0)
    lo,hi=L.min(),L.max(); ink=L>lo+dtype(FRAC)*(hi-lo)
    ys=np.where(ink.any(1))[0]; xs=np.where(ink.any(0))[0]
    m=ink[ys.min():ys.max()+1,xs.min():xs.max()+1].astype(np.float64)
    ye=np.linspace(0,m.shape[0],GR+1).round().astype(int); xe=np.linspace(0,m.shape[1],GC+1).round().astype(int)
    g=np.empty((GR,GC))
    for r in range(GR):
        for c in range(GC):
            b=m[ye[r]:max(ye[r]+1,ye[r+1]),xe[c]:max(xe[c]+1,xe[c+1])]; g[r,c]=b.mean() if b.size else 0
    return np.round(g.reshape(-1)*255).astype(np.int32)
from gameplay.score import _ensure_full_frame
for name in ["streak__035__cap0420.png"]:
    s=[x for x in corpus if x.path.name==name][0]
    img=_ensure_full_frame(s.image)
    c64=cov(img,np.float64); c32=cov(img,np.float32)
    t=cat.note_tmpl.astype(np.int32)
    print(name,"SAD float64",int(np.abs(c64-t).sum()),"  SAD float32",int(np.abs(c32-t).sum()))
PY

Got your edits. New ROIs (consistent 8-wide×15-tall digit cells, 10-wide note):
- note `{150,392,160,407}`, H `{165,392,173,407}`, T `{179,392,187,407}`, U `{194,392,202,407}`

**Answer to your question:** these are **absolute** to the 720×480 canonical frame — fixed pixel positions, *not* adjusted by scoreboard detection. The score reader has a chrome-registration mechanism (`calibrate_score` → a `(dx,dy)` block offset found by matching the scoreboard's static frame/chrome), but firmware v0 deliberately doesn't use it — every streak/score/multiplier ROI is a fixed band. That works because the HDMI-capture rig is physically stable (the scoreboard renders at the same pixels every frame; only minor A2D aliasing varies, which the relative-threshold coverage already absorbs). If the rig ever drifted, wiring registration in would shift all these ROIs by the detected offset — but today they're absolute.

The header is generated, so your hand-edits get overwritten on the next `export-c`. Let me port your ROIs into `metadata.py` (the source), relearn the masks at those boxes, and regenerate:

225	static void streak_cell_cov_roi(const uint8_t *frame, int w, int h,
226	                                const uint16_t roi[4], int is_light)
227	{
228	    int x0 = roi[0], y0 = roi[1], x1 = roi[2], y1 = roi[3];
229	    int W = x1 - x0, H = y1 - y0;
230	
231	    static float lum[GP_STREAK_CELL_MAX_H * GP_STREAK_CELL_MAX_W];
232	    float lo = 1e30f, hi = -1e30f;
233	    for (int r = 0; r < H; r++)
234	    {
235	        int fy = y0 + r;
236	        for (int c = 0; c < W; c++)
237	        {
238	            int fx = x0 + c;
239	            float v = 0.0f;
240	            if (fx >= 0 && fx < w && fy >= 0 && fy < h)
241	            {
242	                const uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)fy * (uint32_t)w + (uint32_t)fx) * GP_BPP;
243	                v = (float)((double)p[0] * 29.0 + (double)p[1] * 150.0 + (double)p[2] * 77.0) / 256.0f;
244	            }
245	            lum[r * W + c] = v;
246	            if (v < lo) { lo = v; }
247	            if (v > hi) { hi = v; }
248	        }
249	    }
250	    float thr = is_light ? (lo + (1.0f - GP_STREAK_INK_FRAC) * (hi - lo))
251	                         : (lo + GP_STREAK_INK_FRAC * (hi - lo));
252	    for (int i = 0; i < W * H; i++)
253	    {
254	        s_scell_ink[i] = is_light ? (lum[i] < thr ? 1u : 0u)

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-10 17:45:52Z)**_

Good question to pause on. Short answer: **no — we don't need floating point anywhere in the streak (or score/multiplier) reader.** The whole pipeline can be integer, and that's a *better* fix than the `double` I just reached for. Here's the reasoning, no changes yet.

## Where FP currently is, and why it isn't needed

**1. Luma** — `(B*29 + G*150 + R*77) / 256`
The numerator is already integer (≤ 65280). The `/256` is just rescaling to 0–255, and it **cancels** in every use: we only ever compare luma against a threshold derived from the same luma (min/max of the cell). So we can drop the divide entirely and work in the raw integer scale.

**2. Ink threshold** — `luma > lo + FRAC*(hi-lo)`, `FRAC = 0.5`
With FRAC = 0.5 the threshold is just the **midpoint**, so the test is exactly:
- bright ink: `2*luma > lo + hi`
- dark ink (units wheel): `2*luma < lo + hi`

Pure integer, and provably identical to the float comparison (no rounding). If FRAC were ever not 0.5, it's still integer: `(luma-lo)*den` vs `(hi-lo)*num`.

**3. Coverage grid** — already integer in C: `(sum*255 + n/2)/n`. Only Python computes it in float.

**4. Grid cell edges** — `gp_edge` uses `lround((double)i*extent/n)`; the integer form is `(i*extent + n/2)/n`.

**5. Everything downstream** — L1 match, note-SAD, argmin, the tracker — already integer.

So the only genuinely floating-point operations are the luma dot-product's divide and the edge rounding, both of which are removable.

## Why integer is the *better* answer (not double)

- **Exact parity by construction.** The reason C and Python disagreed on a borderline `known`/`present` flag isn't just float32-vs-float64 — there are two deterministic rounding-mode mismatches hiding in the float path: `np.round` is **banker's rounding** (half-to-even) while C's `(sum*255+n/2)/n` and `lround` are **half-up**, and `np.linspace().round()` vs `lround`. Integer math with one defined rounding removes those gaps entirely. Double only papers over the float32 part.
- **Speed.** The SAM9X75 is an ARM926EJ-S — **no hardware FPU**. Every `float`/`double` op is soft-float (library emulation); `double` is the *slowest* option. These readers run per-observation at ~3 Hz so it's not a bottleneck, but there's no reason to pay soft-float when the whole thing is naturally integer.

## Scope / caveats

- **Multiplier** reader is already pure integer.
- **Score** reader uses the same float-luma + `gp_edge` pattern; it *works* today only because it compares a final value with big argmin margins (float slop can't flip it). It could/should convert the same way, but that's a separate change with its own cross-check.
- The **screen classifier / song matcher** use float *normalization* over their fingerprint vectors — that's the "soft-float over small vectors" the journal calls out, a genuinely different thing and out of scope here.
- To keep parity obvious, I'd convert **both** sides (C and the Python prototype) to the same integer formulas, so the cross-check proves equality rather than us reasoning about float64 exactness.

**Recommendation:** revert the `double` change and instead make the streak coverage integer (midpoint threshold + integer edges), mirrored in `score.py`. Bit-exact parity, faster, simpler. Want me to do that for the streak reader now (and optionally the score reader in the same pass)?

found a bug in monotonic streak logic. I saw a misread on the tens place. say a 3 instead of 0. after that, every roll of ones place forced a tens increment even though it clearly read a lower number. 11x read as 14x, 12x read as 15x, etc. a clear read of a digit needs to trump the automatic rollover logic.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-10 17:58:03Z)**_

That's a real bug, and your diagnosis is exactly right: the tracker's forward-only monotonic search (`[last, last+jump]`) can never represent a value *below* `last`, so once a tens misread bumped `last` up, a confident tens=0/1 read had no matching candidate in the window — the search just tracked the rolling units and drifted the tens upward. Monotonic was overriding a clear read.

The fix is your rule: **a confident digit is authoritative for its place; the rollover/carry logic only fills *unknown* places.** That also makes a confident *misread* a self-correcting one-frame blip instead of a permanent lock. Let me rewrite the tracker (host + firmware) around that.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-10 18:12:18Z)**_

This is the crux: it's a **genuine per-frame ambiguity, not a fixable template bug.** Look at the glyph on the misread frames — the "0" wheel renders with a nearly-*closed* top loop and an open bottom loop, which is exactly an "8":

```
  0-template        8-template        glyph @1573 (a "0" wheel)
  @@@- @@@@         @@@@ @@@@@         @@@@ @@@@@   ← top loop nearly closed
  @@@- @@@@         @@@@@@@  (bar)     @@@@ @@@@@
  @@@- @@@@         @@@@ @@@@@         @@@@   @@@   ← bottom loop open
```

The wheel's zero has a center slash/seam, and A2D aliasing closes the top loop on ~half the frames — so it **alternates 0,8,0,8 frame-to-frame**, and the 8-frames match the 8-template *better* (4590 vs 6885). No confidence threshold or template tweak fixes that; per-frame it truly looks like an 8.

So it has to be handled **temporally**. My recommendation — and it cleanly subsumes your lock fix:

**Debounce per place: a *changed* digit must repeat for 2 consecutive confident reads before it commits.**
- The 0↔8 alternation never persists → the spurious 8 never commits → tens stays 0. Flicker gone.
- A *real* digit change is sustained → commits after one extra frame (~300 ms lag, invisible).
- **Can't lock**: the value follows the debounced reads up *or* down, so a sustained lower read (your 11x correction) always wins — no monotonic window, no forward-only trap.
- The big hundreds blips (→900) die the same way (never persist).

This replaces the monotonic search entirely (no `max_jump`/window), keeps "clear read trumps" (a *sustained* clear read is authoritative), and fixes both the lock and the newly-surfaced flicker.

I haven't built it yet — it's a real tracker change and you're steering closely. Want me to implement the debounce (host + firmware), or would you rather commit the lock fix as-is first and treat the 0/8 flicker separately?

authoritative for its place (a clear digit trumps the rollover logic, so a
misread self-corrects next frame); an unreadable wheel is filled (holds last,
or resets to 0 on a higher-place carry). This replaced a monotonic forward
window that could lock the value high on a tens misread.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-10 18:45:17Z)**_

Here's the diagnosis — and it's fixable:

## What's happening with units-9

| wheel | median dist | p90 | max | gated by `UNK_DIST=9500` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hundreds | 1189 | 3825 | 5423 | 0/46 |
| tens | 276 | 6450 | 6885 | 0/46 |
| **units** | 972 | 7605 | **12309** | **3/41** |

The units wheel (dark-on-light, always rolling) has a much **fatter distance tail** than the tens/hundreds. The two units-9 exemplars that land at ~12300 are **classified correctly as 9** — but their distance exceeds the 9500 gate, so they're marked *unreadable* and the tracker throws them away. That's the "rarely detects 9": it's recognized, then discarded by a gate tuned for the cleaner white-on-dark wheels.

Two root contributors:
1. **Under-sampled templates.** The units bank has only 2–7 exemplars per digit (9 has 4, 6 has 2). A template averaged from 4 noisy dark-on-light glyphs is a loose fit, so even correct 9s match far from it.
2. **One global gate** for three wheels of different quality — too strict for the units wheel.

## Options (increasing leverage)

**A. Per-cell confidence gate (quick).** Give the units wheel a looser `UNK_DIST` (its distances legitimately run higher). The ~12300 units-9s would pass while tens/hundreds keep the tight gate. Cheap, directly fixes the reported symptom. Risk: admits a few more units misreads — but that's exactly what the **pending debounce** absorbs, so these pair naturally.

**B. Grow the labeled corpus (durable, best).** More units exemplars — especially 9 and 6 — sharpen the templates so real digits match *closer*, lowering distances across the board (helps every wheel, not just the gate). The 6549-frame capture has plenty of material. Cost is a labeling pass (hand-read montages like the original 46, or auto-label units at settled frames using the now-working tens/hundreds tracker).

## Recommendation

Do **B** as the real fix and let **A** ride along — but B is a labeling effort I don't want to spin up unilaterally given how closely you've been steering the ROIs and frames. My suggestion: **do the debounce first** (it's already queued and makes the reader forgiving of the looser gate), then a corpus-growth pass with the per-cell gate.

Want me to (1) start the debounce now, (2) do a units-focused corpus-labeling pass (I'll generate 9/6 montages for you to eyeball), or (3) just apply the quick per-cell gate to unblock 9 detection immediately?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-10 19:04:11Z)**_

Now I see the exact mechanism — it's a **carry-roll misread**, not a flicker. At the 99→100 carry (frames 1571–1579), the hundreds wheel is *mid-roll* and reads `9` confidently for **two** frames (1575–1576), so debounce commits it → 900. Debounce can't catch a 2-frame misread. Also frame 1575 briefly shows 0 because the tens committed (→0) before the hundreds did.

The streak physically can't jump 90→900 in one poll, so the right backstop is a **symmetric plausibility clamp** on the per-frame value change (reject jumps larger than a streak can gain per poll). Symmetric, so unlike the old forward-only window it can't lock. Let me prototype it over the capture to pick the threshold before editing source:

class T:
    def __init__(s,maxstep): s.ms=maxstep; s.reset()
    def reset(s): s.val=0;s.seen=False;s.dg=[0,0,0];s.pend=[-1,-1,-1];s.pn=[0,0,0]
    def upd(s,r):
        if not r.present: s.reset(); return 0
        if not s.seen:
            if sum(r.known)<2: return 0
            s.dg=[r.digits[i] if r.known[i] else 0 for i in range(3)];s.pend=[-1,-1,-1];s.pn=[0,0,0];s.seen=True
        else:
            snap=(list(s.dg),list(s.pend),list(s.pn)); carry=False
            for i in range(3):
                if r.known[i]:
                    d=r.digits[i]
                    if d==s.dg[i]: s.pend[i]=-1;s.pn[i]=0
                    else:
                        s.pn[i]=s.pn[i]+1 if d==s.pend[i] else 1; s.pend[i]=d
                        if s.pn[i]>=DEB[i]: s.dg[i]=d;s.pend[i]=-1;s.pn[i]=0;carry=True

            nv=s.dg[0]*100+s.dg[1]*10+s.dg[2]

            s.val=nv; return nv

544	class StreakTracker:
545	    """Reconcile noisy per-frame odometer reads into a streak value.
546	
547	    Presence is binary: the odometer is either locked (shown, streak ≥ ~25) or not
548	    (absent / mid-slide). **When it is not present the streak has reset — go straight
549	    to 0** (that is the only reset path; a broken streak makes the counter disappear).
550	
551	    While it is present, a confident wheel read is authoritative for its place, but a
552	    *changed* digit must be **debounced** — confirmed by `cfg.debounce[place]`
553	    consecutive confident reads before it commits. The slow wheels (hundreds, tens)
554	    need 2, so a single-frame misread (e.g. the tens 0↔8 aliasing flip) never sticks
555	    yet a sustained real change still commits; the units wheel is immediate (1). A
556	    committed change carries: unreadable lower places reset to 0 (a rollover). An
557	    unreadable place otherwise holds its last digit. First appearance seeds from the
558	    confident wheels (unknown places 0) once ≥2 agree. Debounce follows reads up *or*
559	    down, so it never locks.
560	    """
561	
562	    def __init__(self, config: StreakConfig = DEFAULT_STREAK_CONFIG) -> None:
563	        self.cfg = config
564	        self.reset()

cd /Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
gameplay: streak tracker debounce + plausibility clamp

Fixes a reported streak lock and two failures it surfaced, all in the
stateful tracker (gp_streak_track / StreakTracker).

The prior monotonic forward window [last, last+30] could not represent a
value below last, so a tens misread that nudged last up locked in -- every
units roll then forced the tens higher (11x read as 14x, 12x->15x...).
Switching to "confident read trumps" fixed the lock but unmasked two
pre-existing misreads the window had hidden:
- Tens 0<->8 flicker: the odometer's slashed zero closes its top loop under
  A2D aliasing, so a tens "0" matches the 8 template better and reads 8
  confidently, alternating frame-to-frame (100<->180).
- Carry-roll blip: at 99->100 the mid-roll hundreds wheel reads 9 confidently
  for ~2 frames -> a 900 flash.

Fix, both symmetric so they correct downward and never lock:
- Per-place debounce (GP_STREAK_DEBOUNCE {2,2,1}): a changed digit commits
  only after N consecutive confident reads. Slow wheels (hundreds/tens) N=2
  kills single-frame flips; units N=1 stays responsive. A committed change
  carries (unreadable lower places reset to 0); an unreadable place holds.
- Plausibility clamp (GP_STREAK_MAX_STEP 50): reject a committed per-frame
  value change a streak can't make per ~3Hz poll (the 2-frame carry misread
  that clears debounce). The seed bypasses it, so a real reappearance snaps in.

gp_streak_state_t gains pend[3]/pend_n[3]. Over the 6549-frame capture: 0
implausible jumps (was 94), max back to 304, anchors exact; host suite 74.

Still open (next): units-9 detection -- the dark-on-light units wheel has a
fat distance tail, so a correct 9 exceeds the confidence gate and is dropped;
needs more units exemplars from the capture.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -2
```

`ScreenDashboard_ApplyStreak(0)` set an **empty** string, and `lestring_set_utf8("")` doesn't repaint over the previously-drawn glyphs — so the prior count stayed on screen. Your two reset paths were both *posting* 0 correctly — the label just wasn't clearing:

- **Miss:** the tracker resets to 0 once the odometer isn't locked.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-10 22:13:33Z)**_

Good catch — that's a real logic gap. The lag is because at 49→50 the **units updates immediately (→0) while the tens is debounced/mid-roll and holds 4** → shows `40`, then the tens catches up → `50`. But a units wrap `9→0` *is* the carry signal: the tens must have stepped, so we should update it promptly rather than trusting the lagging tens wheel.

The clean fix: on a confident units read, round the previous value **up** to the next value with that units digit — `prev + ((u - prev) mod 10)`. That gives 49→50 (delta 1), and works for any delta (41→50, 47→52…). Let me look at the current tracker to slot it in:

   re-rounds a stale value. If a wrong-high tens was corrected downward, the
